# AGENTS.md: instructions for AI coding assistants

You are helping a team at **Hackreation x ERI** (Oct 31, 2026), a one-day hackathon. Coding time is a few hours, and demos are short (about 3 minutes).

## Read before writing code
0. `wiki/ESSENTIALS.md`: the one-page rules. Always enforce these.
1. `wiki/event/hackreation.md`: schedule, challenges, judging
2. The PRD for the team's challenge in `wiki/prds/`
3. `wiki/stack/<tech>.md` for how to build on the stack correctly (hooks, escaping, Expo APIs, RLS), then `wiki/company/tech-stack.md`: **build on the recommended stack** (HTML/CSS/jQuery, PHP, MySQL, WordPress; Expo + Supabase for mobile)
4. `wiki/domain/` for quick rules, and `wiki/knowledge/` for the deep, sourced knowledge base (benefits, employment law, compliance, the Wisconsin landscape, datasets, ERI org). Check each page's `last_verified` and `confidence`.

## Hard rules
- **Synthetic data only.** Use your project's `fixtures/` (or `data/job_seekers.csv`, `data/job_postings.csv`). Never ask for, invent realistic, or accept real client info (names, SSNs, case notes, benefits).
- **No connections to ERI systems.** Prototypes are standalone.
- **Accessibility is required**, by ERI's own list in `wiki/domain/accessibility.md`: labels, keyboard, focus, contrast, live regions, plain language. WCAG is a useful reference, not a claim: say "we did the keyboard pass and the screen reader pass", never "compliant" ([CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), section 7).
- **DVR's provider agreement says any AI tool used with a DVR consumer's information needs that consumer's prior written or verbal consent** (see `wiki/knowledge/compliance/vr-confidentiality-34-cfr-361-38.md`). Design AI features so they can be switched off or gated behind recorded consent.
- **Billing (only if you build a billing tool; none of P1 to P4 does):** flag only. Never write logic or copy that suggests documentation wording to reach a higher rate. A person approves every billing decision.
- **Benefits math:** label results "estimate only" and route to Wisconsin WIPA (1-877-826-1752).
- **Secrets:** read API keys from env vars or `.env` (git-ignored). Never hard-code them.
- Keep dependencies minimal. Prefer no build step. Explain any new dependency in the team README.
- Work inside your project folder `challenges/p<n>-.../`. Don't modify `starters/`, `data/` or `wiki/` unless asked.

## Defaults
- PHP 8.2+ (8.3 preferred; 8.1 is end of life), PDO with prepared statements, escape all output (`htmlspecialchars` / WordPress `esc_html`).
- WordPress: prefix with `eri_`; shortcode or REST; no paid plugins.
- Expo: SDK 58 (see `starters/expo-supabase/AGENTS.md`); use `npx expo install`.
- Write a short `README.md` in the team folder with run steps that take under 10 minutes.

<!-- FILE: wiki/ESSENTIALS.md -->

# Hackathon essentials (read this, skip the rest)

Everything a team needs on rules and data for Oct 31, on one page. The deep [knowledge base](knowledge/README.md) is optional background.

## ERI in 30 seconds
- A Madison-based nonprofit (since 1990, with staff in Milwaukee too) that helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs.
- Work can shrink SSI or SSDI (Social Security disability checks) or affect Medicaid (health coverage). Fear of that stops people from saying yes to jobs.
- ERI is paid mostly per service, by Wisconsin DVR and Social Security, and only when work is documented and claimed.
- A small web team runs ERI's WordPress sites. Build on the [recommended stack](company/tech-stack.md) (plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that could be pasted into WordPress) so they can keep it.

## The 6 rules
1. **Fake data only** (privacy law protects client data). Use `data/` or your project's `fixtures/`. No real names, case notes, benefits amounts or diagnoses, ever. A Codespace port you make Public can be opened by anyone with the link, so fake data only there too. The repo is public: anything you push is world-readable.
2. **No connection to ERI systems.** Your prototype stands alone.
3. **AI is allowed, optional, and for fake data only.** An assistant you run yourself is fine: a chat in another browser tab, a tool on your own laptop, or GitHub Copilot in a Codespace if your account has it. Paste only synthetic data and repo code, and leave nothing that needs a paid key in the project folder. The backup team editor has no assistant. In real life, DVR requires the client's consent before any AI tool touches their info; at the event, AI may only see synthetic data.
4. **Benefits answers are estimates** (wrong benefits info hurts people). Show "Estimate only, talk to a benefits specialist: WIPA 1-877-826-1752." Never say "you'll keep your SSI."
5. **Only if you build a billing tool (none of P1 to P4 does): billing tools flag, people decide** (this is public money). Find work that was done but not billed. Never suggest wording to get a higher rate.
6. **Accessible or it doesn't count.** Keyboard works, labels on inputs, visible focus, good contrast, plain words ([checklist](domain/accessibility.md)).

## Getting started
Open a GitHub Codespace (free account) or use your own laptop (git and Node 20 or newer). The captain forks the repo and everyone works from the team fork. No account or no Node? The backup team editor (address and password on your team card) works in any browser. Steps, help and hand-in are in [START-HERE.md](../START-HERE.md); times and place are on the [event page](event/hackreation.md).

## Sample data you get
ERI's four projects (P1 to P4) each carry their own fake data in `challenges/p<n>-.../fixtures/`. That is all you need. The shared `data/` folder has more fake records (`job_seekers.csv`, `job_postings.csv`) if you want them; its DVR, Ticket and county files are for billing tools only, and none of P1 to P4 is one.

## Numbers you might need
Benefits numbers are for any project that shows an estimate; their source is [wiki/domain/ssa-work-incentives-2026.md](domain/ssa-work-incentives-2026.md) (SSA Red Book), and they are estimates to verify before you hard-code anything. The 2027 figures were announced on 2026-10-14 (the source page says so). The DVR rows are for billing tools only (none of P1 to P4).

| Thing | Value |
| --- | --- |
| SSI max federal payment (2026 / 2027) | $994 / $1,029 a month |
| SSDI earnings line, SGA (2026 / 2027) | $1,690 / $1,770 a month |
| SSDI trial work month (2026 / 2027) | $1,210 / $1,270 a month |
| SSI rough math | check drops $1 for every $2 earned after the first $85 |
| DVR job placement pay to ERI | $1,600, or $2,000 (20+ h and insurance or ≥ $12/h), or $2,200 (35+ h and insurance or ≥ $16/h) |
| DVR monthly job support | $1,600 (instruction) or $500 (retention) per month employed |

## Don't pitch employers on
- The Section 503 "7% goal" (rescinded Sept 2026) or the WOTC tax credit (lapsed for hires after 2025); sources: [knowledge base](knowledge/README.md) and [Rehabilitation Act page](knowledge/employment-law/rehabilitation-act.md). Pitch retention, accommodations (most cost little or nothing; see askjan.org), and ERI support instead.

## Where to send people (put these in your app)
- Benefits questions: **Wisconsin WIPA 1-877-826-1752**
- Rights or a DVR dispute: **Disability Rights Wisconsin / Client Assistance Program 800-928-8778**
- Accommodation ideas: **askjan.org**

## What this tells a hacker
- **ERI is a WordPress shop with multisite.** A plugin, shortcode or block drops straight into their world.
- They already build **interactive tools** (the transition planning tool, gamified curricula). A new tool is a natural fit.
- **Accessibility is core.** Every site has an accessibility policy and skip links. Yours must too.
- No public mobile app was found. Expo is in their skill set but not yet in production (as far as public info shows).
- No public case-management system was found. Billing and case notes live in internal tools we can't see, which is why PRD 01 uses synthetic CSVs.


<!-- FILE: wiki/company/eri.md -->

# Employment Resources, Inc. (ERI)

**One line:** a Madison, Wisconsin nonprofit (founded 1990) that helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs **without losing the benefits and health care they depend on.**

- **Mission:** "practice and promote innovative services to advance employment opportunities" for people with disabilities.
- **Vision:** people with disabilities can pursue financial security and meaningful work without fear of losing health care or other essential benefits.
- **Values:** Quality, Accountability, Integrity, Inclusiveness, Respect, Trust.
- **HQ:** 4604 Cottage Grove Road, Madison, WI 53716 · (608) 246-3444 · [eri-wi.org](https://eri-wi.org)
- **Footprint:** statewide in Wisconsin, with staff in Madison, Milwaukee, Green Bay, and northeast and northwest WI. Ticket to Work clients come from WI, OH, IN, IL, MN, IA and MI. ERI also runs national technical-assistance web projects.
- **Size:** about 29 staff ([staff page](https://eri-wi.org/staff/)); 10-person board ([board](https://eri-wi.org/about/board/)).

## Money (FY2025, [IRS 990 via ProPublica](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/391681074))
| | |
| --- | --- |
| Revenue | $3.07M |
| Expenses | $3.04M (near break-even) |
| Program service revenue | $1.68M (55%): DVR, SSA, Dane County, DHS contracts |
| Contributions and grants | $1.37M (45%) |
| Net assets | $0.70M |

**Why it matters for you:** margins are thin. A tool that saves staff hours or catches missed billing has real dollar value.

## What ERI does
| Line of work | Plain-English version | Paid by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Incentives Benefits Counseling (WIBS) | "If I take this job, what happens to my SSI/SSDI/Medicaid?" ERI does intake, gets signed releases, verifies benefits and writes a personal benefits report | DVR, IRIS, care managers refer |
| WIPA | Same help, under ERI's federal SSA contract. ERI is Wisconsin's **sole** WIPA provider | SSA cooperative agreement |
| Ticket to Work (ERI PLUS) | Job search and support for SSI/SSDI recipients working toward leaving cash benefits; mostly virtual | SSA Ticket payments |
| Employment counseling and Supported Employment | Find the right job, then help keep it (job coaching, retention) | **Wisconsin DVR** fee-for-service |
| Youth transition (VFPS, CLTS) | Planning for life after high school | Counties, DHS |
| Comprehensive Community Services (CCS) | Mental health and substance-use recovery support | Dane County |
| Pre-driving assessment | Is driver training realistic? | Various |
| Business and employer services | Recruiting and retention consulting for employers hiring people with disabilities | Fee-for-service |
| Training and design | Builds websites, e-learning and LMS content for DHS, universities and national TA centers | Contracts and grants |

## History highlights ([about](https://eri-wi.org/about/))
- 1990: founded
- 1992-95: trained Wisconsin's first work-incentives benefits specialists
- 2000: ERI's benefits-counseling model became an SSA "best practice," feeding the federal program now called WIPA
- 2008: started the Ticket to Work Employment Network (ERI PLUS) and e-learning for benefits specialists
- 2014: Wisconsin PROMISE federal demonstration site
- 2018: built the Explore Work curriculum and site
- 2021: became the sole Wisconsin SSA WIPA provider
- 2024 (Nov): Kweku-TeAngelo Cargile Jr. named Executive Director ([Madison365](https://madison365.com/employment-resources-inc-names-kweku-teangelo-cargile-jr-as-new-executive-director/))

## Where a hackathon can help
1. **Software that connects applicants to opportunities** (the event theme)
2. **DVR billing**: DVR pays vendors like ERI per service milestone, so documentation and invoicing have to line up (see [DVR rules](../domain/dvr-supported-employment.md))
3. Projects a small web team can **actually maintain** (see [tech-stack.md](tech-stack.md))

<!-- FILE: wiki/company/tech-stack.md -->

# Recommended stack

**The recommended stack is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that could be pasted into WordPress as a block or shortcode.** ERI's public sites run on **WordPress** (see [digital-properties.md](digital-properties.md)), so that is what ERI can keep. P1 to P4 already ship that way. The starters below are optional; PHP, MySQL and WordPress plugins are there if your project outgrows a plain page. For a phone-first prototype, Expo + Supabase. **Confirm with ERI before you count on any of these being adopted.**

| Target | Tools | Starter in this repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Websites | HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery | `starters/static-web` |
| | PHP, SQL/MySQL/phpMyAdmin | `starters/php-mysql` |
| | WordPress | `starters/wordpress-plugin`, `starters/eri-job-card` (block) |
| Mobile apps | JavaScript, React Native/Expo, Postgres/Supabase | `starters/expo-supabase` |
| AI | Chat assistants (Claude, ChatGPT) or an API key you bring | `starters/ai-helpers` — **read the limits below first** |

## Pick by project

These are [ERI's four problem statements](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md). Each has a different shape, and the shape decides the stack.

| ERI project | Start here | Why | Only if you need |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **P1** Show Your Skills | `static-web` | Media + a preview page; nothing needs a server if the portfolio exports as a file | `expo-supabase` — if you want a real **view-only link** and native camera. Then you own the hosting question |
| **P2** My Workday Assistant | `static-web`, phone-first | One step at a time is local state. Must work at 320px and on a tablet | `expo-supabase` — if you want it installable with offline tasks |
| **P3** Job Coach Connection | `static-web`, two browser tabs | Employee view and coach inbox are two views over one state. Two tabs on one laptop is an honest demo of a simulated inbox | `php-mysql` or Supabase — if requests must cross **devices**, not tabs |
| **P4** Employer Opportunity Hub | `static-web`, then wrap as a WordPress plugin | Form in, explained matches out. **The most WordPress-ready of the four** and the likeliest for ERI's web team to host first | `php-mysql` — if the industry/task library outgrows a CSV |

**WordPress fit, honestly:** P4 is a natural plugin. P1 can be one, but media uploads are the hard part. **P2 and P3 are stateful apps, not page content** — forcing them into a plugin costs you the day. Build them standalone and say so in the demo.

## Three things no starter here does yet

ERI's statements need these. Nothing in `starters/` demonstrates them, and none is verified in this repo — budget time, and check on your own target browser early.

| Capability | Who needs it | The boring way that works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Photo / video / audio capture** | P1 (required: "at least one non-text method") | `<input type="file" accept="image/*,video/*,audio/*" capture>` gets you the phone camera and mic roll with zero JS. `MediaRecorder` records in-page if you want that. Expo: `expo-camera`, `expo-av` |
| **Audio instructions** | P1, P2 ("listen rather than read") | `speechSynthesis` needs no key, no file and no cost — **but it is UNVERIFIED on the day-of image.** On Linux with no speech voices installed it returns an empty voice list and silently does nothing, and the workspaces are Linux containers. Treat pre-recorded audio files as the real fallback, always ship the text, and verify this at the T-2 dry run |
| **Two roles, one state** | P3 (employee → coach inbox → response) | `localStorage` plus the `storage` event, or `BroadcastChannel`, syncs two tabs on one machine. Real cross-device needs a backend |

Also: **P2 needs step images.** The data generator makes CSVs, not pictures. Use simple icons or take four photos on your phone; ERI asked for pictures with the text, and a step with no picture fails AC-P2.3.

## ERI's limits on AI

Read this before using `starters/ai-helpers`.

ERI put these **out of scope in writing**, and they are not style preferences:

- **No AI-generated assessment of applicant suitability** (P1 §9).
- **No automated hiring or applicant scoring** (P1 §9, P4 §11).
- **Never rank candidates based on disability** (P4 §10).
- **Never suggest an accommodation from a disability label alone** (P4 §10).
- **No automated accommodation decisions**; complex legal questions go to qualified professionals (P4 §10).

So: use an LLM to help you *write code*, to turn text into plain language, or to explain a match **that your own rules already made**. Do not use it to judge a person. A model that outputs "this candidate is a 72% fit" is the exact product ERI said not to build, and it will lose on the rubric.

Two of the bundled prompts (`classify-service-note.md`, `inclusive-job-post.md`) were written for the retired challenges and no longer map to any of the four.

## Ground rules

- **Prototypes stay standalone.** No connections to ERI systems, and no AI agents pointed at anything real.
- Use only data in `data/` and your challenge's `data/`, which is synthetic.
- Prefer no build step and no new paid services. If you add a dependency, say why in your team README.
- Something you hand ERI should run from its README in under 10 minutes.
- **Accessibility is 25% of the score and it is tested, not eyeballed.** Every project above has keyboard, screen reader and plain-language requirements in ERI's own statement.


<!-- FILE: wiki/domain/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility: the bar

ERI serves people with disabilities. **An inaccessible project can't win.** Target WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Must-haves (judges will check in 2 minutes)
- [ ] Works with **keyboard only**: Tab through everything, visible focus ring, no traps
- [ ] Every input has a **visible label**; errors are announced in text, not only by color
- [ ] Headings in order (one `h1`), landmarks (`main`, `nav`), and a skip link
- [ ] **Contrast** 4.5:1 for text; don't rely on color alone
- [ ] Images have `alt` text (decorative = `alt=""`)
- [ ] Usable at 200% zoom and 320px wide (phones)
- [ ] Touch targets at least 44x44 px
- [ ] Plain language: about a 6th-grade reading level for job seeker screens; define acronyms
- [ ] Status updates use `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`; mobile uses `accessibilityLabel`
- [ ] Test once with a screen reader: VoiceOver (Mac/iOS: Cmd+F5), NVDA (Windows), or TalkBack (Android)

## Quick tools
- Browser: Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools > Lighthouse > Accessibility)
- `npx @axe-core/cli http://localhost:8000`
- WebAIM contrast checker

## Beyond compliance
Design **with** disabled users. Teams that test with a person with lived experience during the day get a scoring bonus.


<!-- FILE: wiki/domain/dvr-supported-employment.md -->

# Wisconsin DVR: how vendors like ERI get paid

**DVR** = Wisconsin Division of Vocational Rehabilitation (part of the Department of Workforce Development). It's federally funded under the Rehabilitation Act. DVR helps people with disabilities get jobs and **buys services from vendors** like ERI.

Source: [DVR Statewide Service Fee Structure](https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/service-providers/statewide-service-fee-structure.htm), effective **Jul 1, 2026 to Jun 30, 2028**, and its [appendix](https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/service-providers/tech-specs/appendix.htm). Always check the source; rates change.

## The flow
1. A DVR counselor and the consumer write an **IPE** (Individualized Plan for Employment).
2. DVR issues a **purchase order (PO)**, which is prior written authorization for a specific service. **No PO, no pay.**
3. The vendor contacts the consumer within **5 days** of receiving the PO.
4. The vendor delivers the service and submits the required **report**, usually within **5 business days**.
5. The vendor invoices; DVR pays. A report returned for missing elements must be fixed within **10 business days**.

## Supported Employment (SE) services
| Code here | Service | Rate | Paid when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SE-CP | Career Profile | $1,000 | Meeting, plan, long-term care coordination, report ≤ 5 business days; start ≤ 30 days, finish ≤ 90 days |
| SE-JPDP | Job Preparation and Development **Plan** | $350 | Meeting, plan, report ≤ 5 business days; finish ≤ 45 days |
| SE-JDH | Job Development and **Hire** | $1,600 standard; **$2,000 / $2,200 preferred** | Monthly reports, 90-day reviews, **Hire report ≤ 5 business days after hire** |
| SE-JTA | Job and Task Analysis | $275 | Report within 1 week of job start |
| SE-MSI | Monthly Systematic Instruction (incl. retention) | $1,600 / month | **Only months the consumer is employed**; LTC coordination at 60 days; monthly report ≤ 5 business days |
| SE-RET | Retention (when no SI) | $500 / month | Same as above |
| SE-TLTS | Transition to Long-Term Support | $1,300 (≤ 6 months) / $500 (> 6 months) | After 90+ days employed; transition report |

(The codes in the first column are this repo's shorthand, not DVR's activity codes.)

### Preferred outcome for Job Development and Hire
| Rate | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **$2,200** | 35+ hours/week **and** (health insurance **or** ≥ $16.00/hour) |
| **$2,000** | 20+ hours/week **and** (health insurance **or** ≥ $12.00/hour) |
| $1,600 | Any other qualifying hire |

Ongoing support max: 24 months (age 25+) or 48 months (under 25), unless DVR authorizes more.

## Where revenue leaks (PRD 01)
These are hypotheses that apply to any DVR vendor:
- **Gaps in monthly billing.** A month of support was delivered but never invoiced. Or the person wasn't working that month, in which case it's correctly unbilled.
- **Which milestone does a note support?** The $350 Plan and the $1,600 Hire are **different, sequential services**, each with its own PO. They aren't two codes for the same work. The real risk is a hire that happened but was never invoiced, or invoiced at $1,600 when it met preferred criteria.
- **Late or incomplete reports** can delay or block payment.
- **Do the people who document and the people who bill talk?** Unknown. Ask ERI.

## The compliance line (read this)
DVR money is public, federally funded money. A good tool:
- ✅ finds work that was **authorized and delivered** but not billed, or billed too low
- ✅ tells staff which **required elements are missing** from a note, so it reflects what they actually did
- ✅ warns before report deadlines
- ❌ never suggests wording to qualify for a higher rate than what happened
- ❌ never bills automatically. **A person reviews and approves every flag.**

Billing for services not delivered is fraud (state law and the federal False Claims Act). Building "revenue integrity" is great; building "upcoding" is not.


<!-- FILE: wiki/domain/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **ADRC** | Aging and Disability Resource Center (county info hubs in WI) |
| **CCS** | Comprehensive Community Services: mental health and substance-use recovery program |
| **CIE** | Competitive Integrated Employment: a regular job, at least minimum wage, alongside non-disabled coworkers |
| **CLTS** | Children's Long-Term Support waiver (WI) |
| **CWIC** | Community Work Incentives Coordinator: certified WIPA benefits counselor |
| **DVR** | Wisconsin Division of Vocational Rehabilitation: funds job services, pays vendors like ERI |
| **EN** | Employment Network: an org (like ERI PLUS) that serves Ticket to Work holders |
| **Family Care / IRIS** | Wisconsin long-term care programs (managed care / self-directed) |
| **IPE** | Individualized Plan for Employment: the DVR plan with the job goal |
| **IRWE** | Impairment-Related Work Expense: disability costs subtracted from earnings when SSA counts income |
| **LTC / LTS** | Long-term care / long-term support |
| **Medicaid / BadgerCare** | Health coverage; often the biggest fear about working |
| **PASS** | Plan to Achieve Self-Support: an SSI rule that lets people set aside money for a work goal |
| **PO** | Purchase order: DVR's written authorization to deliver and bill a service |
| **ROI** | Release of Information: client consent to share records |
| **SE** | Supported Employment: job development plus ongoing on-the-job support |
| **SGA** | Substantial Gainful Activity: SSA's monthly earnings line ($1,690 in 2026 and $1,770 in 2027, non-blind) |
| **SI** | Systematic Instruction: structured on-the-job training |
| **SSA** | Social Security Administration |
| **SSDI** | Social Security Disability Insurance (work-history based) |
| **SSI** | Supplemental Security Income (needs based) |
| **Ticket to Work** | SSA program that pays ENs when beneficiaries work and earn |
| **TWP** | Trial Work Period: 9 months of testing work on SSDI |
| **VFPS** | Vocational Futures Planning and Support: ERI's youth transition model |
| **WIBS** | Work Incentives Benefits Specialist (ERI's title) |
| **WIPA** | Work Incentives Planning and Assistance: SSA-funded benefits counseling; ERI describes itself as WI's sole provider (2021-2026 award; check the current award) |


<!-- FILE: wiki/domain/privacy-and-data.md -->

# Privacy and data rules

1. **Synthetic data only.** Use the files in `data/`. Never type, paste or upload real client info: names, SSNs, case notes, benefits amounts, diagnoses.
2. **No ERI system access.** No logins, exports or screenshots of ERI's real tools.
3. **API keys are yours.** Put them in `.env`, which is git-ignored. Never commit them.
4. **Assume public.** This repo is public. Anything you push is visible to everyone.
5. **Design for real privacy later.** If your idea would hold real data, write down in your team README what it would need: hosting, encryption, consent (ROI), access roles, audit logs. ERI decides after the event.


<!-- FILE: wiki/domain/ssa-work-incentives-2026.md -->

# SSI / SSDI and work: 2026 numbers

The #1 reason people with disabilities turn down work is **fear of losing benefits and health care.** ERI's benefits specialists (WIBS / CWICs) answer "what happens if I take this job?"

Source: [SSA Red Book, What's New in 2026](https://www.ssa.gov/redbook/newfor2026.htm). Verify before you hard-code anything.

| 2026 figure | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| SGA (Substantial Gainful Activity), non-blind | $1,690 / month |
| SGA, blind | $2,830 / month |
| Trial Work Period (TWP) month threshold | $1,210 / month |
| SSI Federal Benefit Rate, individual | $994 / month |
| SSI Federal Benefit Rate, couple | $1,491 / month |
| Student Earned Income Exclusion | $2,410 / month, up to $9,730 / year |

**2027 values are out** (3.6% COLA announced 2026-10-14): SGA $1,770 non-blind and $2,950 blind; TWP $1,270; SSI FBR $1,029 individual and $1,544 couple. The **Wisconsin SSI state supplement** rose to $92.16 (individual) on 2026-05-01. Full table: [benefits quick reference](../knowledge/benefits/benefits-quick-reference-2026.md).

## The two programs, simply
- **SSDI** (Social Security Disability Insurance): based on past work. Earnings over the **TWP** amount use up one of 9 trial months. After the TWP, earning over **SGA** can stop the check (with an extended period of eligibility safety net).
- **SSI** (Supplemental Security Income): needs-based. Roughly, SSA ignores the first $20 of any income and $65 of earnings, then **reduces the check $1 for every $2 earned** above that. Medicaid can continue under **1619(b)** even when the check reaches $0.

Rough SSI estimate (earned income only, individual, no other income):
```
countable = max(0, (gross_wages - 20 - 65) / 2)
ssi_check = max(0, 994 - countable)
```

**Any tool must say "estimate only, talk to a benefits specialist"** and route to Wisconsin WIPA: 1-877-826-1752. Real cases involve IRWEs, PASS plans, student exclusions, Medicaid buy-in, and more. An ERI benefits specialist should check any math.

**Penrod, 219 N. Milwaukee St., 2nd floor, Milwaukee**, hosted by [Mitobyte](https://www.meetup.com/mitobyte/events/316630269/) with Employment Resources, Inc. (ERI), closing event of Wisconsin Tech Month. Service animals are welcome.

## Paths: how you get a workspace

Teams have about six people (about 31 people expected, five teams). **There are at most five teams, and a team has at most eight people.** Extra people join a team with an open seat in an extra role (tester, writer, ERI expert), or work from their own Codespace or laptop and push a branch to the team fork. Past 40 people, Joey raises a team's cap on the day; there is no sixth team. ERI job coaches who bring the people they support count toward the 40 seats, and the fake-data and ask-before-you-photograph rules cover everyone. There are two primary doors and one backup.

| Path | Needs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Codespace** (primary) | A free, verified GitHub account | Your own cloud workspace from `.devcontainer/`, opened **from the team fork**. A cold start takes about 10 minutes (in three test runs on Oct 29 it took 6 to 8 minutes, and one of the three stalled for 30+), so make an account and open one test Codespace on Friday night, and create Saturday's during kickoff. If it is not Available after 10 minutes, delete it (it holds nothing yet) and use the backup editor. Run `node -v` once it opens; it should say v20 or newer |
| **Own laptop** (primary) | Git and Node 20 or newer; Python 3 to preview with `npm start` (it runs `python3 -m http.server`) | The four projects have no dependencies: `npm start` and `npm test` in the project folder. Docker is needed only for the retired folders 01 to 03 and the WordPress and php-mysql starters, and is optional. Your own tools and settings already work there. No door has been tested with a screen reader yet, so tell Joey what you find |
| **Team editor** (backup only) | A browser and your team's password. No account | For people with no GitHub account, a laptop that cannot run Node, or a Codespace not ready in 10 minutes. Team N opens `https://hack-teamN.taild76c1b.ts.net` (team 3 opens `hack-team3`). The password is on your team card. **One shared session, one driver**: only the driver edits files; anyone may open an extra terminal tab only to run `npm test` or read output. The editor image has Node 22, Python 3, PHP 8 (cli and sqlite) and git, but no `gh` and no push credentials, so it cannot reach GitHub. Its work gets out through a teammate's Codespace or laptop, or Joey saves the folder ([START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md#path-3-backup-the-team-editor)) |

**The team model.** At kickoff the team picks a **captain** with a GitHub account. The captain forks the repo, adds teammates as collaborators on the fork, and everyone opens a Codespace or clones **from the team fork**. Everyone works on branches in the fork (names: [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md#branch-names)); the captain merges them into the team branch and opens **one** pull request to `josephrobertlopez/hackreation-eri`, titled `Team N: <project>`, by 3:00. Steps: [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md).

No device? No problem. Roles that need only paper, a phone or an iPad are in [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md). Passwords are never in this repo: they are written on the team cards and handed out at team formation. Each team runs only its own editor, so teams never share a port.

## Forming a team (9:00 to 9:30)
- At 9:00 Joey reads out teams 1 to 5 and their tables (there is no team list page; the number and table are printed on each team card), and people place themselves: sit at any table (6 to 8 people per table) and take that team's card. Joey moves people if a table is full or has no one who can run the hello world. If fewer people come, Joey drops the highest-numbered teams (never one that a screen reader replier was given). If more than 40 come, he raises a team's cap on the day; there is no sixth team.
- Mix roles. Each team needs one person who can run the hello world and one who owns plain language and accessibility testing (no code needed).
- Pick your project by agreement in your team. There is no limit per project, and you may switch whenever you like: your project is the one folder your pull request changes (two folders and CI fails it). A backup-editor team says its project at the 2:00 call.
- Roles: captain, navigator, designer, writer, tester, ERI expert, presenter, WordPress lead (see [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md)). The captain forks the repo, adds teammates and opens the team's pull request. The driver is whoever types on the backup editor; it can change during the day. Every team card has a role line to fill in.
- First hackathon? Join a team with a working developer. Ask anything.
- Don't hand accessibility to a teammate with a disability by default. Ask everyone what they want to work on.
- Teams pick one challenge at the kickoff. The old folders `challenges/01-...` to `03-...` are retired; ignore them. Come after team formation? Look for the sign by the door that lists teams with an open seat.

## Challenges

These are ERI's own four projects, in ERI's words: [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md). ERI's sentence "Anyone may attempt one or more" is about the whole event: **each team picks one project today** and sends one pull request. Several teams may pick the same one. Attempts are compared, not merged ([CONTRIBUTING](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)). A team's pull request changes one project folder; a handoff between projects (for example a P1 portfolio file feeding P4) may be shown as a JSON file inside your own project's folder.

**Known gaps in the hello worlds** (the two main ones, so nobody rediscovers them; each project README lists the rest. Not all four have been opened in a real browser yet, so open yours first and tell Joey if it does not load): P2 has no screen to create a task and no reminders yet. The P4 default loads a candidate profile instead of having the employer type the skills; its folder README explains why, and the ERI liaison knows. A team may keep it or switch to ERI's literal step; both are fine. Gaps that a project's README lists as not built are not penalised in any project. If a line in P1 to P3 looks different from ERI's PDF, ERI's words win; Joey holds the PDF and the ERI liaison settles any doubt.

## Getting help
- **In the room:** ask a teammate or a neighbour first. Stuck for 15 minutes? Raise a hand, hold up your team card, or call out your name and "help". Joey is the floating mentor ([who is who](#who-is-who)). From 9:30 to 9:50 he is with the screen reader group, so an organizer takes your hand and the fix sheet in [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md#fix-sheet-the-errors-we-expect) covers the usual errors.
- **Announcements:** the comments on the [Meetup event page](https://www.meetup.com/mitobyte/events/316630269/) carry links and announcements. Posting there needs a Meetup account, so do not rely on it to ask for help; on the day, tell any organizer at the door. Urgent notices (for example Wi-Fi down) are also said aloud and written on the sheet at the front table.
- Ask the ERI liaison about benefits, billing or ERI itself. The liaison is also a judge, so questions and answers go on the front-table sheet where the whole room can read them.
- Headphones are welcome. Need quiet, captions or a text copy of anything? Ask Joey or reply on the Meetup post. Joey replies there with a plain text file (schedule, help, Wi-Fi) by 7:30 on Saturday.
- Screen reader users: tell Joey or reply "Screen reader". Everyone who asks sits together with Joey in one session, 9:30 to 9:50, at a table he names aloud at kickoff and writes on the front-table sheet; joining is optional, and your teammates do the captain steps while you are there. Joey replies to your "Screen reader" message with a table and a suggested team number before Saturday; the table is on the sign by the door, and you may join any team. Start on your own laptop, where your own tools and settings already work.

## Awards
| Award | Decided by |
| --- | --- |
| **The Golden Byte** | The highest weighted judge total. Eligible: a demo, whichever of P1 to P4 the team picked, and a pull request that Joey has the address of before 3:30. Open it by 3:00; if yours is late (a dead laptop, a slow Codespace) it still counts when Joey has the address before 3:30, and Joey writes the commit when he sees it. A backup-editor team tells Joey before 3:30. Being late never costs a team its demo, People's Choice or the Best-in awards, and a delay on Joey's side never costs any team. A recording counts as the demo; no demo means no Golden Byte. A red check does not matter. Ties: see Judging |
| People's Choice | The room, by a show of hands after the last demo, before the totals are read out. Each person raises a hand once and Joey counts. Nobody votes for their own team. A tie is settled by a second show of hands between the tied teams |
| Best in Design, Best in Innovation, Best in Teamwork | The judges agree together while the last totals are added: the team with the most judge nominations wins, and the ERI liaison settles a tie |

Judges hand Joey each team's score page right after that team's slot, so he adds as they arrive (on a calculator, from the judge sheet) and only the last page is left at the end. The People's Choice show of hands and the totals both fall in the 4:20 to 4:30 window, with Joey as host. With five teams the last slot ends at 4:20 and awards are named 4:20 to 4:30; with fewer teams the later slots move earlier.

## Judging

Judges: the ERI liaison and one or two developer judges. Joey hosts and does not score. **Rubric version: draft as of Thu Oct 29; Joey changes "draft" to "final" after the Fri Oct 30, 6 pm confirmation with the ERI liaison.** Any change after that is posted in the Meetup comments and here. Each judge scores only the rows they own, 0 to 5 per row (0 = nothing, 3 = works with gaps, 5 = we would use it). When two judges own a row, the row score is their average, to one decimal. Presentation is the mean of all judges' scores, to one decimal. A team's weighted total is the sum over the rows of (row score / 5) x weight, so the most it can be is 100. Tie order: higher "Solves ERI's problem", then higher "Works end to end", then Joey flips a coin. Joey prints a judge sheet with this table and score boxes. Judges never get a team password. If no developer judge comes, the ERI liaison scores their two rows too and also applies the README cap. If the liaison is absent, Joey names a stand-in before 2:30: another ERI staff member or a developer judge, never Joey. If GitHub is not reachable at the venue, the judge sees the README line in the team's demo on the venue laptop; Joey has it open.

| Criterion | Weight | Looks like | Scored by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Solves ERI's problem | 30% | An ERI staffer says "we'd use that" | ERI liaison |
| Accessible | 25% | Keyboard and screen reader pass ([checklist](../domain/accessibility.md)). The judge's evidence: the demo shows keyboard-only use, the team says which screen reader it used and what its tester found, and the judge may ask for one keyboard action live. With a recording, the clip and the team's tester report are the evidence. A team with no screen reader that did a keyboard pass and says so honestly still scores on the rest of the row | Developer judge |
| Works end to end | 20% | A live demo on synthetic data, not slides | Developer judge |
| ERI could adopt it | 15% | Built on the [recommended stack](../company/tech-stack.md) (plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that could be pasted into WordPress), no paid services, a README that names the run commands (`npm start` and `npm test`), and a clear "What ERI would need" line (see below) | ERI liaison gives the 0 to 5 from the line; a developer judge reads the README on the pull request page, and a "no" (the README is missing, wrong, or needs paid services) caps this row at 2. Either developer judge may apply the cap; a capped row scores the lower of the liaison's score and 2 |
| Presentation | 10% | Clear in 3 minutes | All judges |

## Rules
1. Synthetic data only ([privacy](../domain/privacy-and-data.md)). Say "All data in this demo is fake" at the start of your demo.
2. Work in your project folder, so CI runs. Branch in the team fork. One pull request per team, titled `Team N: <project>`, opened by the captain by 3:00 (Joey opens a backup-editor team's with its driver from 2:30) ([CONTRIBUTING](../../CONTRIBUTING.md), section 5).
3. Code is MIT licensed ([LICENSE](../../LICENSE)), so ERI and anyone can reuse it.
4. Be kind. Everyone starts somewhere.

## Presentations (3:30 to 4:30)
Each team gets a 10-minute slot: 3 for the demo, about 2 for questions, the rest to switch. Joey checks "All data in this demo is fake" at the 3:00 demo check, and a judge stops any demo that shows real data. Awards close the hour. Demos run from the **venue laptop** on the projector, so judges never need a login (how: [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md#show-a-demo-from-the-venue-laptop); a Codespace port set to Public also works). Judges see the live demo; the pull request is the record. Any teammate may present or read a script. A live demo is preferred; a recording of the working demo (up to 3 minutes) is the fallback, and judges score what it shows. Showing from your own laptop is allowed (Joey has USB-C and HDMI adapters). No path costs points, except that judges can score "Works end to end" only on what they see work. Captions on.

Demo template (3 minutes):
1. **Who** it's for and their problem (20 sec)
2. **Live demo** on synthetic data (2 min)
3. **What ERI would need** to adopt it (20 sec). Say it aloud and add it to your project README (where: [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md#one-team-pull-request), answer 5). The developer judge reads the README on the pull request page during questions
4. **Accessibility** you tested (20 sec)

## After the event

Your code stays in your team's pull request. On Sunday Nov 1 Joey sends the ERI liaison one pull request link per team. ERI reviews every project and decides; it does not promise to adopt, host or support any of them. Winners go on the Meetup page.

# Knowledge base

A sourced, dated reference for ERI's work and the hackathon. **It explains rules; it is not legal or benefits advice for any individual.** Route people to WIPA (1-877-826-1752), Disability Rights Wisconsin / CAP (800-928-8778) or an attorney.

Every page follows [_PAGE_SPEC.md](_PAGE_SPEC.md): frontmatter with `last_verified`, `next_review`, `confidence` and sources; **(verify)** marks anything not confirmed from an opened source.

## Areas

| Area | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [benefits](benefits/README.md) | SSI, SSDI, Medicaid, MAPP, Ticket, ABLE, FoodShare, housing |
| [employment-law](employment-law/README.md) | ADA, WFEA, Rehab Act, WIOA, 14(c), WOTC/Schedule A, AI in hiring, FMLA |
| [compliance](compliance/README.md) | HIPAA, Part 2, FERPA, VR confidentiality, SSA data, breach, billing integrity, accessibility, AI policy |
| [wisconsin-landscape](wisconsin-landscape/README.md) | DVR, long-term care, advocacy, workforce, transit, education, counties, peers |
| [datasets](datasets/README.md) | Public data catalog with access, licenses, uses |
| [org](org/README.md) | ERI finances, programs, digital, funders, trends, consulting brief |

## Headline findings (as of 2026-10-23)

- **DVR waitlist:** an Order of Selection waitlist began December 2025 (peak 7,610 on 2026-06-02). DVR began serving from it on 2026-06-02 and aims to clear it by 2027-06-30. A separate provider waitlist (2026-08-31) had 160 of 199 people statewide in WDA 10, ERI's home area: a capacity opportunity.
- **DVR provider agreement:** any AI tool used with a consumer's information requires that consumer's prior written or verbal consent.
- **2027 SSA numbers are out** (3.6% COLA): SGA $1,770, TWP $1,270, SSI FBR $1,029. The Wisconsin SSI supplement rose 10% to $92.16 on 2026-05-01.
- **Section 503's 7% goal and self-ID form were rescinded** (final rule 2026-08-21, effective 2026-09-21). **WOTC lapsed** for hires after 2025-12-31 unless Congress reauthorizes it.
- **14(c) subminimum wage continues:** DOL withdrew its phase-out rule on 2025-07-07.
- **ADA Title II web deadlines moved** to 2027-04-26 (large) and 2028-04-26 (small); the standard is WCAG 2.1 AA.
- **Medicaid work requirement (2027)** applies to BadgerCare childless adults; SSI-Medicaid, MAPP, Family Care/IRIS and SSA-disabled people are generally not subject or are exempt.
- **42 CFR Part 2** compliance date was 2026-02-16.
- **ERI finances:** revenue has been flat at about $3.0-3.3M since FY2018, with net assets covering about 2.8 months of expenses. FY2025 program revenue fell 10.7%.

<!-- FILE: wiki/knowledge/_PAGE_SPEC.md -->

---
title: Knowledge page spec
summary: How every page in wiki/knowledge/ is written, so people and LLMs can trust and maintain it.
last_verified: 2026-10-23
---

# Knowledge page spec (LLM-wiki format)

One topic per page. Target 60-220 lines. Markdown only.

## Required frontmatter
```yaml
---
title: Plain title
summary: One sentence an LLM can use to decide whether to open this page.
tags: [benefits, ssi, wisconsin]
jurisdiction: federal | wisconsin | milwaukee | dane | multi
last_verified: 2026-10-23        # date the sources were last opened
next_review: 2027-01-15          # e.g. after the January SSA COLA, or a law's effective date
review_owner: ERI benefits specialist manager   # a ROLE, never a private person's contact
confidence: high | medium | low  # how sure we are the page is current and correct
sources:
  - title: Source page title
    url: https://...
    accessed: 2026-10-23
---
```

## Required body sections (in this order)
1. `# Title`
2. **TL;DR**: 2-4 bullets with the answer and its key numbers
3. **Key facts**: a table of numbers, dates, thresholds and citations (statute, CFR, POMS section)
4. **How it works**: rules in plain language, using short sentences
5. **Caveats and gotchas**: what people get wrong, what changed recently, what's uncertain. Mark anything you could not confirm from an opened source with **(verify)**
6. **How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this**: concrete design or service implications, and what a tool must NOT do
7. **Related pages**: relative links
8. **Sources**: the same list as frontmatter, as markdown links

## Rules
- Facts come only from sources you actually opened. A search snippet is not a source. Cite primary sources (ssa.gov, ecfr.gov, docs.legis.wisconsin.gov, dhs.wisconsin.gov, dwd.wisconsin.gov, eeoc.gov, dol.gov, hhs.gov) over blogs.
- No legal or benefits advice for an individual. Pages explain rules and route people to qualified help (WIPA 1-877-826-1752, Disability Rights Wisconsin, the Client Assistance Program, an attorney).
- No private information: no personal emails or phones, nothing from internal emails. Public office lines and public program numbers are fine.
- Dates are absolute ("effective 2026-01-01"), never "recently".

# Benefits knowledge pages

These pages explain public benefit rules that affect people with disabilities who work in Wisconsin. They are **not** individual benefits advice. For personal guidance, contact WIPA at **1-877-826-1752**, Disability Rights Wisconsin, or the Client Assistance Program.

| Page | One line |
|---|---|
| [benefits-quick-reference-2026.md](benefits-quick-reference-2026.md) | Every 2026 number (and announced 2027 values) in one cited table |
| [ssi-work-rules.md](ssi-work-rules.md) | SSI income counting, $20/$65/one-half, FBR, resources, SEIE, PASS, IRWE/BWE, deeming, wage reporting, overpayments |
| [ssdi-work-rules.md](ssdi-work-rules.md) | SSDI TWP, SGA, 36-month EPE, grace period, Expedited Reinstatement, subsidies/IRWE, 93-month Medicare |
| [section-1619-and-medicaid-while-working.md](section-1619-and-medicaid-while-working.md) | 1619(a) cash and 1619(b) Medicaid; Wisconsin 2026 threshold $51,711 |
| [wisconsin-medicaid-purchase-plan-mapp.md](wisconsin-medicaid-purchase-plan-mapp.md) | MAPP buy-in: 250% FPL, $15,000 assets, work rule, HEC, premiums, Independence Accounts |
| [wisconsin-medicaid-long-term-care.md](wisconsin-medicaid-long-term-care.md) | BadgerCare Plus vs EBD Medicaid; Family Care, IRIS, CLTS, Katie Beckett; employment services |
| [ticket-to-work.md](ticket-to-work.md) | Ticket eligibility, ENs, 2026 milestone/outcome payments, Timely Progress Reviews, Section 301, CDR protection |
| [able-accounts.md](able-accounts.md) | ABLE age-46 rule (2026-01-01), $20,000 limit, SSI treatment, Wisconsin plan status |
| [foodshare-and-work-requirements.md](foodshare-and-work-requirements.md) | FoodShare ABAWD rules after H.R. 1: ages 18-64, exemptions, FSET, Wisconsin dates |
| [medicaid-work-requirements-2027.md](medicaid-work-requirements-2027.md) | H.R. 1 Medicaid community engagement: BadgerCare adults, exemptions, Wisconsin 2027 timeline |
| [housing-and-other-supports.md](housing-and-other-supports.md) | HUD EID end and HOTMA, Wisconsin SSI supplement and SSI-E, UI for SSDI recipients |

## Maintenance
- Review every January after the SSA COLA, in February for Wisconsin FPL tables, and when POMS SI 02302.200 updates.
- Items marked **(verify)** on any page need a primary-source check before a tool relies on them.
- Page format: see [../_PAGE_SPEC.md](../_PAGE_SPEC.md).

## Sources

sources:
  - title: POMS SI 01130.740, ABLE Accounts (02/26/2026)
    url: https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501130740
    accessed: 2026-10-23

# ABLE accounts

## TL;DR
- Since **2026-01-01**, a person qualifies for ABLE if blindness or disability **began before age 46** (it was 26 before).
- The 2026 annual contribution limit from all sources is **$20,000** (2025: $19,000). Working owners who do not contribute to certain employer retirement plans can add more ("ABLE to Work"), up to the one-person poverty level or their earnings, whichever is less.
- For SSI, the **first $100,000** in an ABLE account is not a countable resource. Over that, SSI is suspended (not ended), and Medicaid continues.
- **Wisconsin has no state ABLE plan yet.** 2023 Wisconsin Act 267 authorizes one, and DFI is working on it. Residents can open an account with any state's plan that accepts nonresidents.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Age of onset | before 46th birthday, effective 2026-01-01 (before 26 earlier) | POMS SI 01130.740; SSI ABLE spotlight |
| Annual contribution limit | $20,000 (2026); $19,000 (2025) | POMS SI 01130.740; ABLE NRC 2026 |
| ABLE to Work extra, 2026 | $15,650 continental US / $19,550 AK / $17,990 HI (ABLE NRC); SSA spotlight lists $15,960 / $19,950 / $18,360 (conflict, see caveats) | ABLE NRC 2026; SSI ABLE spotlight |
| SSI resource exclusion | first $100,000 | POMS SI 01130.740; SSI Spotlight on Resources |
| Over $100,000 | SSI suspended, no time limit; Medicaid continues | SSI ABLE spotlight |
| Housing distributions | not income; a resource if kept into the next month | POMS SI 01130.740 |
| MAPP asset test | ABLE accounts excluded | DHS MAPP page |
| Accounts per person | one | Wisconsin DFI |
| Wisconsin plan | none yet (DFI developing one under 2023 Wis. Act 267) | DFI ABLE page; DFI release 2026-04-14 |
| Wisconsin tax | subtraction from income for deposits to any state's ABLE account (per ABLE NRC) | ABLE NRC Wisconsin review |

## How it works
**Who can open one.** A person who is blind or disabled with onset before age 46. They either get SSI or SSDI on that basis, or self-certify with a doctor's diagnosis (per the ABLE Act's general rules) **(verify)** the certification rules with the chosen plan. One account per person.

**Money in.** Anyone can contribute: the owner, family, friends, or a trust. The total from all sources is $20,000 in 2026. A working owner can add more from their own earnings under ABLE to Work. Contributions are not SSI income to the owner, but the owner's wages are still counted as earned income when received.

**Money out.** Distributions for **qualified disability expenses** (QDEs) are not income for SSI and are not federally taxed. QDEs include education, housing, transport, employment training and support, assistive technology, health, and basic living expenses. For SSI:
- Housing distributions kept past the month they are received count as a resource.
- Funds held for a non-housing QDE stay excluded while waiting to be spent.

**SSI and Medicaid.** The first $100,000 is excluded. If the excess over $100,000 (alone) puts the person over $2,000, SSI is suspended but Medicaid continues, with no time limit. If **other** resources cause the excess, normal rules apply. After 12 months of suspension, SSI ends.

**Why it matters for work.** ABLE lets a worker on SSI or in 1619(b) save past the $2,000 limit. It also lets MAPP members save outside the $15,000 limit. It works well with ERI's employment goals: car repairs, training and work clothes are QDEs.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Conflicting ABLE to Work figures.** ABLE NRC (2026 update) uses the prior-year poverty guideline ($15,650 continental). The SSA SSI spotlight lists $15,960. Another FAQ on the same SSA page says $19,000. ABLE NRC's ABLE to Work page shows an outdated "$19,000" annual limit and a total of $35,650. **(verify)** with the chosen plan or IRS guidance before quoting a number.
- Whether H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21, 2025-07-04) changed ABLE rules, for example by making ABLE to Work, 529 rollovers or the Saver's Credit permanent, was not confirmed in sources we opened. **(verify)**
- Medicaid payback: on death, the state may claim remaining funds for Medicaid costs. That is the general ABLE rule, but we did not confirm Wisconsin specifics. **(verify)**
- Wisconsin's own plan may launch later. Recheck the DFI page at each review.
- Wisconsin tax treatment comes from ABLE NRC (2016 Wisconsin Act repealing the state plan and adding a subtraction). **(verify)** on the Wisconsin Department of Revenue ABLE page before advising.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A savings helper can show: "Up to $100,000 in ABLE does not count for SSI. Spend housing withdrawals in the same month." It must route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752** before large deposits or withdrawals.
- An eligibility check should ask "Did your disability begin before age 46?", not 26. Older content online still says 26.
- Do NOT recommend a specific state plan or investment. Link to ablenrc.org plan comparisons and to Wisconsin DFI.
- Do NOT treat ABLE to Work amounts as certain until the conflict above is resolved.

# Benefits quick reference 2026

## TL;DR
- Every number below was read from a primary source on 2026-10-23. Use the 2026 column for months through December 2026.
- SSA announced 2027 values on **2026-10-14** (3.6% COLA). They take effect for January 2027 benefits. SSI for January 2027 is paid 2026-12-31.
- Rows marked "our arithmetic" are derived and should be labeled that way in tools.

## Key facts
| # | Item | 2026 | 2027 (announced) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | COLA | 2.8% | 3.6% | [2026 fact sheet](https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2026.html); [2027 fact sheet](https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html) |
| 2 | SSI FBR, individual | $994/mo | $1,029/mo | 2026 and 2027 fact sheets |

| 34 | Medicaid work requirement income test | $580/mo (80 x $7.25) | starts 2027-01-01 | [CMS fact sheet](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/medicaid-community-engagement-requirement-certain-individuals-interim-final-rule-comment-period-cms) |
| 35 | FoodShare ABAWD ages / hours | 18-64 / 80 hrs per month | | [DHS Ops Memo 26-04](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/dms/memos/ops/dms-ops-2026-04.pdf) |
| 36 | Overpayment default withholding | SSDI 50%; SSI 10% | | [SSA Resolve an overpayment](https://www.ssa.gov/manage-benefits/resolve-overpayment) |
| 37 | HUD elderly/disabled deduction | $525 | | [HUD PIH 2024-38](https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/OCHCO/documents/2024-38pihn.pdf) |

## How it works
- SSA indexes the FBR, SGA, TWP, SEIE and quarter of coverage every January. The $20 and $65 exclusions, the $2,000/$3,000 resource limits and the ABLE $100,000 exclusion are fixed in law and are not indexed.
- Wisconsin amounts (supplement, FPL tables, MAPP, Family Care limits) change on Wisconsin's own schedule: May 2026 for the supplement, February for the FPL tables, January for waiver limits.
- Ticket payments use the rate in effect in the month the milestone is reached.

## Caveats and gotchas
- Row 6 is our arithmetic and ignores the Wisconsin supplement, unearned income and IRWE.
- Row 17 (1619(b)) uses the pre-May-2026 Wisconsin supplement **(verify)** at the 2027 POMS update.
- Row 27 has conflicting sources **(verify)**.
- Rows 14, 15, 17 and 20-24 for 2027 were not published as of 2026-10-23.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Load these values as **dated configuration** (value, effective_from, effective_to, source_url), not hard-coded constants. Select the value by the month being estimated.
- Every estimator screen must say "Estimate only, not a benefits determination" and give WIPA **1-877-826-1752**.
- Do NOT display a number without its year and source link.

# FoodShare (SNAP) work requirements in Wisconsin after H.R. 1

## TL;DR
- H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21, signed **2025-07-04**, section 10102) raised the able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) time-limit age from 18-54 to **18-64**. It lowered the child exemption to a child **under 14** and removed the exemptions for homeless people, veterans, and former foster youth.
- Wisconsin applied the age and child changes from **2025-11-01**. The tribal exemption started **2025-10-01**. Discretionary exemptions for ages 55-59 ended **2025-12-01**, and remaining changes, including ages 60-64, took effect **2026-03-01** (DHS Ops Memo 26-04).
- Rule: ABAWDs must work, volunteer or join a work program **80 hours/month**. Otherwise they get only **3 months of FoodShare in 3 years** (current period: 2025-01-01 to 2027-12-31).
- **Disability exempts people.** Getting any disability benefit (SSI, SSDI, VA disability, workers' comp), or being physically or mentally unable to work, makes a person "unfit for work".

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Federal law | H.R. 1, Pub. L. 119-21, sec. 10102(a), effective 2025-07-04 | FNS memo 2025-10-03 |
| ABAWD age range | 18-64 (was 18-54) | FNS memo; DHS P-03606 |
| Child exemption | dependent child 13 or younger in the household (was under 18) | FNS memo; DHS Ops Memo 26-04 |
| Removed exemptions | homeless, veterans, former foster youth 18-24 (WI: 2025-11-01) | FNS memo; DHS Ops Memo 26-04 |
| Added exemption | American Indian / Urban Indian / California Indian (WI: 2025-10-01) | FNS memo; DHS Ops Memo 26-04 |
| Hours | 80/month of work, volunteering, a work program, or a mix | DHS FoodShare Work Requirement |
| Time limit | 3 countable months in 36; current period 2025-01 to 2027-12 | DHS FoodShare Work Requirement; P-03606 |
| Disability exemption | "unfit for work", incl. any disability benefit regardless of amount | DHS Ops Memo 26-04 |
| Basic (general) work rules | ages 16-59 | DHS FoodShare Work Requirement |
| SNAP admin cost share | WI share rises from 50% to 75% on 2026-10-01 | DHS Federal Changes page |
| SNAP benefit cost share | state pays 5-15% if error rate above 6%, from 2027-10-01 | DHS Federal Changes page |

## How it works
**Two separate rule sets.**
1. *Basic work rules* (ages 16-59): accept a suitable job, do not quit without good cause, and so on. People working 30+ hours a week, or earning the same at federal minimum wage, are exempt.
2. *ABAWD work requirement / time limit* (ages 18-64): meet 80 hours a month or have an exemption. Otherwise, after 3 countable months, FoodShare stops for that person until they meet the requirement for 30 days or become exempt.

**Exemptions in Wisconsin (DHS list, 2026).** Pregnant; unable to work because of physical or mental health (including chronic homelessness and getting disability payments); living with a child 13 or younger; tribal member; caring for a child 5 or younger in another home, or for someone who cannot care for themselves; getting or applying for unemployment compensation; enrolled at least half-time in school or training; in W-2; in AODA treatment.

**How disability is shown.** DHS memo 26-04 says getting any temporary or permanent disability payment from a government or private source qualifies as "unfit for work". It also lists examples of conditions such as long-term illness, depression, trouble concentrating, and trouble walking or climbing stairs. Self-attestation is generally accepted unless it is questionable.

**FSET (FoodShare Employment and Training).** Free and voluntary. It offers job search help, training (CNA, forklift, CNC and similar), GED/HSED, and support costs such as bus fare, tools and clothes, for up to 90 days after getting a job. Taking part counts toward the 80 hours. Household members 16+ can join even if they are exempt.

## Caveats and gotchas
- People 60-64 are **not** subject to basic work rules but **are** subject to the ABAWD time limit. FNS also bars mandatory E&T for ages 60-64.
- Homelessness alone is no longer an exemption. *Chronic* homelessness (no fixed nighttime residence, and none expected within 30 days) can still make someone "unfit for work".
- Parents whose only children are 14-17 are now subject to the time limit.
- A lost exemption mid-certification is not applied until the next interview screening (from 2025-11-01).
- The Wisconsin SSI supplement increase (2026-05-01) counts as income for FoodShare and may slightly reduce FoodShare (DHS Ops Memo 26-12).
- A separate DHS memo (Ops 26-31) covers time-limit suspensions for high-unemployment areas in federal fiscal year 2027. We did not open it. **(verify)** which Wisconsin areas, if any, are suspended.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A screener should ask about disability benefits first. Anyone on SSI or SSDI should see "People who get SSI or SSDI are often exempt from the FoodShare work requirement. Your income maintenance agency decides. Ask them, or call WIPA at 1-877-826-1752."
- For job seekers not on disability benefits, show the 80-hour options. Note that ERI or DVR employment services may count as a work program only if they are approved as one **(verify)** with the local FSET agency.
- When estimating income changes, remind users that higher wages can lower FoodShare. Route them to WIPA **1-877-826-1752** for combined benefits planning.
- Do NOT tell anyone they are exempt as a final decision. The income maintenance agency decides.

# Housing and other supports

## TL;DR
- **HUD Earned Income Disregard (EID) is closed to new families.** Under HOTMA, public housing agencies (PHAs) had to stop enrolling families after **2023-12-31**. HOTMA instead raised the elderly/disabled family deduction to **$525** and moved the medical expense threshold from 3% to **10%** of income, with phased hardship relief. HUD will enforce HOTMA sections 102/104 for all PHAs from **2027-01-01**.
- **The Wisconsin SSI state supplement rose 10% on 2026-05-01**, to **$92.16/month** (individual) and $145.26 (couple). It was the first increase since 1994. **SSI-E** (Exceptional Expense) adds a higher state amount: a $197.75 total state payment for an individual, so $1,191.75 combined with the 2026 FBR.
- **SSDI recipients can now get Wisconsin unemployment insurance (UI).** A federal court enjoined Wis. Stat. 108.04(12)(f) from **2025-07-20**. DWD is processing past claims for people denied between 2015-09-08 and 2025-07-29.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| HUD EID enrollment cutoff | PHAs must have stopped enrolling by 2023-12-31 | HUD PIH 2024-38 |
| HOTMA elderly/disabled deduction | $525 (statutory from 2024-01-01; systems compliance delayed) | HUD PIH 2024-38 |
| HOTMA medical/disability expense threshold | 10% of annual income (was 3%), phased in, with hardship relief | HUD HOTMA highlights; HUD FAQs 2026-09-29 |
| HOTMA asset limit | $100,000 net family assets (inflation-adjusted); retirement accounts excluded | HUD HOTMA highlights |
| HOTMA enforcement for all PHAs | from 2027-01-01 (MTW and some PHAs later) | HUD FAQs 2026-09-29 |
| WI SSI state supplement (independent living) | individual $92.16; couple $145.26 (from 2026-05-01; was $83.78 / $132.05) | DHS Ops Memo 26-12 |
| WI SSI-E state add-on | individual $105.59; couple $379.90 (was $95.99 / $345.36) | DHS Ops Memo 26-12 |
| WI SSI-E total state payment | individual $197.75; couple $525.16 | DHS P-20679; P-23129 |
| Federal + SSI-E combined (2026) | individual $1,191.75; couple $2,016.16 | DHS P-20679 |
| Caretaker Supplement | $275 first child, $165 each additional (since 2023-07-01) | DHS P-23129 |
| UI and SSDI | 108.04(12)(f) enjoined from 2025-07-20 | DWD release 2025-10-14; Clearinghouse |
| UI back pay class | initial claims 2015-09-08 to 2025-07-29 | DWD release 2025-10-14 |

## How it works
**HUD EID (historical) and HOTMA.** EID used to exclude new earnings from rent calculations for some public housing and Housing Choice Voucher families with disabilities. Under the HOTMA income rule, no family can start EID after 2023-12-31. Families already in EID finish it under HUD guidance (PIH 2023-27, Attachment G). Since enrollment ended in 2023 and EID ran on a 24-month clock, few or none should still have it in late 2026 **(verify)** the end date with the PHA. Today the work-related help in HUD rent comes mainly from the $525 deduction, the medical/disability assistance expense deduction (over 10% of income), and **Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS)** escrow accounts. Rent is generally 30% of adjusted income, so higher wages raise rent.

**Wisconsin SSI supplement.** Wisconsin runs its own state supplementary payment (SSP). Anyone with a federal SSI payment of any amount gets the full state payment. Living-arrangement categories: independent living, or living in another's household. The state supplement is not COLA-adjusted. The 2026-05-01 increase came after 32 years with no change.

**SSI-E (Exceptional Expense).** For SSI recipients who either live in a qualifying substitute care setting with high costs, or live in a natural residential setting and need **40+ hours/month** of long-term support services. A county or long-term care agency certifies it.

**UI for SSDI recipients.** In *Bemke v. Pechacek* (W.D. Wis. No. 3:21-cv-00560), the court held on 2025-07-14 that Wisconsin's SSDI bar violated the ADA and the Rehabilitation Act by disparate impact. It enjoined enforcement from 2025-07-20. It then ordered remedies on 2025-08-20 for people denied UI or made to repay. The Legislature did not repeal the statute. DWD says it will process UI claims for SSDI recipients who meet all other UI rules. DWD is mailing notices to class members.

**How UI interacts with other benefits.** For SSI, UI is **unearned** income, so it reduces SSI almost dollar for dollar after $20. UI also counts as income for FoodShare and Medicaid. For SSDI, UI does not reduce the check, but statements made on a UI claim about being able to work could be looked at during a CDR **(verify)** with WIPA or Disability Rights Wisconsin.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The DWD SSDI program page could not be opened on 2026-10-23. We do not know if there was an appeal to the Seventh Circuit or whether the injunction was made permanent. The Clearinghouse listed the case as ongoing (summary updated 2026-02-19). **(verify)** the current status with DWD or the court docket.
- The SSI-E "$197.75" figure is the regular supplement plus the SSI-E add-on ($92.16 + $105.59). Do not add $197.75 on top of $92.16.
- The 1619(b) threshold chart for 2026 still uses the old $83.78 supplement (see the 1619 page).
- Wisconsin Homestead Credit and other state tax credits were not reviewed for this page. **(verify)** if a tool needs them.
- HOTMA rules apply to public housing and vouchers. Multifamily (project-based Section 8) timelines differ **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A benefits calculator for Wisconsin SSI must use the **current** state supplement ($92.16 from 2026-05-01) as a separate line. For SSI-E cases, use the total state payment.
- A rent estimator must not apply EID to new cases. It can show a "rent goes up about 30 cents per extra dollar of adjusted income" note, and route users to their PHA.
- Job-loss guidance for SSDI recipients can say "You may be able to apply for Wisconsin unemployment." It must add "Check with WIPA 1-877-826-1752 first, because UI affects SSI and FoodShare."
- Do NOT tell anyone they will get UI back pay. DWD decides.

# Medicaid work (community engagement) requirements starting 2027

## TL;DR
- Section 71119 of Public Law 119-21 (enacted **2025-07-04**) requires certain adults to show "community engagement" to get or keep Medicaid. States must start by **2027-01-01**. The HHS Secretary can grant good-faith exemptions, which must end by 2028-12-31.
- In Wisconsin it applies to **BadgerCare Plus adults 19-64** who are not pregnant and have no dependent child under 19 at home. That is about **200,000** people, and DHS's first estimate is that about **63,000** could lose coverage.
- How to meet it: **80 hours in a month** of work, volunteering, a work program or a mix; or at least half-time school; or **$580+ income in a month** (80 x federal minimum wage).
- **Not subject**: SSI Medicaid, MAPP, Family Care, IRIS, Partnership, people with an SSA disability determination, Medicare enrollees, and other listed exemptions. Wisconsin new applicants start **2027-01-01**. Current members start at renewals due **2027-03-31** and later.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Statute | Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 71119, adds SSA 1902(xx) | Medicaid.gov overview slide |
| Federal start | by 2027-01-01 (earlier at state option) | Medicaid.gov overview; CMS fact sheet |
| Good-faith exemption | ends no later than 2028-12-31 | Medicaid.gov overview |
| Interim final rule | CMS-2454-IFC, issued 2026-06-01 | CMS fact sheet |
| Who (federal) | adults 19-64 in the expansion group or similar 1115 coverage, not on Medicare | CMS fact sheet |
| Who (Wisconsin) | BadgerCare Plus adults 19-64, not pregnant, no dependent child under 19 at home at least 40% of the time | DHS work page; DHS webinar 2026-07-30 |
| Test | 80 hrs/month, or half-time school, or $580/month income | CMS fact sheet; DHS work page |
| Look-back (WI) | applicants: month before applying; members: 1 month since last approval | DHS webinar 2026-07-30 |
| WI new applicants | from 2027-01-01 | DHS work page |
| WI current members | renewals due 2027-03-31 and later | DHS webinar 2026-07-30 |
| WI notices | letters August 2026; texts and emails September 2026 | DHS webinar 2026-07-30 |
| WI numbers | about 200,000 subject; about 63,000 at risk (initial estimate) | DHS webinar 2026-07-30 |

## How it works
**Exemptions (federal list, used by Wisconsin).** Pregnant or postpartum. Medically frail or with special medical needs. Parent or caretaker of a child 13 or under or of a disabled person (Wisconsin also exempts parents of a child under 19 living with them). American Indian / Alaska Native. Veterans with a total disability rating. People meeting TANF/W-2 work rules, or in a FoodShare household and not exempt from FoodShare work rules. In SUD treatment. Incarcerated, or released within 3 months. Former foster youth. States cannot add exemptions.

**Medically frail (CMS IFC, 42 CFR 435.554).** Five categories:
1. Blind or disabled as defined in SSA section 1614.
2. Substance use disorder (unless in stable recovery for 5+ years).
3. Disabling mental disorder.
4. Physical, intellectual or developmental disability that significantly impairs one or more activities of daily living.
5. Serious or complex medical condition.

The condition must significantly impair the ability to comply. States must check data first (ex parte), using claims, encounter and HIE data. Self-attestation is allowed with limits until 2028-01-01. Medical frailty is reverified at least every 12 months.

**Short-term hardship (Wisconsin plans to allow).** Inpatient or similar care; a county under a disaster declaration; a county with high unemployment; extended travel for medical treatment.

**Verification in Wisconsin.** No monthly reporting. DHS checks at application and at annual renewal. It uses data first, and providers will not need to fill out DHS medical exemption forms. Non-exempt people who don't comply are denied or disenrolled after notice. They can reapply any time. People denied for this reason cannot get Marketplace premium tax credits.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Most ERI participants are not subject.** People on SSI, MAPP, EBD Medicaid, Family Care or IRIS, or with an SSA disability determination, are outside BadgerCare Plus or exempt. The risk is disabled workers who are on **BadgerCare Plus** with no disability determination. Depending on their situation, a medical frailty exemption, an SSA disability determination or MAPP may be relevant. WIPA or Disability Rights Wisconsin can help a person sort out which, if any, applies.
- Homelessness and getting unemployment compensation are **not** exemptions in Wisconsin.
- The CMS fact sheet is inconsistent about caretakers: "under 14" in one place, "13 and under" in another (the same thing for whole years).
- Six-month eligibility renewals for expansion adults (another H.R. 1 provision) were not described on the Wisconsin pages we opened. **(verify)** whether and when they apply to Wisconsin's BadgerCare adults.
- An earlier DHS partner page listed the start as "December 31, 2026". The newer DHS member page and webinar say 2027-01-01 for applicants. Use 2027-01-01.
- The IFR comment period and any final rule could change details. **(verify)** at the next review.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A screener should first ask "What Medicaid do you have?" If the answer is SSI, MAPP, Family Care, IRIS or Medicare, show "This rule likely does not apply to you."
- For BadgerCare Plus adults: show the three ways to comply. Show that 80 hours of work, or $580 earned in one month, is enough. Show exemptions in plain language. ERI job placement can help people meet the rule.
- Remind people of DHS's general guidance: keep their address current, use an ACCESS account, and read DHS letters.
- Route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752** or Disability Rights Wisconsin for exemption questions.
- Do NOT say a person "will lose Medicaid". Do NOT decide medical frailty. DHS decides.

# Section 1619(a), 1619(b) and Medicaid while working (Wisconsin)

## TL;DR
- **1619(a)**: an SSI recipient keeps getting a (reduced) SSI check even when earnings are above SGA, as long as countable income still leaves a payment.
- **1619(b)**: when wages bring the SSI check to $0, Medicaid usually continues if gross earnings stay under the state threshold. For **Wisconsin in 2026 the threshold is $51,711/year** (2025: $49,368).
- Wisconsin is a "1634 state". People eligible for SSI, including those in 1619(b) status, get Wisconsin Medicaid without a separate application.
- Above the threshold, SSA can calculate an individualized threshold. If that fails too, the [Medicaid Purchase Plan (MAPP)](wisconsin-medicaid-purchase-plan-mapp.md) is the main Wisconsin option.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| WI 1619(b) threshold 2026 (disabled) | $51,711/yr | POMS SI 02302.200 (chart effective 2026-01-20) |
| Components 2026 | base $26,887 (already includes twice the annual state supplement, $2,011) + Medicaid per capita $24,824 = $51,711 | POMS SI 02302.200 |
| WI 1619(b) threshold 2025 | $49,368/yr | POMS SI 02302.200 |
| Separate WI threshold for blind | none | POMS SI 02302.200 |
| WI Medicaid determination type | 1634 state | POMS SI 01715.020 |
| Federal SSI break-even (wages only) 2026 | about $2,073/mo | our arithmetic from FBR $994 (2 x 994 + 85) |
| Restart SSI/Medicaid without new application | within 12 months (non-work reasons); EXR within 60 months after work-related termination | Red Book, SSI only |

## How it works
**1619(a), cash while over SGA.** SGA does not end SSI after the initial application. SSI keeps paying while countable income is below the FBR plus the state supplement. Requirements: eligible for at least one SSI payment month before working at SGA, still disabled, and meeting other SSI rules. No separate application is needed. The person just reports wages.

**1619(b), Medicaid after the check reaches $0.** SSA lists six conditions:
1. Was eligible for an SSI payment for at least 1 month.
2. Would still be eligible for SSI except for earnings.
3. Still has a disability.
4. Still meets other rules, including the $2,000 resource limit.
5. Needs Medicaid to keep working.
6. Gross earnings are not enough to replace SSI, Medicaid and any publicly funded attendant care. For most people, this means "under the state threshold".

**The Wisconsin threshold.** SSA adds up:
- the yearly earnings that would bring federal and Wisconsin SSI to zero (the base amount), plus
- Wisconsin's average yearly Medicaid cost per person.
For 2026 that is $51,711 per year of **gross** earnings, about $4,309 per month (our arithmetic).

**Individualized threshold.** If earnings are over $51,711, SSA can figure a personal threshold. It counts the person's actual Medicaid use, IRWE, BWE, PASS-excluded income and publicly funded attendant care. People with high Medicaid costs, such as Family Care or IRIS members, may stay eligible far above the chart amount.

**What happens to Medicaid.** In 1619(b) status, Wisconsin Medicaid continues on the SSI basis. That includes any Family Care, IRIS or other waiver enrollment, if other rules are met. If 1619(b) ends:
- Wisconsin must review the person for other Medicaid categories before closing.
- MAPP (income up to 250% FPL, assets up to $15,000, premiums above 100% FPL) is the usual next step for workers with disabilities.
- SSI-related Medicaid (EBD) with a deductible, or BadgerCare Plus, may also apply.

**Restarting.** If SSI stops for non-work reasons, cash and Medicaid can restart within 12 months without a new application. If it stopped because of earnings, Expedited Reinstatement is available for 5 years.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The threshold is compared with **gross** wages for the year, not with countable income.
- Resources still matter. Saving above $2,000 in countable resources ends 1619(b) even if earnings are low. ABLE accounts (first $100,000 excluded) help here.
- The 2026 chart uses 2023 Medicaid cost data because 2024 data was not available (POMS note).
- The 2026 POMS base amount uses the old Wisconsin supplement ($83.78 x 12 x 2 = $2,011). The supplement rose to $92.16 on 2026-05-01 (DHS Ops Memo 26-12). SSA might not update the 2026 chart. The 2027 chart may be higher. **(verify)** with the next POMS release.
- The 2027 Wisconsin threshold was not published as of 2026-10-23. Expect a new chart in early 2027.
- SSA does an annual 1619(b) review. People must keep reporting wages monthly even when they get no check.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- An estimator should compare the person's projected **annual gross earnings** with $51,711 (2026). Below: "Under the 2026 chart amount. Medicaid often continues under 1619(b) if the other conditions are met." Near or above: "You may still qualify through an individualized threshold or MAPP. Talk to WIPA."
- Always label results "Estimate only" and route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752**.
- Use year-specific thresholds. Do not hard-code $51,711 past 2026.
- Ask about the resource test (savings, ABLE) along with earnings.
- Do NOT tell someone they "will lose Medicaid" because of a raise. Many people fear this, and it stops them from working. Show the 1619(b) and MAPP paths instead.
