# SSDI work rules (TWP, SGA, EPE, Medicare while working)

## TL;DR
- In 2026, any month with gross earnings over **$1,210** uses one of 9 **Trial Work Period (TWP)** months, counted in a rolling 60-month window. Full SSDI is paid during the TWP.
- After the TWP comes a 36-month **Extended Period of Eligibility (EPE)**. SSDI is paid for months under **SGA**: $1,690/month (non-blind) or $2,830/month (blind) in 2026. It is suspended in months over SGA.
- The first SGA month after the TWP starts the cessation. SSDI is paid for that month and a 2-month **grace period**.
- Premium-free Medicare Part A continues for at least **93 months** after the TWP ends. **Expedited Reinstatement** is available for 5 years after benefits stop.

## Key facts
| Item | 2026 | 2027 (announced) | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| TWP month threshold | $1,210/mo gross (or 80+ self-employment hours) | $1,270/mo | SSA TWP page; Red Book |
| TWP length | 9 months (not consecutive) in a rolling 60 months | same | 20 CFR 404.1592; SSA TWP page |
| SGA, non-blind | $1,690/mo | $1,770/mo | SSA SGA page; 2027 fact sheet |
| SGA, blind | $2,830/mo | $2,950/mo | SSA SGA page; 2027 fact sheet |
| EPE re-entitlement period | 36 months after TWP | same | Red Book, SSDI only |
| Grace period | cessation month + 2 months | same | Red Book, SSDI only |
| Expedited Reinstatement window | 60 months from termination; up to 6 months provisional pay | same | Red Book, SSDI and SSI |
| Extended Medicare | at least 93 months after last TWP month | same | Red Book, SSDI only |
| Medicare Part A buy-in premium | $565/mo (reduced $311) | not yet published | Red Book What's New 2026 |
| Medicare Part B standard premium | $202.90/mo | not yet published | Red Book What's New 2026 |
| Default Title II overpayment withholding | 50% of monthly benefit | | SSA Resolve an overpayment |

## How it works
**1. Trial Work Period.** Each month with gross earnings above $1,210 (2026) is a TWP month. Self-employed people also use one with more than 80 hours of work. After 9 TWP months in any 60-month window, the TWP ends. SSDI is paid in full for every TWP month, no matter how much the person earns.

**2. Extended Period of Eligibility (EPE).** The EPE starts the month after the 9th TWP month. During the first 36 months:
- Month at or under SGA: SSDI is paid.
- Month over SGA: SSDI is not paid (after the grace period).
- No new application is needed to restart. The person reports when earnings drop.

**3. Cessation and grace period.** The first month of SGA-level work after the TWP is the cessation month. SSDI is still paid for that month and the next two.

**4. After the 36 months.** The first month of SGA work after the 36-month re-entitlement period ends entitlement. Then the person needs Expedited Reinstatement or a new application.

**5. How SGA is measured.** SSA starts from gross earnings. It then subtracts:
- **IRWE**: impairment-related costs the worker pays.
- **Subsidies and special conditions**: support from the employer or a job coach worth more than the work's value. Examples include extra supervision, a job coach, or lower productivity at full pay. Supported employment via ERI or DVR can create a subsidy.
- **Unincurred business expenses** (self-employment).
- **Unsuccessful work attempts**: work that ended within 6 months because of the impairment is not counted (during the EPE, up to the cessation month).

The TWP test uses gross earnings. IRWE and subsidies do not lower TWP counting.

**6. Expedited Reinstatement (EXR).** If benefits stopped because of work, the person can ask to restart within 5 years. They must be unable to do SGA because of the same or a related impairment. SSA can pay up to 6 months of provisional benefits during the medical review. After 24 payable months in the Initial Reinstatement Period, the person gets a new TWP, a new EPE and new extended Medicare.

**7. Medicare while working.** Premium-free Part A continues for at least 93 months after the last TWP month, as long as the disability continues. After that, a person under 65 can buy Medicare (Part A $565/month in 2026, or $311 with 30+ quarters). Wisconsin Medicaid programs such as MAPP or a Medicare Savings Program may help **(verify)** which one fits.

**8. Overpayments.** Work causes overpayments when SSA learns about SGA months late. For new Title II overpayments, SSA withholds **50%** of the monthly benefit by default if the person does not repay within 30 days. SSA set the default to 100% for overpayments after 2025-03-27. Its current overpayment page states 50%. **(verify)** the exact date the 50% rate started, in SSA instruction EM-25029. A person can ask for a lower rate, a waiver, or an appeal. Asking within 30 days pauses collection.

## Caveats and gotchas
- SSDI has no "$1 for $2" rule. During the EPE, benefits are all or nothing by month. One dollar over SGA can mean $0 SSDI that month. An estimator must show this cliff.
- TWP months are counted even when the person did not report them. Old, unreported work often uses up TWP months without the person knowing.
- SSA can count earnings in the month they were earned, not paid. Check timing rules with WIPA.
- Childhood disability beneficiaries (CDB/DAC) and widow(er)s follow the same SGA rules, but other entitlement rules apply. **(verify)** with WIPA for these cases.
- The EXR "provisional benefits" rule (up to 6 months) comes from the Red Book SSDI-and-SSI page. The SSDI-only page does not mention it.
- 2027 Medicare premiums were not published as of 2026-10-23. SSA said 2027 premium amounts will be in my Social Security in late November 2026.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A work timeline tool should track TWP months, EPE months, the cessation month and the grace period. Inputs should be monthly gross earnings and month-specific SGA/TWP values.
- Ask about IRWE and subsidies (job coach, ERI supported employment). These change SGA results and are a big reason to get WIPA help.
- Always show "Estimate only. SSA makes the decision." and route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752**.
- Show the cliff clearly: "Earning over $1,690 in a month after your Trial Work Period may stop that month's SSDI check."
- Do NOT tell anyone a TWP month "doesn't count" or that they "won't be overpaid." Do NOT compute final overpayment amounts. Route those to WIPA, SSA, or Disability Rights Wisconsin.

# SSI work rules (income counting, exclusions, resources, reporting)

## TL;DR
- SSI is a needs-based cash benefit. In 2026 the federal benefit rate (FBR) is **$994/month** (individual) and **$1,491** (couple). SSA has announced **$1,029 / $1,544** for 2027, paid starting 2026-12-31.
- Work rarely makes SSI stop suddenly. After the $20 general and $65 earned income exclusions, SSI goes down **$1 for every $2** of remaining wages.
- The resource limit is **$2,000** for an individual and **$3,000** for a couple. ABLE balances up to $100,000 and PASS set-asides are excluded.
- Wisconsin adds a state supplement of **$92.16/month** for an individual (effective 2026-05-01, up from $83.78). Wages must be reported to SSA monthly.

## Key facts
| Item | 2026 value | 2027 (announced) | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| FBR, individual | $994/mo | $1,029/mo | SSA COLA fact sheets 2026, 2027 |
| FBR, couple | $1,491/mo | $1,544/mo | SSA COLA fact sheets 2026, 2027 |
| COLA | 2.8% | 3.6% | SSA COLA fact sheets; press release 2026-10-14 |
| General income exclusion | $20/mo | same (not indexed) | 20 CFR 416.1124; Understanding SSI, Income |
| Earned income exclusion | $65 + one-half of the rest | same | 20 CFR 416.1112; Red Book |
| Student Earned Income Exclusion (under 22) | $2,410/mo, $9,730/yr | $2,500/mo, $10,080/yr | SSA studentEIE page |
| Resource limit | $2,000 individual / $3,000 couple | same | SSI Spotlight on Resources |
| ABLE exclusion | first $100,000 | same | SSI Spotlight on Resources; POMS SI 01130.740 |
| WI state supplement, individual living independently | $92.16/mo (from 2026-05-01) | not COLA-adjusted | DHS Ops Memo 26-12 |
| Wage report deadline | 6th of following month (SSA web page); 10th (SSA 2026-08-01 article) | | SSA wage reporting pages |
| Default SSI overpayment withholding | 10% of SSI payment | | SSA Resolve an overpayment |

## How it works
**Earned and unearned income.** Earned income is wages, net self-employment earnings, and sheltered workshop pay. Unearned income is everything else, such as SSDI, pensions, unemployment, and cash gifts. Unearned income lowers SSI almost dollar for dollar after the $20 exclusion.

**In-kind support and maintenance (ISM).** Free or reduced-cost shelter can lower SSI. Since 2024-09-30, food no longer counts as ISM. Shelter still does.

**Order of the earned income math (simplified):**
1. Subtract the Student Earned Income Exclusion, if eligible (applied first).
2. Subtract any unused part of the $20 general exclusion.
3. Subtract $65.
4. Subtract IRWE (impairment-related work expenses).
5. Divide the rest by 2.
6. Subtract BWE (blind work expenses) and PASS set-asides, if any.
7. The result is countable earned income. Add countable unearned income. Subtract the total from the FBR.

SSA's own example: $317 in wages, minus $20, minus $65, divided by 2, gives $116 countable. $994 minus $116 = $878 federal SSI.

**Break-even point.** With only wages and no other income, the federal SSI check reaches $0 at about (2 x FBR) + $85 per month. For 2026 that is about $2,073/month (our arithmetic: 2 x $994 + $85). Medicaid can continue past that point under Section 1619(b) (see related page).

**Student Earned Income Exclusion (SEIE).** For people under 22 who regularly attend school, college or job training. School thresholds: college 8 hours/week; grades 7-12 at least 12 hours/week; training 12 hours/week (15 with shop practice).

**PASS (Plan to Achieve Self-Support).** A written plan (form SSA-545) with a work goal and a timeline. Income and resources set aside under an approved PASS are not counted. PASS can let someone with SSDI also qualify for SSI. SSA has PASS specialists (via 1-800-772-1213).

**IRWE.** Costs for items or services a person needs to work because of their impairment, that they pay for themselves without reimbursement, and that are reasonable. Examples: some medications, attendant care, transport. Not allowed: health insurance premiums, or non-service animals.

**BWE (blind only).** Blind work expenses can include any work expense, such as taxes, meals at work, and transportation. They are subtracted after the one-half step, so they help more than IRWE.

**Deeming.** Some income of another person counts toward SSI when the person lives with an ineligible spouse, when a disabled child under 18 lives with parents, or when a noncitizen has a sponsor. Parental deeming stops at age 18. So many young adults see SSI rise at 18.

**Resources.** Countable resources must stay at or under $2,000 (individual) as of the first moment of each month. Excluded items include the home, one vehicle, household goods, burial funds up to $1,500, PASS funds, and ABLE funds up to $100,000.

**Reporting wages.** SSI recipients must report gross wages each month. Methods: my Social Security, the SSA Mobile Wage Reporting app, the automated phone line (1-866-772-0953), or the Payroll Information Exchange (PIE). With PIE, SSA gets wages directly from the employer (sign up with form SSA-8240). The person still needs to report until SSA confirms PIE is working.

**Overpayments.** SSI payments are based on income in the same month, so late reports create overpayments. If the person does not repay or respond within 30 days of the notice, SSA withholds 10% of the SSI payment by default. Asking for a waiver or appeal within 30 days pauses collection.

## Caveats and gotchas
- People often think one dollar earned costs one dollar of SSI. That is wrong for wages. It is about $1 lost for every $2 earned after $85.
- SSDI counts as **unearned** income for SSI. A person with both gets far less benefit from the $65 exclusion.
- The Wisconsin supplement rose 10% on 2026-05-01. It was the first change since 1994. Older materials still say $83.78. Wisconsin pays its own supplement, so it may be on a separate payment.
- SSA pages disagree on the wage reporting deadline: the wage page says "by the sixth day of the month," and the 2026-08-01 article says "the 10th." Tell people to report by the 6th. **(verify)** the regulatory deadline in POMS.
- SSI is paid on the 1st. When the 1st falls on a weekend or holiday, it is paid earlier. That is why the January 2027 increase arrives 2026-12-31. Two payments in one month do not mean an overpayment.
- Resources of an ineligible spouse or parent can be deemed too. This page does not give 2026 deeming allocation amounts. **(verify)** in POMS SI 01320 before using them.
- 2027 values are announced but take effect 2027-01-01. A tool must use the rate for the month being estimated.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- An SSI estimator must apply exclusions in the order above. It must show "Estimate only, not a benefits determination" and route the user to WIPA at **1-877-826-1752**.
- The estimator must ask whether the person also gets SSDI or other unearned income, lives with a spouse or parents (deeming), and pays for any IRWE or BWE. If the answers are unknown, show a range, not one number.
- Include the Wisconsin supplement as a separate line. Show it as a state payment.
- Pick the FBR by month. Use $994 through December 2026 and $1,029 from January 2027.
- Push wage reporting. Offer reminders (6th of the month) and link to PIE and the SSA app. Never collect SSA login details.
- Do NOT tell anyone they "will lose SSI" or "will be overpaid." Do NOT give a final answer on deeming, PASS approval, or overpayment waivers. Route those to WIPA or a benefits specialist.

# Ticket to Work

## TL;DR
- Adults **18 through 64** who get SSDI or SSI based on disability can use their Ticket. It is free and voluntary. They assign it to one **Employment Network (EN)**, such as ERI PLUS, or use state VR (DVR).
- While the Ticket is assigned and the person makes **timely progress**, SSA does **not** start a medical Continuing Disability Review (CDR).
- ENs are paid only when the beneficiary earns. For 2026: Phase 1 milestones are **$1,904** each (4 milestones, at $1,210/month earnings). Maximum total payments are **$34,453** (SSDI) and **$32,498** (SSI) under milestone-outcome, or **$38,268 / $35,640** under outcome-only.
- Ticket Help Line: **1-866-968-7842** (TTY 1-866-833-2967), Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET.

## Key facts
| Item | 2026 value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Eligible ages | 18 through 64 | SSA Pub 05-10061 |
| Phase 1 milestones (SSDI and SSI) | 4 x $1,904 = $7,616; earnings $1,210/mo for 1, 3 of 6, 6 of 12, 9 of 18 months | 2026 Payments at a Glance |
| Phase 2 milestones | SSDI up to 11 x $571 = $6,281; SSI up to 18 x $319 = $5,742 (earnings above SGA) | 2026 Payments at a Glance |
| Outcome payments (milestone-outcome method) | SSDI up to 36 x $571 = $20,556; SSI up to 60 x $319 = $19,140 (above SGA and $0 federal cash benefit) | 2026 Payments at a Glance |
| Total milestone-outcome max | SSDI $34,453; SSI $32,498 | 2026 Payments at a Glance |
| Outcome-only method | SSDI 36 x $1,063 = $38,268; SSI 60 x $594 = $35,640 | 2026 Payments at a Glance |
| SGA used in payments | $1,690 non-blind / $2,830 blind | 2026 Payments at a Glance; SSA SGA |
| Timely Progress Review | every 12 months of Ticket use | Choose Work FAQ; 20 CFR 411.180 |
| Reassign to keep CDR protection | within 90 days of unassigning | Choose Work FAQ |

## How it works
**Assigning a Ticket.** The beneficiary chooses an EN. They can talk to as many ENs as they like first. The EN checks eligibility with the Ticket Program Manager. The EN and the person sign an **Individual Work Plan (IWP)**. With state VR, the plan is an IPE. A person can work with only one EN at a time. Someone with an open DVR case finishes or closes it before getting EN services. DVR can hand off to an EN after closure (**Partnership Plus**) **(verify)**, since the pages we opened did not describe Partnership Plus.

**What ENs provide.** Career planning, job placement, and ongoing supports. ERI PLUS can pair this with WIPA benefits counseling, but WIPA is a separate, neutral service.

**How ENs are paid.** SSA pays ENs only on earnings evidence. The payment rate in effect in the month the milestone or outcome is reached applies.
- Phase 1 milestones: gross earnings of at least $1,210/month (2026 TWP level).
- Phase 2 milestones: earnings above SGA.
- Outcome payments: earnings above SGA **and** a $0 federal cash benefit.

**Timely Progress Review (TPR).** Every 12 months, SSA checks progress toward the work goal. Under 20 CFR 411.180:

| Ticket-use period | Work test (or education alternative) |
|---|---|
| 1st 12 months | 3 months with earnings at or above the TWP amount; or HS diploma/GED; or 60% of a degree or vocational program |
| 2nd (24 months) | 6 months at TWP level; or another 75% of program |
| 3rd (36 months) | 9 months above SGA; or finish a 2-year degree, certificate or vocational program |
| 4th (48 months) | 9 months above SGA; or more 4-year credits |
| 5th and later | 6 months with earnings that stop SSDI/SSI cash; or degree completion (through the 6th) |

Work and education percentages can be combined to total 100%.

**Medical CDR protection.** SSA will not start a medical CDR while the Ticket is "in use" and progress is timely. Protection does not cover work CDRs (reviews of earnings). Putting the Ticket in inactive status stops the protection for those months.

**Section 301.** If SSA finds medical improvement while someone is in an approved program that started before the improvement decision, benefits can continue. Approved programs include an EN's IWP, a VR IPE, a PASS, or an IEP for ages 18-21. SSA must find the program likely to lead to leaving the rolls.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The TPR table above is from the SSA-hosted CFR page. **(verify)** it matches the current eCFR text before using it in a tool.
- Ticket protects against **medical** reviews only. Earnings still reduce or stop checks under normal SSDI/SSI rules.
- SSA had not published 2027 EN payment rates as of 2026-10-23. Milestone thresholds will follow the 2027 TWP ($1,270) and SGA ($1,770 / $2,950) **(verify)** when SSA publishes "2027 Payments at a Glance".
- "Ticket to Work" ads are not always from SSA. Only official ENs listed on choosework.ssa.gov should be assigned Tickets.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- An intake tool can explain Ticket in plain language. It can check eligibility questions (age 18-64, SSDI/SSI based on disability) and offer a warm handoff to ERI PLUS. It must also say the person can choose any EN or DVR.
- An EN revenue model can use the 2026 table above. It must mark rows as "payment rate when attained" and must never forecast an individual's earnings as fact.
- A TPR tracker for staff should show months worked at the TWP level versus SGA, by Ticket-use year.
- Always pair Ticket talks with benefits counseling: WIPA **1-877-826-1752**.
- Do NOT promise that Ticket "protects your benefits." It only stops medical CDRs while progress is timely.

## Related pages
- [SSDI work rules](ssdi-work-rules.md)
- [SSI work rules](ssi-work-rules.md)
- [Benefits quick reference 2026](benefits-quick-reference-2026.md)

# Wisconsin Medicaid and long-term care

## TL;DR
- **BadgerCare Plus** is income-based Medicaid for ages 0-64. Adults qualify at or under 100% FPL ($1,330/month for one person, from 2026-02-01). **SSI-related (EBD) Medicaid** is for people who are 65+, blind or disabled. It has a $2,000 asset limit and the $20 and $65-and-one-half income credits.
- Adult long-term care runs through **Family Care / Family Care Partnership** (managed care organizations) or **IRIS** (self-directed). In 2026, both use a **$2,000 asset limit** and a **$2,982/month** income limit. People with income up to $10,854.80 may qualify with a cost share.
- Children: **CLTS** waiver (under 22; the waitlist has ended) and **Katie Beckett Medicaid** (under 19; parents' income is not a barrier).
- All of these list supported employment and competitive integrated employment (CIE) as services. Members of Family Care, IRIS, SSI Medicaid and MAPP are not subject to the federal work requirement that starts 2027-01-01.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| BadgerCare Plus adult limit | 100% FPL = $1,330/mo (household of 1), 2026-02-01 to 2027-01-31 | DHS BadgerCare FPL page |
| BadgerCare pregnant/children | 306% FPL = $4,069.80/mo (household of 1 table) | DHS BadgerCare FPL page |
| EBD (SSI-related) assets | $2,000 individual / $3,000 couple | DHS SSI-Related Medicaid |
| EBD income | 100% FPL after credits: $1,330 individual, $1,803.33 couple; deductible if over | DHS SSI-Related Medicaid |
| Family Care / IRIS asset limit 2026 | $2,000 | DHS P-10059 (01/2026) |
| Family Care / IRIS income limit 2026 | $2,982/mo gross (equals 3 x $994 FBR); up to $10,854.80 with possible cost share | DHS P-10059 |
| Family Care age / scope | 18+; frail elders and adults with disabilities; statewide since 2018 | DHS Family Care |
| CLTS age | under 22 | DHS CLTS eligibility |
| Katie Beckett age | under 19 | DHS Katie Beckett eligibility |
| ForwardHealth Member Services | 800-362-3002 | DHS pages |
| IRIS Call Center | 888-515-4747 | DHS IRIS page |

## How it works
**Which "door" a person uses.**
- *SSI recipient*: Wisconsin Medicaid comes with SSI (1634 state). It continues under 1619(b) while working.
- *Disabled, not on SSI, low income*: SSI-related (EBD) Medicaid, if assets are at or under $2,000. Otherwise BadgerCare Plus, if income is at or under 100% FPL.
- *Disabled and working with more income or assets*: the [Medicaid Purchase Plan (MAPP)](wisconsin-medicaid-purchase-plan-mapp.md).
- *Needs long-term care*: contact the local **Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC)**. The ADRC does the Long-Term Care Functional Screen and options counseling.

**Family Care.** A Medicaid long-term care benefit for adults 18+ who are frail elders or have a physical, intellectual or developmental disability. They must be Medicaid-eligible, functionally eligible, and have a long-term condition expected to last over 90 days. Members choose a managed care organization (MCO). The MCO plans and buys services. **Family Care Partnership** also covers acute and primary care.

**IRIS (Include, Respect, I Self-Direct).** The same people qualify, but the participant gets a budget and directs services. They hire their own workers through a fiscal employer agent and get guidance from an IRIS consultant agency. The listed employment supports include CIE exploration, individual and small-group supported employment, prevocational services, and vocational futures planning.

**Cost share.** In Family Care and IRIS, people with income above the $2,982 limit (up to $10,854.80) may owe a monthly cost share. It is based on income, housing and medical costs. More earnings can mean a higher cost share. That is a real "work cost" a benefits plan must model.

**Children.**
- **CLTS**: a Medicaid home and community-based waiver for children under 22 who need an institutional level of care. It funds non-medical supports. It now has continuous enrollment, with no waitlist.
- **Katie Beckett Medicaid**: Medicaid for children under 19 with a disability who need institutional-level care. Parents' income and assets do not block eligibility.
- At 18, the child's own income and resources start to matter (SSI parental deeming ends). This is the time to plan SSI, Medicaid and the move to adult long-term care.

**Employment services and Medicaid.** DHS policy calls CIE "the first and preferred employment outcome". In SFY 2021, only about 11% of working-age Family Care, Partnership and IRIS members had CIE. Their median pay was $9.50/hour for 12.5 hours/week. A person can get DVR services (where ERI is a Supported Employment vendor) and later long-term job supports through Family Care or IRIS. Long-term care programs usually expect DVR to be used first for services DVR can fund **(verify)** in the Family Care benefit package and IRIS policy manual.

## Caveats and gotchas
- People mix up BadgerCare Plus and EBD Medicaid. Disability-based coverage (EBD, MAPP, waiver programs) is the safer category for workers with disabilities. BadgerCare adults face the 2027 federal work requirement and the 100% FPL income cap.
- The $2,982 Family Care/IRIS limit equals 300% of the 2026 FBR (our arithmetic). It will change on 2027-01-01 with the new FBR ($1,029 x 3 = $3,087, unconfirmed). **(verify)** in DHS P-10059 2027 edition.
- The DHS pages we opened do not show the spousal impoverishment amounts or the cost-share formula. **(verify)** in the Medicaid Eligibility Handbook.
- Moving from 1619(b) to MAPP can keep Family Care or IRIS eligibility, but cost share and premium rules interact **(verify)** case by case with the ADRC or MCO.
- CLTS was renewed in 2022 for five years. Expect a renewal around 2027 **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A "which Medicaid am I on?" helper can map answers (SSI? long-term care? age? working?) to likely programs. It should then say "Confirm with ForwardHealth Member Services 800-362-3002 or your ADRC."
- Earnings estimators for Family Care or IRIS members must warn that cost share can change, and route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752**.
- For youth turning 18, show a checklist: SSI redetermination at 18, the end of parental deeming, CLTS ending at 22, and Katie Beckett ending at 19.
- Do NOT tell anyone they will or will not qualify for Family Care or IRIS. Functional and financial eligibility are decided by the ADRC and the income maintenance agency.

- [Wisconsin DHS, IRIS](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/iris/index.htm)

# Wisconsin Medicaid Purchase Plan (MAPP)

## TL;DR
- MAPP lets Wisconsin adults (18+) with a disability buy into full Medicaid while working. Family income can go up to **250% FPL**, and countable assets can go up to **$15,000**.
- Members must have **work activity at least once a month**. Job seekers can meet this through **Health and Employment Counseling (HEC)**, for up to 9 months plus a 3-month extension.
- There is no premium if the person's own gross monthly income is at or under 100% FPL. Above that, premiums **start at $25/month** plus 3% of net income above the FPL.
- Changes: Independence Accounts can take up to **100% of gross earnings** (was 50%), under 2025 Wisconsin Act 225, for MAPP renewals received on or after 2026-08-01 (DHS Ops Memo 26-26). The rule giving one extra month to pay before disenrollment started with December 2025 premiums. MAPP is **not** subject to the 2027 federal Medicaid work requirement.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Age | 18+ | DHS MAPP page |
| Disability | determined by Wisconsin Disability Determination Bureau (or SSA) | DHS MAPP page; P-00181 |
| Income limit | family income at or under 250% FPL | DHS MAPP page |
| Asset limit | $15,000 individual (home, one car, ABLE excluded) | DHS MAPP page |
| Premium threshold | individual gross income above 100% FPL ($1,330/mo in 2026 for one person) | DHS MAPP page; DHS SSI-related page |
| Premium formula | $25 + 3% of (net income minus FPL), rounded down | P-00181; 09/2025 webinar |
| Premium due | 10th of the month; disenrolled if not paid by end of the following month | DHS MAPP page; 09/2025 webinar |
| Independence Account cap | 100% of gross earnings (from 2026-08-01; was 50%) | DHS Ops Memo 26-26 |
| Inheritance exclusion | up to $40,000 (later date, not yet in effect) | DHS Ops Memo 26-26 |
| HEC length | 9 months + possible 3-month extension; max 2 times in 5 years, 6 months apart | P-00181 |
| HEC coordinator | 866-278-6440 | P-00181 |

## How it works
**Who qualifies.** Wisconsin residents age 18+, determined disabled, with family income at or under 250% FPL and individual countable assets at or under $15,000. For eligibility, the earned income deduction works like this: subtract $65, divide the rest by two, and add $65 back. IRWE and large out-of-pocket medical costs (over $500/month) are also deducted.

**Work requirement.** Members must have paid work, self-employment, or in-kind work in at least one month at a time. Volunteering does not count. There is no minimum hours or earnings amount on the DHS page. A temporary health-related exemption is available (form F-10127). Premiums are still owed during an exemption.

**Health and Employment Counseling (HEC).** HEC is for members who are not working but want to. They make an action plan and keep MAPP for up to 9 months, with a possible 3-month extension. They can use HEC twice in 5 years, with at least 6 months between uses. Application form F-00004.

**Premiums.** Premiums are based on the member's **own** income, not household income. The DHS example: $2,000 gross minus $300 allowed expenses = $1,700. Minus the 2025 FPL of $1,304.17 = $395.83. Times 3% = $11.87. Plus $25 = $36 (rounded down). Payment options include ACCESS AutoPay (drawn on the 3rd), EFT, wage withholding and check. Hardship waivers can last up to 12 months and can be backdated 3 months.

**Independence Accounts.** Members can deposit earnings into a registered Independence Account (form F-10121). It does not count toward the $15,000 asset limit. The yearly cap is 100% of gross earnings for renewals received on or after 2026-08-01 (Ops Memo 26-26). The same memo describes a $40,000 inheritance asset exclusion that takes effect later, under a future memo **(verify)**. Deposits over the cap add a penalty to the premium over the next 12 months.

**Why it matters for working people.** MAPP is the main "next step" when someone loses 1619(b) or does not qualify for SSI. Examples: an SSDI beneficiary earning above SGA, or a worker whose earnings pass the 1619(b) threshold. MAPP gives full ForwardHealth Medicaid benefits and can cover Family Care or IRIS eligibility for working members **(verify)** cost-share interaction with the ADRC.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The DHS page does not list a 2026 premium example. The 3% formula comes from P-00181 (11/2025), which used the 2025 FPL. Use the current FPL, which is $1,330/month for one person from 2026-02-01 (per DHS SSI-related and BadgerCare FPL pages).
- 250% FPL for a household of one is about $3,325/month in 2026 (our arithmetic from $1,330). **(verify)** against DHS's MAPP income table before showing it in a tool.
- How unearned income such as SSDI is treated for the premium (versus earned income) is not spelled out on the pages we opened. **(verify)** in the Medicaid Eligibility Handbook, chapter 26.
- The $40,000 inheritance exclusion is enacted (2025 Wisconsin Act 225) but not yet in effect. DHS will announce the effective date in a later memo.
- MAPP members are listed by DHS as **not subject** to the federal Medicaid work requirement that starts 2027-01-01. MAPP's own work rule still applies.
- Missing a premium no longer ends coverage right away. Coverage ends at the end of the month after the due month (first applied to December 2025 premiums, ending January 31, 2026).

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A screener can flag "possible MAPP" when someone is working (or open to HEC), is disabled, has family income likely at or under 250% FPL, and has assets at or under $15,000. Show "Estimate only" and route the user to WIPA **1-877-826-1752** or the local income maintenance agency.
- A premium estimator must use the current-year FPL and the individual's income, and show the $25 minimum. Do not present it as a bill.
- Promote Independence Accounts as a savings tool for MAPP members.
- Do NOT say "MAPP requires X hours." No hours minimum appears in DHS materials.
- Do NOT confuse MAPP's work rule with the federal BadgerCare work requirement.

# 42 CFR Part 2 (substance use disorder records)

## TL;DR
- Part 2 protects records that identify a patient of a **federally assisted SUD "program"**. That is an organization that **holds itself out as providing, and provides**, SUD diagnosis, treatment or referral for treatment. It also binds **"lawful holders"**, meaning anyone who receives those records through consent or an exception.
- HHS published the 2024 final rule on 2024-02-08 (fact sheet date). The **compliance date of 2026-02-16 is confirmed** on the HHS fact sheet (updated 2026-01-30).
- The rule moves Part 2 closer to HIPAA:
  - One consent can now cover all future treatment, payment and health care operations (TPO).
  - HIPAA breach notification applies to Part 2 records.
  - HIPAA-style civil and criminal penalties replace the old Part 2 criminal-only penalties.
- What did not change: records **still cannot be used against a patient in legal proceedings** without specific consent or a court order. **SUD counseling notes** need their own separate consent.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Final rule date | 2024-02-08 (HHS fact sheet header) | HHS fact sheet |
| Effective date | 2024-04-16 **(verify)**, not stated on the fact sheet | 89 FR (Feb. 2024) |
| Compliance date | **2026-02-16** | HHS fact sheet |
| "Program" | A person (other than a general medical facility) that holds itself out as providing, and provides, SUD diagnosis, treatment or referral. Also covers identified SUD units and staff in general medical facilities | 42 CFR 2.11 |
| Federally assisted | Federally conducted, licensed or authorized (e.g., DEA registration), supported (e.g., Medicare or Medicaid participation **(verify scope)**), or tax-assisted | 42 CFR 2.12(b) |
| Lawful holder | Someone bound by Part 2 because they received records through consent with a disclosure notice, or through an exception | 42 CFR 2.11 |
| Qualified service organization (QSO) | A vendor that serves a program (data processing, billing and similar) under a written agreement to be bound by Part 2 | 42 CFR 2.11 |
| SUD counseling notes | A clinician's notes on a private SUD counseling session, kept separate from the record. Need specific consent and cannot ride on a TPO consent | 42 CFR 2.11, 2.31(b) |
| Consent elements | Patient name, discloser, description of the information, recipients, purpose, right to revoke, expiration, signature and date. TPO consents add redisclosure and refusal statements | 42 CFR 2.31 |
| Security | Formal written policies for paper and electronic records covering transfer, destruction, access and de-identification | 42 CFR 2.16 |
| Breach | The HIPAA Breach Notification Rule applies to unsecured Part 2 records | 42 CFR 2.16; HHS fact sheet |
| Segregation | Not required (records do not have to be segmented) | HHS fact sheet |
| Accounting of disclosures | Compliance date deferred until HHS revises the HIPAA accounting rule | HHS fact sheet |

## How it works
1. **Is there a Part 2 program?** Look at what the organization *holds itself out* as doing. A CCS program that advertises and delivers substance use treatment or referral may be one. So may a unit or staff member whose primary function is SUD care. A supported-employment team that only learns about a person's SUD history in passing is usually not a program. However, it may still be a **lawful holder** of records it received.
2. **Does the record identify a patient as having an SUD,** directly or by inference, and did it come from a program? If yes, Part 2 rules attach to it and follow it to every lawful holder.
3. **Consent.** Since 2026-02-16 a patient can sign one consent for all future TPO uses. HIPAA covered entities and BAs that receive records under that consent may redisclose them as HIPAA allows. A consent for use in legal proceedings must be separate. Every disclosure made under a consent must carry a copy of the consent or a clear description of its scope.
4. **Wisconsin adds its own rule.** Wis. Stat. 51.30 covers "alcoholism or drug dependence" treatment records and requires its own written informed consent. The family-member disclosure exception in 51.30(4)(b)20 **does not apply** to alcohol or drug dependence records.
5. **SSA forms.** The SSA-827 is written to satisfy both HIPAA and Part 2 for disclosures to SSA. SSA says it will not redisclose alcohol and drug information without proper Part 2 consent.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Whether ERI is a Part 2 program or a lawful holder is unconfirmed.** It depends on what ERI's CCS role publicly offers (for example, SUD counseling or recovery services) and what records ERI receives from Dane County. **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. Does any ERI service hold itself out as SUD diagnosis, treatment or referral?
  2. Does ERI receive SUD-identifying records from Dane County CCS or other providers? Under what consent?
  3. Does ERI have a QSO agreement, or Part 2 terms in a BAA, with each vendor that touches these records?
  4. Do ERI's consent forms meet both 42 CFR 2.31 and Wis. Stat. 51.30(2)?
  5. Has ERI's Notice of Privacy Practices been updated for Part 2? (The rule aligned Part 2's patient notice with HIPAA's NPP.)
- The single TPO consent is **not** a blanket release. It does not cover legal proceedings or SUD counseling notes, and it does not reach recipients outside TPO, such as an employer.
- Peer recovery support is a covered CCS service (DHS). Notes from peer sessions may carry SUD information, so treat them as Part 2 unless counsel says otherwise.
- Under 42 CFR 2.12, how far "federally assisted" reaches through county Medicaid was not fully read for this page **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** synthetic data only. Do not build demo personas with real SUD histories. Fake ones should be clearly labeled as fictional.
- **Production:**
  - Tag SUD-derived fields with a `part2: true` flag. Hide them from roles without a documented need, such as job developers and benefits staff.
  - Store consent records as structured data: scope, recipients, expiration, revocation date and whether the consent is TPO.
  - Block any disclosure that has no matching valid consent, and log every disclosure.
  - Attach the required notice or consent copy to every outbound disclosure automatically.
- **A tool must NOT:** infer or flag SUD status from other data, for example by AI classification of case notes. It must not include SUD details in employer-facing outputs. It must not mix SUD counseling notes into general case notes or AI summaries.

# Compliance, privacy and accessibility index

## TL;DR
- **Hackathon ground rule:** synthetic data only. Never use real participant, student, beneficiary or billing data in code, prompts, demos or screenshots.
- **AI and DVR consumers:** the DVR provider agreement requires **prior written or verbal consumer consent for any AI tool**.
- **Key dates:**
  - Part 2 compliance: 2026-02-16
  - ADA Title II web rule: 2027-04-26 for large entities, 2028-04-26 for small entities and special districts (moved by DOJ's 2026-04-20 IFR)
- These pages explain rules. They do **not** give legal advice. Open questions are framed as **questions for ERI's counsel/compliance**.

| 45 days | Wisconsin 134.98 notice outer limit | [wisconsin-breach-notification](wisconsin-breach-notification.md) |
| 24 hours | Written incident notice to DVR | [vr-confidentiality](vr-confidentiality-34-cfr-361-38.md) |
| 1 hour | SSA contractor incident reporting (applicability to WIPA: verify) | [ssa-data-and-consent](ssa-data-and-consent.md) |

# Draft AI use policy for ERI

> **Status: DRAFT for ERI leadership and counsel review.** It is not legal advice and is not adopted ERI policy.

## TL;DR
- **Default rule:** only **synthetic or properly de-identified data** goes into AI tools. PHI, SUD records, SSNs, school records and DVR case data stay out of AI tools unless all three of these are true: (1) the tool is on an ERI-approved list, (2) a signed **BAA or data agreement** covers that exact product and feature, and (3) every program-specific consent is in place.
- **DVR's provider agreement requires consumer consent for AI.** "The use of any AI tool requires the prior written or verbal consent of the DVR consumer" (Attachment A, item l). This applies *even with* a BAA.
- **A human reviews every AI output** before it reaches a participant, employer, funder or claim. AI never writes service documentation for billing.
- Use **NIST AI RMF 1.0** (released 2023-01-26) and its Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1, 2024-07-26) as the governance frame: **Govern, Map, Measure, Manage**.

## Key facts
| Item | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| NIST AI RMF 1.0 | 2023-01-26, voluntary. Being revised under the White House AI Action Plan | NIST |
| GenAI Profile | NIST AI 600-1, 2024-07-26 | NIST |
| Cloud vendors and PHI | A vendor storing PHI is a business associate even if the data is encrypted and it has no key. A BAA is required | HHS cloud guidance |
| De-identification | Safe Harbor (18 identifiers) or Expert Determination | 45 CFR 164.514(b) |
| Section 1557 AI rule | Covered entities must identify and mitigate discrimination risk from patient care decision support tools. Compliance within 300 days of 2024-07-05 (about 2025-05-01) | 45 CFR 92.210, 92.1 |
| DVR AI rules | Prior written or verbal consumer consent. AI-held records must meet agreement sections 7.1 (security) and 7.3 (confidentiality) | DVR Agreement Att. A (l), (m) |

**Vendor BAA availability (from vendor pages opened 2026-10-23; recheck before relying on it):**

| Vendor | BAA offered? | Scope notes |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Claude) | Yes | First-party API and Claude Enterprise **with the HIPAA configuration enabled**. Many features are excluded (e.g., Console, mobile app, connectors/MCP, Files and Batch API, web fetch). Team plan not addressed. Consumer plans not covered |
| OpenAI | API only | API BAA after review, limited to zero-data-retention-eligible endpoints. "We do not offer a BAA for ChatGPT" at present |
| Google Workspace | Yes | Accepted in the Admin console. Covers "HIPAA Included Functionality," including some Gemini-in-Workspace features. The Gemini app and NotebookLM are not named on the page **(verify)** |
| Microsoft | Yes | Through the Online Services DPA, by default. In-scope services listed include Microsoft 365 services, Copilot and Copilot Chat (Commercial and GCC). Azure OpenAI not named explicitly **(verify)** |

## How it works (draft policy text)
1. **Scope.** This policy covers all staff, contractors, volunteers and hackathon participants, and any AI tool, including features built into other software.
2. **Approved tools.** IT and compliance keep a list showing each tool's allowed data class (see [Data classification](data-classification-for-eri.md)). Unlisted tools may be used with **public or synthetic data only**.
3. **Data rules:**
   - Never enter SSNs, Medicaid IDs, diagnoses, SUD information, IEP content or DVR case data into a consumer AI product (free or personal accounts).
   - For confidential data, use only an approved enterprise tool with a BAA or data agreement, with retention settings checked and the covered features confirmed.
   - Program consents apply on top: DVR AI consent, 42 CFR Part 2, Wis. Stat. 51.30 and FERPA redisclosure limits.
4. **Consent and transparency.** Record DVR consumer AI consent (date, method, staff member). Tell participants when AI helped produce something that affects them. Never present AI output as a human's words.
5. **Human review.** A qualified staff member checks every AI-assisted output for accuracy, tone and privacy before use. **Prohibited uses of AI:**
   - writing or "completing" service notes used for billing
   - choosing billing codes
   - making eligibility or benefits determinations
   - giving individualized benefits or legal advice without a WIPA or CWIC-certified reviewer
6. **Bias and fairness.** Before using AI in matching, screening, prioritizing or assessing people:
   - **Map** the use and who could be harmed (for example, disability, race, age).
   - **Measure** outcomes by group on test data.
   - **Manage** by fixing or dropping the use.
   - Document all of this. Do not use AI to infer disability, diagnosis or SUD status.
7. **Accessibility.** AI-generated content must meet WCAG 2.1 AA or better ([web accessibility](web-accessibility-law-and-standards.md)).
8. **Security.** Use SSO and MFA on approved tools. Do not put credentials in prompts. Report incidents to the privacy lead immediately (DVR's deadline is 24 hours).
9. **Governance.** The compliance contact keeps an AI use register (tool, purpose, data class, owner, review date) and reviews the policy every year.

## Caveats and gotchas
- A BAA covers only the named products and features. Turning on a connector, plugin or file feature can take data outside the BAA (see the Anthropic exclusions above).
- Whether DVR's AI consent rule covers synthetic or de-identified data was not addressed on the DVR pages **(verify with DVR)**.
- Vendor terms change often. The pages above showed "updated" dates of 2025 and 2026 **(recheck before procurement)**.
- HHS has issued other AI-related guidance and strategies. Only 45 CFR 92.210 was opened for this page **(verify any further HHS AI guidance)**.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. Which data classes may go into which enterprise AI tools?
  2. Does ERI's CCS or Dane County contract restrict AI or offshore processing?
  3. Do ERI's WIPA and EN terms restrict AI use with SSA-derived data?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon rules:** synthetic data only. Label demo personas "FICTIONAL." Do not paste real emails, case notes or forms, even redacted ones. Show a human-review step in every demo.
- **Build in:** consent gates, data-class tags on inputs, logging of prompts and outputs (with no PHI in logs), and a visible "AI-assisted" label.
- **A tool must NOT:** send data to an AI service that has no confirmed BAA or data agreement for that data class. It must not make automated decisions about people's services. It must not train or fine-tune models on participant data.

    accessed: 2026-10-23

    url: https://wilawlibrary.gov/jury/files/criminal/1870.pdf
    accessed: 2026-10-23
  - title: 2013 Wisconsin Act 226 (renumbering MA fraud provisions)
    url: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/2013/related/acts/226/28
    accessed: 2026-10-23
  - title: Wisconsin DHS P-02877, Fraud, Waste, and Abuse in Wisconsin Medicaid (01/2021)
    url: https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/publications/p02877.pdf
    accessed: 2026-10-23
  - title: Wisconsin DHS P-02790, Provider Self-Audits
    url: https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/publications/p02790.pdf
    accessed: 2026-10-23

# Billing integrity and false claims

## TL;DR
- The federal **False Claims Act** (31 U.S.C. 3729-3733) makes anyone who *knowingly* submits, or causes someone to submit, a false claim liable for **3x damages plus a per-claim penalty**. The penalty is **$14,308 to $28,619 per claim** for penalties assessed after 2025-07-03. "Knowingly" includes **reckless disregard and deliberate ignorance**, and no intent to defraud is needed. Whistleblowers (qui tam relators) can sue and share in the recovery.
- In Wisconsin, criminal Medical Assistance fraud moved from Wis. Stat. 49.49 to **Wis. Stat. 946.91** under 2013 Wisconsin Act 226 (effective 2014-04-10, per the jury instruction). Intentionally making a false statement of material fact in a Medicaid claim is the core offense. Many of these offenses are **Class H felonies**.
- Medicaid overpayments must be **reported and returned within 60 days** of identification, even if they came from an innocent error (OIG GCPG). Wisconsin DHS OIG accepts **provider self-audits**.
- A billing-completeness tool may help ERI **bill everything it delivered and documented**. It must never help ERI bill for anything it *didn't* deliver and document. Human review and an audit trail are required.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| FCA liability | Knowingly presenting a false claim, using a false record material to a claim, conspiracy, or reverse false claims | 31 USC 3729; DOJ |
| "Knowing" | Actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance or reckless disregard. No specific intent required | OIG GCPG II.C |
| FCA penalty | $14,308 to $28,619 per claim (assessed after 2025-07-03), plus 3x damages | 28 CFR 85.5 |
| FCA recoveries | More than $2.9 billion in FY2024 (DOJ, all sectors) | DOJ |
| 60-day rule | Report and repay identified overpayments within 60 days | OIG GCPG II.C |
| WI MA fraud (criminal) | Intentionally making a false statement of material fact in an MA claim, knowing it is false. Payment need not be received | Wis. Stat. 946.91(2)(a); JI-1870 |
| WI renumbering | 49.49 mostly renumbered to 946.91; many offenses Class H felonies with fines up to $25,000 | 2013 Wis. Act 226 |
| WI fraud examples | Billing for services not rendered, **upcoding**, forging or altering documents, kickbacks | DHS P-02877 |
| WI hotline | 877-865-3432 or reportfraud.wisconsin.gov (anonymous allowed) | DHS P-02877 |
| WI self-audit | Choose claims and scope, check each against rules, document the method, return overpayments. Self-audited claims are excluded from later OIG audits | DHS P-02790 |
| CCS documentation | Corrections take effect from the date made and must be dated and explained. No backdating | DHS CCS page |
| DVR invoicing | Within 60 days. Signed certification that the amount "accurately represents hours expended and/or deliverables that were completed," is from the last 60 days (or the PO timeframe) and is unpaid. No double-billing | DVR Agreement 9.3.1-9.3.2 |
| DVR backup | Timecards and payroll on request within 15 business days. DVR may withhold payment during a discrepancy | DVR Agreement 9.3.3, 9.3.7 |
| DVR authorization | No PO, no pay. Services outside the PO dates or scope are not paid | DVR vendor page |
| OIG GCPG | Published 2023-11-06. Voluntary, nonbinding | OIG |

## How it works
**What "upcoding" means.** Upcoding is billing for a more expensive service, code, unit count or rate than the one actually delivered and documented. Examples: billing a longer session than happened, or billing a higher milestone than was reached. (This is a working definition. DHS lists upcoding as fraud without defining it.) Related errors include **unbundling** (splitting one service to bill more), **duplicate billing** and **billing undocumented time**.

**OIG's seven elements (GCPG, 2023):**
1. Written policies and procedures
2. Compliance leadership and oversight
3. Training and education
4. Effective lines of communication and disclosure programs
5. Enforcing standards: consequences and incentives
6. Risk assessment, auditing and monitoring
7. Responding to detected offenses and corrective action

**Small entities (GCPG IV.A).** A small organization may name a **compliance contact** instead of a full compliance officer. Where possible, that person should not do billing or coding, and should not provide legal services. The contact reports at least **quarterly** to the CEO, who is ultimately responsible. Templates and training may come from consultants or associations, but they must be tailored to the organization. Routine monitoring includes **monthly screening against the LEIE and state Medicaid exclusion lists**, plus licensure checks.

## Caveats and gotchas
- Whether DVR fee-for-service invoices, which are paid with federal VR grant funds, are "claims" under the FCA is a legal question. Assume federal-funds billing carries FCA risk **(verify with counsel)**.
- The current text of Wis. Stat. 49.49 and 946.91 could not be opened (blocked to automated reading). Penalty details come from the Act 226 summary and the jury instruction **(verify)**. Whether Wisconsin still has a civil Medicaid false-claims statute with qui tam (formerly 20.931) was not confirmed **(verify)**.
- A tool that *suggests* billable items creates risk. If people accept suggestions without checking them against documentation, ERI may be acting with "reckless disregard."
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. Does ERI have a compliance contact or officer, a written plan, and monthly exclusion screening?
  2. How does ERI find and return overpayments within 60 days?
  3. What do Dane County's CCS contract and DVR audits require for documentation before billing?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
**A compliant billing-completeness tool:**
1. **Source of truth is the service record.** The tool compares *documented, signed, dated* service entries against authorizations (DVR PO, CCS service plan) and invoices already submitted.
2. **It finds gaps both ways.** It flags documented services that were not billed (missed revenue). It also flags billed items with no documentation, which are possible overpayments to return.
3. **It never creates a billable item.** It cannot write or "complete" notes, back-fill times, or pick a higher code or milestone. Missing documentation goes back to the staff member who delivered the service, and late entries are labeled as late.
4. **A human makes every decision.** A named reviewer approves each flagged item. Invoice certification stays a human signature.
5. **Audit trail.** The tool logs who reviewed what, the rule that fired, the decision, and timestamps. History is append-only.
6. **Built-in checks:** PO date windows, the 60-day DVR invoice limit, duplicates across invoices, units capped at time documented, and staff exclusion status.
7. **Reporting:** a monthly compliance summary to the compliance contact, and an overpayment queue with a 60-day countdown.

**A tool must NOT:**
- Optimize for revenue by suggesting higher codes or milestones.
- Auto-submit claims or invoices.
- Edit or backdate notes.
- Hide flagged overpayments.
- Use AI to generate service documentation after the fact.

**Hackathon:** use synthetic service logs and fake POs. Demo the overpayment flag as prominently as the missed-revenue flag.

# Data classification for ERI

## TL;DR
- ERI's data falls into four classes. Some records carry rules from several programs at once. **Always apply the strictest rule that touches a record.**
- **At the hackathon, every class except Public is synthetic only.** No real participant data goes into any repo, demo, prompt or screenshot.
- **Production** needs four things for any Restricted or Confidential data: an approved system, a BAA or data agreement where required, consent tracking, and access logging.

## Key facts: classes
| Class | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **R: Restricted** | A program-specific federal or state rule plus breach exposure. Harm if leaked is severe | SUD records, CCS clinical records, SSNs, SSA system data, IEPs |
| **C: Confidential** | Personal data under contract or statute | DVR case data, benefits amounts, employment history, billing |
| **I: Internal** | Non-personal business data | Fee schedules, staffing plans, aggregate counts (n of 11 or more) |
| **P: Public** | Already published | Program descriptions, public rules, this wiki |

## Key facts: data types
| Data type | Likely source | Governing rule(s) | Class | Hackathon | Production needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUD diagnosis or treatment info | CCS, referrals | 42 CFR Part 2; Wis. Stat. 51.30; HIPAA | R | Synthetic only | Part 2 consent tracking, `part2` flag, role limits, QSO or BAA with vendors, separate counseling notes |
| Mental health diagnoses, CCS notes and plans | CCS (Dane County) | HIPAA (as CE or BA, see [page](hipaa-and-ccs.md)); Wis. Stat. 51.30; DHS 36 | R | Synthetic only | BAA-covered host, minimum-necessary roles, append-only edits, audit log |
| CCS billing and service units | CCS | HIPAA; Medicaid rules; FCA and Wis. Stat. 946.91 | R | Synthetic only | Reconciliation against signed documentation, human approval, 60-day overpayment queue |
| SSNs | All programs | Wis. Stat. 134.98; SSA rules; HIPAA identifier | R | Fake 9XX numbers only | Encrypted at rest, masked in UI, never in logs or AI prompts |
| SSA records (benefit amounts, BPQY, Ticket status) | WIPA, EN, SSA-3288 | SSA award or agreement terms; Privacy Act (SSA side); SSA-3288 scope | R/C | Synthetic only | Suitability-cleared staff, consent expiration tracking, encrypted transfer, incident reporting within 1 hour **(verify)** |
| Ticket Portal and SSA system access | EN, WIPA | SSA suitability, extra-security accounts | R | Never | Named accounts only, SSA-approved equipment |
| DVR case data (IRIS number, plans, reports) | DVR | 34 CFR 361.38; DVR Agreement 7.1, 7.3, Att. A | C | Synthetic only | US hosting, full-disk encryption, consumer consent for any AI, 3-year retention then destroy, 24-hour incident notice |
| DVR invoices and POs | DVR | DVR Agreement 9.3; FCA risk **(verify)** | C | Fake POs | 60-day window, certification signed by a human, backup within 15 business days |
| IEPs, evaluations, school referrals | Schools, youth transition | FERPA redisclosure (34 CFR 99.33); IDEA 300.622; Wis. Stat. 118.125 | R | Synthetic only | Consent by the right signer, age-18 re-consent, purpose limits, no forwarding |
| CLTS waiver youth data | County CLTS | Medicaid HCBS; HIPAA or 51.30 as applicable **(verify)** | R | Synthetic only | Same as CCS until counsel decides otherwise |
| Employer contacts and job placements | All employment programs | DVR or SSA consent before disclosing disability status | C | Fake employers | Consent before sharing any participant information with an employer |
| Financial account and card numbers | Payroll, donors | Wis. Stat. 134.98; PCI DSS (industry) | R | Test numbers | Tokenized, never stored in plain text |
| Staff background checks | DVR, SSA | DVR Agreement; SSA suitability | C | None | HR system only |
| University and DHS LMS learner data | Web and LMS contracts | Contract; possibly FERPA "school official" role **(verify)** | C | Synthetic only | Contract-specified hosting and accessibility |
| Aggregated outcomes (n of 11 or more) | Reporting | Program small-cell rules **(verify threshold)** | I | OK if synthetic | Small-cell suppression |

## How it works
1. **Tag at intake.** Every field or document gets a class and a list of rule sources (e.g., `["part2","51.30","hipaa"]`).
2. **The highest class wins.** A DVR report that mentions SUD treatment is Restricted under Part 2, not just Confidential.
3. **Consent is per rule.** Each rule has its own consent: Part 2 consent, 51.30 consent, SSA-3288, FERPA or IDEA consent, DVR written consent, DVR AI consent. One signature rarely covers everything.
4. **Retention follows the longest legal or contract rule.** Destroy securely after that (DVR: 3 years after final payment). SSA requires NIST SP 800-88 disposal.

## Caveats and gotchas
- This table covers *likely* data types. ERI should check it against an actual data inventory **(verify)**.
- Synthetic data must not be derived from real records by swapping names, because indirect identifiers can remain. Generate it from scratch.
- The n of 11 or more small-cell threshold is a common convention, not a rule confirmed for ERI's funders **(verify)**.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:** Is this classification correct for ERI's CCS and CLTS roles? Which systems are approved for each class?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Put a `data_class` and a `rules[]` tag on every data model in hackathon code. Reject non-synthetic input in demo mode.
- Use a shared synthetic dataset with obviously fake markers: "FICTIONAL" names, 9XX SSNs, `TEST-` IRIS numbers.
- **A tool must NOT:** mix classes in one export without the stricter controls. It must not log Restricted fields. It must not send any R or C data to unapproved AI or cloud services.

# FERPA and youth records

## TL;DR
- FERPA binds **schools**, not ERI directly. When a school discloses education records to ERI, though, FERPA's **redisclosure limit** (34 CFR 99.33) travels with them: ERI may use them only for the purpose they were given for, and may not pass them on without consent.
- IDEA sets a key rule for transition. Before a school releases personally identifiable information to an agency **providing or paying for transition services** (such as DVR or a vendor like ERI), it needs **consent from the parent, or from the student once they reach the age of majority** (34 CFR 300.622(b)(2)). The same consent is needed to invite that agency to the IEP meeting (300.321(b)(3)).
- In Wisconsin, rights **transfer to the student at 18** unless a court has found the student incompetent. The school notifies the student and parents (DPI form M-7). FERPA rights also transfer at 18 (34 CFR 99.5).
- Wisconsin pupil-records law (Wis. Stat. 118.125) makes all pupil records confidential and lets the person authorizing a release choose **which behavioral records** go out.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Education records | Records directly related to a student and kept by the school or someone acting for it. Excludes sole-possession notes, law enforcement unit records, and treatment records of students 18 or older | 34 CFR 99.3 |
| PII | Direct identifiers (name, family names, address, SSN, student ID) plus indirect ones (date and place of birth) and anything that identifies the student "with reasonable certainty" | 34 CFR 99.3 |
| Eligible student | 18 or older, or attending a postsecondary institution | 34 CFR 99.3 |
| Transfer of FERPA rights | Parents' rights pass to the eligible student | 34 CFR 99.5 |
| Written consent | Signed and dated. Specifies the records, purpose and recipients. Electronic consent is OK if it authenticates the signer | 34 CFR 99.30 |
| Redisclosure | Recipients may not redisclose without consent and may use the records only for the stated purpose | 34 CFR 99.33 |
| Disclosure log | Schools record each request and disclosure | 34 CFR 99.32 |
| Transition consent | Consent from the parent, or the student at the age of majority, before PII goes to agencies providing or paying for transition services | 34 CFR 300.622(b)(2) |
| IEP invitation | With consent, invite agencies likely to provide or pay for transition services | 34 CFR 300.321(b)(3) |
| Age-of-majority notice | The IEP must state, at least **1 year before** the age of majority, that the student was told about rights that will transfer | 34 CFR 300.320(c) |
| Wisconsin age of majority | 18, unless the student has been adjudicated incompetent. The LEA notifies student and parents (form M-7) | DPI M-7 guide; Wis. Stat. 115.807 **(verify text)** |
| Wisconsin pupil records | All confidential. Behavioral records (psych tests, evaluations, conversation records) vs. progress records (grades, attendance) | Wis. Stat. 118.125 |
| Adult pupil and parents | A school may share an adult pupil's records with a parent if the pupil is the parent's tax dependent, unless the pupil objects in writing | Wis. Stat. 118.125 |

## How it works
1. **Referral from a school.** A school may share IEP or evaluation data with ERI only with consent that names ERI (or a class of recipients), the records and the purpose. For transition services, that consent comes from the parent (student under 18) or from the student (18 or older, not adjudicated incompetent).
2. **Once ERI has the records.** They are no longer "education records" in ERI's hands. ERI is still bound by the redisclosure condition the school must attach. If DVR or a CLTS waiver agency also needs them, ERI needs a **new consent** or must have the school disclose directly.
3. **At 18.** The student signs their own consents from then on. Parents keep no automatic access to ERI's files. A guardian appointed by a court, or a supported decision-making agreement under Wis. Stat. ch. 52, changes who signs or who helps **(verify the specifics with counsel)**.
4. **ERI's own records** about youth (job coaching notes, DVR reports) are not FERPA records. They are governed by DVR rules (see [VR confidentiality](vr-confidentiality-34-cfr-361-38.md)), by HIPAA or 51.30 if clinical, and by ERI's contracts.

## Caveats and gotchas
- People often assume "the parent signed at 16, so we're fine." Consent given by a parent **before** the transfer of rights may need to be re-obtained from the student at 18. Ask counsel how to treat ongoing consents **(verify)**.
- The text of Wis. Stat. 115.807 could not be opened (the site blocked automated reading). The age-18 rule here comes from DPI's M-7 guide.
- University LMS and web contracts may involve FERPA "school official" status, where the contractor acts for the institution under 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1). That is a contract question for counsel, and different from the youth-services question.
- School-based health or psychological records may be covered by HIPAA or Wis. Stat. 146.81-84 rather than FERPA in some settings **(verify)**.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. Do ERI's school referral forms meet 34 CFR 99.30 and 300.622, and do they name every downstream recipient (DVR, county, CLTS)?
  2. How does ERI re-consent at the age of majority?
  3. Do ERI's contracts with universities make ERI a "school official" with FERPA duties?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** synthetic students only. Do not upload real IEPs, even redacted ones, because indirect identifiers can re-identify a student "with reasonable certainty."
- **Production:**
  - Track `consent_signer` (parent, student or guardian), `student_dob` and an **age-18 alert** 90 days ahead to prompt re-consent.
  - Store the source and purpose limits of school records, and block forwarding them to recipients outside the consent.
  - Separate behavioral records from progress records.
- **A tool must NOT:** auto-share IEP content with employers or DVR without a matching consent. It must not keep sending parents information after 18 without the student's consent. It must not use IEP disability details in job-matching models without review (see [AI use policy](ai-use-policy-for-nonprofits.md)).

- [IDEA regulations, 34 CFR 300.321(b)](https://sites.ed.gov/idea/regs/b/d/300.321/b)

- [Wis. Stat. 118.125 Pupil records](https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/118/125)
- [Wisconsin DPI, Sample Form Guide M-7](https://dpi.wi.gov/sped/laws-procedures-bulletins/procedures/sample/forms-guide-m-7)

# HIPAA and ERI's CCS work

## TL;DR
- HIPAA reaches a **health care provider** only if it **transmits health information electronically in connection with a standard transaction** (for example, a claim). An organization that "furnishes, bills, or is paid for health care" is a provider. Whether ERI is a covered entity depends on **who submits the CCS claims and how**. That is a question for ERI's counsel/compliance, not something this page can settle.
- In Wisconsin, CCS is a **county-run, state-certified program** (Wis. Admin. Code ch. DHS 36) that bills Medicaid. A contracted agency like ERI is most likely either (a) a business associate of Dane County, (b) a provider receiving PHI for treatment, or (c) a covered entity in its own right if it bills electronically. **Treat all CCS data as PHI** whichever answer applies.
- Wisconsin's mental health records law (Wis. Stat. 51.30) applies to CCS treatment records **whatever ERI's HIPAA status**. It requires informed written consent for most releases.
- Any tool that stores CCS data in a cloud service needs a **BAA with that vendor**. HHS says this holds even when the vendor only stores encrypted data and has no key.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Covered entity (provider) | A provider who transmits health information electronically in connection with a covered transaction | 45 CFR 160.103 |
| Health care provider | Any person or organization that "furnishes, bills, or is paid for health care in the normal course of business" | 45 CFR 160.103 |
| Business associate | A person who creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on behalf of a covered entity. Subcontractors of a BA are BAs too | 45 CFR 160.103 |
| Workforce | Employees, volunteers and trainees under the entity's direct control, paid or not | 45 CFR 160.103 |
| Minimum necessary | Limit uses, disclosures and requests to the minimum needed. Does not apply to disclosures for treatment, disclosures to the individual, or uses under an authorization | 45 CFR 164.502(b), 164.514(d) |
| BAA contents | 10 required elements, including safeguards, breach reporting, subcontractor flow-down, and return or destruction at termination | 45 CFR 164.502(e), 164.504(e), 164.308(b) |
| Breach presumption | An impermissible use or disclosure is presumed to be a breach unless a 4-factor risk assessment shows a low probability of compromise | 45 CFR 164.402 |
| Notice to individuals | Without unreasonable delay, **no later than 60 days** after discovery | 45 CFR 164.404 |
| Notice to media | If **more than 500** residents of a state are affected | 45 CFR 164.406 |
| Notice to HHS | 500 or more affected: within 60 days. Fewer than 500: annual log, due within 60 days after calendar year-end | 45 CFR 164.408 |
| BA to covered entity | No later than 60 days after discovery (a BAA can set a shorter deadline) | 45 CFR 164.410 |
| "Secured" PHI | PHI that is encrypted or destroyed per HHS guidance. Only unsecured PHI triggers notification | HHS breach guidance |
| De-identification | Safe Harbor (remove 18 identifiers, with no actual knowledge of re-identification) or Expert Determination | 45 CFR 164.514(b) |
| Wisconsin treatment records | Confidential. Release needs informed written consent, except in listed situations | Wis. Stat. 51.30(4)(a), (2), (4)(b) |

## How it works
**Step 1: Is ERI a covered entity?** The test is about conduct, not organization type. ERI delivers psychosocial rehabilitation, so it is a "health care provider." It becomes a *covered entity* only if it (or a billing agent working for it) sends standard electronic transactions such as 837 claims or eligibility checks. DHS describes CCS as a program that counties and tribes run and DQA certifies. The county program may contract with providers, and the contracted provider must share service documentation for the CCS file. If Dane County submits the Medicaid claims and pays ERI under a contract, ERI may not be a covered entity for that work. If ERI submits claims itself, it likely is.

**Step 2: If not covered, is ERI a business associate?** If ERI creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI "on behalf of" the county CCS program (documentation, service logs, billing data), it is likely a business associate. Counties often require a BAA from contracted agencies either way. ERI should check its Dane County contract **(verify)**.

**Step 3: Wisconsin law applies either way.** Wis. Stat. 51.30 makes treatment records for mental illness, developmental disabilities, alcoholism or drug dependence confidential. A valid consent must be in writing and name the recipient, the subject, the purpose, the specific information, the effective period and the signing date, and carry a signature. Exceptions without consent include billing and collection, audits and program evaluation, and coordination within county departments. For SUD records, see [42 CFR Part 2](42-cfr-part-2.md).

**Minimum necessary in practice.** Policies must name who in the organization needs access, which categories of PHI each role needs, and on what conditions. Routine disclosures can follow standard protocols. Non-routine ones need individual review. A job developer usually does not need a participant's full diagnosis history.

**BAAs.** Every vendor that stores or processes CCS data for ERI needs a BAA. Cloud vendors are not "conduits," because the conduit exception covers transmission-only services. If ERI is itself a BA, its subcontractors need BAAs that flow down the same terms.

**Breach.** HIPAA has a 60-day outer limit for notice to individuals. BAAs and county contracts may require faster reporting to the county **(verify ERI's contract)**.

## Caveats and gotchas
- "We don't bill Medicaid directly" does not mean "HIPAA doesn't apply." BA status, the county contract and Wis. Stat. 51.30 can each impose obligations. This page does not decide ERI's status. Bring these **questions to ERI's counsel/compliance**:
  1. Who submits CCS claims to ForwardHealth for services ERI delivers: ERI, a billing vendor, or Dane County?
  2. Does ERI's Dane County CCS contract include a BAA, and what is its breach-reporting deadline?
  3. Does ERI conduct any other HIPAA standard transaction electronically, for any program?
  4. Which ERI systems (EHR, email, file share, AI tools) hold CCS data, and does each vendor have a signed BAA?
- Encryption makes PHI "secured" for breach purposes. It does **not** remove the need for a BAA, and it does not by itself satisfy the Security Rule.
- DHS says CCS documentation errors cannot be fixed retroactively. Corrections take effect on the date they are made and must be dated and explained, and backdating is improper. Tools must keep an edit history.
- HHS proposed changes to the HIPAA Security Rule in 2025. Their final status was not confirmed for this page **(verify)**.
- Wisconsin's patient health care records statute (Wis. Stat. 146.81-146.84) may also apply. It was not opened for this page **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** use **synthetic data only**. Do not put real or "lightly scrubbed" CCS records into any tool, demo or prompt. Data counts as de-identified only if it meets Safe Harbor (all 18 identifiers removed, including dates more specific than the year and ZIP codes beyond the first 3 digits) or has an Expert Determination.
- **Production design requirements** for any tool touching CCS data:
  - The hosting vendor has a signed BAA. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
  - Role-based access maps to the minimum-necessary policy, so job developers see employment-relevant fields only.
  - Audit logs record who viewed or changed what, and when.
  - Edits are append-only, with no overwriting of past entries (this matches the DHS correction rule).
  - A consent-tracking field records 51.30 and Part 2 consents with their expiration dates.
  - A breach-response hook tells the privacy lead the same day.
- **A tool must NOT:** send CCS data to consumer AI chat tools, personal email or unapproved cloud storage. It must not export bulk PHI to spreadsheets without a logged purpose. It must not display SUD details to staff who lack a Part 2 need.
