# SSA data, consent forms and Ticket Portal security

## TL;DR
- **SSA-3288** is how a beneficiary lets SSA release their records to ERI, for example benefit amounts or a BPQY-type summary.
  - The current edition is **04-2026** (OMB 0960-0566).
  - It is good for **one-time use** unless the form says otherwise, and lasts **1 year** from signing. Requests for medical records expire after **90 days**.
  - SSA rejects "any and all records" requests.
- **SSA-827** authorizes medical sources to send records **to SSA**. It is valid for **12 months**. It is written to meet HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2.
- Ticket to Work Employment Network (EN) staff who handle Ticketholder PII must pass **SSA suitability**. Ticket Portal users need a **my Social Security account with extra security**.
- WIPA staff use SSA-issued equipment and SSA's data system. Their award terms carry SSA data-security rules. Those terms are not fully public, so treat SSA's contractor rules (FIPS 140-2 encryption, report incidents **within 1 hour**, US-only storage) as the likely baseline **(verify against ERI's actual WIPA award)**.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| SSA-3288 edition | 04-2026, "Discontinue Prior Editions," OMB 0960-0566 | SSA-3288 |
| What 3288 can release | SSN verification, current SSDI or SSI amounts, amounts for a date range, Medicare entitlement, medical records (date range or complete), other named records | SSA-3288 |
| 3288 validity | One-time use unless specified. 1 year from signature. 90 days for medical records | SSA-3288 |
| 3288 minors | A parent or guardian may release only a minor's **non-medical** records, and must explain the best interest | SSA-3288; POMS GN 03305.005 |
| Minors consenting | A minor may consent to their own records if able to decide; age 12 is the baseline, judged case by case | POMS GN 03305.005 |
| Guardians of incompetent adults | Paper only, wet signature, proof of guardianship | POMS GN 03305.005 |
| Electronic consent | Accepted only on SSA-3288-OP1 through SSA's website | POMS GN 03305.005 |
| SSA-827 validity | 12 months from signature. Revocable in writing | SSA-827 page |
| SSA-827 scope | Covers SUD, mental health (not psychotherapy notes), HIV and genetic information. SSA says it won't redisclose SUD information without Part 2 consent | SSA-827 page |
| EN suitability | Required for anyone accessing SSA systems or information. Paperwork goes in 30 business days before work starts. Report an arrest or status change within 1 business day | EN Security and Suitability Guide |
| EN PII | ENs must have "secure systems in place to protect the confidentiality of PII." Staff handling Ticketholder PII need a favorable suitability determination | EN qualifications page |
| EN insurance | At least $500,000 per occurrence | EN qualifications page |
| EN accessibility | ADA-compliant locations and **Section 508-compliant** electronic information | EN qualifications page |
| Sending documents to SSA (EN) | SSA or partner email, GSO account, or a password-protected encrypted attachment | EN Security and Suitability Guide |
| Ticket Portal | Suitability, plus a my Social Security account with extra security | Ticket Portal page |
| WIPA equipment (2013 terms) | Government-issued laptops with two-factor sign-in to the data system (ETO at the time). No thumb drives, no extra software. Destroy beneficiary information at the end of the award | WIPA FAQ |
| SSA contractor baseline | FIPS 140-2 encryption in transit and at rest. Report incidents **≤1 hour** after discovery. US-only storage. NIST SP 800-88 disposal. Confidential information goes only in encrypted attachments from non-SSA email | SSA InfoSec clause |

## How it works
1. **Getting benefit data for WIPA or EN work.** The beneficiary signs an SSA-3288 naming ERI and the specific record types, for example "current monthly SSI payment." Check each box separately and give date ranges. Staff with SSA system access follow their award's rules instead.
2. **Within ERI.** SSA-derived records (benefit amounts, SSN verification, Ticket assignment status) are PII under SSA's rules and under ERI's agreements. They are also often linked to health data.
3. **Ticket Portal.** Only suitability-cleared staff, each with their own extra-security account, may access it. Credentials are never shared.
4. **Sending to SSA.** Use the portal or GSO, or an encrypted attachment with a password sent separately. Never put PII in an email body from ERI's own email system.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The WIPA FAQ opened here is from the **2013** competition. Current WIPA cooperative agreement terms, the data system and the PII rules may differ. The "SSA Information Security and General Privacy Requirements" document is an **acquisition (contract) clause**, and whether it applies word for word to WIPA cooperative agreements is unconfirmed **(verify)**.
- Whether WIPA staff still use SSA-issued laptops and which data system is current were not confirmed **(verify)**.
- Rules on Ticket Portal session limits and credential sharing were not found on the pages opened **(verify the Ticket Program Agreement)**.
- A 3288 from a parent cannot cover a minor's medical records, so youth benefits work needs another route.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. What PII, incident-reporting and equipment terms are in ERI's current WIPA award and Ticket Program Agreement?
  2. Is the 1-hour reporting rule in ERI's WIPA terms, and who reports?
  3. May WIPA-derived benefits data be shared with ERI's DVR or CCS teams, and under what consent?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** use synthetic beneficiaries with fake SSNs from the never-issued 900-999 range (for example 9XX-XX-XXXX), and fake benefit amounts. Do not connect to SSA systems or the Ticket Portal, and do not screen-scrape them.
- **Production:**
  - Store SSA-3288 metadata (record types, date range, expiration) and block use after it expires.
  - Mask SSNs everywhere by default.
  - Keep any SSA-system work on SSA-approved equipment only.
  - Encrypt exports to FIPS 140-2 validated standards **(verify the requirement)**.
  - Route incidents to the privacy lead immediately so the 1-hour clock can be met.
- **A tool must NOT:** hold or use Ticket Portal or SSA credentials. It must not send SSA-derived data to AI tools without a confirmed legal basis. It must not use benefits data for purposes the beneficiary didn't consent to.

- [POMS GN 03305.005 Who May Consent](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/POMS.NSF/lnx/0203305005)

# VR confidentiality and Wisconsin DVR vendor rules

## TL;DR
- 34 CFR 361.38 binds the **state VR agency** (Wisconsin DVR). DVR may share personal information with service providers only if they **agree not to pass it on** further. DVR passes these duties to vendors through its **Service Provider Agreement**.
- The agreement (section 7.3) bars ERI from releasing any DVR consumer's personal information **without the consumer's prior written consent**. It also says the confidentiality and IT security standards **apply to AI**.
- **Attachment A, item l:** "The use of any AI tool requires the prior written or verbal consent of the DVR consumer." This is the most important rule for hackathon tools.
- Other key terms:
  - Report security incidents to DVR **in writing within 24 hours**.
  - Keep records for **3 years after final payment**, then destroy PII.
  - Store consumer data **in the United States**.
  - Use full-disk encryption and only authorized business email accounts.
  - Invoice within **60 days**, with a signed accuracy certification.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| State unit policies | Written confidentiality policies for all personal information, including photos and name lists. Data released only under a written agreement | 34 CFR 361.38(a)(1) |
| Use limit | Use only for purposes directly connected with administering the VR program | 361.38(b) |
| Service providers | DVR may get information from providers who agree not to redisclose except as (c)-(e) allow | 361.38(b) |
| Harmful medical or psych information | Released through a third party the person chooses, not directly | 361.38(c)(2) |
| Audit and research | Only under a written agreement with 5 conditions, and no PII in the final product without consent | 361.38(d) |
| Release to other programs | With informed written consent and a written agreement, limited to what the recipient needs | 361.38(e)(1) |
| Provider confidentiality | No release without the consumer's prior written consent. Report unauthorized disclosures immediately. Duty survives termination | Agreement 7.3 |
| AI | Confidentiality and IT security standards apply to AI. **Any AI tool needs prior written or verbal consumer consent.** AI-held records follow 7.1 and 7.3 | Agreement 7.1, 7.3; Att. A (l), (m) |
| Incident notice | To DVR in writing **within 24 hours**, including any police report | Agreement 7.1 |
| Cyber controls | Full-disk encryption; encryption and security apps on mobile devices; weekly backups; passwords of 8+ characters changed every 90 days; auto-lock (e.g., 5 minutes); authorized business email only | Agreement Att. A (e, g, h, n, p) |
| IT updates | 90 days from notice to meet updated security requirements | Agreement 7.1 |
| Data location | All DVR consumer case data stored in the U.S. | RFA 4.1.3 |
| Retention | 3 years after final payment on a case, then destroy PII "immediately" | Agreement 3.7, 7.1 |
| Audit rights | DVR may inspect during the term and up to 3 years after | Agreement 6.3 |
| Documentation on request | Within 15 business days | Agreement 9.3.3 |
| Invoicing | Within 60 days after service. Signed certification that the amount "accurately represents hours expended" and was not already paid | Agreement 9.3.1, 9.3.2 |
| Authorization first | No purchase order (authorization), no pay. Services outside the PO dates are not paid | Vendor info page |
| Report transmission | Upload in the Service Provider Portal (preferred), then URL upload, fax or email | Scanning methods page |
| Monthly SE reports | Generally due within 5 business days after month-end | SE tech spec |
| Background checks | Once per agreement cycle. Notify DVR within 2 business days of a new arrest or investigation | 2025 reminders; RFA 4.1.5 |
| Insurance | At least $1,000,000 general liability | RFA 4.3.5 |

## How it works
1. DVR issues an **Authorization for Services** (a purchase order) for each consumer and service. ERI does nothing billable before the PO start date.
2. ERI gets consumer information from DVR under the agreement. ERI may use it only to deliver the authorized service.
3. Sharing with employers, a county, CCS or SSA needs the **consumer's prior written consent**. The SE tech spec also says to get consumer permission before contacting employers.
4. Reports go to DVR through the **Service Provider Portal** where possible. Use the specific DVR form for each service and phase (for example, DVR-18212-E for monthly Systematic Instruction).
5. Each invoice carries the accuracy certification. ERI must be able to produce timecards and other backup within 15 business days if asked.
6. Three years after final payment, ERI destroys the consumer's PII, both electronic and paper, in a way that protects confidentiality.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **AI consent is required even for "internal" tools.** Examples include drafting a DVR report with an AI assistant or transcribing a meeting. The agreement treats verbal consent as valid, but ERI should document it. Ask counsel or DVR whether de-identified or synthetic use needs consent at all **(verify)**.
- The agreement PDF shows no revision date. The SE tech spec refers to the **2026-2028** term beginning **2026-07-01**. Confirm that the PDF opened here is the current-term version **(verify)**.
- The agreement does not explicitly require encrypted email. SSA rules do (see [SSA data and consent](ssa-data-and-consent.md)). Prefer the portal.
- Medicaid-eligible services cannot carry cancellation fees (vendor info page).
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. What does ERI's AI consent script and form say, and where is consent recorded?
  2. Which ERI systems hold DVR data, and are they all US-hosted with full-disk encryption?
  3. Who sends the 24-hour incident notice to DVR?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** synthetic DVR consumers only. A demo that would put *real* DVR data into an AI tool would need documented consent from each consumer, so do not do it.
- **Production:**
  - Add an `ai_consent` field (date, method, staff member) and block AI features for a consumer without it.
  - Check the PO before any billable work.
  - Track report due dates (5 business days after month-end) and the 60-day invoice window.
  - Keep US-only hosting.
  - Run a retention job that flags cases 3 years after final payment for destruction.
- **A tool must NOT:**
  - Run AI on a DVR consumer's data without recorded consent.
  - Generate report content for services that weren't delivered.
  - Auto-submit invoices without human sign-off on the certification.
  - Store DVR data outside the U.S. or in personal email.

# Web accessibility law and standards

## TL;DR
- **ADA Title II web rule** (28 CFR part 35, subpart H; published 2024-04-24). State and local governments must make web content and mobile apps conform to **WCAG 2.1 Level AA**. The standard is 2.1, not 2.2.
- **DOJ moved the deadlines** in an interim final rule effective **2026-04-20**:
  - Governments with 50,000+ residents: **2027-04-26** (was 2026-04-24).
  - Governments under 50,000 and special districts: **2028-04-26** (was 2027-04-26).
- Content a **contractor or vendor posts for a government is not exempt**. ERI's web and LMS work for Wisconsin DHS, counties and UW campuses is therefore inside the rule. Building to WCAG 2.1 AA is a contract-delivery requirement, not an extra.
- **WCAG 2.2** is the current W3C Recommendation (the dated version opened is 2024-12-12). Building to **2.2 AA** covers 2.1 AA except for the removed 4.1.1 Parsing criterion, and is a sensible default.
- **Title III** (private businesses): DOJ's position (2022-03-18 guidance) is that the ADA covers websites. DOJ has not set a technical standard and points to WCAG and Section 508.

## Key facts
| Item | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Title II rule published | 2024-04-24 | ADA.gov web guidance note; FR |
| Title II standard | WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Equivalent alternatives are allowed if they give the same or greater access | ADA.gov fact sheet |
| IFR | 91 FR 20902, effective 2026-04-20, comments were due 2026-06-22 | Federal Register |
| New dates | 50k+: **2027-04-26**. Under 50k and special districts: **2028-04-26** | IFR; ADA.gov |
| Standard changed? | No. The IFR changed only the dates | IFR |
| Reason given | DOJ overestimated what entities could do, given staffing, remediation automation and litigation exposure | IFR |
| Exceptions | Archived content; preexisting conventional documents (unless used to access services); third-party content not posted for the government; password-protected individualized documents | ADA.gov fact sheet |
| Contractors | Content posted by vendors or contractors for a government is covered | ADA.gov fact sheet |
| Title III | ADA applies to businesses' web offerings. No regulatory standard | ADA.gov guidance (2022) |
| WCAG 2.2 | W3C Recommendation, current dated version 2024-12-12. Adds 9 success criteria (6 at A or AA). Removes 4.1.1 Parsing | W3C |
| Section 508 | Federal agencies' ICT. Revised standards (final 2017-01-18, effective 2018-01-18) harmonized with WCAG 2.0. Contractors are reached through FAR 39.2 procurement | Section508.gov |
| SSA EN requirement | ENs must have Section 508-compliant electronic information | Ticket to Work EN page |

**New in WCAG 2.2 at Level A and AA:**
- 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
- 2.5.7 Dragging Movements
- 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
- 3.2.6 Consistent Help
- 3.3.7 Redundant Entry
- 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)

## How it works
- **ERI as a government web vendor.** DHS, Dane County, the City of Madison and UW are Title II entities. When ERI builds or edits their web content, LMS courses or mobile apps, that content must conform by the entity's compliance date. Large entities such as the State of Wisconsin, Dane County and UW campuses fall under the 2027-04-26 date. Expect contracts to require WCAG 2.1 AA (or 2.2 AA), plus conformance reports and remediation warranties.
- **Federal work.** For federal contracts, Section 508 applies through procurement. Agencies ask for an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR), usually based on the VPAT template **(verify the format each agency wants)**.
- **ERI's own site and tools.** As a private nonprofit open to the public, ERI falls under Title III. As an SSA EN, its electronic information must be Section 508-compliant. Recipients of HHS funding are also subject to the 2024 HHS Section 504 rule, which adopted WCAG 2.1 AA. Its compliance dates (originally 2026-05-11 for recipients with 15+ employees) and any 2026 extension were not confirmed **(verify)**.
- **Wisconsin.** A state IT accessibility policy from the Wisconsin Department of Administration (Division of Enterprise Technology) was not located or opened for this page **(verify)**.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The task brief cited April 2026 and April 2027 deadlines. **Those were replaced** by the 2026-04-20 IFR. Because it is an interim final rule, DOJ could still change it after reviewing comments **(watch)**.
- Moving deadlines doesn't lower contractual or litigation risk. Title II and Title III lawsuits rely on the ADA's general obligations whatever the rule's dates.
- PDFs and LMS course files posted after the compliance date are not "preexisting." Documents people still use to apply for services are never exempt.
- Automated checkers catch only part of WCAG. Manual and assistive-technology testing is still needed.
- WCAG 2.2's original Recommendation date of 2023-10-05 is from the brief. The version opened was the 2024-12-12 update **(verify the original date on the W3C history page)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Every hackathon UI should target WCAG 2.2 AA:**
  - keyboard-only operation
  - visible focus that is not obscured
  - targets of at least 24x24 CSS px
  - text contrast of at least 4.5:1
  - labeled form fields
  - no drag-only interactions
  - no cognitive-test logins
  - captions for any video
- ERI's users include people with disabilities, so accessibility is core to the service, not just compliance.
- **Deliverables:** an accessibility statement, a test log (automated checks plus manual keyboard and screen reader testing), and known issues.
- **A tool must NOT:** rely on "accessibility overlay" widgets as a fix. It must not post inaccessible PDFs for government clients. It must not use CAPTCHA without an accessible alternative.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:** What accessibility warranties and indemnities are in ERI's DHS, county and university contracts? Do any name WCAG 2.2 or a date earlier than the rule's?

## Related pages
- [SSA data and consent](ssa-data-and-consent.md)
- [AI use policy](ai-use-policy-for-nonprofits.md)

- [ADA.gov Fact Sheet, Title II web rule](https://www.ada.gov/resources/2024-03-08-web-rule/)

# Wisconsin data breach notification (Wis. Stat. 134.98)

## TL;DR
- Wisconsin's law protects a person's **name** (last name plus first name or initial) **linked to** any one of these elements, unless the element is public, encrypted, redacted or otherwise unreadable:
  - SSN
  - driver's license or state ID number
  - a financial account or card number, with any code or password that gives access
  - a DNA profile
  - biometric data
- An entity that conducts business in Wisconsin and maintains personal information must notify affected people within a **reasonable time, not more than 45 days** after learning of the unauthorized acquisition.
- No notice is needed if the acquisition creates **no material risk of identity theft or fraud**, or if an employee acted in good faith and used the data lawfully.
- 134.98 is **one of several clocks**:
  - HIPAA: 60 days
  - DVR: **24 hours** to DVR in writing
  - SSA contractor rules: **1 hour** to SSA **(verify for ERI's awards)**
  ERI's incident plan must run all of them in parallel.

## Key facts
| Item | Rule | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Entity | A non-individual that conducts business in Wisconsin and maintains personal information in the ordinary course. Also state government. DATCP adds cities, villages, towns and counties | 134.98(1)(a); DATCP |
| Personal information | Name plus SSN, DL or state ID, financial account number with access code, DNA profile, or biometric data | 134.98(1)(b); DATCP |
| Exclusions | Element is publicly available, or encrypted, redacted or altered to be unreadable | 134.98(1)(b) |
| Trigger | The entity knows personal information "has been acquired" by an unauthorized person | 134.98(2) |
| Deadline | Reasonable time, **not to exceed 45 days** after learning of the acquisition | 134.98(3)(a) |
| Method | Mail, or a method previously used with the person | 134.98(3) |
| Service providers | A non-owner storing the data notifies the owner as soon as practicable (unless a contract says otherwise) | 134.98(2)(bm) **(verify paragraph letter)** |
| Credit bureaus | If 1,000 or more people need notice from one incident, notify the nationwide consumer reporting agencies | 134.98(2)(br) **(verify paragraph letter)** |
| No-risk exception | No material risk of identity theft or fraud | 134.98(2)(cm) |
| Law enforcement delay | Police may ask for a delay. The clock starts when the delay ends | 134.98(5) |
| GLBA exemption | Financial institutions compliant with 15 USC 6801-6827 (with a breach policy) | 134.98(3m)(a) |
| Health care exemption | DATCP: "Certain health plans and health care providers are not covered by Wisconsin's law." The exact statutory text (likely HIPAA-compliant covered entities) was not visible **(verify)** | DATCP |
| Private lawsuits | Noncompliance is not negligence by itself but may be evidence of it. The annotation says there is no private right of action (*Fox v. Iowa Health System*, 2019) | 134.98(4) |
| Local laws | Preempted (cities, villages, towns and counties may not enact their own) | 134.98(6m) |

## How it works
1. **Find out what was exposed.** A name plus an SSN or account number triggers 134.98. Diagnoses or case notes alone do not, but they likely trigger HIPAA, 51.30, Part 2, DVR or SSA duties.
2. **Was it encrypted?** Properly encrypted data falls outside the definition. Keep proof of encryption.
3. **Assess the risk.** Document the "material risk of identity theft or fraud" analysis, whatever the conclusion.
4. **Notify within 45 days** by mail. Tell people, on request, what was taken.
5. **1,000 or more people:** also notify the credit bureaus.
6. **Run the other clocks** at the same time: DVR within 24 hours, SSA within 1 hour if applicable, and the county or covered entity under the BAA. For HIPAA, individuals within 60 days, and HHS and media if 500 or more.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The DATCP page says "more than 1,000"; the statute text read here says "1,000 or more." Follow the statute.
- The health-care exemption in sub. (3m) could not be read in full. Even if it covers ERI's CCS work, it would **not** cover ERI's non-health data, such as employee SSNs, donor card numbers or DVR and WIPA data **(verify with counsel)**.
- Contract clocks are much shorter than 45 days. Missing the DVR 24-hour notice is a contract breach even when no individual notice is owed.
- **Questions for ERI's counsel/compliance:**
  1. Is ERI exempt from 134.98 for any category of data under sub. (3m)?
  2. Does ERI's incident-response plan list every clock (DVR, SSA, county BAA, HIPAA, 134.98) and who owns each one?
  3. Does ERI have cyber insurance with breach-response services?

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Hackathon:** never load real SSNs, card numbers or ID numbers. Use 9XX SSNs and test card numbers.
- **Production:**
  - Encrypt every store that holds SSNs or account numbers, so a lost laptop may fall outside "personal information."
  - Log access so the scope of an incident can be measured.
  - Provide an "incident" button that starts the clocks and notifies the privacy lead.
- **A tool must NOT:** keep SSNs in plain text, in logs or in AI prompts. It must not decide by itself that "no notice is required." That is a documented human decision with counsel.

- [SSA data and consent](ssa-data-and-consent.md)
- [Data classification](data-classification-for-eri.md)

## Sources

- [Wisconsin DATCP, Wisconsin's Data Breach Notification Law](https://datcp.wi.gov/Pages/Publications/IDTheftDataBreach607.aspx)
- [Wisconsin DATCP fact sheet (rev 10/23)](https://datcp.wi.gov/Documents/IDTheftDataBreach607.pdf)

# Public data catalog for the ERI hackathon

## TL;DR
- Ten pages catalog the public data a job matcher (PRD 02) or a DVR billing checker (PRD 01) might use, focused on Milwaukee, Dane, Waukesha, Racine, Kenosha and Rock counties.
- **Build on synthetic `data/` first.** Public data *enriches* it: wages, job demands, commute times, accommodation ideas, referral links.
- **PRD 01 needs no public dataset.** Billing rules come from DVR documents (see `wiki/domain/dvr-supported-employment.md`) and the synthetic `data/dvr/` files.
- Run `tools/fetch_public_data.sh` **on your own machine** to download the openly downloadable starter files into `data/public/` (git-ignored by a `.gitignore` the script writes).

## Key facts: the starter kit (top 8, ranked)
| # | Dataset | Why it's in the kit | Access | License | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **O*NET 31.0** (Work Context, Abilities, Occupation Data) | Turns a job title into concrete demands (standing, lifting, noise, public contact), which drives accommodation hints and "why it fits" text. One download, no key | Zip or CSV download | CC BY 4.0 (attribution) | [occupations-and-wages](occupations-and-wages.md) |
| 2 | **MCTS GTFS** (Milwaukee) | The event is in Milwaukee, and "can I get there by bus?" is in the PRD's user stories. Powers commute-time and near-bus checks | Direct zip, no key | MCTS Developer Terms (disclaimer + data dates) | [transit-gtfs](transit-gtfs.md) |
| 3 | **BLS OEWS May 2025** (metro file) | "Typical pay here" next to each posting. Flags low-wage postings for review. Covers Milwaukee-Waukesha, Madison, Racine, Kenosha and Janesville-Beloit | Direct zip (XLSX) | Public domain | [occupations-and-wages](occupations-and-wages.md) |
| 4 | **USAJOBS Search API** (`HiringPath=disability`) | The only open, reusable *live* job feed. Shows real Schedule A federal openings near Milwaukee and Madison | Free key + email header | Open license for Public Data | [jobs-and-postings](jobs-and-postings.md) |
| 5 | **JAN A to Z / SOAR** | Trusted accommodation ideas to link from each match ("ideas to discuss with the employer") | Web links (no API) | JAN works are U.S. government works | [accommodations](accommodations.md) |
| 6 | **Madison Metro GTFS** | ERI is in Madison. Second commute-time city. Feed valid through about 2026-12-05 | Direct zip, no key | City of Madison developer license (rider-assistance use) | [transit-gtfs](transit-gtfs.md) |
| 7 | **Census ACS 2020-2024** (B18140, S1810, S1811, C18120) | County context for a specialist or employer dashboard: disability rate, employment gap, earnings gap | Census API, free key | Census API ToS (disclaimer, no re-identification) | [disability-population](disability-population.md) |
| 8 | **Referral directories** (DVR offices, ADRC contacts, Ticket to Work Find Help / WIPA) | Every benefits or eligibility flag must route to people. These are the official places to send them | Web links + public phone lines | Public information | [services-directories](services-directories.md) |

**Honorable mentions:** SSA county SSI and SSDI counts (outreach maps), WisConomy WDA projections (growing jobs), USAspending (Section 503 contractor list for business development).

## How it works: the catalog
| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [jobs-and-postings.md](jobs-and-postings.md) | USAJOBS API, Job Center of Wisconsin, NLx Research Hub, Wisc.Jobs, city and county boards, Indeed, LinkedIn, Handshake (no scraping) |
| [occupations-and-wages.md](occupations-and-wages.md) | O*NET database and Web Services, BLS OEWS May 2025 area codes, WisConomy projections by WDA, BLS LAUS, BLS API |
| [accommodations.md](accommodations.md) | JAN SOAR, A to Z, Situations & Solutions, reuse terms, ODEP centers (EARN, PEAT, LEAD) |
| [disability-population.md](disability-population.md) | ACS S1810, S1811, C18120, B18140 via the Census API; Cornell disabilitystatistics.org; SSA SSI and OASDI county tables; SSDI annual report; WRC annual reports |
| [transit-gtfs.md](transit-gtfs.md) | GTFS and GTFS-rt for MCTS, Madison, Racine, Janesville (Waukesha and Kenosha unconfirmed); Mobility Database and Transitland; r5py and OpenTripPlanner |
| [employers-and-contractors.md](employers-and-contractors.md) | Section 503 (7% goal rescinded 2026), OFCCP 2026 status, USAspending and SAM.gov APIs, WEDC, library business databases, WOTC |
| [services-directories.md](services-directories.md) | 211 Wisconsin, ADRCs, DVR offices, Family Care MCOs, IRIS, Ticket to Work Find Help (ENs, WIPA, PABSS), USA.gov Benefit Finder |
| [nonprofit-and-funding-data.md](nonprofit-and-funding-data.md) | ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API, IRS 990 e-file, 990-PF, Candid, Grants.gov extract and Simpler.Grants.gov API, WI DHS and DWD grants |
| [geography.md](geography.md) | TIGER/Line 2026, ZCTA relationship files, HUD USPS crosswalk API, LTSB municipal boundaries, SCO parcels, OpenStreetMap ODbL |

## Caveats and gotchas
- Items marked **(verify)** on each page could not be confirmed from an opened official page on 2026-10-23. Check them before relying on them.
- Feeds expire (Madison GTFS around 2026-12-05, Janesville around 2026-12-10). Data releases land during event week (ACS 2025 1-year is scheduled for 2026-10-29).
- "Public" doesn't mean "open license": MCTS, Madison Metro, JCW, 211 and the library databases all have their own terms.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Download once, precompute small CSVs (occupations, wages by MSA, commute minutes, county context), and load them into MySQL or WordPress. Live APIs are optional extras.
- Put keys in `.env` (`USAJOBS_API_KEY`, `USAJOBS_EMAIL`, `CENSUS_API_KEY`, `HUD_API_TOKEN`). Never commit them.
- Show the source and vintage for every public number, plus any required attribution (O*NET CC BY, Census API disclaimer, MCTS "not sponsored", OSM).
- **Must NOT:** scrape job boards, mix public aggregates with client records, or present estimates as eligibility decisions.

# Workplace accommodation resources (JAN, ODEP)

## TL;DR
- **JAN (askjan.org)** is the main free source of accommodation ideas, funded by DOL's Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP). Its phone line is (800) 526-7234.
- Tools: **SOAR / Accommodation Search** (`askjan.org/soar.cfm`), the **A to Z** (by disability, limitation, work-related function, topic or accommodation), and the **Situations & Solutions Finder** (real examples).
- JAN's copyright page says JAN-created works are U.S. government works that "individuals may use… with impunity." Material JAN cites from others may be copyrighted.
- There's **no API or bulk download**. Link to JAN pages, or hand-curate a small mapping table with citations.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **JAN SOAR (Accommodation Search)** | Search box with popular terms (e.g. "ADHD", "Parking") leading to accommodation ideas for work and education | Web only, `askjan.org/soar.cfm`. No API or download found | JAN works are not copyrightable (government work). Third-party content cited by JAN may need permission | Ongoing, no schedule stated | Link to it from "accommodation ideas" in the matcher |
| **JAN A to Z** | Listings by Disability, Limitation (e.g. Lifting, Reading, Noise Sensitivity), Work-Related Function (e.g. Getting to and From Work, Performing Job Tasks, Tolerating Environment), Topic, Accommodation | Web, `askjan.org/a-to-z.cfm`. Print and MyJAN save. No API | Same as above | Ongoing | Build a small hand-made table: limitation → JAN URL |
| **JAN Situations & Solutions Finder** | Real accommodation examples from JAN customer feedback, filterable by disability, limitation and occupation | Web, `askjan.org/sitsol/index.cfm`. "Copy Filters Link" makes shareable URLs. PDF export | Same as above | Ongoing | Specialist prep: example accommodations for an occupation |
| **ODEP-funded centers** | JAN; EARN / AskEARN (employer recruiting, hiring, retention); PEAT (accessible workplace technology); LEAD Center (WIOA policy); CAPE-Youth | Web resources. URLs for PEAT, LEAD and CAPE-Youth not given on the ODEP page **(verify)** | Federal resources, generally public **(verify each site)** | Varies | Employer-facing pitch material (AskEARN), and accessible tech guidance (PEAT) |

## How it works
- The A to Z's **Limitation** and **Work-Related Function** views line up well with O*NET Work Context (e.g. a job high in "standing" pairs with JAN's standing and stamina limitation ideas).
- JAN's own caution: the A to Z is "a starting point" and examples "may not work for every person or workplace." An example doesn't mean a condition is a disability.
- JAN content was prepared under ODEP grant #26475OD000008-01-00. JAN states the opinions don't necessarily reflect DOL policy.

## Caveats and gotchas
- JAN's homepage menu no longer says "SOAR", but `soar.cfm` still works as "Accommodation Search" and calls itself the front end for SOAR.
- The copyright page sets no attribution rule. Cite JAN anyway: it's good practice and helps users find the source.
- We did not review JAN's `robots.txt` or any rate policy. Don't crawl JAN. Link to it, or copy a handful of entries by hand with citations.
- Accommodations are decided in an interactive process between the worker and the employer. A tool can suggest *ideas to discuss*. It can't say what an employer must provide.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- In the matcher, when a job has a demanding work-context flag or a seeker lists an accommodation, show "Ideas to discuss" with 1-3 JAN links. Use plain-language labels.
- Keep the mapping in a small CSV (`limitation, jan_url, plain_label`) committed to the team folder. Cite askjan.org.
- **Must NOT:** label a person's disability from their answers, rank people by accommodation need, or tell an employer an accommodation is or isn't "reasonable." Route ADA questions to JAN (800-526-7234) or Disability Rights Wisconsin.

- [occupations-and-wages.md](occupations-and-wages.md): O*NET work context
- [services-directories.md](services-directories.md)
- [../../domain/accessibility.md](../../domain/accessibility.md)
- [README.md](README.md)

# Disability population and benefits data

## TL;DR
- **Census ACS** is the source for "how many people with disabilities, employed, and earning what" by county. The newest 5-year data (2020-2024) came out on 2026-01-29. The **2025 1-year** release is scheduled for **2026-10-29**, two days before the hackathon **(verify it happened)**.
- **SSA county counts (December 2025):** SSI recipients total 107,505 statewide and 39,348 in Milwaukee County. SSDI disabled-worker beneficiaries total 136,029 statewide and 22,785 in Milwaukee County.
- **For county-level counts, use the SSA "OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County"** release. The DI Annual Statistical Report is state-level and national. Its 2025 edition came out in October 2026.
- **DVR (WRC report, FFY 2025):** 33,687 consumers served, 3,429 successful employment outcomes, average hourly wage $17.04 (median $15.00).

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ACS S1810** Disability Characteristics | Population with a disability by sex, age, race and disability type | data.census.gov, or the API at `api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/subject` (e.g. `S1810_C01_001E` = total civilian noninstitutionalized population) | Census API ToS: show "This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau." No re-identification | 1-year every fall (areas 65k+). 5-year each winter | Size of the population per county or tract |
| **ACS S1811** Economic characteristics by disability status | Employment, labor force, earnings, industry and occupation by disability status (age 16+) | Same subject endpoint (`S1811_C01_001E` = population 16+, `S1811_C01_002E` = employed, …) | Same | Same | Employment gap, with vs without disability |
| **ACS C18120** Employment Status by Disability Status | Labor force, employed, unemployed and not in the labor force, with or without a disability | Detailed endpoint `api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5` (`C18120_001E`…`_011E`) **(verify each variable's label before use)** | Same | Same | Simple counts for a dashboard |
| **ACS B18140** Median earnings by disability status by sex | `B18140_001E` total. `_002E` with a disability. `_005E` no disability (16+ with earnings, inflation-adjusted dollars) | Detailed endpoint | Same | Same | "Earnings gap" context |
| **Census Data API key** | Free key | Request at census.gov/data/developers/api-key.html. Append `&key=…`. Limits without a key not confirmed **(verify)** | ToS above | n/a | Put it in `.env` as `CENSUS_API_KEY` |
| **Cornell disabilitystatistics.org** | ACS disability estimates (national, state, county, congressional district), Annual Disability Status Reports, EEOC charge summaries, as maps and tables | Web tool. No API mentioned. Built by the Northeast ADA Center (NIDILRR-funded) | © Cornell University 2026. Reuse terms not stated **(verify)** | Follows ACS releases **(verify)** | Quick sanity checks and ready-made charts |
| **SSA SSI Recipients by State and County, 2025** | December 2025 SSI recipients and payments by county, eligibility category and age | HTML, PDF and Excel: `ssi_sc/2025/wi.html`, `wi.pdf`, `wi.xlsx`. Released August 2026 | U.S. government work **(verify any SSA reuse note)** | Annual | Where SSI recipients are, for outreach planning |
| **SSA OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County, 2025** | December 2025 beneficiaries by county and type, incl. **disabled workers** | `oasdi_sc/2025/wi.html`, `wi.pdf`, `wi.xlsx`. Released August 2026 | Same | Annual | SSDI disabled-worker counts per county |
| **SSA Annual Statistical Report on SSDI, 2025** | National and state DI tables (awards, terminations, demographics, work incentives) | `statcomps/di_asr/`, PDF and Excel. 2025 edition released October 2026 | Same | Annual | State context. The 2024 report put WI DI beneficiaries at 4.2% of people aged 18-64 |
| **DVR / WRC annual reports** | Council findings on DVR: consumers served, outcomes, wages. FFY basis | PDFs for 2023, 2024 and 2025 at dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/partners/wrc/ | State publication | Annual (after each FFY) | Statewide outcome benchmarks. No county or WDA counts |

### SSA county counts, December 2025
| County | SSI recipients (total) | SSDI disabled workers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wisconsin | 107,505 | 136,029 |
| Milwaukee | 39,348 | 22,785 |
| Dane | 7,204 | 8,640 |
| Waukesha | 3,045 | 6,400 |
| Racine | 5,177 | 5,665 |
| Kenosha | 3,263 | 4,335 |
| Rock | 3,447 | 4,530 |

Sources: SSA `ssi_sc/2025/wi.pdf` (Table 3) and `oasdi_sc/2025/wi.html` (Table 4). People can receive both SSI and SSDI, so **don't add the two columns**.

## How it works
- **Wisconsin FIPS:** state `55`. Counties: Milwaukee `079`, Dane `025`, Waukesha `133`, Racine `101`, Kenosha `059`, Rock `105`.
- **Example call** (5-year, six counties):
  `https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5?get=NAME,B18140_001E,B18140_002E,B18140_005E&for=county:079,025,133,101,059,105&in=state:55&key=$CENSUS_API_KEY`
- Each estimate (`E`) has a margin of error (`M`). Show both, or at least warn when the MOE is large (small areas, tracts).
- ACS "disability" covers six difficulty questions (hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, independent living). It undercounts some groups (e.g. some mental health conditions) **(verify wording against ACS documentation)**.

## Caveats and gotchas
- A 2026-08-06 Census notice said the 2025 1-year release date was "being determined" under Departmental Administrative Order 216-26. The banner now says 2026-10-29. Check again before you cite 2025 figures.
- 1-year ACS covers areas of 65,000+ people only. All six focus counties qualify, but use 5-year data for tracts and small cities.
- SSA tables count people in **current-payment status**. They are not applicants, and not everyone with a disability.
- The WRC report has no county or WDA breakdown. Don't present statewide DVR averages as local.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Use these numbers as **aggregate context only** (dashboards, grant narratives, outreach maps). They never describe an individual.
- Precompute a tiny `county_context.csv` with the six counties, and cite the source and vintage on screen.
- **Must NOT:** combine ACS or SSA aggregates with synthetic client rows to "estimate" anyone's benefits or disability, or present ACS numbers without the Census API disclaimer.

# Employer and federal contractor data

## TL;DR
- **Section 503 changed in 2026.** A DOL final rule (91 FR 54482, published 2026-08-21, effective 2026-09-21) **rescinded the 7% utilization goal (41 CFR 60-741.45) and the self-ID requirement (60-741.42)**. Non-discrimination, accommodation and outreach duties remain for federal contractors, so they're still a reasonable outreach list, but there's no longer a numeric goal to pitch. See [rehabilitation-act](../employment-law/rehabilitation-act.md).
- **Who's a federal contractor in WI?** Use the **USAspending API** (no key) for awards to WI recipients. Use the **SAM.gov Entity API** (free personal key, only 10 requests a day without a SAM role) for registered entities with WI addresses.
- **WOTC** has vocational rehabilitation referral and SSI recipient target groups. Its authorization ran to **2025-12-31**, and we found no confirmed extension **(verify)**. DOL publishes national certification totals (FY2024: 1,577,683). State detail appears to be in PDFs.
- Library business databases: **Milwaukee Public Library offers AtoZdatabases** (remote with a City of Milwaukee card). We did not find Data Axle/ReferenceUSA listed at MPL.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **USAspending.gov API** | Federal awards (contracts, grants) by recipient, place and agency | `https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/…`. "Endpoints do not currently require any authorization." Useful: `GET /api/v2/recipient/state/55/`, `GET /api/v2/recipient/state/awards/55/`, `POST /api/v2/recipient/`. Award search endpoints (e.g. `/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/`) are not on the endpoint index we read **(verify)** | Federal data. No license terms stated on the API page **(verify)** | Agencies report regularly **(verify cadence)** | List of WI federal contractors, so ERI can pitch Section 503 hiring support |
| **SAM.gov Entity Management API** | Registered entities: name, UEI, addresses, NAICS, PSC, business types, POC names | `https://open.gsa.gov/api/entity-api/`. Personal Public API Key from your SAM.gov account page. Filter `physicalAddressProvinceOrStateCode=WI` | Public data tier only (FOUO and sensitive need federal system accounts) | Live | Enrich contractor names with NAICS and address. **10 requests a day** without a SAM role, so pull once and cache |
| **OFCCP** | Section 503 and VEVRAA enforcement | dol.gov/agencies/ofccp. No open contractor dataset on the home page. FOIA Library linked | Federal | n/a | As of the page we read: pending compliance reviews administratively closed; the Section 503/VEVRAA AAP certification period closed; VEVRAA/503 obligations "remain in effect" |
| **WEDC** | WI economic development: SizeUpWI (free market research), export data, available sites, programs, Workforce Innovation Grant reports, annual report | wedc.org. No API listed | WEDC site terms **(verify)** | Varies | Employer prospect lists by industry (SizeUpWI). Context on grants |
| **Data Axle / ReferenceUSA** | Commercial business lists | Through library subscriptions. **Not found** in MPL's A-G database list. Not visible in the first 50 of 175 Madison PL eResources **(verify)** | Vendor license. Typically personal or non-bulk use only **(verify)** | Vendor | Don't plan on it for the hackathon |
| **AtoZdatabases** (MPL) | "30 million business and executive profiles" | Remote access for City of Milwaukee cardholders | Vendor license **(verify bulk-export limits)** | Vendor | Manual employer research by a specialist. No scraping or bulk export into the app |
| **WOTC statistics** (DOL ETA) | Certifications nationally by fiscal year, wage band and occupation | `dol.gov/agencies/eta/wotc/performance`. FY2024 PDF "State and National Details" **(verify WI figures in the PDF)** | Federal | Annual | Employer pitch: hiring a DVR referral or SSI recipient may earn a tax credit, if WOTC is authorized |

## How it works
- **Section 503 basics:** contractors with more than 100 employees measure utilization by the same job groups they used under EO 11246 (per the eCFR text). Smaller contractors may measure their whole workforce. Paragraph (h) bars using the goal as a quota or ceiling. The eCFR text still references EO 11246 job groups after the EO's revocation. How OFCCP handles that is **(verify)**.
- **WOTC target groups** (IRS page) include *vocational rehabilitation referral* (state VR plan, a Ticket to Work Employment Network plan, or a VA program) and *qualified SSI recipient* (SSI for any month ending within the 60 days before the hire date).
- **USAspending FIPS:** Wisconsin is `55`.

## Caveats and gotchas
- Federal contractor status isn't a quality rating. A big award doesn't mean the employer hires locally or has openings.
- SAM data includes point-of-contact names. Don't show personal contact data in a public demo.
- WOTC: both the DOL and IRS pages (IRS reviewed 2026-07-20) still say "authorized until December 31, 2025." Don't tell employers the credit is available without checking current law.
- OFCCP's status page has no updates after mid-2025 items plus a moratorium for VAHBP providers through 2027-05-07. Check it again before relying on it.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Stretch feature:** "Employers who may value Section 503 hires." Build a cached list of WI recipients from USAspending, joined to the synthetic postings by employer name, with a plain-language note on why it matters.
- Keep this for ERI business development staff, not job seekers. Never imply an employer "must hire" someone.
- **Must NOT:** scrape library databases, present WOTC as guaranteed, or show SAM POC personal data.

## Related pages
- [jobs-and-postings.md](jobs-and-postings.md)
- [nonprofit-and-funding-data.md](nonprofit-and-funding-data.md)
- [README.md](README.md)

- [DOL OFCCP](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/ofccp)
- [USAspending API](https://api.usaspending.gov/)
- [USAspending API endpoints](https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/endpoints)

# Geography and boundaries data

## TL;DR
- **TIGER/Line 2026** shapefiles (boundaries as of 2026-01-01) were released 2026-10-14. They're at `www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2026/`. Use them for counties, tracts, places and ZCTAs.
- **ZIP ≠ ZCTA.** Use the Census **2020 ZCTA-to-county / tract / place relationship files**, or the **HUD USPS crosswalk** (quarterly; API needs a free token sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`).
- **Wisconsin boundaries:** municipal (city, village, town) from **LTSB** (`gis-ltsb.hub.arcgis.com/pages/download-data`). Statewide parcels **V12** from the SCO (shapefile or FGDB, plus a REST service).
- **OpenStreetMap** data is **ODbL**. Credit OpenStreetMap and its contributors. Derived databases you distribute must be share-alike. OSM's own tile servers aren't free for third-party apps.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Census TIGER/Line** | Shapefiles: states, counties, tracts, block groups, places, ZCTAs, roads | Web picker `census.gov/cgi-bin/geo/shapefiles/index.php`. Bulk at `www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2026/` | No license stated on the page. Census products are generally public domain **(verify)** | Annual (2026 vintage released 2026-10-14) | Map layers. Point-in-county or tract lookup |
| **Census 2020 ZCTA relationship files** | ZCTA to county, tract and place, with area overlaps | Linked from the 2020 Relationship Files page (direct URLs not captured) **(verify file URLs)** | Same | Per decennial geography | Turn a seeker's ZIP into county and tract for ACS context |
| **HUD USPS ZIP Crosswalk** | ZIP-Tract, ZIP-County, ZIP-CBSA (and reverse) with residential, business and other address ratios | Files after login at huduser.gov. API: `GET https://www.huduser.gov/hudapi/public/usps?type=2&query=WI` (`type` 1-12, e.g. 1 = zip-tract; `year` and `quarter` optional). Header `Authorization: Bearer $HUD_API_TOKEN` | Dataset page: "No special restrictions." A separate HUD User API ToS applies **(verify text)** | Quarterly, out by the end of the following month. 2023Q1 onward uses 2020 geographies | Assign a ZIP to a county when it crosses county lines (use the residential ratio). Check the `type` code for ZIP-county **(verify: type 2)** |
| **WI municipal boundaries** (LTSB) | City, village and town boundaries, collected each spring for the Census Boundary and Annexation Survey | `https://gis-ltsb.hub.arcgis.com/pages/download-data`. Monthly-dated snapshots (e.g. January 2025, July 2025) | Not stated **(verify)** | Snapshots, frequency not stated | "Is this job in the City of Milwaukee?" filters |
| **WI statewide parcels V12** (SCO) | Statewide parcel polygons and attributes | Shapefile or FGDB at `sco.wisc.edu/parcels/data/`, by county at `/parcels/data-county/`. REST: `services3.arcgis.com/n6uYoouQZW75n5WI/arcgis/rest/services/Wisconsin_Statewide_Parcels_DB/FeatureServer/0` | Not stated **(verify; ask help@sco.wisc.edu)** | Annual versions. Coverage map as of 2026-06-30 | Rarely needed. Possible geocoding of employer addresses |
| **GeoData@Wisconsin** | UW catalog of WI geospatial data | `geodata.wisc.edu`. "Available to download for free" | Varies by dataset | Varies | Find other layers (e.g. bus routes, county GIS) |
| **WI LIO** (county Land Information Offices) | County GIS: addresses, roads, parcels | Per county. Contact list via DOA and WLION (wlion.org) | Varies by county **(verify)** | Varies | Usually not needed for the hackathon |
| **OpenStreetMap** | Streets, footpaths, POIs; the routing base for r5py and OTP | Extracts (e.g. a Geofabrik Wisconsin `.pbf`, whose page blocked our check) **(verify URL)**. Don't use OSM's tile or Nominatim servers in an app without reading their usage policies | **ODbL 1.0.** Attribution to OpenStreetMap and its contributors, and make clear it's ODbL. Derived databases you distribute stay ODbL. Docs are CC BY-SA 2.0 | Continuous (extracts daily) | Walk and transit routing. Base map with attribution |

## How it works
- **Geocoding:** synthetic data already has `lat`/`lon` and `zip`. For real addresses later, the Census Geocoder is an option **(not reviewed; verify)**.
- **ZIP to county:** use the HUD ZIP-County file and pick the county with the highest residential ratio. Keep the ratio so you can show uncertainty.
- **FIPS:** WI = 55. Milwaukee 55079, Dane 55025, Waukesha 55133, Racine 55101, Kenosha 55059, Rock 55105.

## Caveats and gotchas
- ZCTAs are Census approximations of ZIP areas. PO Box-only ZIPs have no ZCTA, and HUD files leave out PO-box-only ZIPs too.
- HUD ratios may not sum to exactly 1.00, and they shift slightly each quarter because of re-geocoding.
- An app that shows an OSM-based map must show the attribution on the map.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Ship a pre-built `zip_county.csv` for the six focus counties instead of calling the HUD API live. If you call it, read `HUD_API_TOKEN` from `.env`.
- Keep maps simple: use Leaflet with an OSM-compatible tile provider whose terms allow your use, plus attribution.
- **Must NOT:** geocode or store real client home addresses (synthetic data only), or hammer the public OSM or Nominatim servers.

- [transit-gtfs.md](transit-gtfs.md)
- [disability-population.md](disability-population.md)
- [README.md](README.md)

- [HUD USER, USPS ZIP Crosswalk Files](https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/usps_crosswalk.html)
- [HUD USER, USPS ZIP Crosswalk API](https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/uspszip-api.html)
- [SCO, Data](https://www.sco.wisc.edu/data/)
- [SCO, Municipal Boundaries](https://www.sco.wisc.edu/data/municipal-boundaries/)
- [SCO, Parcels](https://www.sco.wisc.edu/data/parcels/)

# Job postings data sources

## TL;DR
- The only open, documented, reusable job API that covers Wisconsin is **USAJOBS** (federal jobs). It needs a free key, and `HiringPath=disability` returns announcements open to Schedule A applicants. OPM's terms let you reuse the data, including commercially.
- **Job Center of Wisconsin (JCW, run under DWD)** has no public job-postings API. Its RSS feeds give only posting and resume *statistics*. Link to its search instead of copying listings.
- **NLx Research Hub** paused new data requests in 2026 while it moves to a new access model. Job matching and product development are *not currently authorized* uses. Don't plan on it for Oct 31.
- **Indeed, LinkedIn and Handshake:** do not scrape. Handshake's terms ban crawling and scraping outright. Indeed bans scraping in the program terms we read. LinkedIn blocks automated reads of its own terms page. For the hackathon, use `data/job_postings.csv` (synthetic) plus USAJOBS.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **USAJOBS Search API** | Federal job announcements (title, agency, location, pay, schedule, hiring paths, closing date) | `GET https://data.usajobs.gov/api/Search`. Free key from developer.usajobs.gov/apirequest/. Headers: `Host: data.usajobs.gov`, `User-Agent: <your email>`, `Authorization-Key: <key>`. Code-list endpoints need no key | "Public Data" is under an open license: copy, reformat and redistribute, commercial use OK. Attribution is encouraged, not required. Don't imply OPM endorsement or present altered data as official | Live (announcements open and close daily) | Federal jobs in Milwaukee, Madison and elsewhere, filtered by `HiringPath=disability` (Schedule A) |
| **Job Center of Wisconsin** (jobcenterofwisconsin.com) | Statewide job bank, resume bank, Skill Explorer, WisConomy LMI | Web search only. No job-posting API found. RSS: `RSS.aspx?Topic=JobPostingStatistics` and `?Topic=ResumeStatistics` (statistics only) | DWD terms: content is "AS IS". Employers may not resell or repost resumes. Nothing on scraping either way **(verify with DWD before automating)** | Live | Deep-link job seekers and specialists to JCW searches. Don't copy listings |
| **NLx Research Hub** (NASWA + DirectEmployers) | Real-time and historical postings from employers and state job banks | API or monthly files, **after** a signed Data Use Agreement. New requests paused (2026), "check back in November" | DUA required. Raw postings can't go to third parties. Only aggregates or code can be shared. Currently authorized only for state LMI work and discrete nonprofit research. Job matching, product development and AI training are not currently authorized | Daily (real-time feed), monthly files | Not for the hackathon. Possible later research partnership with DWD LMI |
| **Wisc.Jobs** (wisc.jobs) | State of Wisconsin government jobs | Web portal with account and email alerts. No API documented **(verify)** | Not reviewed **(verify)** | Live | Link to it for state jobs. Many are in Madison |
| **City and county boards** | City of Milwaukee (E-Notify job alerts). Milwaukee County, MPS, MMSD and the State of Wisconsin are "separate employers" with their own application sites | Web only. Dane, Waukesha, Racine, Kenosha and Rock county boards not reviewed **(verify)** | Each site's own terms **(verify)** | Live | A curated link list in the app ("public-sector jobs near you") |
| **Indeed** | Commercial aggregator | Official channels only: Indeed API and Developer Portal (separate API terms) | Smart Sourcing terms: "scraping the database… is strictly prohibited" and resume-extraction software is forbidden. We could not see a general site-wide scraping clause in the text we read **(verify the Site Rules)**. Treat all scraping as off-limits | Live | Don't scrape. A job seeker can paste a link by hand |
| **LinkedIn** | Professional network and jobs | Official partner APIs only **(verify)** | LinkedIn's servers refused our automated read of its User Agreement and help pages (robots disallowed). That alone is a strong signal. Its "prohibited software" page is widely reported to ban scrapers **(verify)** | Live | Don't scrape. Don't use LinkedIn data in demos |
| **Handshake** | Student and early-career jobs via university partners | No public API in the terms we read | Bans accounts created "through… scripts, bots, or automated crawlers" and "collecting content through crawling, scraping, or caching… without our express consent." Also bans using its data to build competing services | Live | Only useful through a school's career center. Not a data source |

## How it works
- **USAJOBS query for Schedule A jobs near Milwaukee:**
  `https://data.usajobs.gov/api/Search?HiringPath=disability&LocationName=Milwaukee,%20Wisconsin&Radius=50&ResultsPerPage=100`
  Other useful parameters: `Keyword`, `PositionScheduleTypeCode` (1 full-time, 2 part-time), `RemoteIndicator`, `DatePosted` (0-60 days), `WhoMayApply=public`, `Fields=full`. Separate multiple values with semicolons.
- USAJOBS limits: 500 rows per page and 10,000 rows per query. The code-list endpoints have no limit.
- The USAJOBS `DISABILITY` hiring path matches announcements whose text mentions "individuals with a disab…" or "Schedule A".
- JCW search is behind its own web UI. Its RSS gives counts, not listings.

## Caveats and gotchas
- USAJOBS covers **federal** jobs only. In southern Wisconsin that means a small pool (VA, USPS, other agencies). Don't oversell it.
- Schedule A eligibility is a federal hiring authority with its own proof-of-disability letter. The app should explain it in plain language and link to the announcement. It must not decide eligibility.
- NLx access rules changed in 2026. Re-check after November 2026.
- We found no DWD statement that JCW feeds NLx. Whether JCW listings flow into NLx is **(verify)**.
- We could not open LinkedIn's terms ourselves. The no-scraping claim for LinkedIn is **(verify)**, though LinkedIn has sued scrapers and blocks bots.
- Wisc.Jobs and the county job boards were not opened beyond what's noted. Their terms are **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Build on synthetic `data/job_postings.csv`.** Optionally add a live "federal jobs (Schedule A)" panel from USAJOBS. Read the key from `.env` (`USAJOBS_API_KEY`) plus your email as `USAJOBS_EMAIL`. Never commit them.
- Show the USAJOBS source, the retrieval date and a link to the official announcement. Add "not endorsed by OPM."
- **Must NOT:** scrape Indeed, LinkedIn, Handshake or JCW. Store or redistribute NLx raw postings. Submit applications on anyone's behalf. Tell a user they "qualify" for Schedule A.
- For non-federal jobs, deep-link to the JCW, Wisc.Jobs and city or county job pages, and let the specialist paste postings in by hand.

# Nonprofit and funding data

## TL;DR
- **ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API v2** is free with no key: `https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/api/v2/search.json?state%5Bid%5D=WI&q=…` and `/organizations/{EIN}.json`. It's built on IRS data. Its exact terms for the API are **(verify)**.
- **IRS Form 990 e-file data:** yearly zip files of XML returns plus a CSV index (e.g. `index_2026.csv`). 2026 has 10 zips so far, page updated 2026-10-22. Foundation **990-PF** returns are part of the same series.
- **Grants.gov:** a daily full-database XML extract (`GrantsDBExtract[YYYYMMDD]v2.zip`, no login seen). The **Simpler.Grants.gov API** needs a key via Login.gov (60 requests per minute, 10,000 a day).
- **Candid** (Foundation Directory, grants data) is mostly paid. A free account gives profiles. It also sells APIs.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API** | Organization profiles and 990 financials (revenue, expenses, assets, filings, PDF links) | `GET /api/v2/search.json` (keyword, `state[id]`, NTEE, subsection; 25 per page) and `GET /api/v2/organizations/:ein.json`. No key mentioned. PDF links are rate limited | "Using the API means you agree to ProPublica's Data Terms of Use." The archived Data Store terms (cite ProPublica; no reselling; no full republication) may or may not be the ones that apply **(verify)** | As IRS releases data | Peer benchmarking (other WI supported-employment nonprofits), and funder lookups by EIN |
| **IRS Form 990 Series e-file** | XML of e-filed 990, 990-EZ, 990-PF, 990-T **(verify forms included)** | `irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads`. ZIPs of XML by year, CSV index per year | U.S. government data. Public returns | Several zips per year (2026: 01A-09A + 05B) | Bulk analysis of foundation grants (990-PF Part XV lists grants paid) **(verify part number)** |
| **Foundation 990-PFs** | Private foundation returns: assets, grants paid, grantee names | In the IRS e-file data above. Also as PDFs or parsed data via ProPublica | As above | Annual per foundation | Find WI foundations that fund disability employment |
| **Candid** (candid.org) | 1.9M organization profiles, 3M annual grant transactions; funder search; APIs; custom datasets | Free registration for profiles. Paid subscriptions and APIs (pricing page not read). Free access at Funding Information Network libraries not confirmed **(verify)** | Commercial license | Continuous | Development staff prospecting. Not for the hackathon |
| **Grants.gov XML Extract** | The whole Grants.gov opportunity database | Daily zip at `https://prod-grants-gov-chatbot.s3.amazonaws.com/extracts/GrantsDBExtract[YYYYMMDD]v2.zip` (pattern from the extract page). No login step seen | Federal data. Grants.gov Terms & Conditions linked from the API page **(verify)** | Daily, about 4:40 AM ET | Filter by CFDA/ALN, keyword ("disabilit", "vocational rehabilitation") |
| **Simpler.Grants.gov API** | REST search of funding opportunities | Docs at `api.simpler.grants.gov/docs`. Key from your Simpler.Grants.gov account (Login.gov). 60 req/min, 10,000/day. Keys disabled after 30 days unused. Read-only | No formal ToS on the developer page **(verify)** | Live | A "new federal funding this week" alert for the development team |
| **Grants.gov legacy APIs** | Applicant and Grantor system-to-system APIs | grants.gov/api. Not a public search API | Grants.gov T&C | n/a | Not needed |
| **WI DHS grant opportunities** | Current unawarded DHS solicitations (Requests for Application) | HTML table at `dhs.wisconsin.gov/business/solicitations-list.htm`. Bids go on VendorNet and the WI Public Notices site. No feed | State public information | As posted | Watch for disability-related RFAs |
| **WI DWD grants** | e.g. Wisconsin Fast Forward / Workforce Innovation announcements | No single grants page loaded for us (`dwd.wisconsin.gov/grants/` failed). News items like the 2026-06-29 WFF release **(verify the grants hub URL)** | State | As posted | DVR-adjacent workforce funding |

## How it works
- The **EIN** is the join key across ProPublica, IRS e-file and Candid.
- IRS e-file XML schemas change by tax year. Parse with care and use the CSV index to find the filings you need, instead of unzipping everything.
- The Grants.gov extract is large (the whole database). For a demo, filter it offline to a few opportunities.

## Caveats and gotchas
- 990 data lags 1-2 years behind the fiscal year.
- ProPublica's API is "a work in progress and subject to change."
- Candid's free tier is limited. Don't promise grant-level detail without a subscription.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Not core to Challenges A or B. It's a good **backlog** idea for ERI's development team (funder prospect list, grant deadline alerts).
- **Must NOT:** scrape Candid, or republish ProPublica data in bulk.

# Occupations, wages and projections data

## TL;DR
- **O*NET 31.0** is the current release. It is free to download (Excel or MySQL zip, plus per-file CSV and JSON) under **CC BY 4.0**. Use Work Context, Abilities and Work Activities to describe a job's physical and sensory demands.
- **BLS OEWS May 2025** is the newest wage data (tables page updated 2026-05-15). Metro file: `oesm25ma.zip`. **Kenosha is now its own MSA (area 0028450)**, not part of the Chicago division.
- **WisConomy** publishes 2022-2032 long-term projections for each of the 11 WDAs, and 2024-2034 statewide, as Excel downloads.
- BLS data is public domain. The BLS API v2 needs free registration (500 queries a day).

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **O*NET 31.0 Database** | About 1,000 occupations: tasks, skills, abilities (94,640 rows), work context (305,389 rows), work activities, education, tools | Zips: `db_31_0_excel.zip`, `db_31_0_mysql.zip` at onetcenter.org/dl_files/database/. Per-file CSV and JSON, e.g. `db_31_0_csv/work_context.csv`, `db_31_0_csv/abilities.csv`. No full-database text zip is listed | **CC BY 4.0.** Credit "O*NET 31.0 Database" and USDOL/ETA, link the license, and note changes. Say USDOL/ETA hasn't endorsed your changes. Include the "O*NET® is a trademark of USDOL/ETA" notice. Use the version number | Quarterly. The primary update is in Q3 | Map a job title to SOC/O*NET-SOC. Show "standing", "lifting", "noise" and "public contact" levels to match accommodations |
| **O*NET Web Services** | API over the same data, plus keyword search ("cashier" → SOC) | Register at services.onetcenter.org/developer/signup. O*NET staff approve organizations. API keys per project. Current API appears to be v2 **(verify)** | Must agree to ToS and Data License. Show data in a free, public area with no login. Credit and link to O*NET Web Services. Personal use isn't supported. Rate limits not stated **(verify)** | Serves the latest release (31.0) | Title-to-occupation search in the matcher. For the hackathon, the downloaded CSV is simpler |
| **BLS OEWS** (May 2025) | Employment and hourly or annual wage percentiles by SOC and area | `https://www.bls.gov/oes/special-requests/oesm25ma.zip` (metro and nonmetro, XLSX). `oesm25st.zip` (states). Browse at data.bls.gov/oes | Public domain. BLS asks for a citation. BLS logo is trademarked | Annual. May reference period, released in spring. Kenosha release was 2026-07-31 | "Typical pay for this job in Madison": median and 25th percentile next to the posting's wage |
| **WisConomy projections** (DWD) | Long-term industry and occupation projections and "Hot Jobs" | Excel per WDA (2022-2032) and statewide (2024-2034) from each WDA page, e.g. `wisconomy/pub/wdaSE.htm` | DWD site terms. No specific open license stated **(verify)** | Every two years | "Growing jobs in your area" hints for career exploration |
| **BLS LAUS** | Labor force, employment and unemployment rate by state, metro, county and city | Flat files at download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/la/. BLS API v2 (series IDs) | Public domain | Monthly. Annual revisions **(verify schedule)** | Context only, e.g. county unemployment on a dashboard |
| **BLS Public Data API v2** | Time series for LAUS, OEWS and others | Register at data.bls.gov/registrationEngine/. 500 queries a day, 50 series per query, 20 years, 50 requests per 10 seconds. Renew yearly | Public domain data. Developer ToS linked from the API pages **(verify text)** | n/a | Optional. Files are easier for a one-day build |

### OEWS area codes for southern Wisconsin (May 2025)
| Area | OEWS code | Counties (per WisConomy) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Milwaukee-Waukesha, WI | 0033340 | Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Washington, Waukesha |
| Madison, WI | 0031540 | Columbia, Dane, Green, Iowa |
| Racine-Mount Pleasant, WI | 0039540 | Racine |
| Kenosha, WI | 0028450 | Kenosha |
| Janesville-Beloit, WI | 0027500 | Rock |
| South Central WI nonmetro | 5500003 | Rest of south-central WI **(verify county list)** |

### Wisconsin WDAs (for WisConomy projections)
| WDA | Name | Counties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Southeast | Kenosha, Racine, Walworth |
| 2 | Milwaukee | Milwaukee |
| 3 | WOW | Ozaukee, Washington, Waukesha |
| 10 | South Central | Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Jefferson, Marquette, Sauk |
| 11 | Southwest | Grant, Green, Iowa, Lafayette, Richland, Rock |

## How it works
- **Join key:** use the 6-digit SOC code (e.g. `35-3023`). O*NET uses O*NET-SOC (`35-3023.01`), so take the first 7 characters to join to OEWS.
- **O*NET Work Context** gives levels (e.g. "Spend Time Standing", "Sounds, Noise Levels Are Distracting", "Exposed to Hazardous Conditions"). **Abilities** rates levels such as Static Strength, Near Vision and Hearing Sensitivity. These describe the *typical* job, not a specific employer.
- **OEWS** gives mean wages and the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles. Some cells are suppressed (`*`, `**`, `#`). Handle them as missing.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Kenosha:** older notes put Kenosha in the "Lake County-Kenosha County, IL-WI" metro division (code 29404). The May 2025 OEWS lists **Kenosha, WI MSA 0028450** instead, under the newer OMB delineations **(verify which delineation year)**.
- WisConomy's MSA list says "Racine, WI". BLS names it "Racine-Mount Pleasant, WI". Same area.
- WDA projections are 2022-2032, while statewide projections are already 2024-2034. Don't mix the two vintages in one chart.
- BLS sometimes blocks scripted downloads that lack a descriptive User-Agent (our automated fetch of the zip was refused). Send a User-Agent with your contact email **(verify current BLS policy)**.
- O*NET describes occupations. It must not be used to decide that a *person* "can't" do a job.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Precompute a small `occupations.csv` (SOC, title, median wage per MSA, 3-5 work-context flags). Load it in PHP or MySQL. No live API is needed.
- Show the wage as "typical pay in this area (BLS May 2025)" next to the posting wage. Flag postings below the area's 25th percentile so a specialist can review them.
- Use work-context flags to *suggest accommodations to discuss* (link to JAN), never to filter people out.
- Add the O*NET CC BY attribution text in the app footer.

# Service directories for referrals

## TL;DR
- **Link out. Don't copy.** None of these directories offers a public API or an open data license that we could confirm. A tool should deep-link to them and show a few public phone lines.
- **Key public lines:** DVR (800) 442-3477. ADRC statewide 844-WIS-ADRC (844-947-2372). Ticket to Work Help Line 1-866-968-7842 (TTY 1-866-833-2967). WIPA via the Ticket to Work Find Help tool. Wisconsin WIPA 1-877-826-1752 (per the project wiki).
- **DVR waitlist:** "Effective June 2, 2026, DVR will begin serving individuals from its waitlist" (DVR home page).
- **Benefits.gov** now redirects to **USA.gov Benefit Finder** (`usa.gov/benefit-finder`), which has a "Disabilities" category.

## Key facts
| Dataset | What | Access / API | License / ToS | Refresh | How ERI uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **211 Wisconsin** | Statewide information and referral resource database | `211wisconsin.org` redirects to `211wisconsin.communityos.org` (VisionLink CommunityOS). Pages: Data Collection, Privacy, Database Policy (`/inclusion-exclusion-policy`), 211 Counts (`wi.211counts.org`, which failed to load for us). No API mentioned | No data-sharing or reuse terms found **(verify; ask 211 Wisconsin about data-sharing agreements)**. Operator not named on the page **(verify)** | Live | "Other help near you" link. Don't scrape |
| **ADRC directory** (DHS) | 68 ADRC and Tribal ADRS contacts as cards (name, phone, TTY, email, service area, addresses), filterable by county | `dhs.wisconsin.gov/adrc/contacts.htm` (web) | State public information | As DHS updates | Link from benefits and long-term-care flags. Milwaukee 414-289-6874, Dane 608-240-7400, Waukesha 866-677-2372, Racine 866-219-1043, Kenosha 800-472-8008, Rock 855-741-3600 |
| **DVR office locator** | Statewide map of DVR offices, plus a DVR Staff Directory PDF | `dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/about/locations.htm`, `…/contacts.htm`. Central office: 201 E. Washington Ave, Madison. (608) 261-0050 / (800) 442-3477 | State public information | As updated | "Apply to DVR" link. The staff directory has individuals' names, so link to it, don't import it |
| **Family Care MCOs** | MCOs with counties served and member-services lines: Anthem, Community Care, iCare, Inclusa, Lakeland Care, My Choice Wisconsin | `dhs.wisconsin.gov/familycare/mcocontacts.pdf`. Region maps P-01790 and P-01789. Reconfiguration timeline P-03225 | State public information | Changes with regional reconfiguration **(verify the P-03225 timeline)** | Explain who manages long-term care supports. Link only |
| **IRIS** (self-directed) | IRIS consultant agencies (ICA) and fiscal employer agents (FEA) | `dhs.wisconsin.gov/iris/ica.htm`, `/iris/fea.htm`. Whether they list agencies by county is **(verify)** | State public information | As updated | Link only |
| **Ticket to Work Find Help** | Directory of Employment Networks (EN), Workforce ENs, VR agencies, **WIPA** projects and **PABSS** | `choosework.ssa.gov/findhelp`. Search by ZIP, filter by provider type and in-person or virtual. No download or API mentioned | Federal site. Disclaimer and privacy pages only | As SSA updates | "Find a benefits counselor (WIPA)" and "Find an EN" buttons. ERI itself may be listed as an EN **(verify)** |
| **USA.gov Benefit Finder** | Federal benefits screener in 12 categories, incl. "Disabilities". Replaces the Benefits.gov URL (redirect seen 2026-10-23) | Web only. No API mentioned | Federal | As updated | Link from a "Other benefits" section |

## How it works
- Most of these are **directories of organizations**. They are public, but they're maintained by others and change often. A stale copy in an app is worse than a link.
- Medicaid long-term care in Wisconsin runs through ADRCs (the front door), then Family Care (MCOs) or IRIS (self-directed).
- The Family Care MCO counties for our six focus counties come from the DHS PDF. Several MCOs serve each county (e.g. Milwaukee: Anthem, Community Care, Inclusa, My Choice Wisconsin).

## Caveats and gotchas
- The DVR waitlist note (June 2, 2026) is from the DVR home page. Check the Order of Selection FAQ (`dvr/policy-guidance/eligibility/oos-faq.htm`) for current category status **(verify)**.
- The MCO list includes **Anthem** for Family Care in Milwaukee and western counties. That's new compared with older lists. Confirm against DHS P-01790.
- 211 data may be licensed under agreements with Inform USA standards or local partners. Ask before reusing it **(verify)**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Put a static "Get help" panel in the app: DVR, ADRC (county-specific number), WIPA, Ticket to Work Find Help, 211. Show the source and the date checked.
- **Must NOT:** import staff names or emails from DVR or ADRC directories, decide someone's eligibility, or present a referral as an application.
