# ERI consulting brief

## TL;DR
- ERI is a **$3.07M, 29-person specialist** organization. Its core assets are statewide benefits-counseling expertise (ERI describes itself as the sole Wisconsin WIPA agency since 2021; the 2021 project period ended 2026-06-30 and the follow-on award is **(verify)**) and a rare in-house web/LMS team. It runs on **thin margins**: 0.9% in FY2025, five loss years out of fifteen, and about 2.8 months of net assets.
- Revenue has been **flat at $3.0-3.3M for eight years** and depends on government rules it doesn't control (SSA, DVR, Dane County). The December 2025 DVR waitlist shows how fast fee income can stall.
- **Top 3 moves (highest impact per unit of effort):** (1) DVR billing integrity and days-to-report, (2) shift job development toward **preferred outcomes**, (3) a reviewed **knowledge base / AI assistant for benefits counselors** that stretches WIPA and CCS capacity.

## Key facts

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| FY2025 revenue / expenses / surplus | $3,065,352 / $3,038,876 / $26,476 | ProPublica |
| FY2025 program service revenue | $1,679,493 (-10.7% vs FY2024) | ProPublica |
| Net assets, FY2025 | $701,212 (about 2.8 months of expenses) | ProPublica, derived |
| Staff listed | 29. Employment Specialists 6, benefits roles 6, web/design/training 6 | ERI staff page |
| DVR preferred vs standard hire fee | $2,000-2,200 vs $1,600 (SE); retention $2,200 vs $1,600 (JD) | DVR fee schedule 2026-2028 |
| Ticket SSDI full value per beneficiary | up to $34,453 (P1 $7,616 + P2 $6,281 + outcomes $20,556) | SSA Ticket, 2026 |
| DVR waitlist peak | 7,610 (2026-06-02); DWD goal to end it by 2027-06-30 | DWD |
| VRTAC-QE | Grant concluded; resources online through 2026 | tacqe.com |

## SWOT

| Strengths | Weaknesses |
|---|---|
| Wisconsin WIPA agency (self-described sole provider since 2021; current award **(verify)**); 35+ years (founded 1990) | Thin margins; 2.8 months of net assets; five loss years since 2011 |
| Multi-payer mix: SSA, DVR, Dane County, DHS, federal TA | Flat revenue since FY2018; FY2025 fee revenue down $202K |
| In-house web/LMS shop serving national TA centers | Public storefront has placeholders ("$XX", lorem ipsum, 2023 dates) |
| Statewide staff (Milwaukee, Green Bay, NE and NW WI) | Few public outcome metrics ("80+ graduates", "hundreds") |
| Candid Gold Transparency seal; "Excellent" EN rating | CCS and employment-counseling capacity below demand; waitlists closed |
| New ED (named Nov 2024) with a mandate for "next phase of growth" | Leadership transition still recent |

| Opportunities | Threats |
|---|---|
| DVR re-activation surge (7,610 waitlisted) and $11.05M reallotment | DVR state funding "will not sustain" next biennium (DWD) |
| Preferred-outcome fee premiums | WIPA 2021 agreements ended 2026-06-30; next terms not public **(verify)** |
| BadgerCare 80-hour rule (2027) drives demand for benefits counseling | SSA staffing target of 50,000 (2025-02-28 plan); slower SSA processing hurts Ticket payment timing |
| Tech in-kind (Azure $2K/yr, Ad Grants $10K/month) | ODEP and Supported Employment grants targeted in federal budget requests |
| Replacing VRTAC-QE work with new TA-center or state LMS clients | Competitors for DVR POs; employer-services market is crowded |

## Strategic opportunities (ranked by impact / effort)

| # | Opportunity | Impact | Effort | Why (cited) | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **DVR billing integrity**: report-deadline tracker, PO-to-payment reconciliation, returned-report fixes | High | Low | Fees pay only after reports land within 5 business days; returned reports must be fixed in 10 business days | Pull 12 months of POs vs paid invoices and measure leakage |
| 2 | **Preferred-outcome job development** | High | Low-Med | +$400-600 per SE hire; +$600 per JD retention; Rapid Hire $1,900 vs $1,600 | Get the DVR appendix criteria; aim job development at jobs that genuinely offer more hours, higher wages or insurance. The rate follows the job actually obtained and documented, never how a note is worded |
| 3 | **Benefits-counselor KB / AI assistant with human review** | High | Med | 6 benefits staff cover the whole state for WIPA; CCS "delays because demand is higher than our available capacity"; BadgerCare rule starts 2027 | Hackathon prototype on public SSA/DHS sources; CWIC sign-off on every answer |
| 4 | **Ticket payment capture** (earnings evidence, milestone claims) | Med-High | Low | Phase 1 milestones $1,904 each at $1,210/month earnings; SSA pays only on proof | Check every assigned Ticket against payment history |
| 5 | **Fix and monetize the web/LMS shop** | Med | Low (fix) to Med (sell) | VRTAC-QE ended; Training Center shows "$XX"; 6-person team already in place | Clean up the storefront in 30 days; one-page offer for TA centers and state agencies |
| 6 | **Productized employer services** (accommodation consulting via JAN/EARN, inclusive job posts, retention support; federal contractors as an outreach list) | Med | Med | Business page offers recruiting, retention and consultations. Note: Section 503's 7% goal was rescinded 2026-09-21 and WOTC lapsed for hires after 2025-12-31, so don't sell on those | Pilot 3 paid employer packages built on retention and accommodation value |
| 7 | **Milwaukee expansion** | High | High | Two Milwaukee-area specialists already; GMF lists workforce development; GMWC employment cycle closed to 2028 | Partner-first model (a Milwaukee CBO) before opening an office |

## Risks
- **Revenue concentration and policy risk:** SSA (WIPA and Ticket) and DVR together likely make up most revenue **(verify)** with Schedule B or the audit.
- **WIPA re-competition or gap:** a smaller or delayed award would hit benefits capacity directly **(verify)**.
- **DVR 2027-2029 biennium:** DWD says current funding won't sustain services. A second waitlist is possible.
- **AI risk:** a wrong benefits answer can cause an overpayment or lost coverage. Every answer needs human review, citations and dated rules.
- **Key-person risk:** a small leadership team, and a 6-person web team on a premium-plugin WordPress stack.

## KPIs to track (monthly unless noted)

| KPI | Definition | Why |
|---|---|---|
| DVR outcome rate | Closed-employed / DVR referrals accepted (rolling 12 months) | Core quality and fee driver |
| Preferred-outcome % | Preferred hires / all hires (SE and JD) | Fee premium capture |
| Days-to-report | Median business days from milestone event to DVR report submitted; % within 5 | Payment speed; leakage |
| Report return rate | Reports returned / submitted | Billing integrity |
| Revenue per employment specialist | Fee revenue / FTE specialists (quarterly) | Productivity |
| Ticket payments | $ and count of P1/P2/outcome payments; active Tickets assigned | Unrestricted revenue |
| WIPA reach | Beneficiaries served, BS&As completed, wait time to first contact | Contract performance |
| Months of net assets / cash | Net assets (and cash) / monthly expenses (quarterly) | Resilience |
| Web/LMS contract revenue and pipeline | $ booked, proposals out | Replacing VRTAC-QE |

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Hackathon projects should map to opportunity #1, #3, #4 or #5 and report a KPI from the table.
- Tools must NOT make individual benefits determinations, store client PII in prototypes, or show unsourced outcome claims.

# ERI digital footprint

## TL;DR
- ERI runs a real in-house web and LMS shop: 6 of 29 listed staff are training, web or graphic design roles. It builds and maintains sites for federal TA centers (NTACT:C, VRTAC-QE, GW-CRCRE/CIT-VR), Wisconsin DHS, and its own youth-transition brands.
- The stack is **WordPress**. The Training Center sits on a multisite install (`sites/13` upload path). Skip links target `#x-main`, which suggests the **Themeco X/Pro theme (likely, not confirmed)**.
- The flagship **ERI Training Center has visible placeholder content**: "Time and Date | $XX" on four paid courses, six lorem-ipsum "Organization Name" cards with "#" links, and 2023 trainings still shown as upcoming.
- One client site has wound down: **VRTAC-QE's grant period has ended**, and its resources stay up "through 2026". That is a revenue line to replace.

## Key facts

| Site | Owner / funder (as stated on site) | ERI role | Observed tech | Status / issues |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| eri-wi.org | ERI | Owner | WordPress (`wp-content/uploads`), Candid widget, site search | Active, (c) 2026. Some deep links return a "redirecting" page to automated fetchers |
| training.eri-wi.org (ERI Training Center) | ERI. DHS-funded CIE courses | Owner | WordPress multisite (`sites/13`), `#x-main` (X/Pro likely), `/courses/` LMS structure, LMS plugin unnamed | "$XX" prices, lorem ipsum, 2023 WIBS / Mental Health Forum dates, duplicated sections |
| training.eri-wi.org/widhs-cie/ | WI DHS CIE initiative | Host | same | Last modified 2023-12-15. Typo "pursing". Generic "Image" alt text. Twitter link |
| beforeage18.org | "Created by Employment Resources, Inc." (funder not named) | Built and maintains | WordPress, `x-main`, OG tags | **Family Transition Planning Tool: 5 questions** produce a custom guide by age, graduation plans, health, benefits status, and family comfort. Mislabeled "Action Steps for Teens" button. `/benefits/` vs `/benefits-and-working/` mismatch |
| transitiondiscoveries.org | **PA Developmental Disabilities Council** grant 1801PABSDD (ACL) | "Powered by ERI" | WordPress, **GTranslate** (English/Spanish), Instagram embed | Active, (c) 2026. 150+ gamified resources, Discovery Cards for sale |
| explore-work.com / .org | Not confirmed | Training, web, enrollment (per ERI) | .org redirects to http://explore-work.com | Content not readable by our fetcher **(verify)** |
| transitionta.org (NTACT:C) | U.S. Dept. of Education grant 8236E250006 | Web dev, maintenance, webinars, accessibility (per ERI) | WordPress, Qualtrics TA form | Active. Footer does not credit ERI |
| tacqe.com (VRTAC-QE) | U.S. Dept. of Education grant H264K200003 | "Designed and managed by ERI" | WordPress, Slider Revolution 7.2.0, mixed http/https links | **Grant ended**. Resources up through 2026. Last modified 2026-02-24 |
| gwcrcre.org / TrainVR.org (CIT-VR) | George Washington University CRCRE | Web, events, enrollment (per ERI) | WordPress, LayerSlider 8.4.1, og:locale en_GB | Active. GW site does not mention ERI |
| promisewi.com, projecte3.com | Wisconsin Promise, Project E3 | "Recent" projects | not checked | Past projects |
| WI ADRC training, WDBN, CIE series | WI DHS | Training materials and LMS | ERI LMS | No public URL for ADRC/WDBN |

## How it works
- ERI sells this work three ways: fee for service, grant collaboration (ERI as subrecipient), and agency contracts (per the Training and Design page).
- One team maintains many WordPress sites. A multisite install lowers hosting cost, but each premium plugin (sliders, LMS, translation) adds patching and licensing work.
- The Training Center doubles as the public storefront for ERI's paid trainings (WIBS, Ticket to Work, WPA, Positive Behavior Supports). Placeholder prices make that storefront unusable for buyers.

## Caveats and gotchas
- Theme and plugin identification is from page markup only. "X/Pro" is inferred from `#x-main` **(verify)**. The LMS plugin is not named **(verify)**.
- The tech-stack observations come from an automated reader. Confirm in wp-admin before planning any upgrade.
- Before Age 18's funder is not named on the home page **(verify)**. Transition Discoveries is Pennsylvania-funded, not Wisconsin-funded.
- Plugin versions (Slider Revolution 7.2.0, LayerSlider 8.4.1) should be checked against current security advisories **(verify)**.
- Don't confuse attribution with ownership. ERI's page lists NTACT:C and GW-CRCRE as clients, but those sites don't name ERI.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Quick wins:** fix the Training Center placeholders, past dates and lorem ipsum. Add real prices or "contact for pricing". Remove empty "Related Training" cards. Fix the Before Age 18 button and link mismatches. Run an accessibility pass on alt text.
- A hackathon project can export the Before Age 18 5-question logic as an open, documented rules file so other sites can reuse it. ERI must approve and own the content.
- Any new tool should plug into the existing WordPress multisite or run as a static add-on. Don't bring a new stack the 6-person team can't maintain.
- Do NOT scrape or copy client-owned (federal TA center) content into hackathon repos without that client's permission.

# ERI financial history (FY2011-FY2025)

## TL;DR
- ERI's revenue doubled from about $1.5M (FY2011-FY2015) to about $3.0-3.3M (FY2018-FY2025), then stopped growing. FY2025: **$3,065,352 revenue, $3,038,876 expenses, $26,476 surplus (0.9% margin)**.
- Margins are thin. Over 15 years ERI netted a cumulative **$298,935**, and 5 of the 15 years were losses (worst: FY2018, -$326,102).
- The mix shifted from contribution-led (80% in FY2011) to fee-led (55-71% program service revenue since FY2017). On the 990, "contributions" includes government grants such as the SSA WIPA cooperative agreement, so 45% "contributions" is not 45% private philanthropy.
- FY2020 shows a one-time bump ($312,953 surplus) in the year ERI received a PPP loan (approved 2020-04-07, $350K-$1M range, 40 jobs).

## Key facts

Fiscal year = calendar year (ProPublica lists "fiscal year ending Dec."). Figures are from the ProPublica-extracted Form 990 data.

| FY | Total revenue | Total expenses | Net income | Margin | Net assets (EOY) | Total liabilities | Contributions & grants | Program service revenue | Program % of revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 3,065,352 | 3,038,876 | 26,476 | 0.9% | 701,212 | 638,029 | 1,366,910 | 1,679,493 | 54.8% |
| 2024 | 3,105,085 | 3,136,678 | -31,593 | -1.0% | 674,736 | 625,394 | 1,207,239 | 1,881,765 | 60.6% |
| 2023 | 3,189,763 | 3,111,783 | 77,980 | 2.4% | 706,329 | 729,694 | 1,293,824 | 1,878,734 | 58.9% |
| 2022 | 3,032,080 | 3,193,430 | -161,350 | -5.3% | 628,349 | 866,638 | 1,039,395 | 1,979,770 | 65.3% |
| 2021 | 3,130,450 | 3,074,989 | 55,461 | 1.8% | 789,699 | 255,013 | 1,332,252 | 1,793,282 | 57.3% |
| 2020 | 3,349,553 | 3,036,600 | 312,953 | 9.3% | 734,238 | 220,093 | 1,447,232 | 1,895,114 | 56.6% |
| 2019 | 2,974,996 | 2,976,537 | -1,541 | -0.1% | 421,285 | 208,228 | 833,168 | 2,124,219 | 71.4% |
| 2018 | 3,034,997 | 3,361,099 | -326,102 | -10.7% | 422,826 | 214,870 | 1,492,950 | 1,539,533 | 50.7% |
| 2017 | 2,426,369 | 2,417,414 | 8,955 | 0.4% | 748,928 | 103,732 | 1,063,589 | 1,361,457 | 56.1% |
| 2016 | 2,190,140 | 1,976,112 | 214,028 | 9.8% | 739,973 | 102,899 | 1,275,623 | 913,861 | 41.7% |
| 2015 | 1,541,871 | 1,474,771 | 67,100 | 4.4% | 525,945 | 117,318 | 779,124 | 762,315 | 49.4% |
| 2014 | 1,630,788 | 1,572,260 | 58,528 | 3.6% | 458,845 | 44,703 | 859,700 | 770,766 | 47.3% |
| 2013 | 1,500,590 | 1,569,986 | -69,396 | -4.6% | 400,317 | 62,180 | 830,817 | 669,435 | 44.6% |
| 2012 | 1,511,297 | 1,463,590 | 47,707 | 3.2% | 469,713 | 159,770 | 963,041 | 547,854 | 36.3% |
| 2011 | 1,554,186 | 1,534,457 | 19,729 | 1.3% | 422,006 | 117,200 | 1,244,674 | 308,849 | 19.9% |

Other data points:

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Total assets, FY2025 | $1,339,241 | ProPublica |
| Executive compensation line, FY2025 | $119,409 (FY2024: $144,353, includes two EDs in a transition year) | ProPublica |
| Investment income, FY2023 | $8,989 | ProPublica API |
| Net assets / monthly expenses, FY2025 | about 2.8 months (701,212 / 253,240) | Derived |
| Cumulative net income FY2011-FY2025 | $298,935 (ties to the change in net assets) | Derived |
| PPP loan | Approved 2020-04-07; Oregon Community Bank; range $350,000-$1M; 40 jobs; NAICS 813219; nonprofit | pppreport.org |
| FY2001-FY2010 | Filings exist as PDFs only; no extracted figures | ProPublica |

## How it works
- **Program service revenue** is what ERI earns by delivering services: DVR milestone fees, Ticket to Work payments, Dane County CCS billing, and training or web-design contracts. It pays only when work is done and reported.
- **Contributions and grants** on Form 990 Part VIII line 1 mixes government grants and cooperative agreements (SSA WIPA, state DHS projects, federal TA subcontracts if structured as grants) with private gifts. ProPublica's extract does not split line 1e (government grants) from private gifts.
- **Two growth steps:** revenue jumped from $1.54M (FY2015) to $2.19M (FY2016) and $3.03M (FY2018). The ERI timeline credits that era with customized employment in seven Wisconsin workforce areas (2017). After FY2018, revenue has stayed between $2.97M and $3.35M for eight years.
- **Losses cluster in transition years:** FY2018 (-$326K) came at the end of the growth spurt. FY2022 (-$161K) was the year ERI moved offices (the About page says it moved to the Acewood location in 2022).
- **Liabilities tripled in FY2022** ($255K to $867K) while revenue was flat. That matches the 2022 office move and would fit an operating lease being recorded on the balance sheet. **(verify)** in the audited statements / Schedule D.
- **FY2025 mix shift:** program service revenue fell $202,272 (-10.7%) and contributions rose $159,671 (+13.2%). The filing alone does not show which programs drove it. **(verify)**

## Caveats and gotchas
- ProPublica figures are extracted from IRS e-files. The full-filing view did not render when we opened it, so Part III (program expenses), Part VIII line 1e and Schedule O were **not** read. **(verify)** against the PDF or ERI's audit.
- **PPP accounting:** ERI's About page lists "Paycheck Protection Program (2020)" among its supporters, and pppreport.org shows the loan. The exact amount, forgiveness, and whether it was booked as FY2020 or FY2021 grant income are not confirmed. The FY2020 surplus is consistent with forgiveness being recognized in 2020. **(verify)**
- Net assets are not cash. Some of the $701K may be fixed assets or restricted money. Liquidity is **(verify)**.
- The FY2024 executive compensation figure covers an ED transition (ProPublica notes two EDs that year). Do not read it as a raise.
- Wisconsin DVR started a waitlist in December 2025 and began activating people from it on 2026-06-02, with a goal of ending it by 2027-06-30 (see [sector trends](sector-trends-2025-2026.md)). FY2025 numbers do not yet show that effect. FY2026 likely will. **(verify)** when the FY2026 990 is filed.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Treat ERI as a **cash-constrained, fee-dependent** organization. A tool that adds staff time without lifting billable outcomes or cutting admin work is a net cost.
- Good targets: speeding up DVR report submission (fees are paid only after reports are accepted), Ticket payment tracking, and grant reporting.
- A dashboard built from this page must label "contributions" as "contributions **and government grants**". It must not present 45% as private donations.
- Do NOT publish internal financial projections or non-public numbers in the wiki. Use only filed 990 data.

# ERI programs deep dive

## TL;DR
- ERI runs **three different payment engines**: (1) **outcome/milestone fees** (DVR, Ticket to Work), paid only after a result is documented; (2) a **cooperative agreement** with SSA for WIPA, a budgeted award (2021 RFA: $50K-$300K per award, period 2021-07-01 to 2026-06-30); (3) **contracts** with Dane County (CCS), Wisconsin DHS, and federal TA centers for training and web work.
- WIPA: ERI says it has been the **sole Wisconsin WIPA agency since 2021**. SSA funds 74 WIPA agencies nationally. ERI's dollar award could **not** be confirmed (usaspending.gov did not render) **(verify)**.
- Public outcome claims are thin: "more than 80+" Ticket "graduates" (no timeframe), an "Excellent" EN satisfaction rating, and "hundreds" helped into jobs.
- 29 staff are listed. Most are Employment Specialists (6) and benefits staff (6), plus a 6-person training/web team.

## Key facts

| Program | Funder / payer | Payment mechanism | Geography | Public outcome claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WIPA** (Work Incentives Planning & Assistance) | SSA, Office of Research, Demonstration and Employment Support | Cooperative agreement (budgeted award, not per-client). 2021 RFA: about 75 awards, $20M total, $50K floor, $300K ceiling, no match | Wisconsin. ERI says "sole agency for the WIPA project with SSA" since 2021 | None published. Referral line 1-877-826-1752 |
| **ERI PLUS** (Ticket to Work Employment Network) | SSA Ticket to Work | Outcome-based: SSA pays milestones and outcomes and does not reimburse costs | WI, OH, IN, IL, MN, IA, MI. Mostly virtual | "More than 80+ people have 'graduated'". "Excellent" in national EN satisfaction surveys |
| **DVR Supported Employment / Job Development** | Wisconsin DVR (federal RSA formula grant 78.7%, state 21.3%) | Fee-for-service milestones on purchase orders. Report deadlines gate payment | Statewide. Staff bios name Milwaukee, Green Bay, NE and NW Wisconsin, Madison | None published **(verify)** |
| **Work Incentives Benefits Counseling / Benefits Applications** | DVR, counties, other purchasers **(verify)** | Fee-for-service **(verify)** | Wisconsin | None published |
| **Dane County CCS** | Dane County CCS. ERI's page says it is funded through WI DHS | County program; provider billing terms not public **(verify)** | Dane County | Demand above capacity: "currently experiencing delays" |
| **Youth transition** (VFPS Youth Transition Navigation, CLTS Youth & Family, Dane County Youth Transition Coordinator) | Counties / DHS CLTS waiver **(verify)** | Contract or waiver billing **(verify)** | Dane County and others **(verify)** | None published |
| **Pre-Driving Assessment** | **(verify)** | **(verify)** | **(verify)** | None |
| **Training & Design shop** | Federal TA centers (ED-funded), WI DHS (ADRCs, WDBN, CIE series), PA DD Council (Transition Discoveries) | "Fee for service, grant collaboration, and agency contracts" | National | Wisconsin Promise "served 2,000 families of teens receiving SSI" |
| **Business & Employer Services** | Employers | Fee for service, grant collaboration, agency contracts | WI and beyond | Cites Accenture 2023 research, not ERI results |

### Ticket to Work payments, 2026 (Milestone/Outcome system)
| Payment | Trigger | SSDI | SSI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 milestones (4) | Earnings at or above $1,210/month for 1, 3 of 6, 6 of 12, 9 of 18 months | $1,904 each, $7,616 total | same |
| Phase 2 milestones | Earnings at or above SGA while still in cash status | 11 x $571 = $6,281 | 18 x $319 = $5,742 |
| Outcome payments | Benefits stop because of work | 36 x $571 = $20,556 | 60 x $319 = $19,140 |

### DVR Supported Employment fees (effective 2026-07-01 to 2028-06-30)
| Milestone | Fee | Timing rule |
|---|---|---|
| Career Profile | $1,000 | Start within 30 days of PO, finish within 90 |
| Job Prep & Development Plan | $350 | Finish within 45 days |
| Job Development & Hire | $1,600 standard; $2,000 or $2,200 preferred | Hire report within 5 business days |
| Job & Task Analysis | $275 | Within 1 week of start |
| Monthly Systematic Instruction | $1,600/month | Monthly report within 5 business days of month end |
| Retention only | $500/month | same |
| Transition to LTS | $1,300 (up to 6 months); $500 (more than 6) | After at least 90 days employed |

Regular Job Development: Plan $550; Hire up to $1,900 (Rapid Hire); Retention $1,600 standard or **$2,200 preferred** (paid at 30/60/90 days).

## How it works
- **WIPA** is free benefits counseling by Community Work Incentive Coordinators (CWICs) for SSDI/SSI beneficiaries aged 14 to full retirement age who are working, have a job offer, are interviewing, are veterans, or are aged 14-25. SSA set it up under the Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act of 1999. It is authorized under Section 1149 of the Social Security Act. Awardees must serve at least 5 business days a week and need SSA Tier 2 suitability for staff.
- **Ticket to Work** pays ERI only when an assigned beneficiary earns. A long-run SSDI outcome is worth up to $34,453 ($7,616 + $6,281 + $20,556) over several years. That is unrestricted revenue, but it lags service by months to years.
- **DVR** issues a purchase order per milestone. ERI earns nothing until the report is submitted and accepted. A returned report must be fixed within 10 business days. Preferred outcomes pay $400-$600 more per hire. Preferred-outcome criteria (DVR appendix): $2,200 for 35+ h/week and (health insurance or ≥ $16.00/h); $2,000 for 20+ h/week and (health insurance or ≥ $12.00/h). Source: https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/service-providers/tech-specs/appendix.htm
- **CCS** is a Dane County program for people with mental health or substance use needs. ERI provides the employment, benefits and education pieces. ERI's page says capacity is below demand.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The WIPA 2021-2026 project period ended **2026-06-30**. ERI's WIPA page was live on 2026-10-23, but we found no public record of the follow-on award, extension, or amount **(verify)**.
- ERI's dollar award on usaspending.gov could not be read (the site needs JavaScript) **(verify)**. The $300K ceiling is per award. ERI may hold more than one award **(verify)**.
- "More than 80+ graduates" is ERI's own wording. Its definition (Ticket outcome status? job?) and timeframe are not stated **(verify)**.
- ERI's employment-counseling waitlist is "closed to new referrals" (CCS page). That limits fee growth.
- DVR ran a statewide waitlist from December 2025. That cut new DVR purchase orders to all vendors until it began unwinding on 2026-06-02 (see [sector trends](sector-trends-2025-2026.md)).

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Build for the **payment trigger**. A DVR report helper that hits the 5-business-day rule, or a Ticket earnings tracker that spots Phase 1 milestones, turns directly into cash.
- A benefits-counseling assistant must route to a CWIC (1-877-826-1752) and must NOT give individual benefits determinations.
- Do NOT store beneficiary PII in hackathon prototypes. WIPA staff need SSA Tier 2 suitability, and tools must respect that.

# Funders and grant opportunities for ERI

## TL;DR
- **Best near-term fits:** United Way of Dane County (Otto Bremer "disability services" fund, up to $75K; workforce training up to $47K; Impact Grants reopen spring 2027), Madison Community Foundation (Dane County program or capacity grants; LOI due in June), and **Kessler Foundation** (national; ERI's ~$3.07M budget clears the $2M Signature and $1M Community thresholds).
- **Milwaukee expansion funders:** Greater Milwaukee Foundation (workforce development is a priority) and United Way GMWC. GMWC's "Reducing Barriers to Employment" cycle runs 07/2026-06/2028, is closed, and **no further cycles are anticipated**.
- **Weak fits as checked:** Bader Philanthropies lists no workforce or disability area today. DOL ODEP lists no grants and its budget is shrinking. The RSA Disability Innovation Fund goes to state VR agencies, so ERI could only join as a subrecipient.
- **Tech in-kind:** Microsoft 365 Business Basic free up to 300 users, Azure $2,000/yr, Google Ad Grants up to $10,000/month, Salesforce 10 free licenses.

## Key facts

| Funder | Focus (as stated on its site) | Typical grant / terms | Timing | Fit for ERI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **United Way of Dane County** | Youth Opportunity, Financial Security, Healthy Community. Otto Bremer fund includes "disability services" | Otto Bremer up to $75K (about $550K for Dane). Customized Workforce Training up to $47K (jobs at $22/hr or more). Impact Grants are 2-year | Impact Grants next open **spring 2027**. Bremer and Workforce windows were May 2026 | **High**. Employment, benefits, local |
| **Madison Community Foundation** | Arts, capacity building, community development, environment, learning (incl. transition-to-adult) | No published max. About 20% funded. No ongoing operations. 1/3 raised beforehand encouraged | LOI portal opens March, LOIs due June, decisions October | **Medium-high**. Capacity-building (e.g. KB/AI tool, CRM) or youth-transition project |
| **Kessler Foundation** (NJ, national) | Employment of people with disabilities | Community Employment Grants need a budget over $1M. Signature (multi-year) needs over $2M. Indirect capped at 15% / 8%. No general operating | Online eligibility quiz, then concept; 1 application per year | **High**. Preferred-outcome job development or employer pilot |
| **Greater Milwaukee Foundation** | Priorities include workforce development. Area: Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Washington, Waukesha | Operating, project and program grants; 1 application per cycle; amounts not posted | Cycle-based; portal at grantinterface.com | **Medium**. Only with a real Milwaukee presence (2 Milwaukee-area specialists listed) |
| **United Way of Greater Milwaukee & Waukesha County** | Key Initiatives incl. "Reducing Barriers to Employment & Advancement" (15,000 people by 2029) | Amounts not posted. LOI required. 501(c)(3), 1+ year local operation | Employment cycle 07/2026-06/2028, **closed, no further cycles anticipated** | **Low now**. Watch the Opportunity and Urgent Need funds |
| **Bader Philanthropies** (Milwaukee) | Healthy Aging/Alzheimer's, Revitalizing Milwaukee (Youth Development, Urban Education, Neighborhoods, Addiction Recovery), International, Founders | Not posted. Preliminary application. Deadlines **May 31 / Nov 30** | Rolling with two deadlines | **Low**. No workforce or disability area listed. Only a youth-development angle in the City of Milwaukee |
| **WI BPDD** | Federally authorized DD council. Over 70% of funds go to local projects | Families Supporting Families (2025): up to 8 x $20K or 1 x $40K, aimed at communities of color and Spanish/Hmong speakers | Posted 2025-07-28 | **Medium**. Youth-transition family outreach with a culturally specific partner |
| **DOL ODEP** | Policy and TA: JAN, EARN, PEAT, LEAD, CAPE-Youth | No grants listed. FY2026 enacted $43.0M, 46 FTE. FY2027 request $33.81M, ends Employment Transition Models grants | n/a | **Low** as a funder. Use JAN/EARN as free employer-services content |
| **ED / RSA Disability Innovation Fund** | e.g. SWTCIE: 14 five-year awards, about $177M (2022), to **state VR agencies** | Subrecipient only | Irregular | **Low-medium**. Partner through WI DVR or a university if a new DIF round opens **(verify)** |
| **SSA** | WIPA cooperative agreements (ERI is the incumbent); Ticket to Work outcome payments | 2021 RFA: $50K-$300K per award | Next WIPA competition **(verify)** | **Core** |
| **Mitsubishi Electric America Foundation** | "Empower youth with disabilities to lead productive lives" | Not posted | "Apply for a Grant" page not opened **(verify)** | **Medium**. Youth transition / Before Age 18 |
| **Microsoft** | Nonprofit tech | M365 Business Basic free up to 300 users; Business Premium $5.50/user/month; Azure $2,000/yr | Register to confirm eligibility | **High**. Cost savings plus Azure for the KB/AI pilot |
| **Google for Nonprofits** | Ad Grants, Workspace for Nonprofits, YouTube Nonprofit, Maps credits | Ad Grants **up to $10,000/month** in search ads. Goodstack validation | 2-14 working days to validate | **High**. Drive referrals to WIPA, Ticket, trainings |
| **Salesforce Power of Us** | CRM | 10 free Nonprofit Cloud or Sales/Service Cloud licenses, discounts after that | Apply via Trailblazer ID | **Medium**. Only if ERI wants a CRM it can maintain |
| **TechSoup** | Donated / discounted software | Site did not load for us **(verify)** | n/a | Medium |

## How it works
- Most local funders (UW Dane, MCF, GMF) fund **projects or capacity, not operations**. A good pitch pairs a concrete project (e.g., a benefits-counselor knowledge base) with measurable outcomes.
- Kessler requires collaborators and other funding. A pitch with WI DVR or an employer partner plus a hackathon-built prototype is a stronger story.
- Federal disability-employment money mostly reaches ERI **through** state agencies (DVR, DHS) or SSA. That is why diversified private money matters.

## Caveats and gotchas
- Grants.gov was not searched in this pass (search budget ran out) **(verify)** for open SSA, ODEP or RSA notices.
- Kessler's 2009 Signature page said the focus was New Jersey. The current FAQ says grants are limited to the U.S. and territories, and Special Initiative grants are NJ-only. Confirm current Signature geography **(verify)**.
- Bader historically funded workforce programs (older news headlines). Its current site does not list them **(verify)** before writing it off.
- UW Dane's FEMA EFSP window was listed both as "closed" and with September 2026 dates on the same page.
- Dollar amounts and deadlines change each cycle. Re-check before applying.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A grants calendar tool could track the windows above (UW Dane spring, MCF March-June, Bader May 31/Nov 30, Kessler annual) with an owner and status for each.
- An AI grant-drafting helper must use only ERI-approved facts (from the [financial history](eri-financial-history.md) and [programs](eri-programs-deep-dive.md) pages) and must flag claims that need sources. It must NOT invent outcome numbers.

# Hackathon value plan

## TL;DR
- Most hackathon code dies within a month. ERI avoids that by deciding **before 2026-10-31** who owns the code, which license applies (MIT), who triages it, and which 1-2 projects it will actually adopt.
- Adopt only what ERI's **6-person web/training team** can maintain on its existing WordPress stack. Pick projects tied to a KPI in the [consulting brief](consulting-brief.md) (days-to-report, preferred-outcome %, Ticket payments, counselor time saved).
- Turn the event into **three lasting assets**: a volunteer pipeline, employer visibility, and a measured impact story for funders (MCF capacity building; Kessler requires collaborators and other funding).

## Key facts

| Item | Decision / fact |
|---|---|
| Event date | 2026-10-31 |
| Code owner | ERI GitHub organization (ERI admins); volunteers contribute under the repo license |
| License | MIT for code; content (KB text, training material) stays ERI-owned unless ERI releases it |
| Data rule | Public and synthetic data only. No client PII, no case notes |
| Maintainers | ERI senior web developer (tech) + one program owner per adopted project |
| Platform constraint | WordPress multisite (existing); static or small add-ons preferred |
| In-kind to lean on | Azure $2,000/yr credits; M365 Business Basic free up to 300 users |
| Funder hooks | MCF capacity-building grants (LOI due June); Kessler Community/Signature grants (ERI budget over $2M) |

## How it works

### Before the event (by 2026-10-30)
- Create an ERI-owned GitHub organization with an MIT `LICENSE`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a code of conduct, and an issue template per challenge. MIT is confirmed (2026-10-23).
- Write a one-page "definition of done" for each challenge: user, KPI, data source, what the tool must NOT do.
- Publish a "no PII" rule and give teams synthetic sample data.
- Get a signed (or click-through) contributor acknowledgment that work is MIT-licensed and that ERI may reuse it.

### On the day
- Every team demos against its KPI and its "must NOT do" list.
- An ERI review panel (program lead, web lead, a benefits specialist) scores each project on value, maintainability, safety, and accessibility (WCAG).

### Triage and adoption (week 1-2)
- **Adopt** (1-2 projects): ERI assigns an owner, a backlog and a release date.
- **Incubate** (2-3): volunteers keep working with an ERI mentor; review again at day 60.
- **Archive** the rest with a README saying what was learned.

### Volunteer pipeline
- Invite top contributors to a standing "ERI Tech Volunteers" group with monthly office hours and labeled "good first issues".
- Offer accessible, remote roles. Volunteers with disabilities are a natural fit and a mission signal.

### Employer visibility
- Thank sponsoring and participating employers publicly (with their consent). Invite them to an inclusive-hiring follow-up, which feeds opportunity #6 in the consulting brief.

### Impact story for funders
- Measure baseline vs after for adopted tools: minutes saved per counselor session, % of DVR reports filed within 5 business days, placeholder fixes shipped.
- Package results into a 2-page brief for MCF, UW Dane and Kessler conversations.

## 30/60/90-day follow-up

| Window | Dates | Deliverables | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **30 days** | by 2026-11-30 | Triage done. 1-2 projects adopted with owners. Repos cleaned (license, README, security check). Training Center placeholder fixes live. Thank-you and results post. Volunteer group launched | ED + senior web developer |
| **60 days** | by 2026-12-30 | First adopted tool piloted with 3-5 staff (human review on; synthetic data until ERI's AI policy, data agreements and any DVR AI consent are in place). Baseline KPIs captured. Incubated projects reviewed (adopt or archive). Employer follow-up meeting held | Program owner + client services director |
| **90 days** | by 2027-01-29 | Pilot results vs baseline. Go/no-go for production. Funder brief written. Grant calendar set (MCF LOI, UW Dane spring 2027, Kessler). Next hackathon or sprint decided | ED + finance director |

## Caveats and gotchas
- An MIT license lets anyone reuse the code, competitors included. That's fine for tools; keep proprietary training content separate.
- Volunteer-built AI tools must not go live without CWIC review, dated sources, and a clear "not advice" disclaimer routing to WIPA (1-877-826-1752).
- Federal TA-center sites (NTACT:C, VRTAC-QE, GW-CRCRE) belong to their clients. Don't use their content or credentials at the event.
- Staff time is the scarcest resource. Adopting more than two projects is a likely failure mode (our judgment, not a sourced finding).

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Teams should read this page and the [consulting brief](consulting-brief.md) KPIs first.
- A project that cannot name its ERI owner, KPI and maintenance plan by demo time should be archived, not adopted.

# Sector trends 2025-2026

## TL;DR
- **Wisconsin DVR is the biggest near-term shock.** DVR started a waitlist for new participants in **December 2025** after a $4.6M state shortfall. It reached **7,610 people on 2026-06-02**. Recovery money came from the Joint Finance Committee ($0.6M SFY26 + $6.4M SFY27, 2026-06-02) and an **$11.05M federal reallotment** (2026-08-31). The goal is to clear the waitlist by **2027-06-30**. DWD warns funding will not cover the next biennium.
- **H.R. 1 (P.L. 119-21, enacted 2025-07-04)** adds an 80-hour/month Medicaid "community engagement" rule. It covers Wisconsin's roughly 190,000 BadgerCare childless adults (April 2026 enrollment; DHS's 2026-07-30 webinar says about 200,000 are subject, see [Medicaid work requirements](../benefits/medicaid-work-requirements-2027.md)) and takes effect in 2027. It also widened SNAP ABAWD time limits to ages 18-64.
- **SSA** set a staffing target of 50,000, down from about 57,000, and is cutting from 10 regions to 4 (2025-02-28). The WIPA 2021 agreements ran to **2026-06-30**. What follows is not confirmed **(verify)**.
- **14(c):** DOL withdrew the phase-out rule on 2025-07-07, so subminimum-wage certificates continue. **ODEP:** FY2026 enacted **$43.0M** (flat), with FTE down from 65 to 46. The FY2027 request is $33.81M.

## Key facts

| Date | Change | Number | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-02-28 | SSA workforce plan | 57,000 to 50,000 staff; 10 to 4 regions; VSIP/VERA; RIF plans due 2025-03-13 | SSA press release |
| 2025-03-21 | SSA to recompete WIPA National Training and Data Center (NTDC) | 12-month base + 4 options | OrangeSlices |
| 2025-07-04 | H.R. 1 / P.L. 119-21 enacted. SNAP changes effective on enactment | ABAWD age 18-54 becomes 18-64; child exception now under 14 only; veteran, homeless and former-foster-youth exceptions removed | USDA FNS memo 2025-10-03 |
| 2025-07-07 | DOL withdraws 14(c) phase-out NPRM (RIN 1235-AA14; NPRM of 2024-12-04) | Any change needs a new rulemaking | Federal Register |
| 2025 (FY26 request) | President's budget: VR State Grants up to $4.504B; **Supported Employment State Grants $22.5M to $0**; ODEP $43.0M to $33.8M | Proposal, not law | ADvancing States; DOL CBJ FY2026 |
| 2025-11-03 | DVR shortfall announced | $21.3M state appropriation for FY2026, $4.6M short; about 2,000 people + 1,000/month affected | DWD |
| Dec 2025 | DVR waitlist (Order of Selection) begins | First in over a decade (per advocates) | DWD 2026-06-02; Channel3000 |
| 2026-06-01 | CMS Interim Final Rule on Medicaid community engagement | 80 hrs/month or $580/month income; ages 19-64; states must implement by 2027-01-01 | NACo |
| 2026-06-02 | JFC releases DVR funds; activation begins | $600K SFY26 + $6.4M SFY27; 7,610 on waitlist | DWD |
| 2026-06-10 | WI DHS begins notifying BadgerCare childless adults | About 190,000 enrolled (April 2026); effective 2027 | Wisconsin Examiner |
| 2026-06-30 | WIPA 2021 project period ends | 74 agencies funded since 2021-07-01 | HigherGov RFA; SSA |
| 2026-08-31 | DVR federal reallotment | $11.05M awarded of $23.5M requested; Category 1 expected off the waitlist by 2026-09-01; DWD expects no need to restart a waitlist through FFY2027 | Governor / DWD |
| FY2026 enacted | ODEP | $43.0M, 46 FTE (FY2025: $43.0M, 65 FTE) | DOL CBJ FY2027 |
| FY2027 request | ODEP | $33.81M; ends Employment Transition Models grants | DOL CBJ FY2027 |

## How it works
- **DVR funding** is 78.7% federal RSA and 21.3% state. When the state match falls short, DVR can't draw all its federal money, so it uses an Order of Selection: Category 1 (most significant), then 2, then 3. Vendors like ERI get fewer new purchase orders, while existing plans continue.
- **BadgerCare work requirement:** Wisconsin did not adopt full ACA expansion. It does cover childless adults up to the poverty line, and the federal rule applies to that group. Medically frail people and others are exempt. DHS must send a noncompliance notice and allow 30 days before ending coverage (per the CMS IFR summary).
- **WIPA** is a fixed set of cooperative agreements. A gap between agreements, or a smaller award, hits benefits-counseling capacity directly.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **SSI/SSDI recipients:** the sources opened for this page did not settle this. The [Medicaid work requirements](../benefits/medicaid-work-requirements-2027.md) page, built from the Wisconsin DHS work page and 2026-07-30 webinar, lists SSI Medicaid, MAPP, Family Care, IRIS, people with an SSA disability determination and Medicare enrollees as not subject. Use that page.
- No public record of the post-2026-06-30 WIPA awards, extension, or Wisconsin amount was found **(verify)**. ERI's WIPA page is still live.
- **PABSS** (Protection and Advocacy for Beneficiaries of Social Security) funding status for 2025-2026 was not confirmed **(verify)**.
- **SSA field office** closures and visit-reduction plans were reported in the press (December 2025). The primary SSA release we opened makes no field-office statement **(verify)**.
- **VR State Grants FY2026 final appropriation** was not confirmed. Only the request was seen **(verify)**. The Supported Employment State Grants zero-out is a request **(verify)** whether it was enacted.
- Grants.gov was not searched in this pass (search budget ran out).

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Benefits counselors** will get questions about the 80-hour BadgerCare rule. A KB entry should explain it, link to DHS, and route people to WIPA or Disability Rights Wisconsin. It must NOT tell anyone whether they are exempt.
- **ERI planning:** model FY2026 DVR fee revenue as down, with recovery in 2027. Build a waitlist re-activation surge plan (Category 1 first).
- A tool must date every rule it shows. These rules are moving, and stale guidance can cost people coverage.

# Wisconsin disability employment landscape (index)

## TL;DR
- Four state agencies run the system:
  - **DWD**: DVR, the workforce boards, apprenticeship and the Equal Rights Division
  - **DHS**: ADRCs, Family Care, IRIS, CLTS and CCS
  - **DPI**: school transition
  - **WisDOT**: s. 85.21 transportation aid
- Counties and nonprofits deliver most services.
- Southern Wisconsin spans **five WDAs**: 1 (Kenosha, Racine, Walworth), 2 (Milwaukee), 3 (Waukesha, Ozaukee, Washington), 10 (South Central, including Dane) and 11 (Southwest, including Rock).
- The facts that matter most in late 2026:
  - the **DVR waitlist** (December 2025 to a target of 2027-06-30)
  - the **WDA 10 provider-capacity gap**
  - the **2027 MCO changes in the southeast counties**

## Key facts
| Page | Answers |
|---|---|
| [dvr-structure-and-process.md](dvr-structure-and-process.md) | DVR offices, the referral-to-closure flow, Order of Selection, vendor fees, FFY2025 outcomes (33,687 served; 3,429 jobs; $17.04/hour; 24.89 hours/week) |
| [long-term-care-system.md](long-term-care-system.md) | ADRCs, MCOs by county, IRIS ICAs, CLTS, the DVR-to-long-term-support handoff |
| [advocacy-and-legal-help.md](advocacy-and-legal-help.md) | DRW and CAP, BPDD, CPD, Survival Coalition, Legal Action, ABLE, ERD |

| [peer-providers-southern-wi.md](peer-providers-southern-wi.md) | Peer and partner providers (low confidence) |

## How it works
Start at the page for the person's question. Each page follows the [page spec](../_PAGE_SPEC.md): TL;DR, Key facts, How it works, Caveats, ERI and tool use, then Sources.

## Caveats and gotchas
- All facts come from pages opened on 2026-10-23. Items marked **(verify)** could not be confirmed.
- The search budget ran out during research. County programs other than Dane and Milwaukee, chambers, Disability:IN, and several peer providers are thin.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Treat these pages as **routing knowledge**: which agency, which office, which phone number. They are not eligibility rules.
- Never present a tool's output as a decision by DVR, DHS or a county.

# Disability advocacy and legal help in Wisconsin

## TL;DR
- **Disability Rights Wisconsin (DRW)** is the state's protection and advocacy organization. Since **2021-09-30** it has also run the **Client Assistance Program (CAP)** for people with concerns about DVR or an Independent Living Center. DATCP ran CAP before that. DRW's toll-free number is **800-928-8778**.
- **Employment discrimination** complaints under the Wisconsin Fair Employment Act (Wis. Stat. §§ 111.31-111.395) go to DWD's **Equal Rights Division** within **300 days**.
- **BPDD** (the DD Council) and the **Council on Physical Disabilities** (Wis. Stat. 46.29) advise on policy and do not provide services. **Survival Coalition** is the cross-disability policy coalition of more than 20 statewide organizations.
- **Legal Action of Wisconsin** merged with Judicare on **2026-01-01**. It gives free civil legal help with benefits, criminal records and driver's licenses (both employment barriers). Intake is **855-947-2529**.
- **The Wisconsin ABLE law** (SB 668, signed **2024-04-04**) told DFI to create an ABLE program. As of 2026 DFI says a multi-state partnership is "the most viable option," and **no Wisconsin plan has launched yet**.

## Key facts
| Organization | Role | Public contact |
|---|---|---|
| Disability Rights Wisconsin | Protection & Advocacy; CAP; Family Care & IRIS Ombudsman; SSI Managed Care External Advocacy; Disability Benefits Specialist Program support; Victim Advocacy | 800-928-8778; disabilityrightswi.org |
| Client Assistance Program (at DRW) | Information, advocacy and limited appeal help on DVR and ILC services; ADA Title I information; free | 800-928-8778 or online form |
| WI Board for People with Developmental Disabilities | Federally authorized DD council. Governor appoints members, and 60% are people with DD or family members. More than 70% of funds go to local projects and advocacy. | 608-266-7826; 101 E. Wilson St, Rm 219, Madison |
| Council on Physical Disabilities | Advisory body created in 1989 under Wis. Stat. 46.29. Writes a state plan and advises agencies. No direct services or ADA enforcement. | dhs.wisconsin.gov/cpd |
| Survival Coalition | More than 20 statewide disability organizations doing joint budget and policy advocacy | (verify website) |
| Legal Action of Wisconsin | Free civil legal aid; merged with Judicare Legal Aid 2026-01-01 | 855-947-2529; legalaction.org |
| DWD Equal Rights Division | Takes WFEA complaints (form ERD-4206); mediation available | 608-266-3131 (DWD); dwd.wisconsin.gov/er |
| DFI ABLE program | State ABLE savings program in development | dfi.wi.gov |

## How it works
- **DVR disagreements.** The person first asks the counselor or supervisor. If that does not resolve it, the person can call CAP. Most CAP help is information, referral or brief coaching. CAP **cannot represent someone at a DVR impartial hearing that has already been requested**, and its capacity for new cases is "very limited." DRW asks people to read its self-advocacy resources first.
- **Family Care / IRIS disputes.** DRW runs the Family Care and IRIS Ombudsman Program for members under 60. **(verify)** the age split: the ombudsman for members 60 and older is usually the Board on Aging and Long Term Care.
- **Workplace discrimination.** State law protects people with a current impairment, a record of one, or a perceived one. It covers alcoholism and drug addiction, and AIDS. Employers must provide reasonable accommodation unless it would cause a hardship. The employee usually has to ask for it. State law **does not** cover discrimination by association, but the ADA does (EEOC Milwaukee office).
- **Policy work.** BPDD funds projects and runs leadership training such as Partners in Policymaking, a six-session class in Madison and online. Survival Coalition issues joint positions on state budgets. In 2025 it backed the enacted budget's Medicaid and special-education increases.

## Caveats and gotchas
- CAP has been **at DRW since 2021-09-30**. Older materials still name DATCP.
- DRW's homepage did not list office locations. **(verify)** the Madison and Milwaukee office addresses before printing them.
- **"ABLE Law."** This page reads it as Wisconsin's ABLE accounts law (SB 668, 2024). If the hackathon brief meant a legal aid organization called ABLE, that is a different item, and none was found for Wisconsin. Ohio's "ABLE" (Advocates for Basic Legal Equality) is not a Wisconsin provider. **(verify)** what was meant.
- **ABLE accounts are still open to Wisconsin residents** through other states' plans. DFI gives the disability-onset rule as "before age 46." This is believed to be the federal ABLE Age Adjustment Act change effective 2026-01-01. **(verify)** For state tax treatment DFI points to DOR.
- The **ERD's own phone** was not on the disability page. Only the main DWD line was shown. **(verify)** the ERD direct line.
- The **Survival Coalition website** was not confirmed from an opened page. **(verify)**
- Applications for the BPDD Partners in Policymaking class were due 2026-10-23, today. The page shows a 2026-2027 class schedule.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Put a **"Get help with a dispute"** route in any consumer tool. DVR problems go to CAP at 800-928-8778. Workplace discrimination goes to ERD, with a 300-day clock. Family Care or IRIS problems go to the DRW ombudsman. Records or license barriers go to Legal Action at 855-947-2529.
- A tool **must not** tell someone whether they have a valid claim, or calculate deadlines for their specific facts. It can show the general 300-day rule and send them on.
- Do not collect details about a dispute in a hackathon prototype.

# County disability programs relevant to employment (southern WI)

## TL;DR
- In Wisconsin, **counties are the access point** for CCS (mental health and substance use recovery), CLTS (children's waiver), the ADRC (which handles adult long-term care enrollment and runs the **disability benefit specialists for ages 18-59**), and much of specialized transportation.
- **CCS** is a Medicaid psychosocial rehabilitation benefit for **all ages**. It can include **job-related skills training**. Dane County launched it in **2015**, and it needs no county match. ERI is a Dane County CCS provider.
- **Milwaukee County DHHS** has a **Disabilities Services Division (DSD)**, the **ADRC of Milwaukee County** (1230 W. Cherry St, 414-289-6874) under Aging & Disabilities Services, and the **Office for Persons with Disabilities** (1220 W. Vliet St). The ADRC lists **Youth Transition** and **Benefits Specialists**.
- Other southern counties run these functions through their **human services departments and ADRCs** (phone list in [long-term-care-system.md](long-term-care-system.md)).

## Key facts
| County | Employment-relevant units (confirmed) | Public contact |
|---|---|---|
| Dane | ADRC (disability and elder benefit specialists, options counseling, Family Care/IRIS enrollment, youth transition); Dept. of Human Services (CCS, CLTS, specialized transportation) | ADRC 608-240-7400, 2865 N. Sherman Ave; DCDHS transportation 608-242-6489 |
| Milwaukee | DHHS Disabilities Services Division (runs CCOP for children); ADRC (I&A, benefits specialists, options counseling, youth transition); Office for Persons with Disabilities (ADA, accessible county services); Behavioral Health (CCS) **(verify)** | ADRC 414-289-6874 |
| Waukesha | ADRC (shared-fare taxi, RideLine, vehicle modification up to $7,000) | ADRC 262-548-7848 / 866-677-2372 |
| Racine | ADRC within Human Services, Aging & Behavioral Health | 866-219-1043 |
| Kenosha | ADRC | 800-472-8008 |
| Rock | ADRC within Human Services | 855-741-3600 |
| Walworth | ADRC | 800-365-1587 |
| Jefferson | ADRC within Human Services, Adult Services | 866-740-2372 |
| Washington | ADRC within Health & Human Services | 877-306-3030 |
| Ozaukee | ADRC | 866-537-4261 |

| Program | Who | Employment link |
|---|---|---|
| CCS | All ages with mental health or substance use needs; screened by the county or Tribal provider | Job-related skills training, peer support; can be named as a DVR LTS resource |
| CLTS | Children with disabilities; county support and service coordinators; continuous enrollment (no waitlist) | Youth job supports and transition planning **(verify the service list)** |
| CCOP (Children's Community Options Program) | Children with disabilities; state program run by counties | Flexible supports |
| ADRC disability benefit specialists | Ages 18-59 | Benefits help, which comes before work-incentive planning (WIPA) |

## How it works
- **CCS.** A county intake worker checks eligibility, meaning unmet needs that could lead to hospitalization in a crisis. The member works with a recovery team to choose services from certified providers. Dane County's 2015 launch drew more than 25 provider agencies. DVR's supported employment guidance names county mental health programs (CSP, CCS) as possible LTS resources and allows a county case worker on the team.
- **CLTS.** The county human services agency coordinates services. In Dane County, case management is contracted out. For example, **Avenues to Community** (Fitchburg) does CLTS support and service coordination under a Dane County DHS contract. ERI's site lists "CLTS: Youth & Family Services."
- **ADRC youth transition** helps students move from children's to adult long-term care. That handoff usually happens around 17.5-18, when adult Family Care or IRIS eligibility is set.
- **Benefit specialists versus WIPA.** ADRC disability benefit specialists help people apply for and keep benefits. Work-incentives planning for SSI and SSDI beneficiaries is WIPA's job (1-877-826-1752). ERI is a WIPA provider.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Milwaukee County naming.** The DSD page still says "Disabilities Services Division." The ADRC brochure header says "Aging & Disabilities Services." **(verify)** the current org chart, and the name and intake path for the Behavioral Health Services/CCS unit. The BHS page could not be opened in this pass.
- **Dane County youth transition programs** beyond the ADRC's youth transition service were not confirmed. **(verify)**
- "**CBS benefits specialists**" in the original brief: no Dane County program by that name was found. The confirmed service is the ADRC's **Disability Benefit Specialist** program (ages 18-59). **(verify)** whether "CBS" meant something else.
- The DHS CCS page did not mention Medicaid or the DHS 36 rule. Dane County's 2015 release calls CCS a Medicaid benefit.
- Each county's phone menu differs. Use the ADRC number as the front door.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Build a **county resolver**: an address leads to the county ADRC, Job Center, DVR office, WDB and transit options.
- In intake, ask whether the person is in CCS or CLTS. If yes, the county team should help coordinate the employment plan, with the person's consent.
- A tool **must not** screen for CCS or CLTS eligibility. Send the person to county intake.

# Wisconsin DVR structure and consumer process

## TL;DR
- The Division of Vocational Rehabilitation (DVR), part of the Department of Workforce Development (DWD), is Wisconsin's public VR agency. In FFY2025 it **served 33,687 people** and had **3,429 successful employment outcomes**, at an **average of $17.04/hour** and **24.89 hours/week**.
- DVR runs **11 Workforce Development Areas (WDAs)** with **35 field offices**. In southern Wisconsin these are WDA 1 (Kenosha/Racine/Walworth), WDA 2 (Milwaukee), WDA 3 (Waukesha/Ozaukee/Washington), WDA 10 (South Central, including Dane) and WDA 11 (Southwest, including Rock).
- An **Order of Selection waitlist took effect in December 2025**. On **2026-06-02** the Joint Committee on Finance approved more funding. DVR is releasing people from the waitlist Category 1 first and aims to end it by **2027-06-30**.
- DVR buys most job services from **contracted vendors** such as ERI, under the Statewide Service Fee Structure in effect **2026-07-01 to 2028-06-30**. Supported employment pays by milestone, for example Career Profile $1,000, systematic instruction $1,600/month and Transition to LTS $1,300.

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Mission | "To obtain, maintain, and improve employment for people with disabilities by working with vocational rehabilitation consumers" | 2025 WRC annual report |
| People served, FFY2025 (2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30) | 33,687 (up from 30,943) | 2025 WRC annual report |
| Successful employment outcomes | 3,429, of which 242 left federal benefits | same |
| Average / median wage at closure | $17.04 / $15.00; competitive integrated employment average $17.81 | same |
| Average hours per week | 24.89 | same |
| Pre-ETS students (ages 14-21) | 3,852; $16,180,077 in Pre-ETS spending | same |
| Federal VR funding / state match | $87,214,145 / $23,604,337 | same |
| Estimated annual earnings of successful closures | $83,715,335 | same |
| Funding split | 78.7% federal (RSA), 21.3% state | DWD press release 2025-11-03 |
| SFY2026 state appropriation (Act 15) | $21.3M, which is $4.6M short of projected need | same |
| People working toward a goal at any time | about 19,000 | same |
| Waitlist start | December 2025 | OOS FAQ; GovDelivery bulletin |
| JFC funding approval | 2026-06-02 | OOS FAQ |
| Target to end the waitlist | 2027-06-30 | OOS FAQ |
| Eligibility deadline | 60 days from application (WIOA) | Extension guidance |
| IPE deadline | 90 days after eligibility | same |
| Successful closure | after 90 days stable in employment (for SE, 90 days after the move to LTS; 34 CFR 363.54) | Program guide; SE guidance |
| Central office | 201 E. Washington Ave, Madison; 800-442-3477 | Locations page |

### Southern Wisconsin DVR offices (public main lines, from the 05/05/26 staff directory)
| WDA | Counties | Offices | Main line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kenosha, Racine, Walworth | Kenosha (8600 Sheridan Rd), Racine (1516 S. Green Bay Rd, Ste 100), Elkhorn (400 County Rd H) | 262-956-6930 |
| 2 | Milwaukee | Milwaukee Central (4201 N. 27th St, Ste 601), Milwaukee South (2701 S. Chase Ave, Ste C), West Allis (1205 S. 70th St, Ste 201) | 414-250-6551 |
| 3 | Waukesha, Ozaukee, Washington | Waukesha (2607 N. Grandview Blvd, Ste 100), West Bend (2200 Green Tree Rd) | 262-956-6830 |
| 10 | Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Jefferson, Marquette, Sauk | Madison Aberg (1801 Aberg Ave), Madison West (7633 Ganser Way, Ste 203), Jefferson (874 Collins Rd), Beaver Dam, Portage, Baraboo | 608-242-4800 (V/TTY) |
| 11 | Grant, Green, Iowa, Lafayette, Richland, Rock | Janesville (Rock County Job Center, 1717 Center Ave, Ste 900), Dodgeville, Richland Center | 800-228-2648 |

DVR's WDAs follow the same 11 county groupings as the WIOA workforce boards. See [workforce-system.md](workforce-system.md).

## How it works
1. **Referral.** A person refers online, by phone at 800-442-3477, or on a paper form. Only basic information is needed. People who get SSI or SSDI because of their own disability are **presumed eligible**.
2. **Application.** DVR contacts the person to review and sign the application. A guardian signs for minors and for adults who have a guardian.
3. **Eligibility (60 days).** DVR gathers disability documentation and can buy assessments. An extension needs a specific agreed date. Staff start the extension request by day 45.
4. **Order of Selection.** An eligible person is put in **Category 1** (most significant disability limitations), **Category 2** (significant) or **Category 3** (all others). The rating looks at seven functional areas: mobility, communication, self-care, self-direction, interpersonal skills, work tolerance and work skills. While the waitlist is in place, people come off it by category and then by application date.
5. **IPE (90 days).** The counselor and the consumer write the Individualized Plan for Employment. It sets the job goal and lists every service. DVR cannot pay for a service that is not in the IPE.
6. **Services.** Services must be necessary, reasonable and appropriate. They include counseling, job development, supported or customized employment, IPS, training grants (FAFSA-based), assistive technology and benefits counseling. The counselor contacts the consumer at least every 30 days.
7. **Closure.** A case closes as successful after 90 days of stable employment. A consumer can ask to close at any time and can reapply later.

### Waitlist rules (Order of Selection, 2025-2027)
- People who already have an **approved IPE keep getting services**.
- A student who received documented Pre-ETS before the eligibility decision can **keep getting Pre-ETS** while on the waitlist. That covers job exploration, work-based learning, enrollment counseling, self-advocacy and workplace readiness. Job coaching, transportation and personal assistance need an IPE.
- **Adults on the waitlist get no DVR services**, and that includes Project SEARCH.
- A person at **immediate risk of losing a job** can ask the local office for specific services.
- The FAQ sends waitlisted people to the Job Center of Wisconsin at 888-258-9966 for other help.

### Vendor (service provider) model
- DVR counselors authorize services by purchase order to providers that have signed the **DVR Statewide Service Provider Agreement**. Providers deliver to the Technical Specifications and are paid by fixed fee or milestone.
- There are **nine statewide services**: Customized Employment, IPS, Internship/Temporary Work, Job & Task Analysis/Systematic Instruction, Job Preparation/Development/Hire/Retention, Student Work-Based Learning, Supported Employment, Vocational Evaluation, and Work Incentive Benefits Services. There are also "Other Services" such as OJT, Partners with Business, Skills to Pay the Bills and Walgreens REDI.
- **Supported Employment fees** (2026-2028): Career Profile $1,000; Job Prep & Development Plan $350; Job Development & Hire $1,600 standard, up to $2,200 preferred; Job & Task Analysis $275; monthly systematic instruction $1,600; retention without SI $500/month; Transition to LTS $1,300 within 6 months, otherwise $500. Hourly SI is $55.
- **Job Development fees**: Plan $550; Hire up to $1,900 with Rapid Hire; Retention $1,600 standard or $2,200 preferred, paid at 30, 60 and 90 days.
- **Supported employment limits**: the fee structure says "the maximum ongoing support DVR can pay for is 24 months for anyone age 25 or above, and 48 months for individuals under age 25," with more months possible based on individual need. Whether the 48 months is a lifetime cap is **(verify)**. For adults 25 and older, the IPE must name the LTS funder. Transition to LTS cannot happen before 90 days on the job.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **The waitlist changes month to month.** The FAQ says funding is approved and DVR is "working through the waitlist," but it does not say which categories are open. Do not tell anyone they will get services by a certain date. **(verify)** the current category status with DVR before publishing.
- **Provider waitlists are a separate thing from the OOS waitlist.** On 2026-08-31, 199 consumers statewide were waiting for a *provider*, and 160 of them were in **WDA 10 (Dane and the counties around it)**. Most were waiting for Supported Employment (85) or Job Development (73). That is ERI's home WDA, and the shortage of provider capacity there is a real opportunity.
- The FFY2025 report gives hours as 24.89. "24.9" is a rounded figure.
- The 2025-11-03 press release came before the waitlist and predicted that about 2,000 people would be affected right away. Do not present those figures as actual waitlist counts.
- WDA 11's Richland Center office had no main line in the directory.
- The fee schedule labeled "August 2026" is the current one. Pages in the archived `_archive/20260901-...` folder hold the 2024-2026 specs.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Treat DVR status as data: *not referred → referred → applied → eligible (category) → waitlisted or active → IPE → service → employed → closed*. A tool can show where someone is in that flow and the next step. It **must not** decide eligibility or category.
- Use the **60-day** and **90-day** clocks to prompt staff follow-up, for example "eligibility due by...".
- If someone is waitlisted, route them to Job Center services, WIPA benefits counseling, county or long-term-care funding, and Pre-ETS for students, instead of a dead end.
- Use the fee schedule for capacity planning only. Do not show billing amounts to consumers.
- Use the WDA 10 provider waitlist figure as evidence when ERI plans capacity.

# School-to-work transition in Wisconsin

## TL;DR
- **Wisconsin starts transition planning at 14, earlier than the federal rule of 16.** A Postsecondary Transition Plan (PTP) is required in the first IEP in effect when the student turns 14, and it is updated every year (Wis. Stat. 115.787(2)(g)1). It needs measurable goals for **education/training, employment and, where appropriate, independent living**.
- **DVR Pre-ETS** serves students **ages 14-21** with an IEP, a 504 plan or a documented disability. Students can get it without a full DVR application. DVR must spend **15% of its budget** on Pre-ETS. In FFY2025, **3,852 students** were served and $16.18M was spent.
- **Project SEARCH** has **29 sites statewide**. About 12 are in southern Wisconsin, mostly hosted by hospitals, with providers such as Goodwill, CEO, MARC, Threshold, DSAW and Community Solution.
- Inclusive college options include **Edgewood University's Cutting Edge** (Madison, active in 2026), **UW-Whitewater LIFE** (ages 18-25, residential) and **Bethesda College at Concordia University Wisconsin** (Mequon; verify current status).

## Key facts
| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PTP start | IEP in effect at age 14; updated yearly | DPI transition page; Bulletin 26.01 |
| PTP submission | to DPI's online application within 30 days of the annual IEP meeting | Bulletin 26.01 |
| Maximum school age | end of the school year in which the student turns 21 | Bulletin 26.01 |
| When to involve DVR | about 2 years before leaving school | Bulletin 26.01; DVR presentation 2026-02-03 |
| Pre-ETS student definition | 14 to under 22, enrolled, with IEP, 504 plan or documented disability | DVR Pre-ETS guide |
| Five required Pre-ETS | job exploration counseling; work-based learning; postsecondary enrollment counseling; workplace readiness; self-advocacy (including peer mentoring) | same |
| Pre-ETS reserve | 15% of the VR budget | same |
| FFY2025 Pre-ETS | 3,852 students; $16,180,077 | 2025 WRC report |
| Project SEARCH sites | 29 statewide | DVR site list |
| Indicator 14 survey | post-school outcomes one year after exit (wipso.org) | DPI |

### Project SEARCH sites in southern Wisconsin (DVR list)
| Host | City | School partner | Provider |
|---|---|---|---|
| Children's Wisconsin | Wauwatosa | CESA 1 | CEO |
| Froedtert Hospital (adult program) | Milwaukee | not listed | CEO |
| Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport | Milwaukee | Milwaukee Public Schools | Goodwill |
| Milwaukee County Zoo | Milwaukee | CESA 1 | Goodwill |
| ProHealth Waukesha | Waukesha | not listed | CEO |
| West Bend Insurance | West Bend | West Bend SD | Threshold |
| Racine Unified Project SEARCH | Racine | Racine Unified | Goodwill |
| UW Health / William S. Middleton VA | Madison | Madison Metropolitan SD | MARC |
| Marquardt Village | Watertown | TBD | DSAW |
| Mercy Health Hospital & Trauma Center | Janesville | Janesville SD | Community Solution |
| Sauk Prairie Health Care | Prairie du Sac | CESA 5 | TBD |
| Kalahari Resort | Wisconsin Dells | CESA 5 | MARC |

No sites were listed in Kenosha, Walworth or Ozaukee counties.

## How it works
- **Schools (DPI).** The IEP team writes the PTP from age-appropriate transition assessments. The district must provide at least one transition service each year. It must invite the student, and with consent it must invite any outside agency (DVR, county, MCO) that may provide or pay for services. Community work placements alongside non-disabled peers count as time in the regular classroom.
- **Transition Improvement Grant (TIG).** This DPI-funded project (witig.org) has about 10 staff. It aims to improve PTP quality, graduation and post-school outcomes, and it supports **County Communities on Transition (CCOT)**.
- **Interagency Agreement on Transition.** DPI, DVR and DHS share responsibility. The **Transition Action Guide (TAG)** is the technical assistance guide that goes with the agreement.
- **Pre-ETS through DVR.** Services can come from DVR staff, contracted providers such as Student Work-Based Learning vendors, or Project SEARCH skills training. **"Potentially eligible" students** can get Pre-ETS without an IPE. Transportation, systematic instruction and personal assistance need an IPE.
- **Under the waitlist (December 2025 onward).** Students who already had documented Pre-ETS can continue. Adults on the waitlist cannot attend Project SEARCH with DVR funding.
- **Let's Get to Work** was a Waisman Center (UCEDD) project with pilot high schools from **spring 2012, for about four years**. **73%** of the students it served had one or more paid work experiences, which is a strong predictor of adult employment.
- **Employment First (2017 Wisconsin Act 178)** requires DWD, DPI and DHS to set joint CIE targets every two years and report each year.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The 14-year start is **state law**. Federal Indicator 13 measures from 16. Do not apply the federal age to Wisconsin students.
- **Bethesda College** status comes from a 2019 WUWM article. **(verify)** that it still runs at Concordia Mequon.
- **UW-Whitewater LIFE.** The page did not show cost or Comprehensive Transition Program (CTP) federal aid status. **(verify)**
- Edgewood is now **"Edgewood University"**. Cutting Edge applications run August 1 to November 30. Its final-year off-campus jobs are arranged with DVR.
- Who partners with BPDD on Let's Get to Work, and which districts took part, were not on the opened page. **(verify)**
- The Project SEARCH list has "TBD" cells. Check before naming providers in public.
- Some sources say "Milwaukee Zoo" and some "Milwaukee County Zoo". The DVR list says "Milwaukee Zoo".

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- ERI runs **VFPS youth transition navigation** and **CLTS youth and family services**. A tool can produce an age-based checklist: 14 means a PTP and a DVR Pre-ETS referral; about 2 years before exit, apply to DVR; 17.5 means guardianship or supported decision-making planning; before 22, line up the LTS funder.
- A tool **must not** write IEP goals or tell a family what a school must provide. Send disputes to DPI or DRW.
- Use the Project SEARCH table for referrals by county. The Kenosha, Walworth and Ozaukee gap is a possible partnership opportunity.

# Employer and business networks for disability hiring (southern WI)

## TL;DR
- **DVR Business Services Consultants (BSCs)** are DVR's employer-facing staff, organized **by WDA**. There are 12 WDA positions plus a section chief, and Milwaukee has a North and a South BSC. In the 2026 listing, the **Milwaukee South and WOW (WDA 3) positions were vacant**. DVR's services to businesses are free and voluntary (800-442-3477).
- DVR's main employer incentive is **On-the-Job Training (OJT)**: **50% of wages for up to 90 days**, or **100% of wages for up to 500 hours in 12 months for students**. "Other Services" include Partners with Business, Skills to Pay the Bills and **Walgreens REDI**.
- **MMAC**, founded in 1861, represents about **2,000 member businesses employing more than 300,000 people**. Its affiliate, the **Milwaukee 7**, is the regional economic development partnership for Kenosha, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Walworth, Washington and Waukesha counties. Neither one listed a disability-inclusion program.
- A **Wisconsin Disability:IN or Business Leadership Network affiliate could not be confirmed** from an opened page. **(verify)**

## Key facts
| Channel | What it offers employers | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| DVR BSCs (by WDA) | Candidate pool, hiring incentives, partner connections, labor market data, ADA and accommodation expertise, inclusive culture, retention resources | 800-442-3477; dwd.wisconsin.gov/dvr/business |
| DVR OJT | 50% wage reimbursement up to 90 days; students 100% up to 500 hours in 12 months | via DVR counselor or BSC |
| DVR "Other Services" | Partners with Business, Skills to Pay the Bills, Walgreens REDI ($55/hour job instruction), Job Shadow, On-the-Job Assessment | fee schedule |
| WDB business services | Recruiting, customized and incumbent worker training, scholarships | see [workforce-system.md](workforce-system.md) |
| MMAC | Business advocacy; Talent pillar (student career development, leadership, Fuel Milwaukee young professionals) | mmac.org |
| Milwaukee 7 | Regional site selection, workforce connections and data | mkeregion.com |
| DWD Equal Rights Division | Employer obligations under the WFEA, reasonable accommodation | dwd.wisconsin.gov/er |

## How it works
- **Dual customer.** The VR system treats employers as customers as well as job seekers. A BSC builds a "customized service plan" with a business. Then DVR counselors and contracted providers like ERI bring candidates, job coaching and retention support.
- **Who does what.** DVR BSCs and workforce boards handle the employer relationship at the regional level. **Providers do the placement work**: job development, job and task analysis, systematic instruction and retention, under DVR's statewide services. Partners with Business is the service where a provider trains **co-workers as natural supports**.
- **Recent DVR employer initiatives** in the FFY2025 report include **autism training with Walmart** and sessions with **SSM Health and Sodexo**.
- **Accommodation basics** employers ask about: under Wisconsin law, the employee generally has to ask. The employer must accommodate unless it would cause a hardship. The employer can choose any accommodation that works.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Disability:IN Wisconsin / Wisconsin BLN.** The national affiliate list and wibln.org could not be read in this pass. **(verify)** whether a Wisconsin affiliate is active and who runs it, before naming one.
- **Chambers.** Local chambers (Madison Region Economic Partnership, Greater Madison Chamber, Waukesha County Business Alliance, Racine/Kenosha chambers) were **not opened**. **(verify)** each before listing contacts.
- Federal **WOTC** lapsed for hires after 2025-12-31 unless Congress reauthorizes it, and the Section 503 7% goal was rescinded effective 2026-09-21. Don't pitch employers on either. See [hiring incentives](../employment-law/hiring-incentives-wotc-schedule-a.md) and [Rehabilitation Act](../employment-law/rehabilitation-act.md).
- BSC vacancies change often. Check the BSC contact page before sending an employer to a WDA.
- Do not promise employers OJT reimbursement. DVR approves it case by case, and it needs an active IPE, which the waitlist affects.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- **Where ERI Business Services fits:**
  1. A **single point of contact** that offers employers a bundle: candidates, job and task analysis, job coaching, Partners with Business co-worker training and benefits-aware onboarding.
  2. **Coordinate with the WDA 10 BSC** and WDBSCW so employers are not approached by several agencies with no coordination.
  3. Use DVR's **provider waitlist gap in WDA 10** (160 consumers on 2026-08-31) as a capacity story for employers who need talent.
  4. **Training and design services**: accessibility and accommodation workshops for MMAC, chamber or WDB members.
- A tool could log **employer needs** (roles, shifts, location against transit, accommodations already in place) and match them to candidate profiles. It **must not** disclose a candidate's disability or benefits to an employer without the candidate's written consent.
