# Wisconsin long-term care system and ongoing employment supports

## TL;DR
- **ADRCs** (Aging and Disability Resource Centers) are the front door to adult long-term care. They offer free options counseling, disability benefit specialists (ages 18-59) and Family Care/IRIS enrollment. Each of the 10 southern counties has its own ADRC. The statewide finder line is **844-947-2372 (844-WIS-ADRC)**.
- **Family Care** (managed care through MCOs) and **IRIS** (self-direction through an IRIS Consultant Agency) are Medicaid waivers. They pay for **supported employment, small-group supported employment, prevocational services and vocational futures planning (VFPS)**.
- In Supported Employment, **DVR pays for up to 24 months of ongoing support** and then hands off to a long-term support (LTS) funder. For adults 25 and older the IPE must name that funder. Family Care, IRIS and CLTS are treated as **comparable benefits**, and the case should move to them after **90 days of job stability**.
- MCO choice is changing. In mid-2026, Milwaukee and Dane each had four Family Care MCOs. DHS has announced new MCOs for **Kenosha, Racine, Walworth, Waukesha, Ozaukee and Washington starting in 2027**, subject to protests and CMS approval.

## Key facts
### Southern ADRCs (DHS contact list)
| County | ADRC | Public phone | Website |
|---|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee | ADRC of Milwaukee County (1230 W. Cherry St) | 414-289-6874 | county.milwaukee.gov/EN/DHHS/Disabilities-Services/Disability-Resource-Center |
| Dane | ADRC of Dane County (2865 N. Sherman Ave) | 608-240-7400 | daneadrc.org |
| Waukesha | ADRC of Waukesha County | 866-677-2372 | waukeshacounty.gov/adrc |
| Racine | ADRC of Racine County | 866-219-1043 | racinecounty.gov/departments/hsd/aging-behavioral-health/adrc |
| Kenosha | ADRC of Kenosha County | 800-472-8008 | kenoshacountywi.gov/155/Aging-and-Disability-Resource-Center |
| Rock | ADRC of Rock County | 855-741-3600 | co.rock.wi.us/departments/human-services/adrc |
| Walworth | ADRC of Walworth County | 800-365-1587 | co.walworth.wi.us |
| Jefferson | ADRC of Jefferson County | 866-740-2372 | jeffersoncountywi.gov (Human Services > ADRC) |
| Washington | ADRC of Washington County | 877-306-3030 | washcowisco.gov (Health & Human Services > ADRC) |
| Ozaukee | ADRC of Ozaukee County | 866-537-4261 | ozaukeecounty.gov/adrc |

### Family Care and Partnership MCOs by county (DHS key contacts, 06/2026)
| County | Family Care MCOs | Partnership MCOs |
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee | Anthem, Community Care, Inclusa, My Choice | Inclusa, My Choice |
| Dane | Community Care, Inclusa, Lakeland, My Choice | Inclusa, My Choice |
| Rock, Jefferson | Community Care, Inclusa, Lakeland, My Choice | Inclusa, My Choice |
| Waukesha, Washington, Ozaukee | Community Care, Inclusa, My Choice | Community Care, My Choice |
| Racine, Kenosha | Community Care, My Choice | Community Care, Inclusa |
| Walworth | Community Care, Inclusa, My Choice | Community Care |

MCO public lines: Anthem 844-509-0835 · Community Care 866-992-6600 · Inclusa 877-622-6700 · Lakeland Care 877-227-3335 · My Choice Wisconsin 877-489-3814 (Family Care) or 800-963-0035 (Partnership) · iCare (Partnership) 414-223-4847.

### IRIS Consultant Agencies (ICAs) serving southern WI
| ICA | Phone | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Advocates4U | 414-755-2020 | statewide |
| First Person Care Consultants | 414-336-2448 | all 10 southern counties |
| LSS Connections | 844-520-1712 | statewide |
| Progressive Community Services | 833-487-8826 | Dane, Jefferson, Rock |
| TMG | 844-864-8987 | statewide |
| MILC | 800-382-8484 | not in the 10 southern counties |

## How it works
- **ADRC first.** An adult who may need long-term care goes to the ADRC. The ADRC screens functional eligibility, gives options counseling and enrolls the person in Family Care, Partnership, PACE or IRIS. ADRC **disability benefit specialists** help people ages 18-59 with public benefits.
- **Family Care.** An MCO gets a monthly payment for each member. The member's interdisciplinary team authorizes services in the member-centered plan. Members can choose among the MCOs certified in their county.
- **Family Care Partnership** adds acute and primary health care to Family Care.
- **IRIS.** The participant directs their own budget. The ICA consultant helps write the plan, and a fiscal employer agent handles payroll.
- **CLTS (children).** This is a Medicaid waiver for children with disabilities, run through **county health and human services agencies**. DHS says the **waitlist has ended**: under "continuous enrollment," children are enrolled as soon as they are found eligible.
- **HCBS employment services** (DHS Employment Initiatives):
  - *Individual supported employment* covers discovery, job development, job coaching, workplace personal assistance, Partners with Business, and work incentive benefits counseling.
  - *Small-group supported employment* serves groups of 2-6 workers.
  - *Prevocational services* are community-based skill building.
  - *VFPS* is team-based planning toward competitive integrated employment (CIE).
  - Wisconsin's Employment First law (2017 Act 178) names CIE the preferred outcome.
- **The handoff from DVR.** The IPE names the LTS source. The team reviews the plan at the Career Profile, at the 60-day on-the-job meeting and before the transition. Transition happens only after 90 days on the job. DVR closes the case 90 days after the transition. The provider earns the $1,300 transition fee only if transition happens within six months of systematic instruction. DVR may pay LTS for youth under 25 for up to 48 months.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **Anthem in Milwaukee** appears in the 06/2026 key-contacts PDF, but the What's New page did not describe a Milwaukee award. **(verify)** whether Anthem is enrolling Family Care members in Milwaukee now.
- **The 2027 southeast changes are not final.** Anthem is new in Kenosha, Racine, Walworth, Waukesha, Ozaukee and Washington. Inclusa is new in Kenosha and Racine. iCare, My Choice and UnitedHealthcare get Partnership expansions. Award letters went out on 2026-07-14, and contracts wait on any protests. Partnership changes also need CMS approval. **(verify)** in January 2027.
- **iCare** is in the key-contacts PDF without a county list. It was added to Partnership in Dane and Rock in January 2025 (DHS release). **(verify)** current Partnership counties.
- DHS has ordered **My Choice Wisconsin** to take corrective action in both programs. No dates were shown.
- The DHS Employment Initiatives page does not say whether someone must try DVR before an MCO will fund supported employment. The HCBS Employment and Daytime Service Manual (P-03793) may say. **(verify)**
- The CLTS page did not give an age limit or the date continuous enrollment started. **(verify)**

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Build the LTS funder into intake. Collect "Family Care / IRIS / CLTS / CCS / none" and the MCO or ICA name early, because DVR needs it in the IPE.
- A tool can show a person's county ADRC and the MCO options for that county. It **must not** recommend one MCO over another or determine program eligibility. Send people to the ADRC for that.
- Flag cases at 60 days on the job so the team can confirm the transition plan before the 90-day mark, which protects the $1,300 transition fee.
- Re-check the MCO table after 2027-01-01.

# Peer disability employment providers in southern Wisconsin

## TL;DR
- Southern Wisconsin has a **mixed field**:
  - large multi-service nonprofits (Goodwill SE WI, LSS, Easterseals WI)
  - legacy rehabilitation and day-service agencies that are moving toward community employment (Curative Care Network, Opportunities Inc., Threshold, Kenosha Achievement Center)
  - disability-specific organizations (DSAW)
  - Centers for Independent Living (IndependenceFirst, Access to Independence)
  - case management and IRIS agencies (Avenues to Community, Progressive Community Services, LSS Connections)
- **Project SEARCH** shows who holds DVR youth contracts in each region: **Goodwill** (Milwaukee and Racine), **CEO** (Milwaukee and Waukesha), **MARC** (Madison and the Dells), **Threshold** (West Bend), **DSAW** (Watertown) and **Community Solution** (Janesville).
- **Capacity is short where ERI is.** On 2026-08-31, **WDA 10 had 160 of the 199** DVR consumers statewide who were waiting for a provider. That makes WDA 10 providers more likely partners than competitors for overflow.
- This page is **low confidence**. Many homepages did not show DVR vendor status or service counties. Read every **(verify)**.

## Key facts
| Organization | HQ / key location | What its own site says (employment-relevant) | DVR vendor? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goodwill Industries of Southeastern WI | Milwaukee area (Workforce Connection Centers) | Training, employment and supportive services for people with disabilities or disadvantages | Holds Project SEARCH provider roles (DVR list); vendor status otherwise (verify) |
| Easterseals Wisconsin | 1468 N. High Point Rd, Ste 202, Middleton | FARM program, AgrAbility, self-employment services, camps; about 10,000 served a year | (verify) |

| Lutheran Social Services of WI & Upper MI | statewide | Skills for Life & Work; mental health and recovery; runs the **LSS Connections IRIS ICA** (844-520-1712) | (verify) |
| Down Syndrome Association of WI (DSAW) | statewide chapters | **States it is a DVR service provider**; supported employment and job coaching; works with Family Care/IRIS for long-term job coaching; Project SEARCH provider at Watertown | Yes (own site) |

| Community Solution | Janesville (Project SEARCH) | Named only on the DVR Project SEARCH list | (verify) |

For comparison, ERI (4604 Cottage Grove Rd, Madison; 608-246-3444) offers:
- employment counseling
- WIPA and work-incentives benefits counseling
- Ticket to Work (ERI PLUS)
- benefits application services
- CCS
- VFPS youth transition navigation
- CLTS youth and family services
- pre-driving assessment
- training and design services
- business and employer services

## How it works
- DVR does not have one public "vendor list" that this pass could open. The most reliable public signals of who holds which DVR roles are the **Project SEARCH roster** and provider-waitlist bulletins. Use DVR's provider directory or a WDA office to confirm vendor status.
- Many legacy agencies combine **facility-based or day services** paid by Family Care with **community employment** paid by DVR. Employment First (Act 178) and DHS's CIE priority push those agencies toward integrated jobs.
- Overlap with ERI is heaviest in **WDA 10** (Dane, Jefferson): Opportunities Inc., DSAW, MARC, Access to Independence and Progressive Community Services. In Milwaukee, Goodwill, CEO, Curative and IndependenceFirst are the anchors.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **"Curative Connections"** is a different organization from Milwaukee's **Curative Care Network**. Curative Connections is believed to be based in the Green Bay area, outside the southern region. **(verify)** which one the brief meant.
- **Easterseals.** The Middleton-based Easterseals Wisconsin site did not mention DVR or Family Care. A separate **Easterseals Southeast Wisconsin** has served Milwaukee in the past, but its page could not be opened. **(verify)** that it exists and what it offers.
- **"Ability Center"** and **"Badger Bay"** from the brief: **no southern Wisconsin disability employment provider by either name was confirmed.** **(verify)** or drop them.
- **Avenues to Community** exists, but it is a CLTS case management agency in Dane County, not an employment provider.
- Other likely peers that were **not checked** in this pass: Kandu Industries (Janesville; site blocked automated reading), Careers Industries (Racine), Lakeside/other Waukesha agencies, Work Opportunities in Rural Communities, the Center for Independent Living for Western WI (out of region) and IPS county programs. **(verify)** before adding them.
- Do not describe any peer's quality or outcomes. None of that came from opened sources.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- Use this page for **referral routing** (for example, a Kenosha family goes to KAC, or Watertown goes to DSAW Project SEARCH) and for **partnership mapping**, not for competitive claims.
- A tool **must not** rank providers or imply DVR endorsement. Consumers have **informed choice** of provider under their IPE. Show options neutrally and send people to their DVR counselor.
- Re-verify the list every six months. Provider rosters change with each DVR contract cycle, and the current one runs 2026-07-01 to 2028-06-30.

# Transportation to work in southern Wisconsin

## TL;DR
- **ADA paratransit costs $3-$4 per one-way ride** in the southern systems: Madison $3.25; Milwaukee, Waukesha, Racine and Kenosha $4.00; Janesville $3. Most systems need **next-day booking**. Approved personal care attendants ride free.
- **Fixed-route reduced fares** for riders with disabilities are $1.25 on MCTS and $1.00 on Madison Metro, with daily, weekly and monthly **fare caps**.
- **BRT.** Milwaukee's **CONNECT 1** runs on the Wisconsin Ave corridor. **CONNECT 2** (27th St) is still in planning. Madison's **Rapid Route A** (east-west) launched in **September 2024**. The north-south BRT is expected to open **about 2028**.
- **Outside paratransit areas,** counties use **s. 85.21** WisDOT aid for elderly and disabled transportation. Examples are Waukesha County's shared-fare taxi and RideLine, and Dane County Human Services rides. These programs have limited hours and need booking ahead, so the commute often decides whether a job match works.

## Key facts
| System | Paratransit name / operator | One-way fare | Service area | Booking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MCTS (Milwaukee Co.) | Transit Plus (Transdev schedules) | $4.00; LTC enrollees may pay more; companion $4; PCA free | All of Milwaukee County plus some of Waukesha and Ozaukee | By 4:30 pm the day before, up to 7 days ahead; same-day pilot for work and health trips |
| Madison Metro | Metro Paratransit | $3.25 cash; 6-ticket book $19.50; PCA free | Close match to the fixed-route area: Madison, Fitchburg, Maple Bluff, Middleton, Monona, Shorewood Hills, Verona, Sun Prairie | Hours about 5:30 am to midnight daily |
| Waukesha Metro | Metrolift | $4.00; attendant free | City of Waukesha plus 3/4 mile of routes | Weekday 5:15 am to 11:55 pm |
| RYDE Racine | DART (Dial-a-Ride) | $4.00 exact | 3/4 mile of fixed routes | Physician certification required |
| Kenosha Area Transit | Care-A-Van (Kenosha Achievement Center) | $4.00; PCA free | Kenosha Co. east of I-94 plus 3/4 mile of routes west | 1 day ahead |
| Janesville Transit | Paratransit (You Buy We Fly LLC) | $3.00 | (verify) | Call operator |

| Fixed route | Adult | Reduced (disability) | Caps (reduced) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCTS | $2.75 | $1.25 | $4/day, $16.50/week, $49.50/month |
| Madison Metro | $2.00 | $1.00 | $2.50/day, $7/week, $28/month |

Public lines:
- Transit Plus: 414-343-1700; Transdev: 414-817-9860
- Madison Metro: 608-266-4466
- Metrolift: 262-524-3636
- RYDE: 262-637-9000
- Care-A-Van certification: 262-653-4290
- Janesville Transit: 608-755-3150

## How it works
- **ADA paratransit eligibility depends on function, not diagnosis.** The question is whether the person can board, ride and exit a bus on their own, or get to a stop. Madison requires a written application **and an in-person assessment** covering gait and balance, route recognition, and memory. A decision comes within 21 days, people can appeal within 60 days, and eligibility is recertified every 3 years. Eligibility can be **conditional**, for example only in snow or ice. Racine, Kenosha and Waukesha require a physician-signed form.
- **Payment is changing.** Transit Plus riders moved to the **WisGo card or Umo app on 2026-01-05**. Paper tickets were last sold 2026-02-27 and remain valid through 2026. Agency-paid rides for long-term care members move to WisGo later in 2026.
- **Agency fares.** Madison is holding a hearing on **2026-10-28** on raising paratransit *agency* fares and contract rates for the Commute Card and Unlimited Ride Pass programs. The $3.25 rider fare is not proposed to change.
- **s. 85.21 county aid.** WisDOT funds counties to transport older adults and people with disabilities. Every county gets at least 0.5% of the appropriation, and the rest is split by each county's share of elderly and disabled residents. Counties may contract with nonprofit or for-profit operators.
  - *Waukesha County ADRC*: shared-fare taxi for people 60+ or with a disability designation (ADRC pays $9 per eligible one-way ride from 2026-01-01); RideLine for wheelchair users; Eras volunteer rides.
  - *Dane County*: Human Services rides (608-242-6489), RSVP driver escort, Stoughton Transit, and **YW Transit** for low-income work trips (608-257-1436).
- **Long-term care.** Family Care and IRIS plans can pay for work transportation. Janesville says LTC members can get passes through their social worker.

## Caveats and gotchas
- **"Paratransit takes as long as the bus."** MCTS says outright that a van trip can take as long as the same trip by bus. Shift start times have to allow for pickup windows.
- **Weekend and late shifts** often fall outside county programs and outside Kenosha's reduced Saturday and Sunday paratransit hours.
- MCTS's opened pages did not give CONNECT 1's exact opening date. A February 2024 post called it "recently launched." **(verify)**
- No opened page gave a launch date for **CONNECT 2**. **(verify)**
- Madison's BRT FAQ links "Route B" to the north-south corridor upgrade. Treat 2028 as a projection.
- The Janesville paratransit service area was not stated. **(verify)**
- The Waukesha Metrolift document is dated **November 2023**. **(verify)** the fares and hours.
- The DVR waitlist means waitlisted consumers **cannot get DVR-funded transportation**.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- A job-match tool should **score commute feasibility**, not just distance: bus or BRT route and frequency at the shift times, whether the address is inside paratransit or the 3/4-mile buffer, county program hours, and the transfer count. A good job with an impossible commute is not a match.
- Show fares as ranges and link to the operator. Do not quote exact fares in ways that will go stale.
- A tool **must not** determine paratransit eligibility. It can explain the process and link to the application.

# Wisconsin public workforce system (southern WI)

## TL;DR
- Wisconsin has **11 Workforce Development Areas**, each with a WIOA board. Five cover southern Wisconsin: **Southeastern WDB** (WDA 1), **Employ Milwaukee** (WDA 2), **WOW** (WDA 3), the **WDB of South Central Wisconsin** (WDA 10, which includes Dane) and the **Southwest WI WDB** (WDA 11, which includes Rock).
- The boards run local **Job Centers** (American Job Centers). DVR offices are often **co-located** in them, for example in Elkhorn, Kenosha, Janesville, Jefferson and Dodgeville. The statewide online system is **jobcenterofwisconsin.com**. To find a local center, call **888-258-9966**.
- **Apprenticeship** reached a record **18,524 registered apprentices** in 2025, and **about 11,400 youth apprentices** took part in 2024-25. Certified pre-apprenticeship had 1,121 completers.
- **Windows to Work** is a DOC-funded reentry employment program that **all 11 WDBs** deliver. In FY2023, 63.5% of released participants found jobs, at an average of $17.61/hour.

## Key facts
| WDA | Board | Counties | Public phone | Website |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Southeastern WI WDB (Southeastern Works) | Kenosha, Racine, Walworth | 262-697-4586 | sewrks.com |
| 2 | Employ Milwaukee, Inc. (1322 N. 8th St) | Milwaukee | 414-270-1700 | employmilwaukee.org |
| 3 | WOW WDB ("WOW Works"); Waukesha County is fiscal agent | Waukesha, Ozaukee, Washington | 262-695-7800 | waukeshacounty.gov/workforcedevelopmentboard; wowwdb.org |
| 10 | WDB of South Central WI (3513 Anderson St, Ste 104, Madison) | Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Jefferson, Marquette, Sauk | 608-249-9001 | wdbscw.org |
| 11 | Southwest WI WDB | Grant, Green, Iowa, Lafayette, Richland, Rock | 608-314-3300 x305 | swwdb.org |

| Job Center (WDA 1) | Address | Phone |
|---|---|---|
| Kenosha County Job Center | 8600 Sheridan Rd, Kenosha | 262-697-4500 |
| Racine County Workforce Development Center | 1717 Taylor Ave, Racine | 262-638-6312 |
| Walworth County Job Center | 400 County Rd H, Elkhorn | 262-741-5180 |

Other southern Job Centers named in the DVR directory as DVR office sites:
- Rock County Job Center, 1717 Center Ave, Janesville
- Workforce Development Center of Jefferson County, 874 Collins Rd, Jefferson
- Iowa County Job Center, Dodgeville

| Apprenticeship (BAS, 2025) | Value |
|---|---|
| Registered apprentices | 18,524 (record, 4th straight year) |
| RA employers / new sponsors | more than 3,095 / 143 |
| Youth Apprenticeship 2024-25 | about 11,400 participants; 16 career areas, 83 occupations |
| Certified pre-apprenticeship | 1,121 completers; 87.9% completion; 43 programs |
| Public site | wisconsinapprenticeship.org |

## How it works
- **WIOA Title I** pays for Adult, Dislocated Worker and Youth services through each board: career services, training scholarships (Southeastern Works lists manufacturing, health care, transportation, construction and IT) and supportive services. Employ Milwaukee also runs **Earn & Learn** (summer youth jobs) and a **reentry** program.
- **Job Centers** offer at least the core services in the Wisconsin Job Center Standards: resource rooms, job search help, employer recruitment help, links to W-2, FoodShare and BadgerCare, UI information and **vocational rehabilitation**. DVR is the WIOA Title IV partner.
- **Job Center of Wisconsin.** jobcenterofwisconsin.com is the job board, résumé and labor-market tool. wisconsinjobcenter.org hosts the directory and information pages.
- **Registered Apprenticeship** is overseen by DWD's Bureau of Apprenticeship Standards (BAS). **Youth Apprenticeship** is for high school juniors and seniors and is run through local consortia.
- **Windows to Work (W2W).** DOC contracts with each WDB. The pre-release curriculum starts 3-12 months before release and covers cognitive intervention, work skills, financial literacy, community resources and job seeking. After release, a W2W coach gives about 12 months of job search and retention help. It runs in 18 adult institutions and 5 county jails. In FY2023 it had 505 enrollments, and 193 of 304 released participants (63.5%) got jobs at $17.61/hour.
- **Other reentry resources:**
  - Ten DOC/DWD **institution-based Job Centers** plus one mobile center. The first opened at Oakhill CI in 2018.
  - Mobile CNC and welding labs.
  - **OARS**, a DOC/DHS program for people with serious mental illness. It starts 6-8 months before release and gives up to 2 years of community support.

## Caveats and gotchas
- The SWWDB website blocked automated reading. Its program list and Job Center addresses (Janesville, Beloit) came from the DVR directory and the DWD map, not from swwdb.org. **(verify)**
- WOW's page did not list Job Center street addresses. It points to wfdc.org. **(verify)** the Waukesha, West Bend and Ozaukee Job Center addresses.
- The WDBSCW homepage lists Windows to Work and Youth Apprenticeship but no Job Center addresses. **(verify)** the Dane County Job Center site. Madison DVR's Aberg Ave office is listed by DVR, not by the board.
- The Windows to Work outcome figures are **FY2023**. **(verify)** whether newer Becky Young reports exist.
- The BAS 2025 review has no disability-specific data. Its footer gives wisconsinapprenticeship.org, not apprenticeship.wi.gov. **(verify)** which URL is canonical.
- "Reentry" and "disability" overlap a great deal, but no opened source gives a count.

## How ERI / a hackathon tool should use this
- ERI's home board is **WDA 10 (WDBSCW)**, and ERI board members also sit on it. The best co-enrollment opportunities are WIOA training funds alongside DVR services, and Windows to Work for returning citizens with disabilities.
- A tool can show the **local Job Center and board by county** and should point waitlisted DVR consumers to them. It **must not** suggest that WIOA eligibility is the same as DVR eligibility.
- Treat apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship as job-match targets that pay a wage. Check entry requirements with the program sponsor.

- [employer-and-business-networks.md](employer-and-business-networks.md)
- [education-and-transition.md](education-and-transition.md): Youth Apprenticeship and Pre-ETS
- [advocacy-and-legal-help.md](advocacy-and-legal-help.md): record and license legal help

# Personas

**Composite and fictional.** These personas are built from public statistics (Wisconsin DVR's FFY2025 report) and ERI's public client stories. No real client is described. Use them to aim your design, then test with real people when you can.

| File | Who |
| --- | --- |
| [job-seekers.md](job-seekers.md) | The **average user** (Marcus) plus 3 other job seekers, a family member, and an employer |
| [attendees.md](attendees.md) | Who's in the room on Oct 31 (5 archetypes) and what they need to know about ERI |
| [eri-staff.md](eri-staff.md) | The **average ERI employee** (Alex, an employment specialist) plus benefits, finance and web roles |

Want to "talk" to a persona? See [`agents/`](../../agents/README.md) for ready-made AI agent profiles.

## The numbers behind them
Source: [Wisconsin Rehabilitation Council 2025 annual report (DVR, Oct 2024 to Sep 2025)](https://www.dwd.wi.gov/dvr/partners/wrc/pdf/2025-wrc-annual-report.pdf)

| Stat | Value |
| --- | --- |
| People DVR served | 33,687 |
| Share under age 25 | about 40% |
| Top primary disabilities | Mental illness 19.7%, autism 12.5%, intellectual 9.9%, ADHD 9.8%, orthopedic 9.2% |
| Successful job outcomes (90+ days) | 3,429 |
| Average wage at closure | $17.04/h (median $15.00) |
| Average hours | 24.9 h/week |
| Top job types | Transportation and material moving; food prep and serving; sales; office and admin; building and grounds |

Wisconsin had 189,194 working-age people with disabilities employed in 2023, a record ([DWD](https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/press/2024/241023-record-high-disability-employment.htm)).


<!-- FILE: wiki/personas/attendees.md -->

# Attendee personas (who's in the room on Oct 31)

**Composite and fictional**, based on who typically comes to Milwaukee community meetups like Mitobyte's Code & Coffee (students, working developers, career changers, designers). About 31 RSVPs as of Oct 29 (about 5 teams), organizers included; this page was first written at about 18. Use these to design the kickoff, the repo and the help desk, not to judge anyone.

| Persona | Background | What they need from us | Risk if we miss it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Priya, 20: CS student** (UWM/MSOE) | Java and Python from class, some React; first hackathon | A clear starting point, permission to ask "dumb" questions, a portfolio piece | Stuck in setup for an hour; leaves at lunch |
| **Devon, 34: working developer** | 8 years of backend work; came for networking and to give back | A real problem, real constraints, a fast path to something shippable | Bored by hand-holding; builds a clever thing ERI can't use |
| **Lena, 29: UX designer** | Figma, accessibility interest, light HTML/CSS | A role that isn't "watch the coders": personas, flows, plain language, a11y testing | Sidelined; the demos look rough |
| **Sam, 41: career changer** | Bootcamp grad, job hunting, knows WordPress from freelance | WordPress-friendly work; something to show employers | Feels behind; quietly disengages |
| **Jordan, 27: developer who is blind** | Uses a screen reader daily; a strong JS developer | Accessible tools and slides; the lived-experience lens is valued, not tokenized | Can't use the hosted IDE or slides; the event contradicts its own theme |

## What every attendee needs to know about ERI (in under 2 minutes)
1. **Who:** a Madison nonprofit since 1990 that helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs.
2. **The tension:** working can affect SSI/SSDI and Medicaid, so fear of losing benefits keeps people from saying yes to jobs.
3. **How ERI gets paid:** mostly fee-for-service from Wisconsin DVR and Social Security, per milestone, so documentation and claiming matter.
4. **Who keeps the code:** a small web team running WordPress. Build on their stack.
5. **The guardrails and why:** synthetic data (privacy law), estimates route to WIPA (wrong benefits info hurts people), flags not decisions (public money).

## Design implications
- **Kickoff:** one slide on ERI, one on the rules, one per challenge, then "how to start". The deep material stays in the repo.
- **Team formation:** mix roles. Every team needs at least one person who can run the hello world and one who owns accessibility and plain language.
- **Roles for non-coders:** persona testing (`agents/`), copywriting at a 6th-grade level, axe and keyboard testing, demo storytelling.
- **Access:** slides with real text and good contrast, a way to start that works with a screen reader. The backup team editor (code-server) and the Codespace are untested with a screen reader. The laptop is the only path we trust, so pair a screen reader user with a mentor on a laptop, and captions or a written run of show.
- **Portfolio value:** PRs, tests, CI badges and a README count, so CONTRIBUTING.md makes the "real SWE experience" explicit.


<!-- FILE: wiki/personas/eri-staff.md -->

# ERI staff personas

ERI has about 29 staff ([public staff page](https://eri-wi.org/staff/)). The most common roles are **employment specialists** and **benefits specialists**, spread across Madison, Milwaukee, Green Bay, and north and northeast Wisconsin. Workload details below are **assumptions to confirm with ERI**.

## 1. Alex: the average employee (employment specialist)
> "I spend more time writing reports than I'd like. If I miss a deadline, we don't get paid for work I already did."

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Role | Employment Specialist (Supported Employment, DVR fee-for-service) |
| Where | Milwaukee area; works from home, the car, and client job sites |
| Background | 3-7 years in human services; bachelor's in psychology, criminology, or rehab; CESP certification likely |
| Caseload | About 15-25 active clients (assumption), at every stage: career profile → plan → job development → hire → monthly support |
| Tools (assumed) | Laptop, phone, email, calendar, a case-notes system, Word/PDF report templates, spreadsheets, DVR portal or email for reports |
| Travel | Lots: client homes, employers, job sites, bus rides with clients |

**A typical week**
- Meets clients to build career profiles and job development plans
- Cold-calls and visits employers; searches job boards for each client
- Coaches at job sites; checks in with supervisors
- Writes a report after almost every milestone, **due within 5 business days** (per DVR rules)
- Coordinates with DVR counselors, long-term care managers, families and benefits specialists

**Goals**
- Get the *right* job for each client, not just any job
- Keep clients employed past 90 days
- Spend less time on paperwork and searching listings

**Pain points**
- Matching is manual: job leads are scattered across emails, job boards and memory
- Report deadlines across many clients; documentation has to show specific required elements
- Not sure if every milestone got billed, since billing may be done by someone else
- Rural and transit barriers make good matches hard

**Tech comfort:** medium. Happy with simple web tools; hates double entry and new logins.

**Design implications**
- A caseload view: "3 reports due this week," "2 new matches for Marcus"
- A copy-ready summary for reports and for clients
- Works on a phone in a parking lot
- No new logins; export to what they already use

---

## 2. Pat: benefits specialist (WIBS / CWIC)
Deep expert in SSI/SSDI/Medicaid rules. Does intake, collects signed releases (ROI), verifies benefits with SSA, and writes individualized benefits reports. Mostly remote and statewide. Pain: chasing signatures and documents; re-explaining the same rules. Wants tools that bring clients in **better prepared**, but will reject anything that gives wrong benefits math.

## 3. Finance director
Owns revenue (program fees were about 55% of FY2025 revenue). Wants every authorized and delivered service billed correctly, and nothing billed that wasn't. Comfortable with spreadsheets and exports; thinks in exception reports and dollars at stake. May come from a healthcare billing background (an assumption, not a description of ERI's actual finance staff).

## 4. Client services director / program manager
Oversees employment and benefits teams. Cares about quality, compliance, deadlines and staff workload. Wants a dashboard of late reports, missing documentation and outcomes.

## 5. Web developer (the maintainer)
ERI's senior web developer has 20+ years building sites and third-party tools (public bio). WordPress multisite. Will inherit your code. Wants: standard stack, no paid lock-in, a README that runs, escaped output, no secrets in code.


<!-- FILE: wiki/personas/job-seekers.md -->

# Job seeker personas

## 1. Marcus: the average user (primary persona)
> "I want a real job, like 20 hours. But my mom says if I make too much I lose my SSI."

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Age | 23 |
| Where | Sherman Park, Milwaukee; rides MCTS buses |
| Disability | Autism (the 2nd most common primary disability at DVR); ADHD |
| Benefits | SSI (federal rate up to $994/month in 2026, $1,029 in 2027; living arrangements can lower it) and Medicaid |
| Programs | DVR (has an IPE); possibly referred to ERI for Supported Employment and benefits counseling |
| Education | High school diploma + a transition program |
| Work history | School-based work experience at a grocery store; a summer job stocking shelves |
| Wants | 20-25 h/week, daytime, stocking, warehouse sorting or kitchen prep (DVR's top job types); about $15-17/h |
| Phone | Android, prepaid data plan; uses YouTube and TikTok, rarely email |
| Reads | Short, plain text; long paragraphs and forms overwhelm him |

**Goals**
- A job he can get to by bus in under 45 minutes
- Clear steps: what to do next, by when
- Money of his own without "messing up" SSI

**Fears and pain points**
- Losing SSI or Medicaid (the #1 fear across ERI's stories)
- Interviews; unclear instructions; noisy, chaotic workplaces
- Job sites with long applications, CAPTCHAs, timed personality tests
- Not knowing who to call: DVR counselor, ERI specialist, or benefits person

**Accommodations that help:** written step-by-step instructions, a quiet space, a job coach for the first weeks, a predictable schedule.

**Design implications**
- Plain language at a 6th-grade level, one action per screen, big tap targets
- Show the bus and the commute time up front
- A benefits "heads-up," never benefits advice: "Talk to a benefits specialist before you say yes"
- Let him share a job with his specialist or his mom in one tap

---

## 2. Dana: working with mental health conditions
> "I can do 15 to 20 hours if the schedule is steady. More than that and I crash."

41, Madison. Depression, anxiety, PTSD; on **SSDI** (inspired by the kind of path in [Susan's story](https://eri-wi.org/susans-story/)). In a recovery program (CCS). Has a college background but wants low-stress work. She has stitched together two or three part-time jobs. Wants a budget that shows SSDI plus wages month by month. Fears using up Trial Work Period months without knowing it.
**Design for:** calm UI, no urgency language, and a "what does this job do to my month" view.

## 3. Renee: the professional returner
> "I was scared to death to leave the security of disability." (paraphrasing the theme of [Sarah's story](https://eri-wi.org/sarahs-story/))

38, Middleton. Epilepsy, now controlled; on **SSDI** and using **Ticket to Work** (ERI PLUS). She has a strong résumé and a career gap. Employers have been hesitant. Needs: flexible schedule, no driving requirement, and help reporting wages to SSA correctly. Very tech-comfortable; uses a laptop and LinkedIn.
**Design for:** filters for "no driver's license required" and "flexible," plus a wage-reporting checklist.

## 4. Jordan (16) and his mom Lisa: turning 18
16, Green Bay. Intellectual disability; on CLTS; IEP at school. Lisa is the main user. She's juggling guardianship vs supported decision-making, SSI at 18, DVR referral, and school-to-work. Uses Facebook groups and ERI's [Before Age 18](https://beforeage18.org) site.
**Design for:** a timeline by age, a checklist, and "print for the IEP meeting."

## 5. Family member / support person (secondary)
Wants visibility without taking over. Often the one reading benefits letters. Needs a "shared with me" view and plain explanations.

## 6. Hiring manager at a Milwaukee employer (secondary)
Runs a warehouse or kitchen and has open shifts. Unsure what accommodations cost (often nothing) and worried about "getting it wrong." Doesn't know ERI exists. Wants pre-screened candidates, one contact person, and job-coach support.
**Design for:** a 2-minute "post a job with ERI" flow, plus an inclusive job-post checker.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/01-funding-gap-finder.md -->

# PRD 01: Funding gap finder

> **RETIRED for Hackreation 2026. Not in scope.** See [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md).
>
> **SUPERSEDED, 2026-10-26.** ERI supplied their own four problem statements;
> this PRD was our guess and is not one of them. See
> [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md) and
> [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-pivot-to-eri-problem-statements.md). The code
> under `challenges/` stays until its replacement runs, because its test
> harness is being ported, not thrown away.

**Status:** v0.2, **Hello world:** [`challenges/01-funding-gap-finder`](../../challenges/01-funding-gap-finder/), **Data:** `data/dvr/`, `data/ticket/`, `data/county/`, **Personas:** finance director, [Alex](../personas/eri-staff.md)

> **Our assumptions (ERI: keep / kill / change)**
> 1. Some delivered work goes unbilled or underbilled across DVR, Ticket to Work and county contracts.
> 2. Billing and case notes live in systems that can export CSV.
> 3. A weekly exception list a person reviews beats any automation.
> 4. This stays a prototype until ERI decides on data access.

## Problem
ERI is paid only when work is **authorized → delivered → documented → claimed**. Each funder has different rules, so gaps hide in the seams: a retention month never invoiced, a Ticket payment never requested, county units under-claimed. Program revenue was $1.68M in FY2025 (all programs), so small leaks add up.

## The one idea
Turn every funder's export into **one common ledger**: `funder, client, period, service, delivered, claimed, expected $, claimed $, evidence`. Then **one check**, expected vs claimed, works everywhere.

## Demo (3 minutes)
"Here are three fake exports. One command builds the ledger. Here are 22 flags: $4.8K DVR, $6.9K Ticket, and 4 county **over-claims** marked as risk. Click one to see the evidence. A person decides."

## MVP: already working in the hello world
- ETL for DVR monthly support, Ticket to Work (simplified), county units
- Generic under/over-claim check, plus a filterable accessible table

## Team stretch goals (pick 1-2)
- DVR Job Development & Hire, including preferred outcomes ($2,000 / $2,200)
- Late-report flags (more than 5 business days)
- Ticket "missing evidence" (no pay stub) as its own action
- A review workflow with an audit trail (who / when / decision) (big)
- Wrap it as a WordPress admin page. Test site and synthetic data only: billing data never goes on ERI's public sites.

## Acceptance criteria (spec)
Each criterion is tested. Scenarios in `challenges/01-funding-gap-finder/features/` are tagged with these IDs, and PHPUnit tests name them in their docblocks.

| ID | Given / When / Then |
| --- | --- |
| AC-01.1 | Given DVR, Ticket and county exports, when the ETL runs, then every row lands in **one ledger** with the same columns |
| AC-01.2 | Given a delivered DVR monthly support note with no invoice, then it is flagged **under-claimed** (3 in the sample) |
| AC-01.3 | Given a month where the note says the client was **not employed**, then it is **not** flagged |
| AC-01.4 | Given a Ticket payment earned (with a pay stub) but not requested, then it is flagged (5 in the sample) |
| AC-01.5 | Given county units delivered > claimed, then it is flagged under-claimed (10 in the sample) |
| AC-01.6 | Given claimed > delivered, then it is flagged **over-claimed (risk)** with a negative amount, never as money to collect (4 in the sample) |
| AC-01.7 | Every flag carries **evidence** (a note id or source row) |

## Adversarial debate
| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "ERI can't use this. It needs real data and IT approval." | True. It's a **prototype + recommendation**. The deliverable is the pattern and the ledger schema; ERI finance staff can map a real export to it later, in house. |
| "Billing tools invite gaming." | Flags only, evidence shown, human decides, over-claims surfaced as risk. Never suggests wording. (See [billing integrity](../knowledge/compliance/billing-integrity-and-false-claims.md).) |
| "Simplified Ticket rules are wrong." | They're labeled simplified, and real rules are in [ticket-to-work](../knowledge/benefits/ticket-to-work.md). The demo proves the *pattern*, not the payment math. |
| "A spreadsheet pivot could do this." | Maybe! If a team proves that with a clear pivot recipe, that's a win too, and cheaper to adopt. |

**Kill it if:** ERI says billing gaps aren't real, or no one will ever export the data, or ERI's billing system already shows these gaps.

## Monday owner
If ERI continues: ERI finance owns the rules. No code owner until ERI decides on data access; billing data never goes on ERI's public sites. **Volunteer follow-up:** one evening walking finance through the ledger schema using the synthetic data. ERI maps its own exports in house, and no real data leaves ERI. ERI decides whether to continue.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/02-job-fit-checker.md -->

# PRD 02: "Is this job right for me?"

> **RETIRED for Hackreation 2026. Not in scope.** See [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md).
>
> **SUPERSEDED, 2026-10-26.** ERI supplied their own four problem statements;
> this PRD was our guess and is not one of them. See
> [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md) and
> [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-pivot-to-eri-problem-statements.md). The code
> under `challenges/` stays until its replacement runs, because its test
> harness is being ported, not thrown away.

**Status:** v0.2, **Hello world:** [`challenges/02-job-fit-checker`](../../challenges/02-job-fit-checker/), **Data:** `data/job_postings.csv`, `data/job_seekers.csv`, **Persona:** [Marcus](../personas/job-seekers.md) (and [agent](../../agents/avg-job-seeker.md))

> **Our assumptions (ERI: keep / kill / change)**
> 1. Fear of losing SSI/SSDI or Medicaid stops people from taking jobs.
> 2. A public, anonymous tool on eri-wi.org that sends people to ERI is useful and safe.
> 3. Plain language and mobile-first matter more than features.
> 4. Nothing typed in is stored or sent anywhere.

## Problem
"Connect job seekers with jobs" breaks down at the moment of a job offer. People can't tell whether it fits: the hours, the bus, and above all *what happens to my benefits*. They either turn it down or call ERI with the same question.

## The one idea
A 4-question check (hours, pay, benefit type, bus) → plain-language result: monthly pay, an SSI/SSDI heads-up with 2026/2027 numbers, and the commute. Always **"Estimate only: call WIPA."** Everything runs in the browser.

## Demo (3 minutes)
Play Marcus: "20 hours at $15, I get SSI, there's a bus." → "About $1,299 a month; your SSI check might be about $387; Medicaid may continue; call WIPA." Then: it's a WordPress shortcode, so ERI's web team could test it on a page.

## MVP: already working in the hello world
- The estimator (SSI rough math, SSDI TWP/SGA, 2026/2027 switch), accessible form, WordPress plugin

## Team stretch goals (pick 1-2)
- Choose a real-looking posting from `job_postings.csv` and score fit against a 3-question profile
- Commute time from MCTS GTFS (big: needs a data download)
- "Send to my ERI specialist" (mailto or print; nothing stored)
- Spanish; a reading-level check

## Acceptance criteria (spec)
Tested by `challenges/02-job-fit-checker/test/` (node:test) and `features/` (Cucumber, tagged with these IDs).

| ID | Given / When / Then |
| --- | --- |
| AC-02.1 | Monthly pay = hours × wage × 4.33, rounded to whole dollars |
| AC-02.2 | Given SSI, then a rough check estimate = federal max − (monthly pay − $85) ÷ 2, never below $0 |
| AC-02.3 | Given SSDI and pay above SGA, then a heads-up; pay between TWP and SGA, then a trial-work note |
| AC-02.4 | Uses the right year's SSA numbers (2026: TWP $1,210 / SGA $1,690; 2027: $1,270 / $1,770) |
| AC-02.5 | **Always** shows "Estimate only" and the WIPA number 1-877-826-1752 |
| AC-02.6 | Given no bus and a commute over 45 minutes, then a commute warning |
| AC-02.7 | The page has **no axe violations**, every input has a label, and focus moves to the result heading |
| AC-02.8 | Makes **no network requests** and stores nothing |

## Adversarial debate
| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "Benefits math online will mislead people." | It's labeled rough, uses conservative wording ("may"), and always routes to WIPA. Before any launch, ERI's benefits staff would need to review the copy. |
| "This isn't connecting people to jobs." | It removes the #1 blocker at the moment of an offer, and it sends people to ERI. Stretch: pick from postings. |
| "SSI rules are more complex (state supplement, deeming, IRWE)." | Yes, which is exactly why it says "rough guess" and hands off to a human. Don't add complexity in one day. |

**Kill it if:** ERI's benefits team says any estimate is too risky to publish. Then fall back to a plain "what to ask before you say yes" checklist.

## Monday owner
If ERI picks it: ERI web team. **Volunteer follow-up:** evening 1, install it on a test page with the web developer. Evening 2, the benefits manager reviews the copy. ERI decides whether and when it goes live.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/03-job-post-checker.md -->

# PRD 03: Inclusive job post checker

> **RETIRED for Hackreation 2026. Not in scope.** See [START-HERE.md](../../START-HERE.md).
>
> **SUPERSEDED, 2026-10-26.** ERI supplied their own four problem statements;
> this PRD was our guess and is not one of them. See
> [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md) and
> [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-pivot-to-eri-problem-statements.md). The code
> under `challenges/` stays until its replacement runs, because its test
> harness is being ported, not thrown away.

**Status:** v0.2, **Hello world:** [`challenges/03-job-post-checker`](../../challenges/03-job-post-checker/), **Data:** `data/job_postings.csv` (46/60 contain planted barrier phrases), **Persona:** hiring manager ([job-seekers.md #6](../personas/job-seekers.md))

> **Our assumptions (ERI: keep / kill / change)**
> 1. ERI wants more employer relationships (Business Services).
> 2. A free, useful tool is a better door-opener than a brochure.
> 3. Employers won't paste anything sensitive; job posts are public anyway.

## Problem
Job posts often include requirements that aren't essential but screen out disabled applicants: lifting 50 lbs for a desk job, "valid driver's license," "must hear the phone." Employers don't notice, and they don't know ERI can help.

## The one idea
Paste a job post → flagged phrases, why they matter, suggested rewrites, an accommodation statement, and **"Talk to ERI Business Services."**

## Demo (3 minutes)
Paste a synthetic posting → score 45/100 → three fixes → the rewritten line → the ERI link. "Every employer who uses this meets ERI."

## MVP: already working in the hello world
- 10 rules, a score, the accommodation statement, the ERI link, and a WordPress plugin

## Team stretch goals (pick 1-2)
- One-click rewrite; more rules with fewer false positives
- Optional LLM rewrite (public text only; demo only, not part of the plugin ERI would host)
- An unbranded, accessible inclusive-hiring checklist page (HTML, not PDF); a "have ERI review my post" link (mailto or ERI's contact page; nothing stored)

## Acceptance criteria (spec)
Tested by `challenges/03-job-post-checker/test/` (node:test) and `features/` (Cucumber, tagged with these IDs).

| ID | Given / When / Then |
| --- | --- |
| AC-03.1 | Given a post with a barrier phrase, then it's flagged with **why** and a **suggested rewrite** |
| AC-03.2 | Given no accommodation statement, then one is suggested |
| AC-03.3 | Given an inclusive post, then **no** flags |
| AC-03.4 | Flags barrier phrases in more than 20 of the 60 sample postings |
| AC-03.5 | Shows "Talk to ERI Business Services" and "guidance only, not legal advice" |
| AC-03.6 | The page has **no axe violations**; result focus moves to the heading |
| AC-03.7 | Pasted HTML is shown as text, never run (no injection) |

## Adversarial debate
| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "Employers may need those requirements." | The tool says "include it only if it's essential." The employer decides. It's guidance, not legal advice. |
| "Low impact for job seekers." | Indirect but real: better posts mean more applicants, and every user is a potential ERI employer partner. |
| "Off-theme." | It's the employer side of "connect job seekers with jobs." |

**Kill it if:** ERI doesn't want to grow employer services right now, or ERI's web team can't maintain a second plugin (see [hackathon value plan](../knowledge/org/hackathon-value-plan.md): adopting more than two projects is a likely failure mode).

## Monday owner
If ERI picks it: ERI web team + Employment Services manager. **Volunteer follow-up:** evening 1, install the plugin on a test page with the web developer. Evening 2, the Employment Services manager reviews the wording. ERI decides whether and when it goes live.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/README.md -->

# PRDs: four, one per ERI project

The projects, in ERI's own words, are in [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md). Each PRD turns one of them into acceptance criteria (`AC-P2.3`). Where a PRD and ERI's document disagree, ERI wins. Which event day, which team and which door: the [event page](../event/hackreation.md).

| # | PRD | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | [Show Your Skills](p1-show-your-skills.md) | [challenges/p1-show-your-skills](../../challenges/p1-show-your-skills) |
| P2 | [My Workday Assistant](p2-my-workday-assistant.md) | [challenges/p2-my-workday-assistant](../../challenges/p2-my-workday-assistant) |
| P3 | [Job Coach Connection](p3-job-coach-connection.md) | [challenges/p3-job-coach-connection](../../challenges/p3-job-coach-connection) |
| P4 | [Employer Opportunity & Support Hub](p4-employer-hub.md) | [challenges/p4-employer-hub](../../challenges/p4-employer-hub) |

**Each PRD has:** an assumptions box, a working hello world in `challenges/`, mock data, personas, and a "who owns it Monday" line. Each project has its own folder, data, tests and spec, so a team never depends on another team.

**Retired:** `01-funding-gap-finder.md`, `02-job-fit-checker.md`, `03-job-post-checker.md` and [cut-list.md](cut-list.md) are kept as history. They are not event challenges: ignore them.

<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/cut-list.md -->

# Cut list (Occam's razor)

> **RETIRED history for Hackreation 2026. Not in scope.** It describes the old three ideas (01 to 03), not ERI's four projects. See [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md).

The razor: **asked for by ERI?** · **usable by ERI's web team within two volunteer evenings?** · **demo-able in about 4 hours?** · **safe without real data?**

| Idea | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full job board / matching platform | Cut | Needs a real job feed, accounts and maintenance. Four teams would build four job boards nobody adopts. The core value moved into PRD 02 |
| Standalone benefits estimator | Merged into 02 | Same user and moment; one tool beats two |
| Form-filling guide (DVR, SSA, benefits forms) | Cut for now | Forms vary and change; wrong guidance has real consequences; it's content-heavy, not code; it overlaps ERI's Benefits Application Services. Good *post-event* content project with ERI's benefits team |
| Accessible intake + release forms | Cut | Touches PII and consent; needs ERI's IT and legal; can't ship from a hackathon |
| Report / case-note drafting with AI | Cut | DVR requires consumer consent for AI; real notes are sensitive. Revisit after ERI has an AI policy |
| Turning-18 navigator | Cut | ERI already has Before Age 18 and its planning tool; better to improve that site than build a new one |
| Spreadsheet pivot "skill" for billing | Kept inside 01 | Allowed as a team's approach in 01 (synthetic data only at the hackathon) |
| Multi-funder revenue platform | Kept as the *story* of 01 | Built for DVR + mocks only; the pattern is what ERI keeps |


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/p1-show-your-skills.md -->

# PRD: Show Your Skills

**ERI project 1** · **Status:** from ERI, 2026-10-26 · **Source:** [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md#project-1-show-your-skills)

**Suggested stack:** `starters/static-web`; the portfolio exports as a file. Media capture via a file input with the `capture` attribute. Use `expo-supabase` only if you want a real view-only link, and own the hosting question. See [tech-stack.md](../company/tech-stack.md#pick-by-project).

> **This PRD is downstream of ERI's own words.** Where it differs from the
> source, the source wins. Our additions are marked *(ours)* and ERI may
> keep / kill / change them.

## 1. Problem

Traditional resumes may not accurately represent a person's abilities,
particularly with limited work experience, a communication disability, or
difficulty describing strengths in writing. Job seekers need accessible ways to
show skills; employers need straightforward ways to see how those skills relate
to job responsibilities.

## 2. Users

| Persona | Goal | Pain today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job seeker with a disability | Show what I can actually do | A resume hides my ability behind writing |
| Job coach / employment specialist | Help organize someone's work examples | No shared place to put photos, video, notes |
| Employer / hiring manager | Understand an applicant's skills fast | Must infer ability from a thin resume |

## 3. Hackathon MVP (ERI's list, verbatim scope)

- [ ] Enter basic profile information
- [ ] Select or enter **three** skills
- [ ] Add **at least one** example of a skill
- [ ] Display it as a simple portfolio
- [ ] Share or export the portfolio

**Out of scope today (ERI):** commercial job board integration, automated
hiring or applicant scoring, employer account management, AI-generated
assessments of suitability, identity verification, production hosting.

## 4. User stories

- As a job seeker, I want to show a video of myself completing a work task so
  employers can see my skills.
- As a person who has difficulty writing, I want to use pictures or audio to
  explain my abilities.
- As a job coach, I want to help someone organize their work examples.
- As an employer, I want to quickly understand an applicant's skills without
  navigating a complicated website.

## 5. Data

`challenges/p1-show-your-skills/fixtures/` — a skills vocabulary and a set of
sample work examples with captions and transcripts, all synthetic. Sample media
only, per ERI §10. *(ours)* Keep the skill names consistent with P4's task
vocabulary so a team can demo the P1→P4 handoff ERI names in P4 §12.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- **AC-P1.1** Given an empty portfolio, when the user enters a display name and
  interests, then the portfolio shows them without requiring a legal name.
- **AC-P1.2** Given the skill step, when the user picks from the list or types
  a custom skill, then three skills can be recorded.
- **AC-P1.3** Given a skill, when the user attaches a photo, audio, video or
  written example, then it appears under that skill with its caption or
  transcript.
- **AC-P1.4** Given a completed portfolio, when an employer opens the preview,
  then at least three skills are identifiable without instruction.
- **AC-P1.5** Given a completed portfolio, when the user chooses to share, then
  a view-only link or downloadable file is produced **and the user chooses what
  it contains**.
- **AC-P1.6** Given any step, when the user navigates by keyboard only, then
  every control is reachable and focus is visible.
- **AC-P1.7** Given any image, audio or video, then a text alternative,
  caption or transcript is present.
- **AC-P1.8** Given the whole flow, then no step imposes a time limit.
- **AC-P1.9** *(ours)* Given the running app, then it makes no network request;
  nothing leaves the browser.

## 7. Accessibility

Keyboard and screen reader, plain-language instructions, alternatives to typed
input, labels/captions/transcripts, no time limits, user controls what is
shared. One real screen reader pass is required, not optional.

## 8. Risks and guardrails

- **Never require disclosure of a disability or diagnosis.** Not a field, not a
  prompt, not an inference.
- Demonstration content only with consent; use the synthetic sample media.
- Do not score, rank or assess the person. ERI put AI-generated suitability
  assessment out of scope explicitly.
- A portfolio is the person's own. Sharing is their decision each time.

## 9. What ERI needs to adopt it

Browser-only, nothing stored server-side, so ERI's web team can review it as a
static page or a WordPress plugin. Media hosting is the open question — a real
deployment needs a decision about where video lives and who can reach it.

## 10. Adversarial debate

| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "This is just a resume builder" | A resume is text. The point is the non-text path: ERI's success criteria require at least one non-text method |
| "Employers won't open a link from a stranger" | Which is why the share artifact must also be downloadable and skimmable in under a minute |
| "Video hosting makes this unhostable for ERI" | True for production. For the hackathon, local sample media; name the hosting decision rather than hide it |

**Kill it if:** a job seeker cannot finish a portfolio in 5–10 minutes with
prepared examples, or an employer cannot name three skills after reading one.

## 11. Monday owner

ERI to name. The adopt path runs through the web team.

## 12. Demo script (3 min)

A job seeker builds a portfolio showing they can organize supplies, greet
customers and follow a checklist. An employer opens it and reads those three
skills back.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/p2-my-workday-assistant.md -->

# PRD: My Workday Assistant

**ERI project 2** · **Status:** from ERI, 2026-10-26 · **Source:** [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md#project-2-my-workday-assistant)

**Suggested stack:** `starters/static-web`, phone-first, usable at 320px. Audio via `speechSynthesis` **only if the workspace image has voices — that is unverified, so test it before building on it**; pre-recorded audio files otherwise. The text is shown either way. See [tech-stack.md](../company/tech-stack.md#pick-by-project).

> **This PRD is downstream of ERI's own words.** Where it differs from the
> source, the source wins. Our additions are marked *(ours)*.

## 1. Problem

Some employees need support to remember task sequences, understand
instructions, transition between activities, or handle a changed workday.
Printed checklists and verbal instructions do not always fit. Job coaches and
supervisors need a simple way to make accessible instructions the employee can
use on their own.

## 2. Users

| Persona | Goal | Pain today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Employee with a disability | Finish the task without asking again | Instructions were verbal and are gone |
| Job coach | Build a task guide quickly | Paper checklists don't carry pictures or audio |
| Supervisor / trainer | Update steps when the process changes | Reprint everything, hope it reaches people |

## 3. Hackathon MVP (ERI's list, verbatim scope)

- [ ] List **three** sample workplace tasks
- [ ] Select a task
- [ ] Show it in manageable steps, **pictures and text**
- [ ] Mark each step complete
- [ ] Show completion progress
- [ ] A simple **"I Need Help"** option

**Out of scope today (ERI):** scheduling or time tracking, payroll, automated
performance evaluation, location tracking, extensive employer management, AI
task analysis.

## 4. User stories

- As an employee, I want pictures for each step so I can finish without asking
  my supervisor repeatedly.
- As an employee, I want to listen to instructions rather than read them.
- As a job coach, I want to quickly create a task checklist.
- As a supervisor, I want to update instructions when a process changes.
- As an employee, I want to say I need help without feeling embarrassed.

## 5. Data

`challenges/p2-my-workday-assistant/fixtures/` — three synthetic tasks with ordered
steps, each step carrying text, an image or icon, and an audio transcript.
"Stock the Shelves" is ERI's suggested demo and should be one of them.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- **AC-P2.1** Given the task list, when it loads, then three tasks are shown
  with large labelled controls.
- **AC-P2.2** Given a selected task, when it opens, then exactly **one step** is
  shown at a time with Back and Next.
- **AC-P2.3** Given a step, then it carries **at least two formats** — text and
  a picture at minimum.
- **AC-P2.4** Given a step, when the user marks it complete, then progress
  updates and the current step and what comes next are both identifiable.
- **AC-P2.5** Given any step, when the user asks to repeat it, then the
  instruction is available again, including the audio.
- **AC-P2.6** Given any screen, then "I Need Help" is reachable in one action.
- **AC-P2.7** Given the whole flow, then nothing expires and no step requires a
  fast response.
- **AC-P2.8** Given a phone-width screen (320px), then the task is completable.
- **AC-P2.9** *(ours)* Given completion data, then it stays in the browser; no
  progress is transmitted anywhere.

## 7. Accessibility

Large clearly labelled controls, images + text + optional audio, plain language
and short sentences, keyboard and screen reader, no time pressure, repeatable
instructions, minimal distraction, works on a phone or tablet.

## 8. Risks and guardrails

- **This is a support tool, not a monitoring tool.** It must not be designed so
  an employer can measure a worker without their knowledge. Progress is private
  to the employee unless they understand and agree to share it.
- Task instructions must reflect real workplace requirements; anything
  potentially unsafe is for qualified staff to review, not a hackathon team.
- Do not gamify completion speed. Measuring how fast a disabled employee works
  is the surveillance failure wearing a friendly hat.

## 9. What ERI needs to adopt it

Phone-first. The coach-authoring side is the part that decides adoption: if
making a guide is harder than writing it on paper, it will not get used.

## 10. Adversarial debate

| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "This is a checklist app" | The MVP is. The requirement that makes it not one is two formats per step plus repeatability |
| "Employers will use it to track people" | Which is why progress is local and private by default, and why that is an AC rather than a value |
| "Coaches won't author content" | Then the tool fails. Authoring effort is the real success criterion; ERI listed it first |

**Kill it if:** a coach cannot build a basic guide from a template, or an
employee cannot complete a five-step task unaided.

## 11. Monday owner

ERI to name — likely employment services rather than the web team.

## 12. Demo script (3 min)

An employee opens "Stock the Shelves," is walked through gathering supplies,
checking labels, placing product and cleaning up, marks each step, and
finishes.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/p3-job-coach-connection.md -->

# PRD: Job Coach Connection

**ERI project 3** · **Status:** from ERI, 2026-10-26 · **Source:** [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md#project-3-job-coach-connection)

**Suggested stack:** `starters/static-web` with two tabs (employee + coach inbox) synced by `BroadcastChannel`. A backend only if requests must cross devices. See [tech-stack.md](../company/tech-stack.md#pick-by-project).

> **This PRD is downstream of ERI's own words.** Where it differs from the
> source, the source wins. Our additions are marked *(ours)*.

## 1. Problem

Employees sometimes need help with a task, a change in routine, or something
unexpected — but asking is hard: a communication disability, not knowing who to
contact, or not wanting to interrupt a supervisor. Coaches support several
people across worksites and cannot always be there in person.

## 2. Users

| Persona | Goal | Pain today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Employee receiving job coaching | Ask for help without a phone call | Typing is hard; interrupting feels worse |
| Job coach | See what kind of help is needed before responding | A missed call says nothing about urgency |
| Workplace support staff | Step in when authorized | No clear boundary of who may receive what |

## 3. Hackathon MVP (ERI's list, verbatim scope)

- [ ] A clearly labelled **"I Need Help"** option
- [ ] Choose from **four** common support needs
- [ ] An optional short text message
- [ ] Send to a demonstration coach dashboard
- [ ] Coach acknowledges and responds
- [ ] Response appears on the employee's screen

**Out of scope today (ERI):** personnel system integration, medical or
emergency response, video calling, automated monitoring, production case
management, multi-agency coordination.

## 4. User stories

- As an employee, I want to ask for help using pictures because typing is hard.
- As an employee, I want to know when my coach has received my request.
- As a coach, I want to see what type of help is needed before contacting them.
- As an employee, I want a simple way to say I am confused or something
  unexpected happened.
- As a coach, I want to reply with a short, clear, easy-to-understand message.

## 5. Data

`challenges/p3-job-coach-connection/fixtures/` — the four support-need options with
icons, a set of predefined employee messages, and predefined coach replies. All
synthetic; the coach inbox is simulated, per ERI's MVP wording.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- **AC-P3.1** Given any screen, then "I Need Help" is present, large, and
  labelled with both icon and text.
- **AC-P3.2** Given a help request, when the employee uses predefined options,
  then it is submitted in **three interactions or fewer**.
- **AC-P3.3** Given a request, then **at least one** non-typed path exists
  (picture or predefined message).
- **AC-P3.4** Given a sent request, then the employee sees clear confirmation
  and a status of sent / seen / answered.
- **AC-P3.5** Given a sent request, then it appears in the coach dashboard with
  its support-need type visible before opening.
- **AC-P3.6** Given a request, when the coach responds, then the response
  appears on the employee's screen.
- **AC-P3.7** Given the session, then the employee can review previous messages.
- **AC-P3.8** Given any screen, then it is clear **who** will receive the
  message.
- **AC-P3.9** Given an urgent or unsafe situation, then the product routes to
  established emergency procedures and does **not** present itself as the path.
- **AC-P3.10** *(ours)* Given the coach dashboard, then the product never
  implies the coach is currently available or will reply within any time.

## 7. Accessibility

Large buttons with icons **and** text labels, short plain-language options,
screen reader and keyboard, alternatives to typing, clear send confirmation,
easy review of prior messages, no deep menus.

## 8. Risks and guardrails

- **AC-P3.9 is the one that matters most.** A help button that looks like it
  summons help, in a real emergency, is harmful. Routine coaching and emergency
  must be visibly different paths.
- Never imply a coach is always available. Status must not read as presence.
- The recipient must be named. "Sent to your coach" is not enough if the
  employee cannot tell who that is.
- This is not monitoring. Coaches see requests, not activity.

## 9. What ERI needs to adopt it

A production version needs real authentication, protected transport, a record
retention policy and stated response expectations. Say that out loud in the
demo — ERI wrote it into the statement and it is the honest framing.

## 10. Adversarial debate

| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "It's a chat app" | A chat app starts with a blank box. Everything here is about not needing one |
| "Creates dependence on the coach" | ERI's own key design question. Favour predefined answers that resolve without contact |
| "Simulated inbox isn't a product" | For one day it is the honest scope; ERI specified a simulated coach inbox |

**Kill it if:** a request takes more than three interactions, or the employee
cannot tell whether it was received.

## 11. Monday owner

ERI to name — employment services, with a web-team review of the transport
question.

## 12. Demo script (3 min)

An employee doesn't understand a new task. They tap "I Need Help," then "I
don't understand my task." The coach sees the type, responds, and the employee
reads it and carries on.


<!-- FILE: wiki/prds/p4-employer-hub.md -->

# PRD: Employer Opportunity & Support Hub

**ERI project 4** · **Status:** from ERI, 2026-10-26 · **Source:** [docs/eri-problem-statements.md](../../docs/eri-problem-statements.md#project-4-employer-opportunity--support-hub)

**Suggested stack:** `starters/static-web`, then wrap as a WordPress plugin — the most WordPress-ready of the four. No LLM scoring of candidates; see [tech-stack.md](../company/tech-stack.md#eris-limits-on-ai).

> **This PRD is downstream of ERI's own words.** Where it differs from the
> source, the source wins. Our additions are marked *(ours)*.

## 1. Problem

Employers may want to hire people with disabilities but lack the experience to
connect a person's skills to their business needs, shape meaningful
responsibilities, respond well to a disclosure, handle an accommodation
request, or plan onboarding. Good resources exist; they are not joined into one
workflow.

## 2. Users

| Persona | Goal | Pain today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small/midsize employer, hiring manager | See how a candidate's strengths meet real business needs | Job descriptions are fixed; strengths don't map onto them |
| Supervisor / HR | Respond correctly to a disclosure or request | Fear of getting it legally wrong |
| Job developer / ERI business services | Facilitate the employer conversation | No shared artifact to work from |

## 3. Hackathon MVP (ERI's list — they named the focus)

ERI: *"focus primarily on the skills-to-tasks matching feature."*

- [ ] Select an industry or business type
- [ ] Describe **three to five** workplace needs or recurring tasks
- [ ] Enter a **fictional** candidate's skills, interests and preferences
- [ ] Suggest matches between skills and tasks
- [ ] **Explain why** each task might be a good match
- [ ] Show a simple employer action plan with next steps

**Optional if time:** disclosure scenario guide, accommodation resource links,
basic onboarding checklist.

**Out of scope today (ERI):** applicant tracking, automatic employment
decisions, ADA compliance management, payroll/HR integration, production
storage of medical or disability information, cross-organization matchmaking.

## 4. User stories

- As an employer, I want to understand how a candidate's skills could meet my
  business needs.
- As a hiring manager, I want to know how to respond when an applicant
  discloses a disability.
- As a supervisor, I want practical ideas for adapting how tasks are taught.
- As an employer, I want help with an accommodation request without assuming
  anything about the person's disability.
- As a job developer, I want something that helps me run the employer
  conversation.

## 5. Data

`challenges/p4-employer-hub/fixtures/` — industries with recurring tasks, a skills
vocabulary, and fictional candidate profiles. *(ours)* Share the skill
vocabulary with P1 so the handoff ERI describes in §12 can be demonstrated.
Resource links: JAN, EEOC, DVR.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- **AC-P4.1** Given the start, when an employer picks an industry and enters
  three to five needs, then the assessment completes.
- **AC-P4.2** Given a fictional candidate's skills and preferences, then **at
  least three** plausible workplace tasks are suggested.
- **AC-P4.3** Given each suggestion, then the reasoning is shown — which skill
  and which stated business need it connects.
- **AC-P4.4** Given the suggestions, then they derive from the employer's own
  entered needs, **never from an assumption about disability**.
- **AC-P4.5** Given a completed session, then a simple next-steps plan is
  produced, including questions to discuss with an employment specialist.
- **AC-P4.6** Given any output, then it links to JAN, EEOC, DVR or equivalent
  trusted resources.
- **AC-P4.7** Given the tool, then it never ranks or scores candidates and
  never makes a hiring or accommodation decision.
- **AC-P4.8** Given any screen, then keyboard and screen reader work, the
  language is plain, and it is usable on a phone.
- **AC-P4.9** *(ours)* Given a complex legal question, then the tool refers to
  qualified professionals rather than answering.

## 7. Accessibility

Keyboard and screen reader, plain-language explanations, clear navigation,
mobile-friendly, accessible forms, no time limits, and no disability-based
assumptions or stereotypes in any copy.

## 8. Risks and guardrails

This PRD has the longest guardrail list because ERI wrote one:

- Do not require a candidate to disclose a disability or diagnosis.
- Get permission before sharing candidate portfolio information.
- Do not rank candidates by disability — automatically or otherwise.
- Do not make automated hiring or accommodation decisions.
- Protect confidential employee information.
- **Never suggest an accommodation from a disability label alone.**
- Refer complex legal questions to qualified professionals.

The failure mode to design against: a tool that looks like it is telling an
employer what a disabled person can do. It matches *stated skills* to *stated
business needs*, and shows its reasoning so a human can disagree with it.

## 9. What ERI needs to adopt it

This is the one with outreach value for ERI Business Services — an employer who
works through it and reaches a next-steps plan is a warm conversation. Worth
asking ERI where that should point.

## 10. Adversarial debate

| Against | Response |
| --- | --- |
| "Skills-to-tasks matching is a lookup table" | For one day, yes — and the explanation of *why* is the product, not the match |
| "Employers won't fill in five needs" | Then the MVP is wrong and it should start from the industry template. Test it on a real employer at the event |
| "This edges toward automated hiring" | AC-P4.7 forbids it and ERI put it out of scope. No scores, no ranking, no decisions |

**Kill it if:** suggestions don't trace to the employer's own stated needs, or
the reasoning isn't shown.

## 11. Monday owner

ERI to name — business services, with the web team on hosting.

## 12. Demo script (3 min)

A retail business needs inventory, merchandising and display upkeep. A
fictional candidate has strong organizational skills and prefers routine work
with merchandise. The tool proposes responsibilities, explains each, and ends
with a draft task plan and questions for an employment specialist.

# Stack best practices

Practical, copy-pasteable pages for teams (and their AI coding assistants) building on ERI's stack in about 4 hours. Code examples match the repo's hello worlds in `starters/` and `challenges/`. Read [../company/tech-stack.md](../company/tech-stack.md) first to pick a starter, and [../../AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) for the hard rules.

Every page uses the LLM-wiki frontmatter from [../knowledge/_PAGE_SPEC.md](../knowledge/_PAGE_SPEC.md) (`last_verified`, `next_review`, `confidence`, `sources`) with these body sections: **TL;DR, Minimal working example, Do / Don't checklist, Security, Accessibility, Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for, How to hand off to ERI, Sources.** **(verify)** marks anything not confirmed from an opened official source.

## Pages

| Page | Use it for | Starter | Confidence | Next review |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Key version facts (as of 2026-10-23)

| Item | Fact | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WordPress | 7.1.x is current (7.1 released, scheduled for 2026-08-19; 7.1.1 scheduled 2026-09-17). 7.0 released 2026-05-20 | make.wordpress.org/core |
| WordPress minimum PHP | 7.4 from WordPress 7.0; Hosting team recommends PHP 8.4/8.5 and MySQL 8.4 for new installs | make.wordpress.org/hosting |
| PHP | Supported: 8.2 (security until 2026-12-31), 8.3 (to 2027-12-31), 8.4 (to 2028-12-31), 8.5 (to 2029-12-31). 8.1 and older are EOL | php.net |
| MySQL | 8.0 EOL April 2026; 8.4 is the LTS line | Oracle MySQL docs |
| Block API | `apiVersion` 3 (since WP 6.3); iframe editor not yet enforced in 7.0 | Block Editor Handbook, make/core |
| OWASP | Top 10:2025 is the current edition | top10.owasp.org |

## Gaps to flag to ERI
- ERI's production PHP, MySQL/MariaDB and WordPress versions are unknown **(verify with ERI's web team)**; pages assume PHP 8.2+ and WP 6.8+.
- `AGENTS.md` says "PHP 8.1+"; PHP 8.1 is end of life. Suggest "PHP 8.2+ (8.3 preferred)".
- `starters/php-mysql/docker-compose.yml` publishes MySQL (3306) and phpMyAdmin (8081) on all interfaces; bind them to `127.0.0.1` on shared networks.
