# AI-assisted coding in this repo

## TL;DR
- **Load the rules first.** Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, which in this repo says "Read and follow AGENTS.md". Copilot's cloud agent and CLI read `AGENTS.md`. Copilot Chat in VS Code reads `AGENTS.md`, but on GitHub.com, JetBrains and other IDEs it reads only `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. For ChatGPT or Claude.ai chat, **paste `llms.txt`** or upload `llms-full.txt`.
- **Give it the PRD** (`wiki/prds/0X-*.md`) and the challenge folder. Ask for **one small diff at a time**, with a test.
- **You own accessibility, security and facts.** The assistant will write `innerHTML` with user input, put keys in front-end code, and invent SSA numbers. Check each one using the checklist below.
- **Never paste real data.** Use only `data/`, which is synthetic. That applies to prompts and screenshots too.

## Minimal working example
### 1. Kick-off prompt (paste as-is, then edit the bracketed parts)
```text
You are helping my team at Hackreation x ERI. Read AGENTS.md, wiki/ESSENTIALS.md,
wiki/prds/02-job-fit-checker.md and wiki/stack/javascript-jquery.md before writing code.
We work only in teams/[our-team]/. Stack: plain HTML/CSS/JS (IIFE pattern like
challenges/02-job-fit-checker/web/job-fit.js), no build step, no new dependencies.
Data: synthetic files in data/ only.
Task: [one feature, e.g. "add a 'commute minutes' field to the form and the core logic"].
Rules: show a short plan first, then a minimal diff. Add or update tests in tests/test.js
(node, no framework, exit code 1 on failure). Use textContent, never innerHTML with input.
Every input needs a visible label; results get focus or a role="status" update.
Benefits numbers must come from wiki/knowledge/benefits/benefits-quick-reference-2026.md
and be labeled "Estimate only" with WIPA 1-877-826-1752. If unsure, say so; don't guess.
```

### 2. Loop: about 20 minutes per cycle
```bash
# after each AI change
node teams/<team>/tests/test.js        # PASS lines, exit 0
bash tools/check.sh                     # repo smoke tests still pass
git diff --stat                         # is the change small and inside teams/<team>/ ?
```
Then do a **30-second keyboard pass**: Tab through it, submit, and listen for the result. Commit. Next small task.

### 3. Review prompt (use a fresh chat, or ask the tool to review its own diff)
```text
Review this diff for: (1) XSS - any innerHTML/.html() with user, CSV, API or LLM text;
(2) secrets in front-end code or committed .env; (3) missing labels, focus handling,
contrast, 44px targets; (4) any number about SSI/SSDI/DVR not traceable to the wiki;
(5) real-looking personal data. List problems with file:line. Don't rewrite code yet.
```

### Pointing each tool at the rules
| Tool | What it reads | Do this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` (here: "Read and follow AGENTS.md"); it can also use `AGENTS.md` | Start in the repo root |
| Copilot cloud agent / CLI | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Nothing extra |
| Copilot Chat (VS Code) | `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Nothing extra |
| Copilot Chat (GitHub.com, JetBrains, others) | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` only | Attach `AGENTS.md`, or ask organizers to add that file (verify that it exists) |
| ChatGPT / Claude.ai chat | Only what you paste | Paste `llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, the PRD and the file you're changing |
| Expo work, any tool | Training data that is often stale | Also give it `https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt` and `starters/expo-supabase/AGENTS.md` |

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** ask for a plan before code, and **reject diffs that touch `starters/`, `data/` or `wiki/`** unless you asked for that.
- [ ] **Do** ask for tests first, or alongside the code ("write a failing test for X, then make it pass").
- [ ] **Do** make the assistant cite a file or URL for every domain fact. "Where did $1,690 come from?" should have an answer: `wiki/ESSENTIALS.md`.
- [ ] **Do** keep AI features in your app **off by default and mockable**. `starters/ai-helpers/php/llm.php` defaults to mock mode.
- [ ] **Don't** paste names, case notes, SSNs, benefit amounts or screenshots of real systems, even "just to test". Use `data/job_seekers.csv`.
- [ ] **Don't** accept a new npm package, framework or build step without a one-line reason in your README.
- [ ] **Don't** let it "fix" a permission error by disabling RLS, adding a service key, or using `permission_callback => '__return_true'` on a write route.

## Security
- **Secrets:** API keys go in env vars (`LLM_API_KEY`) or a git-ignored `.env`, never in prompts you share and never in browser or Expo code. Supabase: only the publishable/anon key goes to clients. The secret/service_role key "bypasses RLS" and must not be sent "over chat".
- **Output is untrusted.** LLM text rendered in your UI goes through `textContent` or `esc_html`. MDN calls `innerHTML` "probably the most common vector for cross-site scripting (XSS)".
- **Prompt injection:** a synthetic job post can contain "ignore previous instructions". Treat model output as data. Never let it pick URLs to call or SQL to run.
- **Consent rule (real life):** DVR requires a consumer's prior consent before any AI tool touches their information (`wiki/knowledge/compliance/vr-confidentiality-34-cfr-361-38.md`). Build a visible on/off switch.

## Accessibility (check it yourself; assistants claim compliance they don't deliver)
- Ask it to "list every input and its label" and "say where focus goes after submit". Then verify that with the keyboard.
- Run Lighthouse and axe on what it built ([html-css-accessibility.md](html-css-accessibility.md)). Don't accept "this is WCAG compliant" as a claim.
- Ask for plain language at about a 6th-grade level, then read it aloud yourself.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for (and how to check)
| Hallucination | How to check |
| --- | --- |
| **Wrong WordPress hooks**: `register_rest_route` outside `rest_api_init`, no `permission_callback` (a `_doing_it_wrong` notice since WP 5.5), `wp_enqueue_script` called at top level instead of in a `wp_enqueue_scripts` callback or a shortcode | Compare with `starters/wordpress-plugin/eri-hello/eri-hello.php`, [wordpress-plugin.md](wordpress-plugin.md) and developer.wordpress.org. Run with `WORDPRESS_DEBUG: 1` and read the notices |
| **Missing escaping in PHP**: `echo $title` | Must be `esc_html()`, `esc_attr()` or `htmlspecialchars()`. Look for `echo` lines |
| **Outdated Expo APIs**: `expo eject`, a global `expo-cli`, "managed vs bare", `npm install` for native modules, `SafeAreaView` from `react-native` | Expo's `llms.txt` lists these as outdated. Use `npx expo install`, `npx expo-doctor`, and the versioned docs for SDK 58 |
| **Expo Router code in the single-`App.js` starter** (or the reverse) | Look at `index.js` and `package.json`: `expo-router` isn't installed here |
| **Invented SSA/benefits numbers** (an old SGA, a "$2,000 TWP", made-up 2027 figures) | Must match `wiki/ESSENTIALS.md` and `wiki/knowledge/benefits/benefits-quick-reference-2026.md`, e.g. SGA $1,690 / $1,770, TWP $1,210 / $1,270, SSI FBR $994 / $1,029 (2026 / 2027) |
| **Invented phone numbers or programs** | WIPA is 1-877-826-1752. DRW/CAP is 800-928-8778. Anything else needs a source |
| **Dead incentives** pitched to employers (the Section 503 "7% goal", WOTC) | `wiki/ESSENTIALS.md` says both are out as of 2026 |
| **Billing "optimization"** copy for PRD 01 | Forbidden. Tools flag and people decide (`AGENTS.md`) |
| **jQuery 3-only APIs** (`$.trim`, `$.isArray`) | Removed in jQuery 4.0. Use native equivalents |
| **Fake test passes**: a test that prints PASS without asserting anything | Read the test. Break the code on purpose and confirm the test goes red |
| **Made-up model IDs or API fields** in `llm.php` calls | Take model IDs from the provider's docs (`LLM_MODEL` env), and keep mock mode working |

## How to hand off to ERI
- In the team README, say **which AI tools you used and for what**, and which parts a human reviewed line by line.
- Remove prompts, chat logs and any pasted data from the repo. Keep reusable prompts in a `prompts/` folder, as `starters/ai-helpers/prompts/` does.
- The final diff should pass `node tests/test.js` and `bash tools/check.sh`, and should carry a short accessibility note. ERI's small team must be able to read every line without an AI.
- Any AI feature ships **disabled by default**, with a mock mode and a note on the consent requirement.

## Sources
- [Claude Code memory (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)
- [GitHub Copilot custom-instruction support by surface](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-instructions-support)
- [Expo llms.txt](https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt): lists outdated LLM assumptions about Expo
- [WordPress register_rest_route()](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/register_rest_route/): `permission_callback` and the `rest_api_init` requirement
- [Supabase API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys) · [MDN innerHTML security](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/innerHTML)

# Docker and dev environments for the event

## TL;DR
- Docker is **optional**. Every starter has a no-Docker path: `php -S` with SQLite, `python3 -m http.server`, `npx expo start`. Use Docker when you need real MySQL or WordPress.
- Replace `sleep 15` and plain `depends_on` with a **healthcheck + `condition: service_healthy`**. Bind ports to **`127.0.0.1`**, keep passwords in a git-ignored **`.env`**, and `docker compose down -v` at the end.
- **Hosted option:** one **code-server container per team** (code-server doesn't do multi-user in one instance), each with its own password, behind Caddy with HTTPS. **Never** mount the Docker socket into a team container.
- **Codespaces:** personal GitHub Free accounts include **120 core hours and 15 GB-month a month** (Pro: 180 and 20). That's about **60 hours on a 2-core machine**. Organization plans have **no** free quota. The default idle timeout is 30 minutes, and retention is 30 days.

## Minimal working example
`starters/wordpress-plugin/docker-compose.yml`, hardened for the day:

```yaml
# compose.yaml - WordPress + MySQL + phpMyAdmin. Passwords come from .env (git-ignored).
services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8.0
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: wp
      MYSQL_USER: wp
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${WP_DB_PASSWORD:?set WP_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes: ["db_data:/var/lib/mysql"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "mysqladmin ping -h 127.0.0.1 -uroot -p$$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD --silent"]  # (verify)
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s
    deploy: { resources: { limits: { cpus: "1", memory: 1g } } }
  wordpress:
    image: wordpress:6-php8.2-apache
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8000:80"]             # localhost only, not the venue Wi-Fi
    environment:
      WORDPRESS_DB_HOST: db
      WORDPRESS_DB_USER: wp
      WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD: ${WP_DB_PASSWORD}
      WORDPRESS_DB_NAME: wp
      WORDPRESS_DEBUG: 1
    volumes:
      - ./eri-hello:/var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/eri-hello   # bind mount: edit live
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy, restart: true }
    deploy: { resources: { limits: { cpus: "1", memory: 512m } } }
  phpmyadmin:
    image: phpmyadmin:5
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8081:80"]
    environment: { PMA_HOST: db, PMA_USER: wp, PMA_PASSWORD: "${WP_DB_PASSWORD}" }
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
volumes:
  db_data:
```

```bash
# .env next to compose.yaml (git-ignored; commit .env.example):
#   WP_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-synthetic-only
#   MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-too
docker compose config            # shows resolved values; fails early if a ${VAR:?} is missing
docker compose up -d && docker compose ps   # db should show "healthy"
docker stats --no-stream         # confirm limits are applied (verify for your Compose version)
docker compose down -v           # remove containers, network AND the db_data volume
```

For `starters/php-mysql`, apply the same changes: a `db` healthcheck, `depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }`, and remove `sleep 15` from the app's `command`. Note that its compose file also publishes MySQL on `3306` to all interfaces. Bind it to `127.0.0.1:3306:3306`, or drop the port.

### Compose notes
- **Volumes:** named volumes (`db_data`) persist data and are managed by Docker. Bind mounts (`./eri-hello:…`) share files with your editor. Mount data you only read as `:ro`, as the php-mysql starter does with `../../data:/data:ro`.
- **`.env`:** used for `${VAR}` interpolation in the Compose file. A value reaches a container only when you reference it under `environment`. Shell variables beat `--env-file`, which beats `.env`.
- **`down` keeps named volumes** unless you pass `-v`. That's handy mid-day and a leak at the end.

## Hosted shared environment: code-server per team
Use this only if laptops can't run the stack. One VM, one container per team, and only the proxy exposed:

```yaml
# ops/compose.yaml on the event VM (organizers only)
services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    ports: ["80:80", "443:443"]
    volumes: ["./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro", "caddy_data:/data"]
  team-a:
    image: codercom/code-server:latest      # pin the exact version you tested
    environment:
      HASHED_PASSWORD: ${TEAM_A_HASHED_PASSWORD:?}   # in compose, escape $ as $$ inside literal hashes
    volumes: ["team_a_home:/home/coder"]
    deploy: { resources: { limits: { cpus: "2", memory: 3g, pids: 512 } } }
    # NO ports: (reached only through caddy). NO /var/run/docker.sock mount.
  # team-b: ...copy for each team
volumes: { caddy_data: {}, team_a_home: {} }
```
```
# Caddyfile - automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt) once DNS points at the VM
team-a.code.example.org {
  reverse_proxy team-a:8080
}
```
- code-server listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` by default. The official Docker image serves on `0.0.0.0:8080` inside the container (verify), which is what lets Caddy reach `team-a:8080` over the Compose network.
- Docs: "Never expose code-server directly to the internet without some form of authentication and encryption". Logins are rate-limited (2 a minute plus 12 an hour). Keep `auth: password`, never `--auth none`.
- Extensions come from **Open VSX**, not Microsoft's marketplace. Some AI extensions may not be available (verify each one before the day).
- Previews: code-server can proxy app ports at `/proxy/<port>/`. WordPress hard-codes its site URL, so it breaks behind a sub-path. For hosted teams, prefer the static, PHP-with-SQLite and Expo-web starters.
- Without the Docker socket, teams can't run `docker compose` in a hosted container. That's the point: the socket gives root on the host.

## Dev Container / Codespaces alternative
Codespaces' default image already includes Node, PHP and Python, so most teams need **no config**. If you want forwarded ports labeled:
```json
// .devcontainer/devcontainer.json
{
  "name": "hackreation-eri",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/universal:2",
  "forwardPorts": [8000, 8080, 8081],
  "portsAttributes": { "8000": { "label": "web" }, "8081": { "label": "phpMyAdmin" } },
  "postCreateCommand": "node --version && php --version",
  "hostRequirements": { "cpus": 2 }
}
```
(The universal image name and tag are a (verify) item. They aren't on the pages opened.) Each member forks the repo into a **personal** account, so the 120 free core hours apply. Stop the codespace at lunch and delete it after the event.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** pin image tags you've tested (`mysql:8.0`, `wordpress:6-php8.2-apache`, `phpmyadmin:5`). Avoid `latest` on event day.
- [ ] **Do** pre-pull images on venue machines the night before (`docker compose pull`). Venue Wi-Fi is slow.
- [ ] **Don't** publish MySQL or phpMyAdmin on `0.0.0.0` on a shared network.
- [ ] **Don't** put real data in any volume. `data/` is synthetic, and that's all that goes in.

## Security (one-day event)
- **Before:** create one random password per team container and hand it out on paper or in a DM, not in a shared channel. Use a dedicated VM in a throwaway cloud project. Open only ports 22 (keys only), 80 and 443.
- **During:** set resource limits per team so one runaway build can't starve others. Don't keep shell history with keys in it, and don't paste API keys into shared terminals.
- **After (same evening):** `docker compose down -v` on the VM, then destroy the VM. Revoke any event LLM keys. Delete Codespaces. Pause or delete Supabase projects. Have teams rotate any personal keys they used.

## Accessibility
- code-server and VS Code have screen-reader modes, but test with the team's own setup first. Some participants will be faster on their own laptop with their own assistive tech. Always offer the laptop path.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- Writing a `version: "3.8"` key on top (verify that it's obsolete in Compose v2; it's harmless but noise) and old `docker-compose` (v1, hyphenated) commands. Use `docker compose`.
- `depends_on: [db]` presented as "waits for MySQL". It only waits for the container to start, not to be ready.
- `privileged: true` or `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` "so Docker works inside code-server".
- Hard-coding `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root` in a file that is going to a shared VM.
- Inventing Codespaces quotas ("60 free hours"). The quota is 120 **core** hours, which comes to 60 hours only on a 2-core machine.

## How to hand off to ERI
- ERI's hosting runs PHP + MySQL and WordPress, not Docker. Hand off the **plugin folder or PHP app**, with Docker as an optional local way to run it.
- README: one `docker compose up` line, the `.env.example` values to set, the ports, and how to reset (`down -v`).
- Delete event-only infrastructure, such as `ops/` and code-server configs, from what you hand over.

## Sources
- [Compose startup order](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order/) · [Compose services](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/services/) · [Deploy/resources](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/deploy/)
- [Interpolation and .env](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/environment-variables/variable-interpolation/) · [Volumes](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/) · [compose down](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/down/)
- [code-server install](https://coder.com/docs/code-server/install) · [FAQ](https://coder.com/docs/code-server/FAQ) · [Guide](https://coder.com/docs/code-server/guide)
- [Dev Container reference](https://containers.dev/implementors/json_reference/) · [GitHub: intro to dev containers](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/setting-up-your-project-for-codespaces/adding-a-dev-container-configuration/introduction-to-dev-containers)
- [Codespaces usage and quotas](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-codespaces) · [Troubleshooting included usage](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-included-usage)

# Expo and React Native (SDK 58)

## TL;DR
- The starter is on **Expo SDK 58**: `expo ~58.0.17`, **React Native 0.88**, **React 19.3.0**, react-native-web 0.21. It needs **Node 22.13+**, 24.3+ or 26+, and odd-numbered Node releases aren't supported. `docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/` showed v58 on 2026-10-23.
- **Always `npx expo install <pkg>`**, never `npm install <pkg>`. It picks the version that matches the SDK.
- **`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined into the JS bundle in plain text.** Only public values go there (the Supabase URL and publishable/anon key). Never a secret.
- **Expo Go on a physical iPhone may not run SDK 58 yet.** Demo on **web (press `w`)**, Android Expo Go, or the iOS Simulator (verify on the day).

## Minimal working example
```bash
cd starters/expo-supabase
npm install                 # first run only: installs what package.json already pins
npx expo start              # w = web, a = Android, i = iOS simulator, or scan the QR code
npx expo install expo-haptics   # adding a package later: ALWAYS this form
npx expo-doctor             # if anything looks off; then: npx expo install --fix
```

A screen that matches `App.js`: single file, no router, with accessibility props.
```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pressable, Text, TextInput, View, AccessibilityInfo, Platform } from 'react-native';
import { jobFit } from './lib/job-fit'; // copy of the challenge 02 core, exported as an ES module

export function FitCheck() {
  const [hours, setHours] = useState('');
  const [result, setResult] = useState(null);
  function check() {
    const r = jobFit({ hoursPerWeek: hours, wagePerHour: 15, benefit: 'SSI', nearBus: true });
    setResult(r);
    if (Platform.OS === 'ios') AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(`About ${r.monthlyEarnings} dollars a month`);
  }
  return (
    <View>
      <Text nativeID="hoursLabel" style={{ fontSize: 18, fontWeight: '600' }}>Hours each week</Text>
      <TextInput value={hours} onChangeText={setHours} keyboardType="number-pad"
        accessibilityLabel="Hours each week" accessibilityLabelledBy="hoursLabel"
        style={{ borderWidth: 2, borderColor: '#555', borderRadius: 8, padding: 12, fontSize: 18, minHeight: 48 }} />
      <Pressable onPress={check} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Check this job"
        hitSlop={8} style={{ minHeight: 48, minWidth: 48, justifyContent: 'center', backgroundColor: '#0b5cad', borderRadius: 8, marginTop: 12 }}>
        <Text style={{ color: '#fff', fontSize: 18, textAlign: 'center' }}>Check this job</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {/* Android announces changes here; iOS uses announceForAccessibility above */}
      <Text accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" style={{ fontSize: 18, marginTop: 12 }}>
        {result ? `About $${result.monthlyEarnings} a month. ${result.disclaimer}` : ''}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```
`challenges/02-job-fit-checker/web/job-fit.js` is a browser IIFE. For Expo, copy the function body into `lib/job-fit.js` with `export function jobFit…`, or require the UMD file (verify that Metro resolves it). Keep the tests pointing at one source of truth.

### App.js vs Expo Router
- The **repo starter deliberately uses a single `App.js` + `index.js`** (`registerRootComponent(App)`), with no router. Keep it for one or two screens.
- A **new** project from `npx create-expo-app@latest --template default@sdk-58` uses **Expo Router** (file-based routes, TypeScript). `--template blank` has no navigation. While Expo is between SDK versions, leaving out the template tag gave an SDK 57 project, per the create-a-project page on 2026-10-23.
- `starters/expo-supabase/AGENTS.md` contains the Expo template's Router rules ("Routes live in `src/app/`"). **They don't apply to this starter.** Tell your AI assistant so.

### Env vars
```bash
# .env (git-ignored in this starter)
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://YOUR-PROJECT.supabase.co
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR-ANON-OR-PUBLISHABLE-KEY
```
- Read them only as `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_NAME`. **Bracket access and destructuring are not inlined.**
- Load order (development): `.env.development.local` > `.env.local` > `.env.development` > `.env`. In SDK 58, other names such as `.env.staging` are ignored, and Expo CLI now sets `NODE_ENV` before it loads `.env` files.
- After you edit `.env`, do a full reload in the app. A restart isn't required.

### Web export (the easiest thing to hand off)
```bash
npx expo export -p web      # writes dist/ (single-page app by default, web.output: "single")
npx expo serve              # preview dist/ at http://localhost:8081
```
`tools/check.sh` already runs `npx expo export --platform web` as a smoke test.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** check `package.json` for the `expo` major version and read `docs.expo.dev/versions/v58.0.0/` before trusting any snippet.
- [ ] **Do** test on web and on at least one real screen reader (TalkBack on Android, VoiceOver on iOS).
- [ ] **Do** keep touch targets at 48 dp or more (`minHeight: 48`, `hitSlop`), labels on every `TextInput`, and `accessibilityRole="header"` on titles.
- [ ] **Don't** create or edit `ios/` or `android/` folders. They're generated (Continuous Native Generation). Configure through `app.json`.
- [ ] **Don't** add a library with custom native code if you'll demo in Expo Go. It needs a development build.
- [ ] **Don't** `npm i -g expo-cli`. It's deprecated, so use `npx expo`. And `expo eject` is gone; the replacement is `npx expo prebuild`.
- [ ] **Don't** rely on `placeholder` as the label.

## Security
- Everything in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` and everything in the bundle is readable by anyone with the app or web build. **Never** put a Supabase `service_role`/secret key, an LLM API key or a database password there.
- LLM calls from a mobile app need a server in between (a Supabase Edge Function or the PHP helper). For the hackathon, mock them.
- Data: synthetic only. The starter falls back to `data/job_postings.json` when no Supabase env vars are set. Keep that offline path working for the demo.

## Accessibility
| Need | React Native prop | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `accessibilityLabel` (or `aria-label`) | Touchables default to their child text |
| Purpose | `accessibilityRole` (`button`, `header`, `link`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `search`…) | `role` takes precedence. Its values differ: `heading` vs `header`, `img` vs `image` |
| State | `accessibilityState={{ checked, selected, disabled, expanded, busy }}` | |
| Extra hint | `accessibilityHint` | TalkBack always reads it; VoiceOver only if hints are on |
| Group | `accessible` on a `View` | Starter list rows do this with one combined label |
| Announce changes | `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` | **Android only**. On iOS use `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility()` |
| Reduce motion | `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` | Skip animations if true |
| Move focus | `AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(ref, 'focus')` | `setAccessibilityFocus` is deprecated |

The starter's `App.js` hard-codes light colors (`userInterfaceStyle: "light"`). If you add dark mode, check contrast for both themes.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- `npm install some-lib` or `yarn add`. Re-run it as `npx expo install some-lib`.
- Generating `app/_layout.tsx` and Router code inside this single-`App.js` starter, or the other way round.
- `const { EXPO_PUBLIC_X } = process.env` or `process.env['EXPO_PUBLIC_X']`. These come out undefined at runtime.
- `import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native'`. It's **deprecated** in favor of `react-native-safe-area-context`, and its `padding` styles are ignored. The starter's `App.js` still does this, so its `padding: 16` may not apply. Fix it with `npx expo install react-native-safe-area-context` and use its `SafeAreaView`.
- Old SDK APIs. SDK 58 changed `expo-file-system` (`File.write()` is async), removed libSQL from `expo-sqlite`, and RN 0.87 removed `InteractionManager`. Check the versioned docs.
- `expo eject`, "managed vs bare workflow", and `expo build:ios`. Expo's own llms.txt lists these as outdated.
- `accessibilityLiveRegion` treated as cross-platform.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. Ship the **web export** (`dist/`) as the primary artifact, because ERI's team runs websites. Store builds and EAS need an Apple or Google developer account that ERI would own. Don't create accounts for them.
2. In the README, include the run steps, the exact `expo` version, the Node version you used, and whether the app works without Supabase (bundled data).
3. Commit `.env.example`, never `.env`.
4. Run `npx expo-doctor` and note any warnings you left in place.

## Sources
- [Expo v58.0.0 reference](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v58.0.0): RN 0.88, React 19.3.0, Node 22.13+
- [SDK 58 beta changelog](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-58-beta): breaking changes, Node versions, Expo Go notes (beta dated 2026-09-15)
- [Expo llms.txt](https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt) · [Create a project](https://docs.expo.dev/get-started/create-a-project.md) · [create-expo templates](https://docs.expo.dev/more/create-expo.md)
- [Using libraries](https://docs.expo.dev/workflow/using-libraries.md) · [Environment variables](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/environment-variables.md) · [Publishing websites](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/publishing-websites.md)
- [Expo Go version mismatch](https://docs.expo.dev/troubleshooting/expo-go-version-mismatch/) · [Expo Go and the App Store, May 2026](https://expo.dev/changelog/expo-go-and-app-store-may-2026.md)

# HTML, CSS and accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

## TL;DR
- Use **native HTML first**: `<label for>`, `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` for radio groups, `<button>`, `<table>`. The APG "strongly encourages" a native `table` over ARIA grids for static data.
- After a submit, **move focus to the result heading**. Use `role="status"` for short updates that shouldn't move focus, such as "12 of 60 jobs". WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) requires status messages to be announced without a focus change.
- Key numbers: text contrast **4.5:1** (large text 3:1), UI and focus contrast **3:1** (1.4.11), reflow at **320 CSS px** (1.4.10), targets at least **24x24 px** for AA (2.5.8). **ERI's bar is 44x44 px**, the AAA level in 2.5.5.
- WCAG 2.2 (2024-12-12) added 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication and 3.2.6 Consistent Help, and **removed 4.1.1 Parsing**.

## Minimal working example
It matches `challenges/02-job-fit-checker/web/` and adds an error summary.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Check a job - Hello ERI</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
  <a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
  <main id="main">
    <h1>Is this job right for me?</h1>
    <div id="errors" role="alert"></div>            <!-- empty until submit fails -->
    <form id="fit-form" novalidate>
      <label for="hours">Hours each week</label>
      <input id="hours" name="hours" type="number" min="1" max="60" required
             inputmode="numeric" aria-describedby="hours-hint">
      <p id="hours-hint" class="hint">Example: 20</p>
      <fieldset>
        <legend>Do you get Social Security disability benefits?</legend>
        <label><input type="radio" id="benefit-ssi" name="benefit" value="SSI" required> SSI</label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="benefit" value="SSDI"> SSDI</label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="benefit" value="none"> No / not sure</label>
      </fieldset>
      <button type="submit">Check this job</button>
    </form>
    <p id="count" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p>  <!-- short, non-focus updates -->
    <section id="fit-result" aria-labelledby="result-h"></section>
  </main>
  <script src="app.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

```js
// app.js: validate, then show errors (and focus them) or show results (and focus the heading)
document.getElementById('fit-form').addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  var f = e.target, errors = document.getElementById('errors');
  errors.replaceChildren();
  var bad = !f.hours.value ? ['hours', 'Enter hours each week.']
          : !f.benefit.value ? ['benefit-ssi', 'Pick an answer about benefits.'] : null;
  if (bad) {
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = '#' + bad[0]; a.textContent = bad[1];
    errors.append(a);                                  // role="alert" announces it
    document.getElementById(bad[0]).focus();
    return;
  }
  var h2 = document.createElement('h2');
  h2.id = 'result-h'; h2.tabIndex = -1; h2.textContent = 'Good to know';
  document.getElementById('fit-result').replaceChildren(h2 /*, ...more nodes */);
  h2.focus();
});
```
The pattern: one message, linked to the field, and then focus goes to that field. Using `novalidate` swaps the browser's error bubbles for your own plain-language messages. Leave it off if you'd rather keep the native bubbles.

```css
:root { --fg:#1b1b1b; --bg:#fff; --accent:#0b5cad; --muted:#555; --error:#b00020; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --fg:#f2f2f2; --bg:#141414; --accent:#7db7ff; --muted:#bbb; --error:#ff8a80; }
}
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { font: 18px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--fg); background: var(--bg);
       margin: 0 auto; max-width: 48rem; padding: 1rem; }
img, table { max-width: 100%; }                        /* 320px reflow */
.skip { position: absolute; left: -999px; } .skip:focus { left: 1rem; top: 1rem; background: var(--bg); padding: .5rem; }
label { display: block; font-weight: 600; margin-top: 1rem; }
input, textarea, select { font: inherit; width: 100%; padding: .6rem; border: 2px solid var(--muted); border-radius: 6px; }
button, fieldset label { min-height: 44px; }           /* ERI target size */
fieldset label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; font-weight: 400; }
:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
#errors a { color: var(--error); font-weight: 600; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
}
```
The palette is the repo's own (`starters/static-web/style.css`). Recheck contrast if you change any color.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** use one `h1`, headings in order, `main` with a skip link, and `lang="en"`.
- [ ] **Do** put a visible `<label>` on every input. A placeholder is not a label.
- [ ] **Do** group radios in `fieldset`/`legend`, and keep the legend short (some screen readers repeat it for each option).
- [ ] **Do** tie hints and errors to fields with `aria-describedby`, and say how to fix the error in text, not only in color.
- [ ] **Do** reflect the outcome in `<title>` or the `h1` on multi-step flows (WAI notifications tutorial).
- [ ] **Do** use `<table>` with `<caption>` and `<th scope="col">` for tabular results, such as a funding-gap list.
- [ ] **Don't** use `aria-live="assertive"` for routine updates. MDN: "extremely annoying… use sparingly".
- [ ] **Don't** inject a live region and fill it in the same tick. It must exist in the initial markup.
- [ ] **Don't** put `role="alert"` and `aria-live="assertive"` on the same element. MDN notes double speech on iOS VoiceOver.
- [ ] **Don't** remove focus outlines, use `tabindex` > 0, or build `div` buttons.
- [ ] **Don't** hide content behind sticky headers. 2.4.11 requires that focus is not entirely obscured.

## Security
- Accessibility code is still code. Error and status messages that echo user input go in through `textContent` ([javascript-jquery.md](javascript-jquery.md)).
- Login screens, if any: no cognitive puzzles or copy-blocking. Allow paste and password managers (3.3.8 Accessible Authentication). Better still, don't add login to a 4-hour prototype.

## Accessibility: 10-minute test routine
1. **Keyboard only:** unplug the mouse. Tab through every control. Is focus visible everywhere? Can you reach and use every control, with no trap? Do Enter and Space work?
2. **Zoom 200% and a 320px-wide window** (DevTools device toolbar, width 320): you should need no sideways scroll for text.
3. **Automated:** Chrome DevTools > Lighthouse > Accessibility, and `npx @axe-core/cli http://localhost:8000` (verify the CLI name and version). Automated tools catch only part of the problems, so fix what they find and keep testing by hand.
4. **Contrast:** WebAIM contrast checker on text, borders and focus rings, in both light and dark mode.
5. **Screen reader, 2 minutes:** VoiceOver (Cmd+F5) or NVDA. Submit the form. You should hear the result heading. Search and you should hear "12 of 60 jobs".
6. **Reduced motion:** turn on the OS setting and reload. Nothing should slide or pulse.
7. **Plain language:** read the result aloud. Aim for about a 6th-grade level, and spell out SSI and SSDI the first time.

### Note on the repo's result pattern
`challenges/02` and `03` put `aria-live="polite"` on the result section **and** move focus to it. Some screen readers may then read the result twice (verify with VoiceOver and NVDA). Pick one: move focus to a heading (good for submit results), or use a live region with no focus move (good for filters).

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- `aria-label` on a `<div>` with no role. ARIA on non-interactive generic elements is often ignored.
- `role="button"` on a `div` without `tabindex="0"` and Enter/Space handlers. Use `<button>`.
- Claiming "WCAG 2.2 AA requires 44x44 targets". AA is 24x24 (2.5.8). 44x44 is AAA (2.5.5) and is ERI's chosen bar.
- Citing "4.1.1 Parsing". It was removed in WCAG 2.2.
- `outline: none` in a CSS reset, `placeholder` used as the label, or color as the only error signal.
- Live regions created by JS right before the message is set.
- An invented "WCAG 3.0 requirement". WCAG 2.2 is the current Recommendation.

## How to hand off to ERI
- Include a short **"Accessibility check"** section in the team README: what you tested (keyboard, zoom/320px, Lighthouse score, which screen reader) and what's still known to be broken.
- Keep the CSS in one file with color tokens on `:root`. ERI's theme can then override `--accent` and friends.
- Keep markup that works without JS where you can (a real `<form>`), so the WordPress version degrades gracefully.

## Sources
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/): criteria numbers and levels, 4.1.1 removed, published 2024-12-12

# JavaScript and jQuery for ERI prototypes

## TL;DR
- **Write plain JavaScript first.** Keep the logic in a file that doesn't touch the DOM and wraps itself in the repo's IIFE/UMD pattern. Then it runs in the browser, inside the WordPress plugin, and in `node tests/test.js`.
- **jQuery is fine** when the page already loads it (ERI's WordPress does, and `starters/static-web` vendors **jQuery 3.7.1**). **jQuery 4.0.0 shipped on 2026-01-17.** 3.x now gets only "critical security patches and bug fixes".
- **Put user text in with `textContent` or jQuery `.text()`.** Never pass user text to `innerHTML` or `.html()` unless you escape it first.
- `fetch()` **does not reject on 404 or 500**. Check `response.ok`. Never put API keys in front-end code.

## Minimal working example
The same three-file shape as `challenges/02-job-fit-checker/web/`: core logic, page glue, and a Node test.

```js
// web/hours.js: core logic with no DOM. Works in browsers, in WordPress and in Node.
(function (root) {
  var WEEKS_PER_MONTH = 4.33;
  function monthlyEarnings(hoursPerWeek, wagePerHour) {
    var h = Number(hoursPerWeek) || 0, w = Number(wagePerHour) || 0;
    return Math.round(h * w * WEEKS_PER_MONTH);
  }
  var api = { monthlyEarnings: monthlyEarnings };
  if (typeof module !== 'undefined' && module.exports) module.exports = api; // Node tests
  else root.eriHours = api;                                                   // browser global, eri_ prefix
})(this);
```

```js
// web/app.js: page glue. Builds nodes with textContent, so there is no XSS risk.
document.getElementById('hours-form').addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  var f = e.target;
  var out = document.getElementById('hours-result');
  var monthly = eriHours.monthlyEarnings(f.hours.value, f.wage.value);
  var h2 = document.createElement('h2');
  h2.tabIndex = -1;                       // so we can move focus here
  h2.textContent = 'About $' + monthly + ' a month from this job';
  var p = document.createElement('p');
  p.textContent = 'Estimate only. Talk to a benefits specialist: WIPA 1-877-826-1752.';
  out.replaceChildren(h2, p);
  h2.focus();
});
```

```js
// tests/test.js: run with `node tests/test.js`. Exits non-zero on failure, so CI and tools/check.sh notice.
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const { monthlyEarnings } = require('../web/hours.js');
let failed = 0;
function test(name, fn) {
  try { fn(); console.log('PASS ' + name); }
  catch (e) { failed++; console.log('FAIL ' + name + ': ' + e.message); }
}
test('20 h x $15 = $1299/month', () => assert.equal(monthlyEarnings(20, 15), 1299));
test('blank input is 0, not NaN', () => assert.equal(monthlyEarnings('', ''), 0));
process.exitCode = failed ? 1 : 0;
```

Load order in HTML: `<script src="hours.js"></script>` and then `<script src="app.js"></script>`, both at the end of `<body>`, the same as the challenge pages.

### The same render with jQuery (when `$` is already on the page)
```js
jQuery(function ($) {                       // safe in WordPress, where $ may not be global (verify)
  var $list = $('#jobs');
  function render(jobs) {
    $list.empty();
    jobs.forEach(function (j) {
      $('<li>').append($('<strong>').text(j.title), document.createTextNode(' - ' + j.employer))
               .appendTo($list);
    });
    $('#count').text(jobs.length + ' jobs');  // #count has role="status"
  }
  // ...call render(...) after loading data
});
```

### fetch with real error handling
```js
async function loadJobs(url) {
  const status = document.getElementById('count');
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) }); // timeout support: (verify)
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Server said ' + res.status);
    return await res.json();                    // throws if the body isn't JSON
  } catch (err) {
    status.textContent = 'Could not load jobs. Please try again.'; // plain words, announced
    console.error(err);
    return [];
  }
}
```

### If you must build HTML strings
```js
function esc(s) {
  return String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, c =>
    ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&#39;' }[c]));
}
list.innerHTML = jobs.map(j => `<li><strong>${esc(j.title)}</strong> - ${esc(j.employer)}</li>`).join('');
```
`challenges/03-job-post-checker/web/app.js` escapes the pasted phrase this way. `starters/static-web/app.js` puts CSV fields into `.html()` without escaping. That's fine for the bundled synthetic file, but **don't copy that pattern** once any value comes from a user, an API or an LLM.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** keep business rules in a DOM-free IIFE file and test them in Node.
- [ ] **Do** use `addEventListener('submit', ...)` on the `<form>`, not `click` on the button. Then Enter works, and so does native `required` validation.
- [ ] **Do** call `e.preventDefault()` and read values with `form.elements` or `form.fieldName.value`.
- [ ] **Do** prefix globals, CSS classes and IDs with `eri` / `eri_` so they don't clash inside WordPress.
- [ ] **Do** use `Array.isArray`, `JSON.parse` and `String.prototype.trim`. jQuery 4 removed `$.isArray`, `$.parseJSON`, `$.trim` and `$.type`.
- [ ] **Don't** use inline `onclick=""` handlers. They break a strict CSP and mix markup with logic.
- [ ] **Don't** add a bundler, a framework or npm packages for a 4-hour prototype. ERI has to maintain it.
- [ ] **Don't** use ES modules (`type="module"`) unless you serve over HTTP. They fail over `file://` with CORS errors, and they don't put anything in global scope, so the IIFE pattern is simpler here.
- [ ] **Don't** load jQuery from a CDN at the venue without a fallback. Vendor it, as `starters/static-web/vendor/` does.

## Security
- **XSS:** MDN calls `innerHTML` "probably the most common vector for cross-site scripting". It won't run `<script>`, but `<img src=x onerror=...>` does run. Use `textContent`, `.text()`, `createElement`, or `esc()`.
- **LLM output is user input.** Escape it, or render it with `textContent`.
- **No secrets in the browser.** Anything in a `.js` file or a `<script>` is public. LLM calls go through PHP (`starters/ai-helpers/php/llm.php`) with keys read from env vars.
- **Don't log data you shouldn't have.** Even with synthetic data, don't `console.log` whole records in code you'll hand off.
- jQuery 4 adds Trusted Types support, which helps if ERI ever enforces a CSP (`require-trusted-types-for`).

## Accessibility
- After a submit, render results into an existing container and **move focus to the result heading** (`tabIndex = -1`, then `.focus()`). See [html-css-accessibility.md](html-css-accessibility.md).
- Live-region text (`role="status"`) must change **after** the region is already in the DOM. Put it in the initial HTML.
- jQuery 4 changed the focus event order to the W3C order (blur, focusout, focus, focusin). Retest any focus or blur handlers if you upgrade.
- Don't build fake controls (`<div onclick>`). Use `<button>`, which you get keyboard support for free.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
| The assistant writes | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `el.innerHTML = '<li>' + userText + '</li>'` | `textContent` or `esc()` |
| `fetch(url).then(r => r.json())` with no `r.ok` check | Check `ok` and show a plain-language error |
| `$.trim`, `$.isArray`, `.size()`, `.bind()` style APIs | Native equivalents. Check [the 4.0 upgrade guide](https://jquery.com/upgrade-guide/4.0/) (verify, linked from the release post) |
| An `OPENAI_API_KEY` constant in `app.js` | Move the call to PHP and read the key from env |
| `import`/`export` plus a webpack config | Use the IIFE pattern above, with no build step |
| A test file that only `console.log`s | Set `process.exitCode = 1` on failure |
| `$(document).ready(...)` using `$` inside WordPress | `jQuery(function ($) { ... })` |

## How to hand off to ERI
1. Put the core logic in its own file, with tests: `node tests/test.js` prints PASS lines and exits 0.
2. Make no build step and load files with plain `<script>` tags, so they drop into `wp_enqueue_script` (see `challenges/02-job-fit-checker/wp-plugin/`).
3. Write down in the README which jQuery version you tested against. On a WordPress page, check it in the browser console with `jQuery.fn.jquery`. The version WordPress bundles is a (verify) item.
4. List every external URL the code calls, and confirm none of them needs a secret in the browser.

## Sources
- [jQuery 4.0.0 release post](https://blog.jquery.com/?p=5047): released 2026-01-17, drops IE<11, removed APIs, slim build drops Deferreds/Callbacks, focus order, Trusted Types
- [jQuery download](https://jquery.com/download/): 4.0.0 is current, Migrate 3.6.0
- [jQuery version support](https://jquery.com/support/): 3.x gets only critical security and bug fixes
- [jQuery .text()](https://api.jquery.com/text/)
- [MDN textContent](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Node/textContent) · [MDN innerHTML](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/innerHTML)
- [MDN Using Fetch](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch) · [MDN JavaScript modules](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules)

# Plain PHP + MySQL best practices

## TL;DR
- **Supported PHP on 2026-10-23:** 8.2 (security fixes until **2026-12-31**), 8.3 (security until 2027-12-31), 8.4 (active until 2026-12-31, security until 2028-12-31), 8.5 (active until 2027-12-31). **8.1 and older are end of life.** Target **8.3+** (the starter's Docker image is `php:8.3-apache`); 8.2 is fine for the event but dies in ten weeks. `AGENTS.md` still says "PHP 8.1+", which is now EOL.
- **MySQL 8.0 reached end of life in April 2026** (per Oracle); use **8.4 LTS**. The starter's `mysql:8.0` image is fine for a demo; tell ERI it was tested on 8.0.
- Every query with input is a **PDO prepared statement**. Every echo goes through `h()` (`htmlspecialchars`). Every POST checks a **CSRF token**. Config comes from **env vars**.
- `php -S` and phpMyAdmin are **local dev tools only**. Never expose either to the internet.

## Minimal working example
Matches `starters/php-mysql/src/db.php` (env-var config, SQLite fallback, exceptions, `utf8mb4`):
```php
<?php // src/db.php
declare(strict_types=1);

function db(): PDO
{
    static $pdo = null;
    if ($pdo) {
        return $pdo;
    }
    $host = getenv('DB_HOST');
    if ($host) {
        $dsn = sprintf('mysql:host=%s;port=%s;dbname=%s;charset=utf8mb4',
            $host, getenv('DB_PORT') ?: '3306', getenv('DB_NAME') ?: 'eri');
        $pdo = new PDO($dsn, getenv('DB_USER') ?: 'eri', getenv('DB_PASS') ?: 'eri');
    } else {
        $pdo = new PDO('sqlite:' . __DIR__ . '/../eri.sqlite');
    }
    $pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE, PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION); // default since PHP 8.0; be explicit
    $pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE, PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
    return $pdo;
}

function h(?string $s): string
{
    return htmlspecialchars((string) $s, ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE, 'UTF-8');
}

function csrf_token(): string
{
    if (empty($_SESSION['csrf'])) {
        $_SESSION['csrf'] = bin2hex(random_bytes(32));
    }
    return $_SESSION['csrf'];
}

function csrf_check(): void
{
    if (!hash_equals($_SESSION['csrf'] ?? '', (string) ($_POST['csrf'] ?? ''))) {
        http_response_code(403);
        exit('Invalid form token. Reload the page and try again.');
    }
}
```
A page with a search (GET) and a save form (POST), like `public/index.php`:
```php
<?php // public/save.php
declare(strict_types=1);
session_set_cookie_params(['httponly' => true, 'samesite' => 'Lax', 'secure' => !empty($_SERVER['HTTPS'])]);
ini_set('session.use_strict_mode', '1');
session_start();
require __DIR__ . '/../src/db.php';

$msg = '';
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST') {             // state changes only on POST
    csrf_check();
    $id = (string) ($_POST['posting_id'] ?? '');
    if (!preg_match('/^[A-Z0-9-]{1,10}$/', $id)) {        // validate (allowlist), don't "clean"
        $msg = 'That job ID is not valid.';
    } else {
        $stmt = db()->prepare('INSERT INTO saved_jobs (posting_id) VALUES (:id)');
        $stmt->execute([':id' => $id]);
        $msg = 'Saved.';
    }
}
$sort = in_array($_GET['sort'] ?? '', ['title', 'posted_date'], true) ? $_GET['sort'] : 'posted_date'; // identifiers: allowlist
$jobs = db()->query("SELECT posting_id, title FROM job_postings ORDER BY $sort LIMIT 25")->fetchAll();
?>
<form method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="<?= h(csrf_token()) ?>">
  <label for="posting_id">Job ID to save</label>
  <input id="posting_id" name="posting_id" required pattern="[A-Z0-9-]{1,10}">
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<p role="status"><?= h($msg) ?></p>
```
Schema (MySQL 8.x only; for the SQLite fallback use `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` and drop the table options). `utf8mb4` stores all of Unicode; `utf8` (a deprecated alias of `utf8mb3`) cannot store 4-byte characters such as emoji. `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` is accent- and case-insensitive; that it is the server default is **(verify)** with `SHOW COLLATION LIKE 'utf8mb4%'`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE saved_jobs (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  posting_id VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
```
Passwords (only if your prototype truly needs logins; prefer WordPress users when it lives in WP):
```php
$hash = password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT);       // store in VARCHAR(255)
if (password_verify($password, $row['password_hash'])) {
    session_regenerate_id(true);                            // new session ID on login
    $_SESSION['user_id'] = (int) $row['id'];
    if (password_needs_rehash($row['password_hash'], PASSWORD_DEFAULT)) { /* re-hash and UPDATE */ }
}
```
Uploads (avoid them at a hackathon; if you must):
```php
$f = $_FILES['doc'] ?? null;
if (!$f || $f['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK || $f['size'] > 2_000_000) exit('Upload failed.');
$mime = (new finfo(FILEINFO_MIME_TYPE))->file($f['tmp_name']);  // never trust $f['type'] or $f['name']
$ext  = ['application/pdf' => 'pdf', 'image/png' => 'png'][$mime] ?? exit('File type not allowed.');
move_uploaded_file($f['tmp_name'], __DIR__ . '/../uploads/' . bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) . ".$ext"); // outside public/
```

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** bind every value (`:name` or `?`). Placeholders replace a **whole value**: `LIKE :q` with `"%$q%"` as the value, never `'%:q%'`.
- [ ] **Do** allowlist anything that can't be bound (column names, `ORDER BY`, `ASC/DESC`, table names).
- [ ] **Do** keep `ERRMODE_EXCEPTION`, catch at the top level, log the detail, show the user a plain-language message. Set `display_errors=Off` outside dev.
- [ ] **Do** use `charset=utf8mb4` in the DSN **and** in table definitions.
- [ ] **Do** read config with `getenv()` from env vars or a git-ignored `.env`; commit a `.env.example` with fake values.
- [ ] **Do** follow PSR-12: 4-space indent, ~120-char soft line limit, class/function braces on their own line, control-structure braces on the same line, visibility on every property and method, no closing `?>` in PHP-only files.
- [ ] **Don't** use `mysqli_query` with string concatenation, `addslashes`, or "escape everything" as the defense (OWASP: strongly discouraged).
- [ ] **Don't** connect as MySQL `root`; give the app a user with only the rights it needs (OWASP least privilege).
- [ ] **Don't** run `php -S` on a public network. The manual: "It should not be used on a public network."
- [ ] **Don't** use `md5`/`sha1` for passwords or pass a custom salt to `password_hash` (ignored since PHP 8.0).

## Security
- **SQL injection:** prepared statements are OWASP's primary defense; the PHP manual notes injection is still possible if other parts of the query are built from unescaped input.
- **XSS:** `htmlspecialchars` converts `& " ' < >` only. It is for HTML text and quoted attributes. For URLs, validate scheme (`http`/`https`) then escape; for JSON to JS, use `json_encode($x, JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP | JSON_HEX_APOS | JSON_HEX_QUOT)`.
- **CSRF:** synchronizer token in the session, compared with `hash_equals` (constant-time), POST-only state changes, `SameSite` cookies as defense in depth.
- **Sessions:** `session.use_strict_mode=1` (off by default, "mandatory for secure sessions"), `cookie_httponly`, `cookie_secure` on HTTPS, `cookie_samesite=Lax`, `use_only_cookies=1`; regenerate the ID on login.
- **Passwords:** `PASSWORD_DEFAULT` is bcrypt today (default cost 12 since PHP 8.4); bcrypt truncates input at 72 bytes.
- **phpMyAdmin:** in `docker-compose.yml`, bind it to localhost (`"127.0.0.1:8081:80"`) and do the same for MySQL (`"127.0.0.1:3306:3306"`); the starter currently publishes both on all interfaces. On any real server: HTTPS only, remove `setup/`, set `AllowRoot` false, use cookie auth plus 2FA or web-server auth, keep it patched. Never hand ERI a phpMyAdmin URL; hand them SQL files.

## Accessibility
- Server-rendered forms: `<label for>` on every field, `required` + a text error message (not color only), errors summarized at the top with focus moved there.
- Put result counts in `role="status"` (the starter does), tables get `<caption>` and `<th scope="col">` (see `challenges/01-funding-gap-finder/public/index.php`).
- `<html lang="en">`, a `<title>` per page, 16-18px base font, visible focus. See `wiki/domain/accessibility.md`.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- `"SELECT ... WHERE id = $_GET[id]"` or `"... LIKE '%$q%'"`: string-built SQL. Also `ORDER BY $_GET['sort']` with no allowlist.
- `PDO::ERRMODE_SILENT` / `@` suppression, or `echo $e->getMessage()` to the browser (leaks DSN, table names).
- Escaping on input (`htmlspecialchars` before INSERT) instead of on output; double-encoded text in the DB.
- `$_SESSION` used without `session_start()`, or a CSRF token that is never checked.
- `utf8` instead of `utf8mb4`; `VARCHAR(60)` for password hashes.
- Hard-coded DB passwords or API keys in `db.php`, or a `.env` committed to git.
- Trusting `$_FILES['x']['type']`, saving uploads under `public/` with the client's file name.
- Code written for PHP 7 (`create_function`, `each()`, missing types) or using functions that don't exist; run `php -l` and the page.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. README with run steps under 10 minutes: `php seed.php && php -S localhost:8080 -t public`, plus the Docker option. State PHP and MySQL versions tested.
2. Ship `sql/schema.sql` (and a seed script using synthetic `data/` only), `.env.example`, no `.env`, no `vendor/` unless needed.
3. Note how it would move into WordPress: PDO calls become `$wpdb->prepare()`, `h()` becomes `esc_html()`, the CSRF helper becomes a nonce, pages become a shortcode. See [wordpress-plugin.md](wordpress-plugin.md).
4. Run `php -l` on every file; optionally `phpcs --standard=PSR12 src public` **(verify PHPCS ships the PSR12 standard in your version)**.

## Sources
- [PHP Supported Versions](https://www.php.net/supported-versions.php) · [PDO prepared statements](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.prepared-statements.php) · [PDO error handling](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.error-handling.php) · [password_hash](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.password-hash.php) · [htmlspecialchars](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.htmlspecialchars.php)

# Web security checklist for hackathon code

## TL;DR
- Five habits cover most of the risk: **bind SQL parameters, escape on output, check a token on every state change, check permission on every endpoint, keep secrets and real client data out of the code.**
- The current list is **OWASP Top 10:2025**: A01 Broken Access Control, A02 Security Misconfiguration, A03 Software Supply Chain Failures, A04 Cryptographic Failures, A05 Injection, A06 Insecure Design, A07 Authentication Failures, A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures, A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures, A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions.
- Run this list **before the demo** and paste it, ticked, into your team README.

## Minimal working example
The same "save a job" action, done safely in both stacks:

| Step | WordPress | Plain PHP (`starters/php-mysql`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Only POST changes data | `WP_REST_Server::CREATABLE` / `admin_post_eri_save` | `if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST')` |
| CSRF token | `wp_nonce_field('eri_save','eri_nonce')` → `check_admin_referer('eri_save','eri_nonce')`; REST: `X-WP-Nonce` with `wp_create_nonce('wp_rest')` | `csrf_token()` in a hidden field → `hash_equals($_SESSION['csrf'], $_POST['csrf'])` |
| Permission | `current_user_can('edit_posts')` in `permission_callback` | `if (empty($_SESSION['user_id'])) { http_response_code(403); exit; }` |
| Validate input | `validate_callback`, `preg_match`, `in_array(..., true)` | same, then reject with a message |
| Sanitize input | `sanitize_text_field(wp_unslash($_POST['x']))`, `absint`, `sanitize_email` | `trim`, `(int)`, `filter_var($x, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` |
| Query | `$wpdb->prepare('... WHERE id = %d', $id)` / `$wpdb->insert($t, $data, $formats)` | `$pdo->prepare('... WHERE id = :id')->execute([':id' => $id])` |
| Output | `esc_html`, `esc_attr`, `esc_url`, `wp_kses_post` | `htmlspecialchars($s, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8')` (the starter's `h()`) |
| JS output | `.text()` / `textContent` | `.text()` / `textContent` |

```php
// WordPress form handler (admin-post.php), all five habits in one handler
add_action( 'admin_post_eri_save', function () {
	if ( ! current_user_can( 'edit_posts' ) ) { wp_die( esc_html__( 'Not allowed.', 'eri-hello' ), 403 ); }
	check_admin_referer( 'eri_save', 'eri_nonce' );
	$id = sanitize_text_field( wp_unslash( $_POST['posting_id'] ?? '' ) );
	if ( ! preg_match( '/^[A-Z0-9-]{1,10}$/', $id ) ) { wp_safe_redirect( add_query_arg( 'eri_err', 1, wp_get_referer() ) ); exit; }
	global $wpdb;
	$wpdb->insert( $wpdb->prefix . 'eri_saved', [ 'user_id' => get_current_user_id(), 'posting_id' => $id ], [ '%d', '%s' ] );
	wp_safe_redirect( add_query_arg( 'eri_saved', 1, wp_get_referer() ) ); exit;
} );
```

## Do / Don't checklist
**Injection (A05)**
- [ ] Every SQL value is a bound parameter (`$wpdb->prepare`, PDO `prepare/execute`). No string-built SQL with request data.
- [ ] Column/table/sort names come from an allowlist (`%i` in `$wpdb->prepare` for identifiers, WP 6.2+).
- [ ] No `eval`, `exec`, `system`, `shell_exec`, `unserialize` on user input. Use `json_decode`.
- [ ] The app's DB user is not `root` and has no admin rights.

**XSS**
- [ ] Every echo is escaped for its context, as late as possible (`esc_html`/`esc_attr`/`esc_url` or `h()`).
- [ ] JS uses `textContent` / jQuery `.text()` / `.val()`. `innerHTML`, `.html()`, `.append(string)` only with fixed, trusted strings.
- [ ] No user data inside `<script>`, inline `on*=` handlers, `style` blocks or unquoted attributes. Pass data with `wp_localize_script` / `json_encode` and attach handlers with `addEventListener` / `.on()`.
- [ ] Rich HTML from users: `wp_kses_post` (WP) or DOMPurify (JS). CSP is defense in depth, not the fix.

**CSRF**
- [ ] Every POST/PUT/DELETE checks a nonce or session token; no state changes on GET.
- [ ] Session cookies are `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure` on HTTPS. Remember OWASP: "XSS can defeat all CSRF mitigation techniques."

**Access control and auth (A01, A07)**
- [ ] Every REST route has a real `permission_callback`; `__return_true` only for public synthetic data.
- [ ] Admin pages check a capability (`manage_options`); `is_admin()` and nonces are not permission checks.
- [ ] Use WordPress logins when inside WP. In plain PHP: `password_hash(PASSWORD_DEFAULT)`, `password_verify`, `session_regenerate_id(true)` on login, `session.use_strict_mode=1`.
- [ ] IDs in URLs (`?client=17`) are checked against the current user; never "security by unguessable ID".

**Secrets, config and data (A02, A04)**
- [ ] API keys and DB passwords come from env vars or a git-ignored `.env`; `.env.example` has fake values. `git grep -nE "sk-|api_key|password\s*="` returns nothing real.
- [ ] Only synthetic data from `data/`. No real names, SSNs, case notes or benefits data, ever.
- [ ] `display_errors=Off` and `WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY` false outside local dev; `php -S` and phpMyAdmin never on a public network (bind Docker ports to `127.0.0.1`).
- [ ] Anything AI-related can be switched off and is gated behind recorded consent (see `AGENTS.md`).

**Dependencies (A03, A08)**
- [ ] Fewest possible dependencies, each explained in the README. Pin versions (no `"latest"`), commit lock files, run `npm audit` / `composer audit`.
- [ ] jQuery and React come from WordPress (`'jquery'` dependency, `@wordpress/element`), not CDNs. If you must use a CDN in a static page, pin the exact version and add `integrity` (SRI).
- [ ] Supported runtimes: PHP 8.2+ (8.1 is EOL; 8.2 security support ends 2026-12-31), WordPress 7.1.x, MySQL 8.4 LTS.

**CORS**
- [ ] No `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on anything that isn't public. Allowlist exact origins; never echo back the request's `Origin` unchecked.
- [ ] CORS is not access control. Endpoints still need auth and CSRF checks.
- [ ] Don't put tokens or session IDs in `localStorage`; one XSS can read it all.

**Errors and logging (A09, A10)**
- [ ] Catch exceptions at the top; show a plain-language message; log the detail server-side. Fail closed (deny) when a check errors.
- [ ] Logs never contain passwords, session IDs, access tokens, API keys, connection strings or PII (OWASP Logging). Log IDs, not names.
- [ ] No `console.log` of form data in shipped JS; no `var_dump`/`print_r` left in pages.

## Security
This whole page is the security section. When unsure, the rules from the WordPress Security handbook apply everywhere: **never trust user input, escape as late as possible, escape everything from untrusted sources (including your own database), never assume, and prefer validation (reject) over sanitization (clean).**

## Accessibility
Security UX must be accessible too: error and "session expired / invalid token" messages are text (not color only), announced via `role="alert"` or moved focus, and tell the person what to do next ("Reload the page and try again"). Don't use CAPTCHAs that fail WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication) **(verify the criterion text if you add one)**.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- Adds a nonce **or** a capability check, not both. Or adds `'permission_callback' => '__return_true'` to make a 401 go away.
- "Sanitizes" input and then concatenates it into SQL; quotes `'%s'` placeholders in `$wpdb->prepare`.
- Escapes on input, then prints raw on output.
- Builds HTML strings in JS from API responses with `+` and `.html()`.
- Sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` to fix a dev CORS error.
- Hard-codes an API key "for now", or writes a seed file with realistic-looking names.
- Prints `$e->getMessage()` or a stack trace to the browser; logs whole `$_POST` arrays.
- Suggests disabling TLS verification or `WP_DEBUG` display on a shared site.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. Paste this checklist into the team README with each box ticked or marked "N/A because ...".
2. List every endpoint/route, its method, its permission check and its CSRF check in one table.
3. List secrets needed (names only, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and where they are read.
4. State that all data is synthetic and that nothing connects to ERI systems.
5. Point to the stack page used: [wordpress-plugin.md](wordpress-plugin.md), [wordpress-blocks.md](wordpress-blocks.md) or [php-mysql.md](php-mysql.md).

## Sources
- [OWASP Top 10:2025](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/) · [SQL Injection Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) · [XSS Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) · [CSRF Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) · [HTML5 Security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) · [Logging](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [WordPress Security](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/) · [Nonces](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/) · [Escaping Data](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/escaping/) · [REST Custom Endpoints](https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/extending-the-rest-api/adding-custom-endpoints/)

# Supabase and Postgres

## TL;DR
- **Turn on RLS on every table.** Tables made in the Dashboard get RLS by default. **Tables made in the SQL editor or migrations do not**, so always write `alter table … enable row level security;`. With RLS on and no policy, the API returns nothing.
- **The publishable key (`sb_publishable_…`, legacy `anon`) is public** and safe in the app. **The secret key (`sb_secret_…`, legacy `service_role`) bypasses RLS and never ships** in a browser, an app, a repo or a chat. Supabase is "deprecating the `anon` and `service_role` keys by the end of 2026".
- **Free plan (2026-10-23):** 2 active projects, 500 MB database, 1 GB file storage, 5 GB egress, 50,000 MAU, and projects **pause after 1 week of inactivity**.
- **Synthetic data only.** Keep the `synthetic boolean default true` column and filter on it in the policy, as the starter does.

## Minimal working example
The starter's migration, `starters/expo-supabase/supabase/migrations/0001_job_postings.sql`, as it is in the repo:

```sql
create table if not exists public.job_postings (
  posting_id text primary key,
  employer text, title text, category text, neighborhood text, zip text,
  lat numeric(9,5), lon numeric(9,5),
  hours_per_week int, wage_per_hour numeric(6,2),
  health_insurance boolean, shift text, remote boolean, near_bus_line boolean,
  description text, posted_date date, synthetic boolean default true
);
alter table public.job_postings enable row level security;
create policy "public read synthetic postings" on public.job_postings for select using (synthetic = true);
```

A per-user table, such as saved jobs, with owner-only policies. This is the docs' pattern, with `(select auth.uid())` for caching:

```sql
create table public.saved_jobs (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  posting_id text not null references public.job_postings(posting_id),
  note text,                                   -- synthetic notes only
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
alter table public.saved_jobs enable row level security;
create index on public.saved_jobs (user_id);   -- index every column a policy filters on

create policy "owners read"   on public.saved_jobs for select to authenticated using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
create policy "owners add"    on public.saved_jobs for insert to authenticated with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
create policy "owners delete" on public.saved_jobs for delete to authenticated using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
```

Client, as in `starters/expo-supabase/lib/supabase.js` (supabase-js v2 with AsyncStorage):
```js
import 'react-native-url-polyfill/auto';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
const url = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const anonKey = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;   // publishable or legacy anon key
export const supabase = url && anonKey
  ? createClient(url, anonKey, { auth: { storage: AsyncStorage, persistSession: true, autoRefreshToken: true } })
  : null;                                                     // null means use the bundled sample data
```
Optional additions from Supabase's React Native auth quickstart: `detectSessionInUrl: false`, and an `AppState` listener that calls `supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh()` when the app is active and `stopAutoRefresh()` otherwise. Both quickstarts current on 2026-10-23 (Supabase's Expo one and Expo's Supabase guide) use `expo-sqlite`'s `localStorage` instead of AsyncStorage, and name the variable `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`. The starter's AsyncStorage setup still matches Supabase's React Native auth quickstart, so you don't need to switch mid-hackathon.

Query with error handling:
```js
const { data, error } = await supabase.from('job_postings').select('posting_id,title,employer').ilike('title', `%${q}%`).limit(25);
if (error) setStatus(`Could not load jobs (${error.message}). Showing sample data.`);
```

Auth basics (only if your PRD truly needs sign-in):
```js
const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password });
const { data: { session }, error: e2 } = await supabase.auth.signUp({ email, password }); // no session = check email
```
Use test emails on a domain you control (or `+test` aliases). Never use a client's email.

### Migrations and seed
```bash
supabase migration new saved_jobs     # creates supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_saved_jobs.sql
supabase db reset                     # local: reapply migrations + supabase/seed.sql
supabase link                         # pick your remote project
supabase db push                      # apply migrations remotely (add --include-seed to seed)
```
No CLI? Paste the SQL into the Dashboard SQL editor, and still commit the `.sql` file.

### CSV import
- **Dashboard:** Table Editor > your table > Insert > Import data from CSV (limit 100 MB). `data/job_postings.csv` fits easily. The column headers must match the table's column names.
- **psql:** `\copy public.job_postings from 'data/job_postings.csv' with (format csv, header true)` (verify against your connection string). Postgres `COPY` is the bulk path the docs point to.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** write one policy per operation (select, insert, update, delete), scoped with `to anon` or `to authenticated`.
- [ ] **Do** test policies as a real client. In the app or `curl`, use the publishable key only and confirm another user's rows come back empty.
- [ ] **Do** keep every schema change in a migration file in the repo.
- [ ] **Don't** use `to anon using (true)` except on data that is truly public. Here, that's only synthetic job postings.
- [ ] **Don't** disable RLS "to get it working". Add the missing policy instead.
- [ ] **Don't** store files with real documents in Storage. Synthetic only, and Storage needs its own policies.
- [ ] **Don't** leave a demo project with open write policies after the event. Pause or delete it.

## Security
- **Key handling:** the publishable/anon key goes in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`. The secret/service_role key lives only in server-side env vars (an Edge Function or PHP). Keep it out of `.env` files in a mobile project, out of URLs, and out of chat. A secret key used from a browser is rejected with 401, but a leaked key still works from other tools, so rotate it if it leaks.
- **RLS is the only wall** between the public key and your data. On UPDATE, `using` picks the rows a user can target and `with check` validates the new row. Leave out `with check` and `using` applies to both.
- With a user token present, RLS applies even to requests made with the secret key.
- Consider turning off "Automatically expose new tables" in the Data API settings, so a forgotten table isn't reachable.
- **Data:** synthetic only. ERI's real systems hold SSA, DVR and health-related information that must never go into a hackathon project (see `wiki/domain/privacy-and-data.md`).

## Accessibility
Not a database concern directly, but:
- Surface errors as plain-language text in a status region, never as a raw Postgres error code alone.
- Auth screens must allow paste and password managers (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8). Use magic links or no login at all if the PRD allows.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- Putting `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in the Expo app "to fix permission errors". **Reject this every time.**
- `create table` in a migration without `enable row level security`, or `alter table … disable row level security`.
- `using (auth.uid() = user_id)` on an insert policy. Inserts need `with check`.
- supabase-js v1 syntax: `supabase.auth.signIn(...)`, `supabase.from(...).select().then(r => r.body)`. v2 uses `signInWithPassword` and returns `{ data, error }`.
- Assuming a `public.users` table exists. Auth users are in `auth.users`.
- Out-of-date free-plan numbers. Check the [pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing).

## Plain Postgres fallback
No account, or the venue network is bad? The app already falls back to bundled JSON. For SQL practice, run Postgres locally and apply the same migration. Strip the Supabase-only parts (`auth.uid()`, `to authenticated`, and policies that reference `auth`):
```bash
docker run --rm -d --name eri-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=eri -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 postgres:18
psql postgresql://postgres:eri@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres -f starters/expo-supabase/supabase/migrations/0001_job_postings.sql
```
(The image tag `postgres:18` is the one Docker's own docs used on 2026-10-23. Pin whatever you test with.) ERI's hosting is PHP + MySQL, so for a staff web tool, `starters/php-mysql` is usually the better fallback.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. Commit `supabase/migrations/*.sql` and a `seed.sql` or CSV of **synthetic** rows only.
2. In the README, list every table, its RLS status and each policy in one line, plus which key the client uses.
3. Hand off **no keys at all**. ERI creates its own project and keys, and the team's project is paused or deleted after judging.
4. Note the Supabase-specific bits (auth, policies) that would need rework to move to ERI's MySQL hosting.

## Sources
- [Supabase API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys): key types, RLS bypass, legacy key deprecation by end of 2026
- [Row Level Security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) · [Securing your API](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api)
- [Database migrations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/database-migrations) · [Import data](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/import-data)
- [Expo React Native quickstart](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/quickstarts/expo-react-native) · [React Native auth quickstart](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/quickstarts/react-native) · [Expo: Using Supabase](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/using-supabase.md)
- [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing.md): free-plan limits as of 2026-10-23


<!-- FILE: wiki/stack/wordpress-blocks.md -->
