# WordPress block (Gutenberg) best practices

## TL;DR
- Use a block when **ERI staff will edit the content** in the block editor. Use a **shortcode** when the output is data-driven, or when the page is built in **Cornerstone (Themeco X/Pro)**, which ERI's main site appears to use. Best handoff: one plugin with a **dynamic block and a shortcode sharing the same PHP render function**.
- `block.json` with `"apiVersion": 3` (introduced in WP 6.3). In WP 7.0 the post editor is iframed only if **every block in the post** is v3+; the iframe is **not enforced** in 7.0 but is planned, so v2 blocks are a liability.
- Scaffold with `npx @wordpress/create-block@latest` (Node **>= 22.13.0** per the package docs). `wp-scripts build --blocks-manifest` plus `wp_register_block_types_from_metadata_collection()` (WP 6.8+) is what `starters/eri-job-card/` uses.
- Prefer **dynamic** (`render.php`) blocks for hackathon code: changing markup later doesn't trigger "This block contains unexpected or invalid content".

## Minimal working example
Scaffold (dynamic variant), then build:
```bash
npx @wordpress/create-block@latest --namespace="eri" --slug="eri-job-card" --variant="dynamic"
cd eri-job-card && npm start          # watch; `npm run build` for production, `npm run plugin-zip` to ship
```
For `viewScriptModule` add `--experimental-modules` to the `build` and `start` scripts (`wp-scripts build --blocks-manifest --experimental-modules`), or scaffold with `--template @wordpress/create-block-interactive-template` **(verify template name in the External Project Templates guide)**.
`src/eri-job-card/block.json` (same attributes as the repo starter, plus `render` and a view module):
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/block.json",
  "apiVersion": 3,
  "name": "eri/eri-job-card",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "title": "ERI Job Card",
  "category": "widgets",
  "icon": "id-alt",
  "textdomain": "eri-job-card",
  "supports": { "html": false, "interactivity": true },
  "attributes": {
    "title":          { "type": "string", "default": "Dishwasher" },
    "employer":       { "type": "string", "default": "Cream City Cafe" },
    "hours":          { "type": "number", "default": 20 },
    "wage":           { "type": "string", "default": "14.00" },
    "accommodations": { "type": "string", "default": "Flexible schedule; written instructions" }
  },
  "editorScript": "file:./index.js",
  "editorStyle": "file:./index.css",
  "style": "file:./style-index.css",
  "render": "file:./render.php",
  "viewScriptModule": "file:./view.js"
}
```
`src/eri-job-card/render.php` (receives `$attributes`, `$content`, `$block`; escape everything):
```php
<?php
$a  = $attributes;
$id = wp_unique_id( 'eri-acc-' );
?>
<article <?php echo get_block_wrapper_attributes(); ?>
	aria-label="<?php echo esc_attr( sprintf( __( '%1$s at %2$s', 'eri-job-card' ), $a['title'], $a['employer'] ) ); ?>"
	data-wp-interactive="eri/job-card" <?php echo wp_interactivity_data_wp_context( [ 'open' => false ] ); ?>>
	<h3><?php echo esc_html( $a['title'] ); ?></h3>
	<p><?php echo esc_html( sprintf( '%s · %d h/wk · $%s/h', $a['employer'], $a['hours'], $a['wage'] ) ); ?></p>
	<button type="button" data-wp-on--click="actions.toggle" data-wp-bind--aria-expanded="context.open"
		aria-controls="<?php echo esc_attr( $id ); ?>"><?php esc_html_e( 'Accommodations', 'eri-job-card' ); ?></button>
	<p id="<?php echo esc_attr( $id ); ?>" data-wp-bind--hidden="!context.open"><?php echo esc_html( $a['accommodations'] ); ?></p>
</article>
```
`src/eri-job-card/view.js` (Interactivity API; namespace must match `data-wp-interactive`):
```js
import { store, getContext } from '@wordpress/interactivity';
store( 'eri/job-card', {
	actions: { toggle: () => { const ctx = getContext(); ctx.open = ! ctx.open; } },
} );
```
`save.js` for a dynamic block returns `null` (only the comment delimiter and attributes are stored):
```js
export default function save() { return null; }
```
Keep `edit.js` from the starter: `InspectorControls` + labelled `TextControl`s, `useBlockProps()` on the wrapper. Render a live preview in the editor with `ServerSideRender` only if needed **(verify package status before adding)**.

**Shortcode fallback for Cornerstone pages** (same plugin, same output):
```php
add_action( 'init', function () {
	wp_register_block_types_from_metadata_collection( __DIR__ . '/build', __DIR__ . '/build/blocks-manifest.php' );
	add_shortcode( 'eri_job_card', function ( $atts ) {
		$atts = shortcode_atts( [ 'title' => 'Dishwasher', 'employer' => 'Cream City Cafe', 'hours' => 20,
			'wage' => '14.00', 'accommodations' => '' ], $atts, 'eri_job_card' );
		return render_block( [ 'blockName' => 'eri/eri-job-card', 'attrs' => array_map( 'sanitize_text_field', $atts ),
			'innerBlocks' => [], 'innerHTML' => '', 'innerContent' => [] ] );
	} );
} );
```
Usage in any Cornerstone text/raw element or classic page: `[eri_job_card title="Line cook" hours="25"]` **(verify which Cornerstone element ERI uses for shortcodes)**. Cast `hours` with `absint()` in render.php if it can come from a shortcode.

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** use `apiVersion: 3`, `$schema`, `textdomain`, and `file:` paths in `block.json`; register from metadata, not by hand.
- [ ] **Do** prefix the block name with the `eri/` namespace and keep the plugin slug `eri-*`.
- [ ] **Do** use `useBlockProps()` in edit, `useBlockProps.save()` in static save, `get_block_wrapper_attributes()` in render.php.
- [ ] **Do** commit `build/` for the handoff (the starter does) so ERI can activate without Node, and pin `@wordpress/*` versions instead of `"latest"`.
- [ ] **Do** use `viewScriptModule` for Interactivity API code and `viewScript` for classic scripts (they're not compatible with each other).
- [ ] **Don't** change a static block's `save()` output after content exists: saved posts fail validation. Add a `deprecated` entry or go dynamic.
- [ ] **Don't** fetch data in `save()` or put secrets in block attributes (attributes are stored in post content, visible in the editor and REST).
- [ ] **Don't** add React libraries the editor already provides; import from `@wordpress/element`, `@wordpress/components`, `@wordpress/i18n`.

## Security
- Attributes are user-editable input. Escape in render.php (`esc_html`, `esc_attr`, `esc_url`, `wp_kses_post` for intended HTML).
- Validate attribute types in `block.json` (`type`, `enum`) and cast in PHP (`absint`, `(float)`).
- `data-wp-context` must be valid JSON: build it with `wp_interactivity_data_wp_context( $array )` (WP 6.5+), never by string concatenation.
- Make REST calls from the editor with `apiFetch` (`@wordpress/api-fetch`); when WordPress loads it, it registers root-URL and nonce middleware so `X-WP-Nonce` is sent. The route still needs a real `permission_callback`.

## Accessibility
- Every editor control needs a visible label (`TextControl label=`). Don't hide settings only in the toolbar.
- Front-end markup: one meaningful heading level that fits the page (the starter uses `h3`), real `<button>` for toggles with `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`, `hidden` for collapsed panels.
- The Handbook asks that **all content sit inside landmarks**; a block is content inside the theme's `main`, so don't add extra `<main>` or `role="region"` wrappers without a label.
- Check keyboard order, visible focus and contrast in both the editor and the X theme front end. See `wiki/domain/accessibility.md` (WCAG 2.2 AA).

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- Emitting `apiVersion: 2` (or 1), `registerBlockType` with all metadata in JS, or old `wp.blocks` globals with no build.
- Static blocks whose `save()` uses `Date.now()`, random IDs or fetched data, which causes validation errors on reload.
- Forgetting `--blocks-manifest` / the manifest file, so `wp_register_block_types_from_metadata_collection()` registers nothing.
- `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or unescaped `echo $attributes['x']` in render.php.
- Mixing `viewScript` and Interactivity API imports; forgetting `"interactivity": true` in `supports`.
- Assuming the site uses the block editor everywhere. ERI's Cornerstone pages may never show your block, so ship the shortcode too.
- `"latest"` dependencies (as in the starter's `package.json`) left in for the handoff, so the build differs next month.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. `npm run build` then `npm run plugin-zip`. The zip must have a root folder named after the plugin.
2. README: block name, attributes, shortcode equivalent, tested WP version (7.1.x) and Node version, and whether `build/` is committed.
3. Show the block in the block editor **and** the shortcode on a Cornerstone or classic page; note which ERI site(s) it targets on the multisite.
4. Run `npm run lint:js` and `lint:css`; run PHPCS on PHP files (see [wordpress-plugin.md](wordpress-plugin.md)).

# WordPress plugin best practices

## TL;DR
- **Current WordPress is 7.1.x** (7.1 released, scheduled for 2026-08-19; 7.1.1 scheduled for 2026-09-17). WordPress 7.0 (released 2026-05-20) raised the **minimum PHP to 7.4**; the Hosting team recommends **PHP 8.4/8.5 and MySQL 8.4** for new installs. Write for **PHP 8.2+** and test on what ERI's host actually runs **(verify with ERI)**.
- Ship one folder, `eri-<thing>/`, with a header, an `ABSPATH` guard, `eri_`-prefixed everything, and a shortcode **or** REST route. Copy `starters/wordpress-plugin/eri-hello/`.
- Security in one line: **validate/sanitize input, check capability, verify nonce, `$wpdb->prepare()`, escape late on output.** REST routes **must** have `permission_callback` (`__return_true` only for public synthetic data).

## Minimal working example
Layout (root stays minimal, per the Handbook): `eri-hello/eri-hello.php` (header + hooks), `uninstall.php`, `includes/data.php` (logic), `assets/` (css/js), `languages/`.

`eri-hello.php`, extending the repo starter with a POST route, a setting and a table:
```php
<?php
/**
 * Plugin Name:       ERI Hello (Hackreation starter)
 * Description:       [eri_jobs] shortcode, REST endpoint and admin page.
 * Version:           0.1.0
 * Requires at least: 6.8
 * Requires PHP:      8.2
 * License:           GPL-2.0-or-later
 * Text Domain:       eri-hello
 */
if ( ! defined( 'ABSPATH' ) ) { exit; }
define( 'ERI_HELLO_DIR', plugin_dir_path( __FILE__ ) ); define( 'ERI_HELLO_URL', plugin_dir_url( __FILE__ ) );
require_once ERI_HELLO_DIR . 'includes/data.php';

// Register assets once; enqueue only where used. $args array (strategy) needs WP 6.3+.
add_action( 'wp_enqueue_scripts', function () {
	wp_register_style( 'eri-hello', ERI_HELLO_URL . 'assets/eri-hello.css', [], '0.1.0' );
	wp_register_script( 'eri-hello', ERI_HELLO_URL . 'assets/eri-hello.js', [ 'jquery' ], '0.1.0',
		[ 'in_footer' => true, 'strategy' => 'defer' ] );
	wp_localize_script( 'eri-hello', 'eriHello', [ 'root' => esc_url_raw( rest_url( 'eri/v1/' ) ),
		'nonce' => wp_create_nonce( 'wp_rest' ) ] ); // JS sends it as the X-WP-Nonce header
} );

add_action( 'init', fn() => add_shortcode( 'eri_jobs', 'eri_hello_shortcode' ) ); // callback RETURNS html
function eri_hello_shortcode( $atts ) {
	$a    = shortcode_atts( [ 'q' => '', 'limit' => 10 ], $atts, 'eri_jobs' );
	$jobs = eri_hello_search_jobs( sanitize_text_field( $a['q'] ), absint( $a['limit'] ) );
	wp_enqueue_style( 'eri-hello' ); wp_enqueue_script( 'eri-hello' );
	ob_start(); ?>
	<section class="eri-hello" aria-labelledby="eri-hello-title">
		<h2 id="eri-hello-title"><?php esc_html_e( 'Sample jobs', 'eri-hello' ); ?></h2>
		<p role="status"><?php echo esc_html( sprintf( _n( '%d result', '%d results', count( $jobs ), 'eri-hello' ), count( $jobs ) ) ); ?></p>
		<ul><?php foreach ( $jobs as $j ) : ?>
			<li><strong><?php echo esc_html( $j['title'] ); ?></strong>, <?php echo esc_html( $j['employer'] ); ?></li>
		<?php endforeach; ?></ul>
	</section>
	<?php return ob_get_clean();
}

add_action( 'rest_api_init', function () {
	register_rest_route( 'eri/v1', '/jobs', [
		'methods'             => WP_REST_Server::READABLE,
		'permission_callback' => '__return_true', // public, synthetic data only
		'args'                => [ 'q' => [ 'type' => 'string', 'sanitize_callback' => 'sanitize_text_field' ] ],
		'callback'            => fn( $req ) => rest_ensure_response( eri_hello_search_jobs( (string) $req['q'], 100 ) ),
	] );
	register_rest_route( 'eri/v1', '/saved', [
		'methods'             => WP_REST_Server::CREATABLE,
		'permission_callback' => fn() => current_user_can( 'edit_posts' ), // capability, not just "logged in"
		'args'                => [ 'posting_id' => [ 'required' => true,
			'validate_callback' => fn( $v ) => (bool) preg_match( '/^[A-Z0-9-]{1,10}$/', (string) $v ) ] ],
		'callback'            => 'eri_hello_save',
	] );
} );
function eri_hello_save( WP_REST_Request $req ) { global $wpdb;
	$ok = $wpdb->insert( $wpdb->prefix . 'eri_saved',
		[ 'user_id' => get_current_user_id(), 'posting_id' => $req['posting_id'] ], [ '%d', '%s' ] );
	return $ok ? new WP_REST_Response( [ 'saved' => true ], 201 ) : new WP_Error( 'eri_db', 'Could not save', [ 'status' => 500 ] );
}

// Settings page under Settings > ERI Hello (Settings API handles its own nonce).
add_action( 'admin_init', fn() => register_setting( 'eri_hello', 'eri_hello_options', [ 'type' => 'array',
	'default' => [ 'limit' => 10 ], 'sanitize_callback' => fn( $v ) => [ 'limit' => min( 100, absint( $v['limit'] ?? 10 ) ) ] ] ) );
add_action( 'admin_menu', function () {
	add_options_page( 'ERI Hello', 'ERI Hello', 'manage_options', 'eri-hello', function () {
		if ( ! current_user_can( 'manage_options' ) ) { return; }
		$o = get_option( 'eri_hello_options' ); ?>
		<div class="wrap"><h1><?php esc_html_e( 'ERI Hello', 'eri-hello' ); ?></h1>
		<form method="post" action="options.php"><?php settings_fields( 'eri_hello' ); ?>
			<label for="eri-limit"><?php esc_html_e( 'Results per page', 'eri-hello' ); ?></label>
			<input id="eri-limit" type="number" name="eri_hello_options[limit]" value="<?php echo esc_attr( $o['limit'] ); ?>">
			<?php submit_button(); ?></form></div>
	<?php } );
} );

// Custom table: dbDelta is picky (each column on its own line, two spaces after PRIMARY KEY, KEY not INDEX).
function eri_hello_install() { global $wpdb;
	require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php';
	dbDelta( "CREATE TABLE {$wpdb->prefix}eri_saved (
  id bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  user_id bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL,
  posting_id varchar(10) NOT NULL,
  created_at datetime DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY  (id),
  KEY user_id (user_id)
) {$wpdb->get_charset_collate()};" );
	update_option( 'eri_hello_db_version', '1' );
}
register_activation_hook( __FILE__, function ( $network_wide ) { // $network_wide: true on "Network Activate"
	if ( is_multisite() && $network_wide ) {
		foreach ( get_sites( [ 'fields' => 'ids' ] ) as $id ) { switch_to_blog( $id ); eri_hello_install(); restore_current_blog(); }
	} else { eri_hello_install(); }
} );
// Activation does not run on update, nor for sites created later: check a stored schema version
// (per site) instead. Alternative for new sites: hook `wp_initialize_site`.
add_action( 'plugins_loaded', function () { if ( get_option( 'eri_hello_db_version' ) !== '1' ) { eri_hello_install(); } } );
```
Reading with `$wpdb`: placeholders unquoted, `%i` for identifiers (WP 6.2+), `esc_like()` for LIKE.
```php
$rows = $wpdb->get_results( $wpdb->prepare(
	"SELECT * FROM %i WHERE user_id = %d AND posting_id LIKE %s",
	$wpdb->prefix . 'eri_saved', get_current_user_id(), '%' . $wpdb->esc_like( $q ) . '%' ), ARRAY_A );
```
`uninstall.php` (runs when the plugin is deleted, not deactivated):
```php
<?php
if ( ! defined( 'WP_UNINSTALL_PLUGIN' ) ) { die; } global $wpdb;
delete_option( 'eri_hello_options' ); delete_option( 'eri_hello_db_version' );
$wpdb->query( "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {$wpdb->prefix}eri_saved" ); // current site only; looping all sites is costly
```
```js
jQuery(function ($) { // assets/eri-hello.js (jQuery bundled with WordPress)
  $.ajax({ url: eriHello.root + 'saved', method: 'POST', data: { posting_id: 'P001' },
    beforeSend: function (x) { x.setRequestHeader('X-WP-Nonce', eriHello.nonce); } })
   .done(function () { $('#eri-msg').text('Saved'); }); // .text(), never .html() with data
});
```

## Do / Don't checklist
- [ ] **Do** prefix functions, options, transients, handles, tables and the REST namespace (`eri_`, `eri/v1`). Handbook: 4-5+ letter prefix, never `wp_` or `__`. Put an `ABSPATH` guard in every file with top-level code.
- [ ] **Do** register assets on `wp_enqueue_scripts`, enqueue inside the shortcode so they load only where used, and use `[ 'strategy' => 'defer' ]` (WP 6.3+). Declare `jquery` as a dependency; **don't** load jQuery from a CDN.
- [ ] **Do** return (not echo) from shortcodes, using `ob_start()` / `ob_get_clean()`.
- [ ] **Do** give REST `args` a `validate_callback` / `sanitize_callback` and return `WP_Error` with a `status`.
- [ ] **Do** gate admin pages with a capability (`manage_options` for settings). `is_admin()` is **not** a permission check.
- [ ] **Don't** run `CREATE TABLE`, `flush_rewrite_rules()` or HTTP calls on every page load; **don't** use `extract()`, `eval()`, `$_REQUEST` or raw `$_GET` in SQL.
- [ ] **Don't** depend on a paid plugin. For a free dependency, use the `Requires Plugins:` header with its wordpress.org slug (added in WP 6.5 **(verify)**).

## Security
- **Input:** `wp_unslash()` then sanitize: `sanitize_text_field`, `sanitize_textarea_field`, `sanitize_email`, `sanitize_key`, `absint`, `esc_url_raw`. The Handbook says validation (reject) beats sanitization (clean).
- **Authorization:** `current_user_can( 'cap' )` in every REST `permission_callback`, admin page and form handler. **CSRF:** forms use `wp_nonce_field( 'eri_save', 'eri_nonce' )` + `check_admin_referer( 'eri_save', 'eri_nonce' )`; AJAX uses `check_ajax_referer()`; REST uses the `wp_rest` nonce in `X-WP-Nonce` (without it, the API treats the user as logged out). Nonces last 12-24 hours and are **never** authentication.
- **SQL:** `$wpdb->prepare()` with unquoted `%s %d %f %i`, or `$wpdb->insert/update/delete` with format arrays. **Output:** escape late, at the echo: `esc_html`, `esc_attr`, `esc_url`, `esc_textarea`, `wp_kses_post` (for allowed HTML), `esc_html__()` for translated text.
- **Multisite:** only Super Admins have `unfiltered_html`, `install_plugins`, `edit_users` on a network. Don't let your plugin give site admins a path around that (e.g. saving raw HTML from a setting).

## Accessibility
- Every input gets a `<label for>`; admin forms use the standard `form-table` markup and `submit_button()`.
- Result counts and save confirmations go in a `role="status"` region; move focus to new content after submit.
- Use real headings (`h2` in content, `h1` only on admin pages), buttons for actions, links for navigation. Front-end CSS must not remove focus outlines; check contrast against ERI's X theme colors. See `wiki/domain/accessibility.md`.

## Common AI-assistant mistakes to watch for
- `'permission_callback' => '__return_true'` on a **write** route, or no callback at all (WP 5.5+ logs `_doing_it_wrong`). Nonce checked but no capability, or the reverse.
- Quoting placeholders (`'%s'`) inside `prepare()`, or interpolating `$_GET` into SQL "because it's sanitized". Hard-coding `wp_` as the table prefix.
- `echo` inside a shortcode (output jumps to the top of the page); escaping early, then concatenating more data.
- `wp_enqueue_script` outside a hook, hard-coded `<script src>` tags, a second copy of jQuery.
- `.html()` / `innerHTML` with API data. `challenges/02-job-fit-checker/.../app.js` builds HTML strings: fine for fixed copy, unsafe for user or API text.
- Invented functions or arguments: check each at developer.wordpress.org/reference. Text domain as a variable, or `__( "Hi $name" )` instead of `sprintf( __( 'Hi %s', 'eri-hello' ), $name )` with a `/* translators: */` comment.
- Assuming single-site: per-site tables need a per-site install, and network-wide settings use `get_site_option()`.

## How to hand off to ERI
1. Run PHPCS with WordPress Coding Standards (WPCS 3.x, Composer-only) and fix or explain what it reports. Rulesets: `WordPress`, `WordPress-Core`, `WordPress-Extra`, `WordPress-Docs`.
   ```bash
   composer config allow-plugins.dealerdirect/phpcodesniffer-composer-installer true && composer require --dev wp-coding-standards/wpcs:"^3.0"
   vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=WordPress-Extra --extensions=php eri-hello/
   ```
2. Zip the plugin folder (`eri-hello/` at the zip root) with `uninstall.php` and a README listing: what it does, shortcode/route names, options and tables it creates, the capability it needs, and tested WP/PHP versions.
3. State whether it was tested **per-site** or **network-activated** (`Network: true` header only if it must be network-wide). Test on a clean multisite: `wp core multisite-install` in the Docker starter **(verify the command works in the starter image)**. No secrets, no external calls, synthetic data only. List every dependency and why.

<!-- FILE: agents/README.md -->

# Agent profiles (simulated users)

Four role-play profiles for **fast, early** usability checks of hackathon prototypes:

| Profile | Simulates | Use it to test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [avg-job-seeker.md](avg-job-seeker.md) | **Marcus**, 23, autistic, on SSI, rides the bus in Milwaukee | Job seeker screens: PRD 02, plain language, benefits fear, commute |
| [avg-eri-employee.md](avg-eri-employee.md) | **Alex**, an ERI employment specialist with about 20 DVR clients | Staff tools: PRD 01 billing checks, caseload, deadlines |
| [avg-attendee.md](avg-attendee.md) | **Priya, Devon, Lena, Sam or Jordan**: hackathon attendees | Event materials: slides, README, PRDs, onboarding |
| [avg-employer.md](avg-employer.md) | **Dana**, a busy Milwaukee hiring manager | Employer tools: PRD 03 job post checker |

## How to use
- **Chat (Claude Pro / ChatGPT):** paste the system prompt, then describe your screens step by step or paste screenshots.
- **Claude Code:** the same profiles are subagents in `.claude/agents/`. Ask: *"Use the avg-job-seeker agent to review challenges/p2-my-workday-assistant/web/index.html."*

## Rules
- These are **composites, not people**. They're a cheap first pass, not evidence. Test with real disabled users and ERI staff before claiming "users love it."
- Only synthetic data goes into any AI tool.
- Watch for the AI flattening disability into stereotypes. If it does, discard that feedback.


<!-- FILE: data/README.md -->

# Synthetic data

**Everything here is fake.** People, employers, PO numbers and notes are all generated by `tools/generate_synthetic_data.py` (seed `20261031`). Nothing comes from ERI's systems. Every row has `synthetic=TRUE`.

Regenerate: `pip install faker && python3 tools/generate_synthetic_data.py`

## PRD 02 / 03: job seekers and postings

| File | Rows | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `job_seekers.csv` | 40 | Job seeker profiles: Milwaukee neighborhood, interests, skills, accommodations, desired hours, transportation, benefits type, DVR/IRIS program, IPE goal |
| `job_postings.csv` | 60 | Fictional Milwaukee employers: title, category, hours, wage, insurance, shift, bus access, description (some include barrier phrases for PRD 03) |

## PRD 01: DVR billing (`dvr/`)

| File | Rows | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fee_schedule.csv` | 7 | Supported Employment services and rates from the WI DVR fee structure (Jul 2026 to Jun 2028) |
| `authorizations.csv` | ~118 | DVR purchase orders: which service was authorized for which client, and when |
| `service_notes.csv` | ~314 | Case notes: date, service, note text, hire details, report submitted date |
| `invoices.csv` | ~242 | What ERI billed: PO, service, month number, amount |

The billing data contains **planted problems** for teams to find: missed months, unbilled hires, underbilled preferred outcomes, and late reports. It also has a **trap**: some months are correctly unbilled because the client wasn't employed. Judges hold the answer key, which is not in the repo.

## PRD 01: Ticket to Work (`ticket/`) and county (`county/`): SIMPLIFIED rules
| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `ticket/tickets.csv` | 15 fake SSDI Ticket holders assigned to ERI PLUS |
| `ticket/monthly_earnings.csv` | Gross earnings per month, and whether a pay stub is on file |
| `ticket/payment_requests.csv` | Payments ERI requested from SSA |
| `county/authorizations.csv` | Units (15-min) authorized per client per month |
| `county/units_delivered.csv` | Units actually delivered |
| `county/claims.csv` | Units claimed, at a FAKE $25/unit |

Simplified Ticket rules (2026): Phase 1 milestone 1 = first month ≥ $1,210 (pays $1,904); milestone 2 = 3rd such month ($1,904); after that, Phase 2 = each month > $1,690 SGA ($571). No pay stub = can't claim yet. Real rules: `wiki/knowledge/benefits/ticket-to-work.md`.

Planted: unclaimed Ticket payments, missing pay stubs, county under-claims, and county **over-claims** (a risk to flag, never money to collect).

### Join keys
`client_id` links authorizations, notes and invoices. `po_number` links authorizations and invoices. `service_code` links to `fee_schedule.csv`.
